headline: Government can cut pension for negligence even without financial loss: HC
content: The government can withhold or reduce an employee's pension for grave misconduct or negligence during service even if no actual financial loss has been caused to the public exchequer, the Punjab and Haryana High Court has ruled.Justice Sandeep Moudgil held that financial loss and misconduct were distinct considerations under Rule 2.2(b) of the Punjab Civil Services Rules, Volume II. The absence of financial loss did not, by itself, prevent the government from exercising its powers under the provision, which permitted withholding or withdrawal of pension, permanently or for a specified period, where a pensioner was found guilty of grave misconduct or negligence."The absence of financial loss, by itself, does not bar the Government from withholding or reducing pension. Financial loss and grave misconduct are two distinct considerations under the pension rules," the court held.The assertion came as Justice Moudgil dismissed a petition filed by a retired Assistant Engineer challenging a 10 per cent cut in his pension with permanent effect. The State’s stand in the matter was that the petitioner, in 2013, “committed serious irregularities in the execution of electrical work.”The State counsel added that the shortcomings, reported by the team on surprise visit, were rectified by the petitioner. The financial loss caused to the State was averted. “But the act of the petitioner, which came to the light only after the surprise checking by Technical Advisor to Chief Minister Punjab made the integrity of the petitioner doubtful. Therefore, the punishment of 10 per cent cut in his pension is fully justifiable.”The petitioner, on the other hand, contended that the electrical work was not found as per the provisions made in the work agreement upon inspected by him on March 4, 2013. The Executive Engineer concerned, was informed vide letter dated March 8, 2013, with a request to direct the contractor to rectify the mistakes. It was also contended that “no financial loss was caused to the government as no payment has been made to the contractor.”Rejecting the argument that financial loss was essential for action under Rule 2.2(b), Justice Moudgil relied on its earlier judgment in the case of “Shadi Lal versus State of Haryana”, which held that "since the procedural irregularities have been found, therefore, the department was competent to impose cut in the pension."Examining the present case, Justice Moudgil asserted: “In the opinion of this Court, once a disciplinary authority concluded in the given set of circumstances of the case that a particular punishment has to be inflicted, then merely because there is a difference in perception would not suggest that the order so passed by the disciplinary authority is incorrect or needs to be varied or modified.”Justice Moudgil added: “If the facts of the case are to be seen, then it was the petitioner who had been charge sheeted for being negligent on official duty who was assigned a particular job where he was eventually held to be negligent. Moreover, had the Technical Adviser to the then Chief Minister, Punjab, had not inspected the work, then payment of inferior work was got to be made to which the Government had to face a loss of lakhs of rupees.”Dismissing the plea, Justice Moudgil concluded the Court did not feel it proper to intervene in the order of cut in the pension or to modify the same “in view the facts and the discretion of the competent authority to impose cut in the pension for a limited period or for whole of the life.”

headline: Delhi pollution: AQI stays above 200, forecast warns of no immediate relief
content: Delhi woke up to another morning of poor air quality on Wednesday, with the city's average Air Quality Index (AQI) at 228 at 7 am, compared with 242 at the same time on Tuesday, according to real-time data from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB). The marginal decline has done little to change the overall picture. Of the 59 monitoring stations in the capital, 56 had valid readings. Thirty-six recorded AQI levels above 200, including five where the readings crossed 300, placing them in the 'very poor' category. Anand Vihar recorded the highest AQI at 336, followed by Delhi Technological University (DTU) at 332. North Campus, Delhi University, recorded 313, while Burari Crossing and IGNOU, Maidan Garhi, reported 305 and 302, respectively. At the other end, Sri Aurobindo Marg recorded the lowest AQI at 140, followed by IMD Lodhi Road at 147 and Patparganj at 148. These locations were in the 'moderate' category. PM10 and PM2.5 were the prominent pollutants in the city's overall reading. NCR cities continue to report poor air Air quality across the National Capital Region (NCR) remained uneven, with several cities recording readings in the poor category. Panchgaon in Haryana reported the highest AQI in the region at 294, followed by Gurugram at 280. Meerut recorded an AQI of 248, followed by Ghaziabad at 240 and Bhiwadi at 236. Bahadurgarh and Dharuhera in Haryana reported readings of 231 and 229, respectively, while Delhi stood at 228. Noida recorded an AQI of 215, while Bulandshahr and Greater Noida reported 211 and 209, respectively. Baghpat was at 206. Rohtak and Sonipat recorded readings of 199 and 190, respectively. Among the better-performing cities in the region, Palwal recorded the lowest AQI at 86, followed by Panipat at 133, Bharatpur at 141 and Hapur at 142. Alwar and Faridabad reported readings of 145 and 155, respectively. Khanna records India's highest AQI Among the 283 cities with valid readings in the CPCB's 7 am dataset, Khanna in Punjab recorded the highest AQI at 323, followed by Jalandhar at 304 and Panchgaon in Haryana at 294. Shamli in Uttar Pradesh reported an AQI of 282, followed by Gurugram at 280. Ballabgarh in Haryana and Anpara in Uttar Pradesh both recorded 255, while Ludhiana in Punjab reported 254. Mandideep in Madhya Pradesh recorded 253. At the other end, Chikkaballapur in Karnataka recorded the lowest AQI at 19, followed by Madikeri in the same state at 24 and Cuddalore in Tamil Nadu at 28. Eloor in Kerala reported 30, while Koppal in Karnataka recorded 34. Aizawl in Mizoram, which had featured among the cleanest cities in the previous day's list, recorded an AQI of 38 on Wednesday. Stubble burning, Delhi vehicles add to PM2.5 load The latest source-apportionment estimates for Delhi by the Air Quality Warning and Integrated Decision Support System for Emissions - Delhi (AIRWISE-Delhi) indicate that vehicular emissions accounted for 20.5 per cent of the estimated PM2.5 load, while stubble burning in the areas near Delhi contributed 2.3 per cent and waste burning add 1.9 per cent. The India Meteorological Department's Air Quality Early Warning System has forecast that Delhi's air quality is likely to remain in the 'poor' category from November 24 to November 27. Its outlook for the subsequent six days indicates that conditions could remain between poor and very poor.

headline: J&K’s heritage, scenic beauty depicted through Chenani-Nashri Tunnel murals
content: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has adorned the portals of the Dr Syama Prasad Mookerjee Tunnel (Chenani-Nashri Tunnel) on National Highway-44 with vibrant murals showcasing Jammu and Kashmir’s rich cultural, architectural, historical and spiritual heritage, besides its scenic beauty and tourism potential.A statement issued by the NHAI on Tuesday said the initiative was part of its highway beautification drive aimed at blending modern infrastructure with the region’s distinctive cultural identity.The murals feature artistic representations of prominent religious, historical and tourist destinations, including the sacred Amarnath Cave, Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine, Shankaracharya Temple, Raghunath Temple, historic Mubarak Mandi Palace, picturesque Dal Lake and the iconic Mughal Gardens.The artwork also depicts modern highway infrastructure, reflecting Jammu and Kashmir’s progress in connectivity and development.“The initiative seeks to blend modern infrastructure with the region’s distinctive cultural identity, transforming the tunnel portals into visually appealing landmarks that celebrate the rich heritage and diverse tourism offerings of Jammu and Kashmir,” the NHAI said.

headline: Delhi court issues non-bailable warrant against Dhruv Rathee: What is 2018 case filed by Vikas Sankrityayan?
content: A Delhi court on Monday issued a non-bailable warrant (NBW) against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in a criminal defamation case filed by social media activist Vikas Sankrityayan, also known as Vikas Pandey, over a video uploaded on Rathee's YouTube channel in 2018. Judicial Magistrate Anam Rais Khan issued the warrant after Rathee failed to appear before the court, according to a PTI report. The matter has been listed for further proceedings on December 3. A detailed order is awaited. The development comes after the court issued bailable warrants against Rathee on October 31, as per a Bar and Bench report. Earlier, on October 17, it had issued a bailable warrant after a process server reported that Rathee's residence was locked while attempting to serve the notice. The court had subsequently directed that fresh summons be sent to Rathee at his Gurugram address in Haryana. During the proceedings, Rathee's counsel submitted that the YouTuber ordinarily resides in Austria and had travelled to India to participate in the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protests in Delhi. The court also noted that Rathee had initially been summoned in July 2019. What is the Dhruv Rathee defamation case? The case dates back to May 2018, when Rathee uploaded a video alleging that the Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) IT cell had attempted to bribe Sankrityayan to malign his reputation. Sankrityayan subsequently filed a criminal defamation complaint, arguing that the allegations made in the video were false and had harmed his reputation. The video was also shared by Arvind Kejriwal, who was then the chief minister of Delhi. Sankrityayan initiated defamation proceedings against both Rathee and Kejriwal. While the case has remained pending since 2018, proceedings against Kejriwal took a different turn after he tendered an apology before the Supreme Court for sharing the video. The proceedings against Rathee, who originally uploaded it, continued before the trial court.Why did the court issue fresh warrants against Rathee?The Saket court had issued a bailable warrant against Rathee on October 17 after he failed to appear for the hearing.However, the warrant could not be executed because it had reportedly been sent to an incorrect address in Austria, according to Bar and Bench.At the October 31 hearing, the court directed that a fresh warrant be issued at Rathee's Gurugram address after being informed about the error.The proceedings also saw the court question the urgency of issuing the warrant after being informed that Rathee had already left India."Ab itni jaldbazi ka koi logic hai?" the court observed, as reported by Bar and Bench.The court subsequently issued fresh bailable warrants before moving to a non-bailable warrant on Monday.Who is Vikas Sankrityayan, alias Vikas Pandey?Vikas Sankrityayan, popularly known as Vikas Pandey, is a social media activist associated with the 'I Support NaMo' online group, which supports Prime Minister Narendra Modi.According to his Facebook profile, Sankrityayan describes himself as a digital creator and writer from Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh. His stated areas of interest include social media misuse and fake news.His X profile identifies him as a software architect associated with IBM India Software Labs. He has also listed his involvement with online groups such as 'I Support NaMo' and 'Hindu IT Cell'.In a Facebook post, Sankrityayan described himself as one of the early targets of Rathee's videos and accused the YouTuber of making false claims about him."I was one of the first victims of fake news peddler Dhruv Rathee," he wrote.

headline: Bisleri under FSSAI scanner, but how many Indian households actually rely on bottled water? Just 1%, survey finds
content: The controversy surrounding Bisleri’s packaged drinking water after the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) flagged a batch from its Goa facility has brought the spotlight back to drinking water safety in India.Interestingly, a LocalCircles survey found, as per multiple news reports, that just 1 per cent of respondents said they rely on bottled water for drinking and cooking instead of treating municipal water, highlighting the limited reliance on packaged water as a primary source for household consumption.84% use purifiers or RO systemsThe survey, covering 29,161 responses from urban households across 284 districts, found that 40 per cent use water purifiers, while 44 per cent rely on RO systems. Another 9 per cent said they boil water before consuming it, while 1 per cent use chlorination, alum or other mineral-based methods. A further 1 per cent reported using other methods to treat water.Trust in tap water declinesOnly 2 per cent of respondents said they consume piped water directly without purification. The proportion of households confident about the safety of untreated municipal water has also declined sharply, from 6 per cent in the 2025 survey to 2 per cent in the latest exercise.The findings come at a time when packaged drinking water brands are facing increased scrutiny following FSSAI's enforcement action against Bisleri International.FSSAI sanctions prosecution against BisleriOn November 1, FSSAI said it had sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International over unsafe packaged drinking water from its Goa manufacturing facility. The regulator also issued an order prohibiting the sale of a specific batch of the product after testing found a bromate level of 12 micrograms per litre, against the prescribed limit of 10 micrograms per litre.Bisleri says issue limited to one batchBisleri, however, maintained that its packaged drinking water is safe for consumption and said the issue was restricted to a single batch manufactured at its Goa facility in September 2025. The company said five of the six samples collected from the plant on September 30, 2025, met the applicable standards, while one sample was found to have a marginally higher bromate level.The company has said it will cooperate with food safety authorities as FSSAI expands its enforcement drive across major packaged drinking water brands.

headline: After 27 years, Odisha restores 29 land plots in Puri to Lord Jagannath Temple, ending a major land dispute
content: The Odisha government has restored ownership records of 0.115 acres of land in Puri to Shree Jagannath Temple after discovering that the property had been incorrectly registered under the names of private individuals. The correction was carried out following the resolution of a revenue case that had remained pending for 29 years, according to a report by Times of India (TOI).The land is situated in Bada Deula Sahi mouza under Puri tehsil. The revision of revenue records covers 29 plots spread across 19 khatas (revenue accounts), which have now been registered in the name of Shree Jagannath Mahaprabhu, represented by the Shree Jagannath Temple Managing Committee.Revenue case pending since 1997 resolvedTimes of India citing officials said, proceedings in the abatement case had been pending since 1997. After the case was finally settled, the revenue department amended the Record of Rights (RoR), removing the names of private individuals and entering the deity's name as the rightful owner.Bada Deula Sahi is considered a distinctive mouza in Odisha's revenue administration as it is exclusively associated with the Shree Jagannath Temple.Odisha steps up efforts to reclaim temple landThe latest restoration is part of the Odisha government's wider drive to identify and safeguard land owned by Lord Jagannath. As part of these efforts, the revenue department has established a dedicated Shree Jagannath Mahaprabhu land cell to address matters concerning the temple's landholdings.Officials told TOI that the specialised cell is tasked with identifying temple-owned properties, clearing illegal encroachments and ensuring that revenue documents correctly reflect the deity's ownership. Similar measures have reportedly resulted in the removal of encroachments from temple properties at various locations and the correction of land records in the deity's name.Minister Suresh Pujari oversees the exerciseThe initiative is being carried out under the supervision of Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari, with senior government officials also participating in the exercise.Shree Jagannath Temple chief administrator Arabinda Kumar Padhee appreciated the officers and employees who contributed to the efforts to safeguard the temple's land assets.Odisha celebrates 'Boita Bandana', Lord Jagannath adorns 'Suna Bhesa' on Kartik PurnimaMeanwhile, people of all ages, from children to the elderly, thronged water bodies across Odisha on the occasion of Kartik Purnima on Tuesday and floated miniature boats to commemorate the ancient maritime history of Kalinga, news agency PTI reported.People started assembling at ponds, tanks, rivers, lakes, and the sea from early in the morning on the full moon day of Kartik month of the Hindu calendar, and set small boats, traditionally made of banana stems or paper, afloat with lighted lamps (diyas), betel leaves, flowers, and offerings in them.Water bodies wore a colourful look as people observed the tradition of 'Boita Bandana' or worship of boats on the occasion.

headline: India may review wheat export policy amid concerns over lower acreage
content: New Delhi: India has initiated inter-ministerial deliberations on a possible review of its liberalized wheat export policy, just three months after allowing unrestricted overseas shipments of the grain, as it assesses domestic production for the current crop year through June 2027, said two people aware of the matter.

headline: Uber, Ola, Mega Cabs fares at Bengaluru Kempegowda airport getting costlier? Here’s what passengers, cab drivers said
content: Passengers and cab drivers at Bengaluru's Kempegowda International Airport (KIA) have accused ride-hailing platforms of manipulating cab availability to push up fares, even as hundreds of taxis allegedly remain idle in airport parking areas, according to a report by Deccan Herald.The reported complaints come amid long passenger queues, failed bookings and extended waiting periods for drivers.Commuters have alleged that they are being pushed towards more expensive cab categories when their preferred rides are unavailable, while drivers say they often spend hours waiting for a single booking, as per the report.The situation has also been compounded by a reported decline in passenger traffic, particularly at the international terminal, which drivers have partly attributed to tensions in West Asia and disruptions to air travel.G Narayana Swamy, president of Karnataka Chalakara Okkuta, told Deccan Herald that hundreds of cabs could be seen parked in the airport's P7 parking zone even as passengers faced long queues at pickup points.He alleged that some authorised cab operators were deliberately restricting vehicle availability to drive up fares.Bangalore International Airport Limited (BIAL), which operates the airport, has nine authorised cab partners, including KSTDC, Mega Cabs, Uber, Uber Black, Ola, Quick Ride, OHM Electric Cabs and WTI, as per the report.Passengers report long waits and expensive cab optionsPassengers have reported waiting between 40 and 60 minutes to secure a ride. Some said their initial bookings did not materialise, leaving them with the option of booking more expensive vehicle categories.A passenger travelling from Goa told Deccan Herald that she found at least 60 people waiting at the Uber kiosk when she arrived at around 7 PM last week.Quick Ride had only one pre-booked SUV available, while drivers at the Namma Yatri kiosk reportedly said that only SUVs could be arranged.The passenger said that after waiting for around 45 minutes, the driver assigned to her booking refused the trip because her destination was not close enough to the airport. She was travelling to Marathahalli.She also alleged that another driver demanded an additional fare, raising concerns over the availability of airport taxis and the enforcement of fare rules.Why are cab drivers waiting for hours? Cab drivers have also raised concerns about declining passenger traffic and operational restrictions, saying these are affecting their earnings. According to the report, drivers said they sometimes wait between two and three hours for a single booking. They are required to remain in designated parking areas until their ride-hailing applications clear them to enter the passenger pickup zone. Drivers have particularly flagged weaker demand at the international terminal, which they partly attribute to tensions in West Asia and disruptions to flight operations. A premium cab operator at the airport said it deploys around 800 vehicles across both terminals, with the bulk of demand concentrated at Terminal 1. The operator told the daily that services generally run smoothly outside peak hours, but longer trip durations affect vehicle availability.

headline: Black jackets, grey wigs and Nvidia pitches: What happened at Vancouver’s Jensen Huang lookalike contest? Who won $200?
content: A contest to find the best lookalike of Nvidia chief Jensen Huang brought together more than 200 registered participants in Vancouver, Canada. The event had an unusual set of challenges, with contestants not only trying to look like the billionaire tech executive but also pitching Nvidia products and making funny pleas to get their jobs or wives back. Organised by Plug Vancouver, the contest was held at Mangos Kitchen and Bar on Howe Street on Sunday, 22 November. The contestants came dressed to look like Huang, wearing black leather jackets, glasses and sneakers. Some also wore grey wigs to copy his hairstyle. The winner was Walter Lim, a retired man from Seattle who drove around three hours to take part in the event. He won the top prize of US$200. The two runners-up received US$50 each. According to the organisers, the event was free for the public and received a much bigger response than expected. Three rounds tested the contestantsThe competition had three rounds, with judges and cheers from the audience helping decide the finalists.The first round was about looks. Contestants had to convince the judges and audience that they looked like Huang, who is known for his black leather jacket, glasses and grey hair.The second round required contestants to pitch Nvidia's latest product. They had to present their ideas while holding a bag of potato chips.One contestant made the crowd laugh by crushing the bag during his pitch and calling the crumbs inside it "microchips".The final round was even more unusual. Contestants had to make a funny plea to get either their wife or their job back. The challenge was a reference to the personal controversy surrounding Huang, which had recently made headlines.Lim eventually won the competition after the finalists faced the audience. He said his sister had told him about the event while he was travelling in Madrid. He then decided to drive from Seattle to Vancouver to take part.Lim said people had often told him that he looked like Huang. He also said that owning a similar leather jacket and wearing the same style of glasses helped him match the Nvidia chief's appearance. Why is Jensen Huang in the news? The contest took place during an unusual period for Nvidia and its chief executive. Huang had stepped down as Nvidia's CEO on November 12 following a controversy involving an alleged extramarital affair with Singapore-based businesswoman Alice Huang. Reports also raised questions about possible links to China and national security. The allegations involving espionage have not been established as fact. His departure led to discussions about the company's leadership and calls from supporters for him to return. However, Nvidia announced on 23 November that its board had reinstated Huang as president and CEO with immediate effect. The company said the board was satisfied with his explanations and ability to lead the business.The Vancouver contest also followed a separate lookalike event in New York linked to Alice Huang, adding to the unusual attention around the Nvidia controversy.Plug Vancouver has previously organised a similar lookalike competition when singer Bruno Mars visited the city.For now, Walter Lim has won the title of Vancouver's Jensen Huang lookalike, along with a US$200 prize.

headline: Gurugram bans smoking in parks, markets and public spaces: What prompted MCG's  ₹200 fine?
content: The Municipal Corporation of Gurugram (MCG) has declared all public places within its jurisdiction as no-smoking zones with immediate effect. Smoking tobacco products, spitting tobacco, and throwing cigarette or bidi butts in these areas are now prohibited. Anyone violating the order can be fined up to ₹200.The order was issued by Municipal Commissioner Pankaj on Monday to improve cleanliness and public health in the city, while reducing people's exposure to tobacco smoke in public spaces, an official told news agency PTI.What prompted MCG to declare public places no-smoking zones?According to the order, smoking and the disposal of tobacco waste in public places can create health risks, particularly for children, women and senior citizens. Such activities also contribute to unhygienic conditions in public areas.The civic body has issued the directive under Section 4 of the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003, which bans smoking in public places.The order also refers to the Prohibition of Smoking in Public Places Rules. These rules require authorities responsible for public spaces to prevent smoking and the disposal of cigarette and bidi butts in public areas and parks.Which places come under Gurugram's no-smoking ban?The restrictions cover all public places falling within the MCG's jurisdiction. These include:- Markets, bus stops, bus stands and public transport facilities.- Parks, green belts, playgrounds and open gyms owned, maintained or managed by the civic body.- Sheds, gazebos and other covered structures in these locations.- MCG offices, community centres, libraries and dispensaries.- Parking lots and toilet complexes.What is the fine for smoking in public places in Gurugram? Anyone found smoking in areas covered by the Municipal Corporation of Gurugram's (MCG) order can be fined up to ₹200. The penalty is provided under Section 21 of the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003, commonly known as COTPA. Section 4 of the Act bans smoking in public places. The Prohibition of Smoking in Public Places Rules, 2008, also make it mandatory for those responsible for public spaces to prevent smoking and the disposal of cigarette and bidi butts. The fine comes at a time when cigarette prices have increased significantly this year. In February 2026, following the introduction of a 40% GST rate and additional excise duty, cigarette prices rose by at least ₹22-25 for a pack of 10 sticks. Premium varieties saw price increases of ₹50-55. A 10-stick pack of Wills Navy Cut, which earlier cost ₹95, was expected to be priced at around ₹120. ITC also increased prices of select cigarette brands in September. The price of a 20-stick pack of Classic Connect rose from ₹390 to ₹428. Are cigarette butts and tobacco spitting also prohibited? Yes. The MCG order prohibits people from throwing cigarette and bidi butts or spitting tobacco in public places. The restrictions extend beyond smoking to include tobacco-related littering. According to the civic body, these activities contribute to unhygienic conditions and can affect public health. The order also points to the risks of passive smoking, particularly for children, women and senior citizens. Who will ensure compliance? The MCG has assigned responsibility for implementing the order to its joint commissioners, the chief medical officer and officials from the sanitation and horticulture departments. These officials have been instructed to monitor compliance in their respective zones and parks. They have also been directed to put up signboards declaring the designated areas as no-smoking zones within 15 days.

headline: What does  ₹1.25L monthly budget look like? ‘ ₹30,000 grocery,  ₹20,000 grooming’: Noida couple’s expenses go viral
content: Owning a home does not always mean that monthly expenses are low. A couple living in Noida has revealed that they spend around ₹1.25 lakh every month, even though they own their house and do not have to pay rent.The couple shared a video on Instagram explaining their monthly expenses. Their spending includes groceries, household help, gym memberships, grooming, food and travel.The expense breakdown has started a discussion on social media, with many people questioning how a couple can spend so much every month without paying rent.Groceries cost ₹30,000, grooming costs ₹20,000According to the couple, groceries are their biggest monthly expense at ₹30,000. They also spend around ₹20,000 on grooming. Their gym memberships and Pilates classes cost another ₹15,000 every month. Supplements such as protein powder and multivitamins add ₹15,000 to their expenses.The couple said they spend around ₹30,000 on groceries every month and another ₹20,000 on grooming. Their gym and Pilates sessions cost ₹15,000, while supplements add another ₹15,000 to their monthly expenses.They also pay ₹10,000 for household help and spend another ₹10,000 on eating out. Home maintenance costs them ₹8,000, while electricity bills come to around ₹5,000. Internet, mobile and OTT subscriptions together cost ₹6,000. Their monthly commute expenses are between ₹5,000 and ₹6,000.Together, these expenses add up to around ₹1.25 lakh every month.The couple also spends ₹10,000 on household help, which includes cooking and cleaning. Their electricity bill is around ₹5,000, while home maintenance costs them another ₹8,000.They spend ₹6,000 on internet, mobile bills and OTT subscriptions. Travelling to work costs them between ₹5,000 and ₹6,000 every month.Renting a home could push expenses to ₹1.75 lakhThe couple also explained how much more they would have to spend if they did not own their home.According to them, renting a similar 3BHK flat in their area would cost around ₹45,000 to ₹50,000 every month.This could take their total monthly expenses from ₹1.25 lakh to nearly ₹1.75 lakh.Their video has received mixed reactions online. Some people questioned the ₹30,000 grocery budget, while others were surprised by the ₹20,000 spent on grooming.Some users also pointed out that spending ₹15,000 on gym memberships and another ₹15,000 on supplements was a personal choice rather than a necessary monthly expense.Others said that the couple's spending showed how expensive certain lifestyles can become in a city like Noida.The couple's video has also started a wider discussion about monthly expenses in Indian cities. Even without rent or home loan payments, costs such as food, fitness, personal care and household help can take up a large part of a family's income.

headline: IIT Bombay's ceiling fan replacement drive: Why are hostel rooms getting wall-mounted fans?
content: Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bombay has begun replacing ceiling fans and fan rods in hostel rooms with wall-mounted fans as part of a campus-wide renovation and maintenance exercise. The move has drawn attention amid renewed concerns over student suicides at premier educational institutions.The replacement drive has been initiated after a student died by suicide in July, but gained renewed attention following the death of 22-year-old BTech student Sahil Wakode in September.The institute is installing wall-mounted fans across its hostels and other utility areas on campus. Images of wall-mounted fans arriving at the Powai campus as part of the renovation work have also circulated widely on social media.While the timing has prompted questions about whether the move is intended to prevent student suicides, the institute has not officially defined the replacement exercise as a suicide-prevention measure.Why is IIT Bombay replacing ceiling fans with wall-mounted fans?The shift comes against the backdrop of repeated student suicide cases at premier educational institutions, including IIT Bombay. Ceiling fans and their supporting rods can potentially be used as ligature points in suicide attempts. Replacing them with wall-mounted alternatives is therefore being viewed as a possible physical-safety intervention in hostel rooms.The move could reduce access to certain potential hanging points in student accommodation. However, it is not clear whether the institute has formally adopted the measure as part of a broader suicide-prevention policy.What happened to IIT Bombay student Sahil Wakode?Sahil Wakode, a second-year BTech student in the Department of Energy Science and Engineering, was found dead in his hostel room at IIT Bombay's Powai campus on September 18.He hailed from Maharashtra's Yavatmal district and was reportedly caught allegedly using a mobile phone to access ChatGPT during a mid-semester examination hours before his death.His death triggered protests and renewed concerns about academic pressure, student welfare and mental health support at India's premier technical institutions.

headline: Bangalore cab driver reveals  ₹20k daily income from Uber, 10 rental cars; passenger stunned - how he does it
content: A conversation between a Bengaluru passenger and a cab driver has triggered a discussion on social media about daily earnings, multiple income streams and the business of operating taxis. What started as an ordinary cab ride to Majestic soon turned into an interesting exchange about the driver's earnings and his fleet of vehicles.Recounting the experience in a post on X, the passenger said he had booked a cab in Bengaluru the previous night. During the journey, he began chatting with the driver about his work and daily life. The conversation eventually shifted to the driver's daily income."Then we started talking about how much he earns in a day. He literally showed me his earnings for the day on Uber: ₹4,800, and that was until 10:30 PM. He was going to drive for another 2 hours," he wrote.However, driving a cab was reportedly not the driver's only source of income.The passenger said the driver also owned 10 Maruti Suzuki Ertiga cars in Mumbai, which he rented out at ₹1,500 per vehicle per day. This reportedly earned him ₹15,000 daily in rental income.When combined with his reported Uber earnings of ₹4,800, the driver's total daily income came to approximately ₹19,800, or nearly ₹20,000, according to the passenger's calculation.The passenger was impressed by the driver's approach to building multiple income sources and the hard work involved in running the business."That is an insane amount, and he is truly earning it through his hard work. This amount is even more than the package of a senior manager at a product company," he added.How did social media users react to the cab driver's earnings? The post has drawn considerable attention online, with users sharing different views on the driver's reported income. While some praised his ability to build a business alongside his cab-driving work, others questioned whether the figures reflected his actual profits. One user pointed out that the income might look impressive but needed to be assessed after accounting for expenses such as fuel, vehicle maintenance, rental costs and the long hours spent behind the wheel. Another user highlighted the benefits and challenges of running an independent business, arguing that being one's own boss offers a level of flexibility that may not always be possible in corporate jobs. A third person said, "10 Ertigas? That's actually impressive if true." What did users say about the costs of running a 10-car fleet? A fourth user questioned how much the driver would actually earn after meeting the costs of operating the fleet. “ ₹15,000 a day from renting 10 cars sounds impressive, but what about EMIs, maintenance, insurance, driver payments and days when the cars aren't running? Still, owning and managing a fleet of 10 vehicles is a serious business in itself. We often underestimate how much business happens outside the corporate world. Would be interesting to know how much he actually takes home after all expenses.”

headline: How the Iran war drove India and China to record Russian oil imports in 2026, and why purchases may ease in 2027
content: India and China are set to import record volumes of Russian crude oil in 2026 as the Iran war disrupts supplies from the Middle East, pushing refiners to seek alternative sources, Reuters reported. Temporary US sanctions waivers have further eased access to Russian barrels, allowing the two countries to increase purchases at a time of heightened uncertainty in global energy markets, However, the surge may prove temporary. Traders and analysts expect Russian oil demand in both countries to moderate in 2027 as Middle Eastern supplies become more readily available and the economics of buying Russian crude change. Seaborne Russian oil shipments to India and China averaged around 3.4 million barrels per day (bpd) through mid-November, approximately 530,000 bpd higher than the corresponding period last year, according to tanker data and industry sources cited by Reuters. The increase has provided Moscow with a significant boost to oil revenues, even as Ukrainian drone strikes have disrupted Russian refining capacity and forced more crude into export markets. Brent crude prices have also climbed nearly a third since the Iran war began, adding to volatility in global oil trade.How the Iran war changed Russian oil flowsThe disruption to Middle Eastern oil supplies following the Iran war has reshaped crude-buying patterns across Asia. As Iranian oil flows declined and concerns mounted over the availability of supplies from the Gulf, India and China increased their reliance on Russian crude to secure adequate feedstock for their refineries.Temporary US sanctions waivers targeting Russian oil have also helped buyers access more shipments by widening the pool of available vessels and suppliers.India and China together accounted for more than 80% of Russia's crude exports, according to estimates cited by Reuters.Moscow is also expecting its overall oil exports to rise this year. Russia's Ministry of Economic Development has forecast a 6% increase to 244.7 million metric tonnes, equivalent to approximately 4.9 million bpd.The higher exports underline how geopolitical disruptions have benefited Russia's oil trade. With traditional supply routes under pressure, Russian crude has become an important alternative for the world's two largest oil importers.India emerges as the biggest buyer of Russian crude India's purchases of Russian oil have climbed to record levels, reinforcing its position as Moscow's largest seaborne crude buyer. Data from tanker tracker Kpler cited by Reuters showed that India's Russian crude imports averaged 1.99 million bpd through early November, around 250,000 bpd higher than a year earlier. The increase comes after Indian refiners had scaled back purchases earlier in the year amid concerns over the possibility of higher US tariffs. However, the disruption to Middle Eastern supplies changed the buying calculus, making Russian crude more important for refiners seeking to maintain supplies. Between January and October, India's Russian crude imports rose about 10% to 1.87 million bpd, accounting for approximately 38% of the country's total crude imports, according to trade sources cited by Reuters. Indian refiners expect the full-year average to reach around 1.9 million bpd. The rise reflects both the availability of Russian barrels and the need to diversify supply sources as the Iran war puts pressure on flows from the Gulf. Why China has also increased its Russian oil imports China has also stepped up purchases, although its overall crude imports have declined. Chinese customs data cited by Reuters showed that Russian oil shipments to the country rose 17% to 2.34 million bpd between January and October. The imports were valued at around $59.6 billion, with Russian crude accounting for roughly a quarter of China's total oil imports during the period. This increase came even as China's overall crude imports fell 15%, highlighting the growing importance of Russian supplies in its import mix.Lower shipping risks and greater reliability have been key factors behind the shift. Muyu Xu, an analyst at tanker tracker Kpler, told Reuters that these considerations had driven the increase in China's Russian crude imports since the war began.Why Russian oil purchases could ease in 2027The outlook for Russian crude will depend significantly on how quickly Middle Eastern oil supplies recover and whether Russian barrels remain competitively priced.If Gulf supplies return to normal in 2027, Indian refiners are likely to have more alternatives.Sources at Indian refiners told Reuters that purchases of Russian crude could move back towards pre-Iran war levels, with buying decisions increasingly determined by price.China could follow a similar path. Greater availability of Middle Eastern crude may reduce the need for Russian supplies, particularly if Russian grades continue to trade at premiums rather than discounts.For Moscow, that could mean a tougher export environment next year. India and China have absorbed record volumes in 2026 partly because the Iran war disrupted their traditional sources of supply and made Russian crude more accessible.If those disruptions ease, Russia will have to compete more directly with oil from the Gulf and other producers. Its ability to retain market share will therefore depend less on geopolitical circumstances and more on the price, availability and shipping costs of its crude.

headline: A different layoff saga: Job-cut emails to employees first, apology later. Why did this company do so? ‘Very sorry’
content: An email intended for internal administrative communication ended up revealing some unwelcome news to employees of Australia's National Australia Bank (NAB). Several workers learnt that their jobs could be at risk through an automated notification before their managers had a chance to speak to them.The bank has apologized after accidentally sending redundancy-related emails to employees before formally informing them about the outcome of their voluntary exit applications. The affected staff members were supposed to receive the decisions directly from their managers. However, an administrative or technical error caused the automated emails to reach them before those conversations could take place.According to Reuters, NAB acknowledged the mistake and said it understood that receiving such news unexpectedly could cause distress."We are very sorry this happened, and that receiving an automated email this way would be upsetting and unsettling to many," the bank said in a statement shared with Reuters.NAB said the notifications were not meant to be sent before employees were informed of the decisions through direct conversations. Following the incident, the bank said it would bring forward discussions with the affected workers.Why is NAB planning to cut 2,500 jobs?The email blunder comes as the Australian lender prepares for a major workforce restructuring. Last month, NAB announced plans to cut 2,500 jobs over the next 12 months, affecting approximately 6% of its total workforce.The bank said the restructuring is intended to simplify its operations and lower costs. As many as 1,500 roles, primarily across corporate functions, are expected to be affected by the end of this year.Which other Australian companies have announced job cuts?NAB's planned workforce reduction comes amid a wider wave of layoffs across Australia. Several companies, including Qantas, Canva, WiseTech and Atlassian, have also announced job cuts this year.For employees seeking voluntary redundancy, the process can already involve considerable uncertainty. Workers have to wait to find out whether their applications have been accepted, when their employment will end and what steps they need to take next.Receiving an unexpected automated email about an employment decision before a formal conversation with management can make an already stressful situation even more difficult.Businesses are increasingly turning to automated systems to handle routine employee communications, including recruitment updates, onboarding instructions, payroll notifications and internal announcements.While these tools help organisations save time and manage communication more efficiently, the NAB incident highlights the potential risks of using automation to deliver sensitive employment-related decisions that can directly affect people's livelihoods.(With inputs from Reuters)

headline: How Russia’s War Machine Traps Asian Workers
content: It was only a matter of time before Russia’s war in Ukraine reached deep into Asia. With signing bonuses as high as $35,000 and promises of a $3,000 monthly income, it should be no surprise that men from Indonesia and the Philippines are taking on jobs advertised as logistics, security, construction and administration, only to be pushed onto the front lines when they arrive.Moscow has a manpower problem, and as governments from India to Nepal along with some African nations step in to prevent their citizens being lured into its forever war, Russia is turning to Southeast Asia’s vulnerable migrant-labor market to help fill the gap.Shady recruitment agents are using social media, opaque contracts and the promise of high wages to attract people desperate for a job, the same ingredients that make migrant workers vulnerable to trafficking networks and scam compounds. Some believe they’re going to work in hotels, construction or other civilian sectors in Russia before discovering that the documents they signed are military contracts.Governments should view this as an early warning signal for their migrant-labor economies. Indonesia is just the latest frontline — and police are treating recent cases as human trafficking when they believe recruits were deceived or coerced, as opposed to voluntarily enlisting.Jakarta should be ideally placed to help citizens caught in this trap. Since he came to power in 2024, President Prabowo Subianto has gone out of his way to build a close relationship with President Vladimir Putin, and has described Indonesia as Russia’s gateway to Southeast Asia. During his time in office, Indonesia has joined the BRICS group of developing nations, while the two upgraded their ties to a strategic partnership last year. A personal president-to-president plea would go a long way. The government has asked Russia to include Indonesia on the list of countries exempted from official recruitment into the military. It’s an important first step; however it’s not clear if Moscow has responded. Police were still intercepting travelers as recently as Nov. 18 and investigating whether they were being trafficked — recruitment is ongoing and will be until Russia says so.Beyond making Indonesia a no-go zone for these agents, the government has another pressing problem: how to bring home those already trapped in the conflict. The Jakarta police say that the contracts run until the recruit’s death or the end of the war. At the very least, Prabowo’s administration could suspend legal job placements to Russia, which go to sectors including manufacturing, construction and hospitality, until the employers can be verified as legitimate. Moscow controls the entire process: It sets the pay and the list of countries whose citizens it no longer takes — and brokers go wherever they can, Radityo Dharmaputra, a lecturer in International Relations at Universitas Airlangga in Surabaya, told me. Radityo is tracking a range of cases, including a prisoner of war held in Ukraine, two reported deaths, and police investigations into 58 victims. Most were lured by the offer of civilian work, he noted.The Philippines is particularly vulnerable, given the size of its migrant labor force. At an Association of Southeast Asian Nations forum on migrant labor last month, Manila reported that it had helped to take down as many as 250,000 online posts linked to fraudulent overseas job offers through cooperation with Meta Platforms Inc. and TikTok. Ukrainian military figures indicate that 128 Filipinos were recruited in the first nine months of the year, a sharp increase from the small numbers previously identified. The Philippines, like Indonesia, doesn’t appear on Russia’s list of excluded countries.Last week’s meeting of Asean leaders missed an important opportunity to intervene. The gathering adopted a declaration on fair and ethical recruitment of migrant workers that explicitly addresses illegal hiring, labor exploitation, cross-border employment scams and human trafficking — precisely the mechanisms Indonesian police say are being used in some Russia cases. Yet it did not publicly single out Moscow or the plight of citizens lured to fight in the Ukraine conflict.Governments and the tech companies used by these networks need to take urgent protective measures, including issuing clear public warnings and guidance on the risks of fraudulent job offers linked to working in Russia. It’s heartening to see that some nations have recognized that many of those who’ve signed up aren’t willing mercenaries. Treating them as trafficked victims creates an opening to negotiate with Russia for their safe return, or with Ukraine if they’ve already been captured on the battlefield. This also lines up with findings from the United Nations Independent International Commission of Inquiry on Ukraine released last month. It reported compelling evidence that Russian authorities, collaborating with overseas agents, had trafficked people from 29 countries using deception or coercion to recruit them into the armed forces. Russia has successfully weaponized economic desperation. Southeast Asian nations need to act before this new channel of underground labor exploitation becomes permanent.More From Bloomberg Opinion:Russian authorities maintain an unofficial a list of countries whose citizens are barred from being recruited to fight in Ukraine. It reportedly includes nations seen as friendly to Moscow, such as China, India, Brazil, South Africa, Turkey, Cuba, Afghanistan, Venezuela, and Iran.This column reflects the personal views of the author and does not necessarily reflect the opinion of the editorial board or Bloomberg LP and its owners.Ruth Pollard is a Bloomberg Opinion columnist covering Asia politics and policy. She previously covered South and Southeast Asia on the Bloomberg government team and was Middle East Correspondent for the Sydney Morning Herald./opinion©2026 Bloomberg L.P.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: NPPA examines extending drug margin caps beyond cancer medicines to other therapies
content: New Delhi: The Centre is examining whether trade margin caps should be extended beyond cancer medicines to other high-cost and essential drugs, including antibiotics, diabetes and heart medicines, as well as biologics, while seeking to avoid disruptions to drug availability and hospital supplies, two government officials said. The Department of Pharmaceuticals (DoP) and the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) are studying how such interventions could be structured, with officials indicating that any expansion would require product-level scrutiny rather than a uniform cap across entire therapeutic categories.

headline: RFK Jr. Calendars Show Meetings With Lilly, Chipotle CEOs
content: (Bloomberg) -- The US Department of Health and Human Services launched a website hosting more than 92,000 documents including Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s calendars and agency correspondence during the Covid-19 pandemic, in what HHS called a push for greater transparency.The documents span agencies across the health department and include records previously released under the Freedom of Information Act and other public documents, HHS said in a news release. The department will update the site as more documents are made public.About a quarter of the documents on the new site have not been previously made public, a spokesperson for HHS said.Though Kennedy has been a frequent and vocal critic of corporate influence in medicine and agriculture, his calendars show many meetings with business leaders in healthcare, food and other industries.The calendars list a meeting with Eli Lilly & Co. Chief Executive Dave Ricks in April 2025, a pull-aside during a visit to Indiana when he also met with Governor Mike Braun. A separate entry for February 2026 shows a meeting with Novo Nordisk A/S. A May 2026 entry shows a call with George Yancopoulos of Regeneron Pharmaceuticals Inc.A meeting with the CEO of Tylenol-maker Kenvue Inc. preceded the administration’s White House news conference in which President Donald Trump told pregnant women to avoid the painkiller, citing unproven theories of a link to autism. The meeting occurred three days after the Wall Street Journal reported that the Trump administration was expected to link the drug to autism.Other entries show meetings with CEOs of infant formula makers, a roundtable with hospital executives and a session with insurance CEOs.Kennedy, who has also criticized the food industry, met in March 2025 with Donnie King, CEO of Tyson Foods Inc. at the time. He has also met with leaders from Chipotle Mexican Grill Inc., Starbucks Corp, and In-N-Out Burgers.Kennedy also met Stacey Kennedy, the US CEO of tobacco company Philip Morris International Inc., the listings show.A June 2026 entry shows a meeting with SoftBank Group Chairman Masayoshi Son along with Mehmet Oz, administrator of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services.Kennedy has had regular meetings with Louisiana Senator Bill Cassidy, a key vote for his confirmation.Three CenturiesThe documents appear to range from as early as 1840 (a handwritten catalog of the surgeon general’s library) through the first half of 2026. More than 10,000 records were from previous centuries, according to search results returned by the site.The site is searchable and offers some initial “collections,” prominently featuring a batch of documents on Covid-19. Other collections include records on infant formula, the opioid crisis and several batches related to FOIA litigation.Kennedy’s calendars show meetings with other cabinet officials and media appearances, including briefings on the ongoing measles outbreak starting in February 2025, when cases were increasing in Texas. HHS said it’s also using artificial intelligence to process public records requests and propose redactions for trade secrets or other information subject to withholding. Thousands of documents have been requested under FOIA and the use of AI will allow quicker searches and reviews, the agency said.The transparency website replaces an online reading room that previously aggregated records released under FOIA and other documents.Last year, the Department of Government Efficiency led by Elon Musk cut thousands of staff across HHS, including in the FOIA departments, impairing the agency’s ability to respond to records requests quickly.The Food and Drug Administration has previously published the agency’s response letters for new drug and biologic applications.--With assistance from Ike Swetlitz, Allison DeAngelis, Daniela Sirtori, Redd Brown, Jeff Kao and Ilena Peng.(Updates with additional details starting in fourth paragraph.)More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

headline: Trump says pardon to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang ‘an option’ but wants him to ‘tell the truth’ to Congress
content: US President Donald Trump reportedly said he was willing to pardon reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang if necessary, but added that he did not believe Huang would need one. Trump also said Huang should “tell the truth” when he testifies before Congress next week.In an exclusive interview with the New York Post on Tuesday, Trump said Huang would not need to invoke his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination. Huang is scheduled to be interviewed by the House Foreign Affairs Committee next Tuesday and appear before the Senate Banking Committee next Thursday.“I don’t think he needs to take the Fifth. I think it’s an interesting story for people,” Trump told the Post. “I think I want him to just tell the truth, and I mean, his lawyers are going to have to advise him, but I’ve always found him to be 100% aboveboard, and you know, a very smart person," the president added.Asked about a pardon for any potential crimes, Trump said, “It’s always an option, I guess, but I don’t think it’ll be necessary.”Trump apparently pressured Nvidia's board to take Huang back, 11 days after he resigned following revelations of extramarital affairs, one with a suspected Chinese spy.Trump told CNBC earlier that he spoke with Nvidia’s board members about reinstating Huang as CEO. “I’ve been speaking to the board directly and indirectly, and I felt very strongly about it,” Trump said.According to US media, both Democratic and Republican members of Congress blasted the reinstatement of Huang before getting answers on whether he was a "national security threat" or violated export controls on shipping chips to communist China.Upset lawmakers previewed a tough grilling of Huang, with Louisiana Republican Sen John Kennedy predicting Huang will plead the Fifth to avoid self-incrimination amid potential criminal prosecution.Trump claimed that he hadn’t learned details of additional affairs that Huang admitted to before being restored as CEO — after the firestorm over his tryst with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang (no relation) and at least two company employees.He also said he didn’t know precisely how many affairs Huang fessed up to as part of his restoration.Why Donald Trump wanted to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEOTrump said that Nvidia’s success was essential to the US retaining an edge in artificial intelligence — and that he’s even open to the company giving the American government an equity stake, noting Intel handed over 10% of its value last year.“I thought about it. I said, ‘You know, maybe I should do it,’ but I didn’t bring it up at this point. It’s probably not too late,” Trump said.The president said he intervened to restore Huang, including by giving assurances that he faced no issues from the executive branch, because if Nvidia picked “the wrong person” to replace Huang, “that would be a terrible thing for our country in many ways.”(With agency inputs)

headline: Petrol and diesel prices today, November 25: Check fuel cost in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru
content: Petrol and diesel prices today, November 25: Petrol and diesel prices have remained largely steady across major cities despite a surge in global crude oil costs due to the US-Iran war, which led to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.Union Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister Hardeep Singh Puri attributed this to the Centre's strategy of cutting excise duties and managing domestic fuel supplies.Here is a look at the petrol and diesel prices in major metropolitan cities as of November 25:New Delhi: Petrol is retailing at ₹102.12 per litre, while diesel is priced at ₹95.20 per litre. The national capital continues to have relatively lower fuel prices compared to other metros.Mumbai: In the financial capital, petrol is priced at ₹111.21 per litre, and diesel costs ₹97.83 per litre.Chennai: Residents in Chennai are paying ₹107.76 per litre for petrol and ₹99.55 per litre for diesel.Kolkata: Petrol costs ₹113.51 per litre, while diesel costs ₹99.82 per litre.Bengaluru: Petrol is priced at ₹110.44 per litre, and diesel at ₹99.56 per litre.Hyderabad: Petrol costs ₹116.15 per litre, while diesel costs ₹104.23 per litre.Petrol and diesel prices in other metro cities today Source: GoodReturnsOil steady after gainOil prices steadied as traders balanced indications of rising global supply against escalating attacks on vessels near the Strait of Hormuz, Bloomberg reported.Brent crude traded around $91 a barrel after climbing 2.3% in the previous session, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) hovered below $82. On Tuesday, Iran claimed a fourth tanker was struck by a mine, according to the Fars news agency, extending a recent wave of vessel attacks by the Islamic Republic.Tehran also warned it would tighten its grip over the Strait of Hormuz until its demands are met, Tasnim reported—highlighting that an end to the nearly nine-month conflict remains out of reach. Even so, crude shipments from the Persian Gulf have surged in recent months, prompting the International Energy Agency (IEA) to forecast that the market will tip into a surplus this quarter.“The reality on the ground is more a ‘war but no war’ situation, with spasms of violence,” Robert Yawger, director of the energy futures division at Mizuho Securities USA LLC, told Bloomberg. Under that scenario, “look for the supply surplus to become the dominant theme in coming weeks,” he added.Brent has dropped sharply this month as Gulf exports climbed and US President Donald Trump held off on renewed strikes against Iran following the US midterm elections.Adding to the downward pressure, a key timespread for the Middle East’s Dubai crude benchmark flipped into a bearish structure this week, signalling that supply is now outpacing demand, Bloomberg noted.

headline: Huawei convicted of stealing trade secrets: What is the case and what does it mean for US-China ties? Explained
content: A US jury convicted Chinese tech giant Huawei Technologies Co of stealing trade secrets Tuesday, but acquitted it of a more serious racketeering allegation, according to the Department of Justice.Huawei Technologies Co, China’s largest technology company, was found guilty of multiple US criminal charges, including defrauding banks about its business in Iran and money laundering, Bloomberg reported.A federal jury in Brooklyn, New York, deliberated for about four days before reaching a verdict Tuesday in a rare US prosecution of a foreign corporation.What are US charges against Huawei?Jurors found Huawei guilty on 10 of the 12 criminal counts it faced — including bank fraud, conspiracy to steal trade secrets, and conspiracy to defraud the United States, the US Department of Justice (DOJ) said.The company was cleared of two charges, including racketeering and obstruction of justice, the report added."No person or company is above the law," US Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a statement. “For decades, Huawei and three of its subsidiaries conducted their business in the United States on the basis of lies and theft,” he added.The equipment manufacturer was accused of attempting to recruit employees of US telecoms firms and obtaining technological information from them in the process, news agency AFP reported.That data allegedly enabled Huawei to develop products similar to its competitors' and sell them at lower prices, according to the original indictment."The misappropriated intellectual property included trade secret information and copyrighted works, such as source code and user manuals for internet routers, antenna technology, and robot testing technology," the DOJ said in a release.Huawei even launched an internal programme offering bonuses to employees who obtained industrial secrets from competitors, prosecutors claimed.The investigation also involved Huawei's business dealings with the government of Iran."Huawei repeatedly lied about the nature of its business in Iran, falsely telling banks, journalists, and the US government that it did not assist Iran's government, military, or intelligence community," DOJ said.The jury ultimately acquitted the company of a racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice."Today's verdict sends an unmistakable message: America will defend its businesses, protect its workers, and safeguard its national security against corrupt foreign corporations that lie, cheat, and steal to get ahead," Assistant Attorney General Tysen A Duva said in a statement.Huawei now faces potential fines, forfeiture and restitution, but the US has not specified the scope of financial penalties it will seek.Why did Trump administration accuse Huawei of ‘spying’?The world's leading telecom equipment manufacturer, Huawei, has been targeted by the Trump administration, which alleges that it poses a risk of spying on behalf of the Chinese government.The United States previously urged countries not to use Huawei infrastructure for the rollout of new 5G mobile networks.For most of that time, the company has been largely excluded from the American market under trade measures imposed by the Trump and Biden administrations in the name of national security, Bloomberg reported.The telecom titan has emerged as China’s de facto national chipmaking champion and is one of a handful of firms central to Beijing’s goal of dominating artificial intelligence and replacing American software and circuitry with local equivalents.What verdict means for US-China ties?The verdict against one of China’s biggest and best-known tech giants lands at a delicate time for US-China relations. According to Bloomberg, it threatens to strain ties already frayed over revelations that the now-reinstated chief executive of Nvidia Corp, Jensen Huang, had an affair with a woman suspected of links to Chinese intelligence.Besides, the conviction is a vindication for the Justice Department, which overcame attempts by Huawei to derail the case before trial and had to navigate years of delays because of the Covid pandemic, which made it difficult for lawyers and witnesses to travel.Along the way, two Chinese intelligence officers were accused in 2022 of trying to bribe a US law enforcement official with $61,000 in Bitcoin to steal evidence and get inside information about the case.From the beginning, the Huawei case heightened tensions between Washington and Beijing while the world’s two largest economies were mired in a trade war.Months later, officials in Trump’s administration labelled the company a national security threat, alleging that it sold telecommunications equipment that China’s Communist Party could use for spying.The initial criminal indictment set off a diplomatic crisis when Huawei Chief Financial Officer Meng Wanzhou, whose father founded the company, was arrested at the US's behest on financial fraud charges while travelling through Canada.Almost three years after Meng was held under house arrest in Vancouver, she reached a deferred prosecution agreement in 2021 that allowed her to return to China, but only after she admitted that the company violated US sanctions by illegally conducting business in Iran.(With inputs from Bloomberg, AFP)

headline: US preparing to raise tariffs on China, India, others; to be added to levies imposed under Section 301 | Here's why
content: US President Donald Trump's administration is reportedly preparing to increase tariffs on several countries, including China and India, arguing that their governments have harmed American companies by supporting domestic industrial production.Citing sources, The Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday (local time) that Jamieson Greer, the US Trade Representative (USTR), is likely to announce the tariffs as soon as this week. The move follows a months-long investigation into industrial subsidies provided by countries including China, the European Union, and 14 other nations. However, sources cautioned that the timeline could change.Why is the US planning to increase tariffs?According to Greer, subsidies and other forms of government support provided to companies in certain countries have created excess industrial capacity in those economies. This allows their firms to flood global markets with cheaper goods, ultimately undermining US producers.While the final tariff rates remain unclear, Trump administration officials have repeatedly said they intend to impose duties similar to those introduced by the US President in 2025, before the Supreme Court struck down his first batch of tariffs in February 2026.The proposed tariff announcement also comes amid a separate controversy involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and allegations that the company's advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips were smuggled into China despite tighter US export restrictions. According to the WSJ, the timing of the tariff move could also be linked to an attempt by the Trump administration to divert attention from questions surrounding what the government knew about the alleged smuggling and its response to the matter.Higher tariffs to cover most products from China, Japan, EU: What we knowThe USTR's announcement is also expected to bring higher tariffs for dozens of countries, including China, Japan, South Korea and the 27 member nations of the European Union. The new duties are likely to cover most products exported from these countries. However, certain industrial goods, including steel, aluminium and automobiles, are expected to be excluded as they are already subject to tariffs under a separate national security provision.Countries that reached trade agreements with the Trump administration, including Japan and the European Union, are expected to retain tariff rates in line with the terms they had agreed to before the Supreme Court's ruling, according to people familiar with the plans. Under this arrangement, the EU, Japan and South Korea could face tariffs of 15% or less, while countries such as Vietnam and India may be subject to higher rates depending on the terms of their respective trade deals with Trump.China, on the other hand, is likely to face higher tariffs than many other countries, as Trump administration officials have pointed to the extensive nature of Beijing's subsidies and their disruptive impact on the global economy. The administration may also introduce provisions allowing it to raise tariffs on countries if their industrial overcapacity increases or they fail to implement policy changes during future trade negotiations with the US, the report added.Tariffs under Section 301The proposed tariffs are expected to be imposed on top of duties announced under a separate measure in July. The measure targeted countries that failed to prevent the trade of goods manufactured using forced labour and set tariff rates ranging from 10% to 12.5% across 60 economies. However, the measure is currently facing a legal challenge in court.Earlier in July, the US announced fresh tariffs on several countries under Section 301. While India was initially placed in the 12.5% tariff bracket, it was moved to the 10% category following discussions on labour practices.The development followed the USTR's decision in March to launch investigations into 60 economies under Section 301(b) of the Trade Act of 1974. The probe aimed to determine whether their trade practices were linked to a failure to enforce restrictions on imports of goods manufactured using forced labour.The duties, ranging from 10% to 12.5%, cover several major US trading partners, including India, the UK, the European Union, Canada and Japan.According to the Office of the USTR, "Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, as amended (Trade Act), is designed to address unfair foreign practices affecting US commerce. Section 301 may be used to respond to unjustifiable, unreasonable, or discriminatory foreign government acts, policies, or practices that burden or restrict US commerce. A Section 301(b) investigation examines whether the acts, policies, or practices are unreasonable or discriminatory and burden or restrict US commerce."

headline: Bangladesh raises garment workers’ minimum wage by 36% to  ₹12,865 after weeks of protests: What we know
content: Bangladesh on Wednesday raised the minimum monthly wage for garment workers by 36% to 17,000 taka ($139 or ₹12,865), the smallest increase in more than a decade, Reuters reported.The decision follows weeks of protests by workers demanding their pay be doubled, which led to factory shutdowns, highway blockades, production disruptions, and clashes with police.The garment industry employs over 4 million people and accounts for more than 80% of Bangladesh's export earnings. It is a major supplier to global retailers such as H&M, Zara, Walmart, Target, and Gap.How does the new wage structure work?A government-appointed wage board approved the revised pay structure on Wednesday after nearly 12 hours of negotiations between worker and employer representatives.According to workers' representative Babul Akhter, the six-member board, which includes two representatives each from workers and employers, passed the new structure in a 4-2 vote.Four members backed the final 17,000 taka minimum wage, while two supported the workers' demand for 18,000 taka.Under the new four-grade structure, monthly wages will range from 17,000 taka for Grade 4 workers to 21,500 taka for Grade 1 workers. The Grade 4 rate is 4,500 taka higher than the previous minimum wage of 12,500 taka set in 2023.The revised wages will take effect on December 1, with workers set to receive the updated pay from January.Smallest hike in over a decadeThe 36% increase is the lowest in more than 10 years, following hikes of 56% in 2023, 51% in 2018, and 77% in 2013.During negotiations, workers scaled down their initial demand from 32,000 taka to 18,000 taka, while factory owners raised their initial proposal from 15,000 taka to 17,000 taka.Factory owners have warned that further pay hikes could push up production costs and hurt global competitiveness. Labour rights groups, however, maintain that higher wages are necessary to protect workers' living standards and ensure long-term stability in the industry.Production losses and shifting ordersThe modest increase may not be enough to end the ongoing unrest that has disrupted factory operations across the country.The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) said 397 factories were unable to operate on Tuesday, while another 84 remained shut under the labour law's "no work, no pay" provision.A BGMEA survey estimated that 317 factories lost roughly $428 million in production over 18 days of disruption, and international buyers shifted orders worth about $254 million to other countries.(With Reuters inputs)

headline: Jeff Bezos' ex-wife MacKenzie Scott donates $12.5 million to two nonprofit organisations: Here's what they do
content: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos' former wife, MacKenzie Scott, a widely known philanthropist, has donated $12.5 million to two Georgia-based nonprofits working to expand access to higher education.Here's what we know about MacKenzie Scott's donationsAccording to a report by The Atlanta Journal-Constitution, the two organisations that received the grants are Achieve Atlanta, which received $8 million to help students in the Atlanta area access and afford post-secondary education, and the Jeannette Rankin Foundation, which received $4.5 million to support women pursuing higher education later in life. The donation to Achieve Atlanta marks Scott's second contribution of the same amount to the organisation, while the grant to the Jeannette Rankin Foundation is the largest single donation in its history. Commenting on the donation, Achieve Atlanta's President and Executive Director Cheryl Watson-Harris said, "This moment belongs to our Scholars," adding, "Their determination, resilience, and aspirations are the reasons Achieve Atlanta exists. This gift affirms what we have always known: talent is equally distributed, even when opportunity is not.”Scott is known for making large, often unsolicited donations to nonprofit organisations and allowing them flexibility in deciding how to use the funds. Her contributions are generally unrestricted, enabling recipients to direct the money towards their most pressing needs and long-term priorities. The latest grants follow the same approach and are part of her philanthropic initiative, Yield Giving.Achieve Atlanta receives second $8 million donation from ScottScott's latest grant marks her second $8 million donation to Achieve Atlanta, following an earlier contribution in 2022. The organisation partners with local school districts and colleges to help students meet higher education costs, continue their studies and graduate.Achieve Atlanta currently supports more than 8,700 students, known as Scholars, across Atlanta Public Schools and six high schools in Fulton County. Its programmes include helping students select colleges, complete applications, access academic guidance and social and emotional support, and find their first jobs.Since 2015, the organisation has distributed more than $75 million in scholarships. Achieve Atlanta said Scott's latest contribution would help it expand its work and create more opportunities for students pursuing higher education.Jeannette Rankin Foundation receives largest-ever single donationFounded in 1976, the Athens-based organisation helps women facing financial barriers to higher education. Its programmes provide grants and assistance to women pursuing vocational and technical qualifications, associate degrees and their first bachelor's degrees.The foundation currently supports more than 400 women scholars annually, up from 86 a few years ago. Its financial assistance is aimed at helping women who might otherwise be unable to continue their education because of economic constraints.Chief Executive Karen Sterk said the grant would enable the organisation to reach more women, noting that its programmes could potentially benefit more than one million women across the United States.The foundation said Scott's team had identified it through independent research and offered the grant without a prior request. It added that the funding would play a significant role in shaping its work over the next five decades.What is MacKenzie Scott's Yield Giving initiative?Yield Giving supports nonprofit organisations working across different sectors in the US. Unlike traditional funding programmes, which often involve formal applications and restrictions on how grants can be spent, Scott typically selects organisations through independent research and offers them unrestricted financial support.The latest contributions follow the same approach, giving both nonprofits the freedom to allocate the funds according to their priorities and objectives.MacKenzie Scott's philanthropic journey after divorce from Jeff BezosScott, who was married to Bezos for 25 years, is an American novelist and philanthropist. After the couple announced their divorce in 2019, she received a 4% stake in Amazon, worth roughly $36 billion at the time. Following the divorce, she pledged to give away the majority of her wealth to charitable causes and signed the Giving Pledge in 2019.Since then, Scott has donated billions of dollars to thousands of nonprofit organisations across the US.
