headline: Witness protection essential to criminal justice system: Kerala HC
content: KOCHI The Kerala High Court has observed that the protection of witnesses is not merely a matter of individual security but an essential prerequisite for effective administration of justice. The Division Bench of Justices Raja Vijayaraghavan and K.V. Jayakumar held that a system which expected witnesses to come forward and assisted the investigation should also ensure their safety. The court thus granted bail to a Sri Lankan national, Muhammed Asmin, who had turned approver in an alleged transnational conspiracy to revive the banned terrorist organisation, the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) through drugs and arms trafficking.The matter came to light when 300 kg of heroin, AK-47 rifles and 1,000 rounds of ammunition were seized. Kerala HC grants bail to Sri Lankan who was part of ‘transnational conspiracy’ to revive LTTE storyline 1 The court observed that Mr. Asmin had spent four years as an undertrial prisoner, and it would be unjust to continue his incarceration any longer given that he was granted a pardon previously by the NIA Special Court, Chennai. Mr. Asmin was accused of facilitating the movement of drug consignments, handling the proceeds of unlawful transactions through hawala channels and converting the proceeds of crime into cryptocurrency. He had received the pardon from the Special Court after agreeing to cooperate with the investigation and fully disclose all his knowledge concerning the alleged offences and other accused. However the court had refused to release him on bail, insisting that continued custody of an approver served the dual purpose of protecting his life and personal safety from possible reprisals at the hands of his former associates and ensuring that the course of justice remains unpolluted by any attempt to influence, intimidate or win him over before he enters the witness box. The High Court clarified that the Special Court was not justified in rejecting Ms. Asmin’s bail citing a rule that was not applicable to him under the Code of Criminal Procedure. The High Court further pointed out that the fundamental rights of the accused should be protected when a trial was prolonged. The court directed that the Kerala Witness Protection Scheme should be implemented without delay to provide security to witnesses as envisioned under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). The court noted that a draft Scheme was currently under consideration of the State government. The court observed that Mr. Asmin should be considered for protection under the Scheme, in view of his role as an approver and his decision to assist the prosecution by giving evidence against the other accused.

headline: Elections 2027 LIVE updates: SP to release manifesto for UP polls tomorrow amid seat-sharing talks with Congress
content: Elections 2027 LIVE updates: The stage is set for the next assembly elections in India, with key states - Uttar Pradesh and Punjab - preparing for the vote in 2027.Ahead of the elections, in Uttar Pradesh, the Samajwadi Party led by Akhilesh Yadav has joined hands with Rahul Gandhi's Congress. Meanwhile, AIMIM's Owaisi and Azad Samaj Party's Chandrashekar Azad have formed an alliance for the UP assembly elections with a goal to "remove the BJP government." The Bahujan Samaj Party, led by Mayawati is also in the mix for the assembly polls.In Punjab, after a six year split caused by the Centre's farm laws, the Bharatiya Janata Party and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) revived their alliance.Union home minister Amit Shah, BJP national president Nitin Nabin, and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal announced the reunion on Guru Nanak Jayanti (November 24, 2026) at a joint press conference at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi.Addressing the crowd, Amit Shah described SAD as the "big brother" ("bada bhai") and stated that SAD will choose the chief minister if the alliance wins.Prime Minister Narendra Modi also hailed the alliance and called it a "natural alliance" in a post on X.The dates and schedule for the UP and Punjab elections is yet to be announced by the Election Commission of India.

headline: Behind Ramdev-Dhirendra Shastri exchange, a jockeying for relevance in poll-bound U.P.
content: New Delhi Two ‘babas’, both perceived as close to the BJP, are facing off as religious and political activities gain pace in poll-bound Uttar Pradesh. Even before the political backlash over his comparison of Lord Ram and Lord Krishna could die down, Bageshwar Dham chief Dhirendra Krishna Shastri faced thinly veiled criticism from yoga guru Baba Ramdev, who on Monday (November 23, 2026) called those who draw such analogies “hypocrites”. Mr. Shastri shied away from escalating the exchange, but the spat has drawn attention as the political plot thickens in India’s most populous State. Political observers see the exchange against the backdrop of caste equations in Uttar Pradesh and Mr. Ramdev’s bid to remain in relevance as a 30-year-old gains increasing traction with his religious discourses in the Hindi heartland.

headline: Punjab elections: 69 Malwa seats in focus as AAP, SAD-BJP choose Moga for campaign launches
content: Moga is emerging as a major political hub ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, with the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and the newly reunited Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD)-BJP alliance choosing the district to launch their respective election campaigns.The political activity underlines the importance of the Malwa region, which accounts for 69 of Punjab's 117 Assembly constituencies and has traditionally played a decisive role in determining the state's electoral outcomes.The AAP will formally kick-start its election campaign with a mega rally, titled the 'Khushal Rally', in Moga on Thursday. The party is expected to use the event to highlight the achievements of its government and consolidate support ahead of the Assembly elections.The SAD-BJP alliance, meanwhile, is preparing to launch its joint campaign from the district on December 8. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to attend the rally, which will be the first major show of strength by the two parties since announcing their alliance after years of separation.The choice of Moga by both political formations is significant given the district's political history and its location in the heart of the Malwa belt. The region has remained central to the electoral strategies of all major parties, with its 69 Assembly seats accounting for more than half of the total constituencies in the state.For the Akali Dal, Moga has also held symbolic importance. The party launched its election campaigns from the district in 1996, 2006 and 2011, before returning to power in 1997, 2007 and 2012, respectively.The AAP, too, has previously used Moga district for major political events. In September 2016, ahead of the 2017 Assembly elections, the party organised a rally at Baghapurana and released its manifesto for farmers.Beyond electoral politics, Moga has a significant historical legacy. Freedom fighter Lala Lajpat Rai hailed from Dhudike village in the district, while the student movement of 1972 also brought the region into political prominence.With two major campaign launches scheduled within a fortnight, Moga is set to become a focal point of Punjab's political activity as parties begin positioning themselves for the 2027 Assembly elections.

headline: Vijayan hails students' protest at Sanskrit University
content: Thiruvananthapuram, Veteran CPI leader Pinarayi Vijayan on Wednesday hailed the recent protest by students of the Sanskrit University in Kalady, saying that it was an agitation to protect educational rights and colleges and urged the public to support such movements.The students were protesting against the suspension of 16 of their college mates for over two months and called off the agitation after the Kerala High Court allowed the suspended students to write their semester exams.Vijayan, in a Facebook post on the occasion of the 32nd anniversary of the Koothuparamba firing incident in which five DYFI activists were killed and several others injured, accused the current UDF government of "handing over" education to the private sector and the Sangh Parivar.Paying tributes to those who died in the Koothuparamba firing, the former chief minister said that it was an example of youth resistance against the commercialisation of education.Five Democratic Youth Federation of India activists K K Rajeevan, Madhu, Shibulal, Babu, and Roshan were killed, and several others were injured in the police firing on protestors agitating against the then UDF government's education policy.Comrade Pushpan, who was seriously injured in the incident, was paralysed for three decades before his death in September 2024."Koothuparamba Martyrs' Day reminds us of the history of the resistance raised by the Left against the moves to commercialise the education sector. Today, as the new UDF government is making intensive efforts to hand over the education sector to the private sector and the Sangh Parivar, the memories of the Koothuparamba struggle are becoming increasingly relevant," Vijayan said.He further said that the current student struggles, like the one at the Sanskrit University in Kalady, are a continuation of the resistance to protect educational rights and colleges."This is not just a need of the students, but a struggle to save the public education and future of the state," Vijayan, who is the opposition leader, said.The support and solidarity of the entire community is essential for these struggles, he said.Vijayan said that the vivid memories of those killed in the firing incident "will always be the energy and strength for the future struggles to protect rights and strengthen pro-people alternatives."This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: BJP intensifies its outreach to retain Purvanchal seats
content: The Bharatiya Janata Party’s (BJP) bid to retain power in Uttar Pradesh for a third term will depend largely on its performance in the Purvanchal (eastern) region that spans 100-120 assembly constituencies, people aware of the matter said. Elections for the 403-member Uttar Pradesh assembly will be held early next year along with four other states.Given the region’s importance, the party is deploying more resources and sharpening its outreach to the non-Yadav OBCs (Other Backward Classes), whose support is central to a favourable election outcome, a BJP leader said, asking not to be named.“After the party’s performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, our assessment showed that the caste composition in the region and the Opposition’s hold over its vote bank will be a formidable challenge for us. There is a large segment of floater voters who moved away from the BJP and voted for the SP; this is what we need to bring back,” the senior party functionary said.The BJP has identified three OBC groups—the Kurmis, the Koeri/Kushwahas and the Rajbhars—that it will aggressively pursue in Purvanchal. It is also relying on its allies: the Apna Dal (S) for Kurmi votes; the Nishad Party for Nishad, Mallah, and Bind communities; and the Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP) for Rajbhars and most backward castes.“Every OBC group is critical (for the party) this election… The party will take care of their concerns about ticket allocation and we will also have targeted campaigns. We are not looking at one big election narrative; there will be micro management,” said a second party functionary.The functionary added: “The Rajbhars, for instance, are a small community. They may be between 4% and 5% of the state’s population but in Purvanchal, they are an important caste group and in places like Ghazipur, Ballia, Azamgarh, Varanasi, Deoria, Gorakhpur and Basti, they have clout that matters in the election outcome,” said the second functionary. The two leaders said that the BJP’s performance in Purvanchal has shown a dip since the 2017 assembly polls, when the party stormed to power, winning 312 of the 403 seats. The party’s tally fell to 255 in 2022.On question on how the BJP will tackle the Samajwadi Party’s strategy of wooing the upper castes and non-Yadav OBCs, and the resentment against the chief minister for allegedly promoting “Thakurwaad”, or giving preference to those from the Thakur/Rajput caste, the second functionary said: “In the run up to the elections, we hear a lot of concerns and complaints. Even if they (SP) give more tickets to non-Yadav candidates, will they make anyone other than a Yadav a CM? Have people forgotten how the other castes were treated when the Yadavs were in power.”And while it is in the process of assessing the anti-incumbency factor against legislators and the issues that can emerge as potential challenges, the BJP is also readying a plan to highlight how it transformed UP from a “lawless” state to a “well-governed” one, said the first functionary quoted above “The other big task for us is to convert the support for the double-engine leadership of Modi-Yogi into votes…” said the first functionary.The BJP refers to its government at the Centre and at the state as a “double engine”.

headline: PM-SETU: Only 15 of 205 ITI clusters clear investment-plan stage in 18 months
content: Eighteen months after the Union Cabinet approved the ₹60,000-crore PM-SETU (Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs) to modernise the country’s Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), only 15 of the 205 identified clusters have secured approval for their strategic investment plans, while just one state, Rajasthan, has incorporated the special purpose vehicle (SPV) for its Bhiwadi cluster, a key step towards managing the upgraded institutes, according to documents of the ministry of skill development and entrepreneurship (MSDE) accessed by HT.Through the PM-SETU scheme, the Centre is seeking to address long-standing structural weaknesses that previous ITI modernisation initiatives between 2007 and 2024 failed to resolve. The latest scheme, which aims to transform ITIs “through industry-led governance into state-of-the-art skilling institutions that produce highly employable youth aligned with industry needs”, is itself facing implementation bottlenecks, particularly in securing industry participation.An internal MSDE review flags difficulties in “building acceptance towards a new implementation model”, “convincing industries to come forward and partner for PM-SETU”, “limited participation of PSUs” and the “absence of major industries” in several regions, particularly the Northeast.Also Read: PM-SETU Scheme: J&K ITIs get ₹470-crore Centre’s boost to transform youth employabilityThe review’s state-wise assessment lists ten states and Union territories (UTs) that had not floated requests for proposals (RFPs) to select industry partners at the time. These include Arunachal Pradesh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Kerala, Ladakh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Nagaland. Five of the states on the list are in the Northeast.To address the delays, the ministry has asked states to maintain continuous engagement with companies, approach major industrial groups and investment hubs, and develop clusters around local economic needs, including sectors such as agriculture, tourism and wellness. It has also urged administrative ministries to encourage public sector undertakings (PSUs) and private companies to partner with ITIs, while exploring income-tax deductions and corporate social responsibility (CSR) funding provisions to attract industry participation.The development comes against the backdrop of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s recent call to end the social stigma around vocational education and accord ITI students the same respect as those studying at Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs). Addressing the fifth Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh in Lucknow on November 21, Modi said parents and relatives sometimes hesitate to disclose that a child is studying at an ITI.Also Read: ₹1,237.58 crore PM-SETU investment approved as ITI modernisation plan expanded across Odisha, Gujarat and TelanganaUnder PM-SETU, the government plans to upgrade 1,000 government ITIs through 200 hub-and-spoke clusters, comprising 200 hub ITIs and 800 spoke ITIs, over five years. The scheme was announced in the 2024-25 Union budget and received Cabinet approval on May 7, 2025. Its total outlay is ₹60,000 crore, with ₹30,000 crore from the Centre, ₹20,000 crore from states and ₹10,000 crore from industry.The Centre has allocated ₹6,140.50 crore for the scheme in 2026-27, against ₹3,000 crore in the previous financial year. The allocation accounts for nearly 64% of the ministry’s total budget estimate of ₹9,540.50 crore for the current financial year.In response to HT’s queries, the MSDE said 36 states and UTs had identified 205 clusters covering 1,005 government ITIs. While 28 states/UTs have floated RFPs to select anchor industry partners (AIPs), only 15 strategic investment plans (SIPs), involving ₹3,688.30 crore, have been approved across eight states and one Union territory. More than 20 other SIPs are in the pipeline, the ministry said.Shareholders’ agreements have been signed for only three clusters in Rajasthan, Gujarat and Andhra Pradesh. Rajasthan is the first state to incorporate an SPV, for its Bhiwadi cluster. The ministry said the approved clusters would become operational in phases, subject to completion of procedural and statutory requirements, including execution of shareholders’ agreements, incorporation of SPVs and signing of licence agreements. It did not specify when the first upgraded ITIs would begin operations.Under PM-SETU’s “state-owned, industry-led model”, an AIP, a private company or PSU, will hold a 51% controlling stake in a non-profit SPV incorporated under Section 8 of the Companies Act. The Centre and state governments will hold 24.5% each. The industry partner must contribute at least 17% of the project cost, while the governments will fund the remaining 83%.Each hub ITI will be eligible for up to ₹81 crore and each spoke ITI for up to ₹40 crore. The hubs are expected to introduce an average of four new courses and upgrade ten existing trades to meet industry requirements. The scheme also envisages modern equipment, augmented and virtual reality (AR/VR) laboratories, digital learning systems and upskilling of at least 95% of existing trainers. The SPVs will have operational autonomy to redesign curricula, training delivery and industry exposure according to local employment needs.Earlier ITI reforms fell shortThe current scheme follows several attempts to improve the ITI ecosystem, including the Vocational Training Improvement Project launched in 2007 and an earlier ITI upgradation scheme launched in 2014. The 2014 scheme, which had an outlay of ₹238.08 crore, had utilised ₹192.65 crore by its closure in March 2024. Only 19 of the 35 targeted ITIs were fully upgraded over a decade, a completion rate of 54%.A 2023 NITI Aayog study cited in HT’s August report found that only 36% of sanctioned instructor posts were filled and just 15% of approximately 95,000 instructors had been trained as per norms. The study also flagged placement rate less than 0.1%, 405 placements against 41.4 million trained, despite annual public spending of around ₹10,000 crore on 3,500 government ITIs, at an average cost of ₹1.32 lakh per student.HT had also reported in August that nearly 4,49,000 ITI seats had been de-affiliated after courses recorded zero enrolment for two consecutive years. Sanctioned seats declined from 2.65 million in 2022-23 to 2.24 million in 2024-25, even as seat utilisation improved from 47.1% in 2022 to 64.6% in 2024.India currently has 13,888 ITIs, including 3,338 government-run and 10,550 privately managed institutes, with 14.70 lakh students enrolled.

headline: 20-Year-Old BITS Pilani Student Develops Mesh Radio For Indian Army: Here's Why It Is Significant
content: A 20-year-old student from BITS Pilani’s Hyderabad campus has achieved a remarkable milestone by developing a compact indigenous mesh radio to allow Indian Army personnel to communicate and share live location data without mobile towers, satellites or SIM cards. The face behind this invention is Samarth Alok Srivastava, a third-year dual-degree student pursuing MSc Physics and BE Mechanical Engineering, who founded the defence technology startup Krathveil Private Limited in May 2026. His batchmate, Shresth Prakash Singh, later joined the startup as co-founder to lead technology operations. Both students are natives of Thane, Maharashtra. Srivastava, who previously worked with Apollyon Dynamics, another BITS Hyderabad defence startup, focused on unmanned systems. He successfully identified critical gaps in ground-level communication systems, particularly for forces operating in areas with limited or no access to conventional network infrastructure. Krathveil has also developed its first product, Krath Control, which is a pocket-sized radio. It pairs with an Android-compatible smartphone capable of running applications such as ATAK (Android Team Awareness Kit). The device connects nearby military units and each device can function as an independent network node, enabling the transmission of voice communications, data, real-time location updates, map markers, and messages between connected units. The network also features a self-healing capability, automatically rerouting traffic through alternative communication paths if a node fails or becomes unavailable. According to the founders, a single communication hop between two elevated locations, such as hilltops, could theoretically span distances of more than 100 km, although the claim is yet to be validated through formal field trials. Why This Invention Matters The development is particularly significant for areas that lack critical network infrastructure. It also addresses a crucial operational requirement. While conventional voice radios enable basic communication, they often fall short of providing a shared operational picture among field units. Imported systems equipped with real-time mapping capabilities can cost around Rs 2 lakh per unit. Krathveil, by comparison, is targeting a price point of approximately Rs 40,000 per unit, cutting down costs by nearly 80 per cent. Designed with Indian terrain in mind and built to support integration with other systems, the platform aims to offer a more affordable alternative without compromising on connectivity and situational awareness.

headline: Maharashtra MPSC Paper Leak: Panel Recommends Minimum Rs 10 Crore Fine, Up To 10 Years In Jail
content: A Maharashtra government-appointed committee has recommended stricter punishment for those involved in leaking question papers for Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) recruitment exams. The proposed penalties include imprisonment of seven to 10 years, a minimum fine of Rs 10 crore and confiscation of the property of those found guilty. The recommendations are part of proposed amendments to the Maharashtra Competitive Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024. The committee, headed by senior IAS officer V Radha, has submitted its second report to the state government, reported Moneycontrol. The proposed changes aim to strengthen the existing law and prevent malpractice in competitive examinations. The committee has also recommended setting up a dedicated Special Task Force (STF) to investigate examination-related offences and establishing special fast-track courts to speed up trials. The panel has further suggested that exam-related cases pending under the law be transferred to these special courts for quicker disposal. It has also recommended that district collectors play a greater role in monitoring examination centres and maintaining a database of suitable venues, called a ‘Venue Bank’. Apart from stricter penalties, the committee has proposed a complete refund of examination fees to candidates who appear for MPSC exams. It has also recommended refunding the fee paid to challenge a provisional answer key if the candidate’s objection is accepted. The panel has suggested increasing the number of vacancies for the MPSC Group-C Combined Preliminary Exam 2026 to more than 16,000. It has also recommended a one-time relaxation of one year in the upper age limit for recruitment exams, the report added. These proposals come amid allegations of irregularities and exam malpractice in several MPSC recruitment tests. The Maharashtra government had constituted the committee on September 4, 2026, following concerns raised by aspirants over the examination process. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has said that the government will make efforts to introduce the proposed amendments during the upcoming Winter Session of the Maharashtra Legislature and try to get the Bill passed in the same session.

headline: India news Live Updates, 25 November 2026: At UN, India urges human-centric approach to AI in conflicts, flags risks of misuse by terrorists
content: India has called for a human-centric and responsible approach to the use of emerging technologies, particularly Artificial Intelligence, in conflict situations, stressing that human judgement and oversight must remain central. Speaking at a UN Security Council debate, India's Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni, highlighted AI's potential in conflict prevention and peacekeeping, while cautioning against its misuse by terrorist groups and non-state actors. Emphasising that technology must support rather than replace human judgement, he also called for equitable access to emerging technologies, particularly for developing countries. headline: Kerala Officials Begin Search For Wild Tusker, Deploy 2 Elephants
content: The Kerala Forest Department's mission to tranquilise and radio-collar Chakkakomban, a wild elephant that has been triggering concerns among residents of Chinnakanal and neighbouring areas in Idukki district, has been temporarily halted after the elephant moved away from the tracking team. Chief Conservator of Forests (CCF) DK Vinod Kumar said the operation would resume at noon. The elephant had moved towards the 80-acre island near the Anayirangal dam, making it difficult for officials to safely administer a tranquiliser dart. Officials are waiting for the elephant to move to suitable terrain before proceeding with the operation. Tranquilising the elephant near the reservoir could endanger its life if it enters the water after being darted. According to Kumar, Chakkakomban usually goes to sleep by 8 am and wakes up around 2 or 3 pm. Since the elephant had covered a considerable distance the previous day, officials decided against disturbing it during its resting hours. The operation began early this morning, with 140 Forest Department personnel splitting into multiple teams to track the elephant, which was initially spotted in the 301 Colony area of Chinnakanal.

headline: ‘Are we beggars?’ Congress fumes as Akhilesh offers 26 seats for UP polls
content: NEW DELHI: Tensions between the "UP ke do ladke" appear to be spilling into the open, with UP Congress working president Imran Masood making his displeasure clear after Samajwadi Party announced its first list of candidates for upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections."Are we beggars?" Congress MP Masood asked, expressing his strong objection over Akhilesh Yadav's decision to offer Congress just 26 "winnable" seats even as seat-sharing negotiations between the two INDIA bloc allies remain under way.The sharp reaction from Masood comes at a time when Congress and Samajwadi Party are still trying to work out an alliance for the upcoming polls. The SP's announcement of its first list of five candidates, largely from western Uttar Pradesh, appears to have added friction to the already delicate negotiations."Where is the alliance? If you are acting like this, then where is the alliance? Our leadership will decide what we need to do; I just don't understand it. Here you say one thing, and there something else happens," Masood told news agency IANS.Making it clear that the final call would rest with the Congress leadership, the MP said he would abide by whatever decision the party takes."This decision has to be taken by our party. What Akhilesh Ji is doing or not doing is not a big issue for me; I am bound by my party, and whatever my party says, I have to do that," he said.Referring to the upcoming visits of senior Congress leaders Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi, Masood said party workers would abide by the directions issued by the leadership."Rahul Gandhi will come, Priyanka Gandhi will come, and whatever instructions our leadership gives us, we have to follow them. SP's announcement makes no difference to us. However, it must definitely be decided whether the fight is against the BJP or against the Congress," he said.The immediate flashpoint is the SP's reported offer of 26 "winnable" constituencies to the Congress, against the latter's reported demand for around 130 seats. Masood said the Congress had not even formally demanded seats from its ally before the SP announced its offer."I don't understand it. It's beyond my understanding; the party has to take a decision on this, I don't understand. Are we beggars? Will you treat us like this- that we aren't even asking you for seats and you declared 26 seats? We didn't even demand seats from you. So if this is your way of working, that you will dictate terms, then a self-respecting person like me does not understand these things," he said.Taking a direct swipe at the SP leadership, Masood added, "You don't care about the alliance anyway. You are just running your own party, so go ahead and run your party- we aren't stopping or doing anything to you."Meanwhile, Congress leader Udit Raj said, "A great deal of permutation and combination is required in Uttar Pradesh; factors like political chemistry, winnability, and the choice of candidates will all be taken into account."The outburst follows a 3.5-hour meeting between the two parties in New Delhi on Tuesday as negotiations over seat-sharing for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections continued. While both sides claimed progress, no breakthrough was announced.Meanwhile, SP has maintained that winnability would be the key factor in deciding the seat-sharing arrangement.After announcing its first list, Akhilesh Yadav said the party had offered Congress 26 constituencies it considered winnable and indicated that discussions would continue."The winning start has been made with the first ‘26 seats’. Working together wisely, things will move forward." he posted in Hindi on X.Congress draws red line at 120 seats in UPCongress has sought 120 seats in the upcoming polls during seat-sharing talks with Samajwadi Party and is "unwilling to settle for fewer", party sources told news agency ANI.Congress submitted a list of 120 constituencies during a meeting with SP leaders in Delhi. The list reportedly includes two seats in Saharanpur, where the SP has already announced candidates, as well as constituencies in Rae Bareli and Amethi, some of which have sitting SP MLAs.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Thirupparankundram 'deepathoon' row LIVE: Temple says Karthigai Deepam lit at Thiruparankundram hill 'as per age-old tradition'
content: Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription The Karthigai Dheepam lit atop the Uchipilyar temple at Thirupparankundram in Madurai on November 24, 2026. | Photo Credit: G. Moorthy Shortly after the deepam was lit, the Arulmighu Subramanian Swamy Temple Executive Officer G. Selvi and Board of Trustees chairman V. Shanmugasundaram jointly stated in a press release that the temple has followed the age-old culture and agama rules in lighting the lamp atop the Thiruparankundram hillock on Tuesday (November 24, 2026). Earlier, the maha deepam was lit at the traditional place at the Uchipillayar deepa mandapam atop Thirupparankundram hill around 6:00 p.m. on Tuesday (November 24, 2026). At the foothills of Thirupparankundram hill stands the Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy Temple, one of the six abodes dedicated to Lord Murugan, while the summit is home to the Sikandar Badusha Dargah, a Muslim shrine. The ‘ deepathoon’ (stone pillar) is located around 50 metres from the dargah. The dispute centres on whether the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp should also be lit at this pillar. Earlier on November 20, a Supreme Court Bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul Pancholi had ordered the ceremonial lamp to be lit at the ‘deepathoon’ on Thirupparankundram hill on the day of Karthigai Deepam festival. The court described the direction as a “temporary, one-time arrangement.” The interim order addressed the Tamil Nadu government’s plea to stay the January 6 judgment.

headline: Former members say EPG report was ‘highly positive’ for India-Nepal ties
content: NEW DELHI A day after Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri termed the report of the India-Nepal Eminent Persons Group (EPG) “not relevant”, arguing that India will take a “forward looking” approach regarding boundary issues with Nepal, a former member of the EPG has said the report was “highly positive” for both India and Nepal and that it was “odd” that the group did not get a chance to present the report to the Government of India. India-Nepal talks focus on energy, connectivity, trade and sports: Vikram Misri shorts 1 “The EPG report was produced after extensive research and field visits. We visited Visakhapatnam and other ports that are of interest to Nepal and spoke with many stakeholders before compiling the report and there are interesting recommendations in the report that could be of great use for India and Nepal and it was highly positive for Delhi-Kathmandu relations,” said Mahendra P. Lama, former professor of Jawaharlal Nehru University, who served as a member of the EPG. India-Nepal ties: What does Modi-Balen partnership promise? | Above the Fold | Nov 23, 2026 India-Nepal ties: What does Modi-Balen partnership promise? | Above the Fold | Nov 23, 2026 Lead: Nepal Prime Minister Balen Shah’s first bilateral visit to India marks a significant moment for ties between the two neighbours. What are the key takeaways from his visit? India-Nepal ties: What does Modi-Balen partnership promise? | Above the Fold | Nov 23, 2026 video 1 The EPG returned to the spotlight on Monday (November 23, 2026) when Mr. Misri announced in a press conference held after the visit of Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah that New Delhi would adopt a “forward-looking” approach to the border issues. “The leaders have given a direction as part of the overall very forward-looking discussions that have been held today for the foreign secretaries to take the task forward. We will do so in a forward-looking manner, taking inspiration from the vision document and from the directions and indeed the spirit in which the discussions were held. I would say that EPG is in the past. We are not looking backward,” said Mr. Misri in response to a question. He described the EPG report as “not relevant”. ‘Not unilateral document’ Former Nepali ambassador and coordinator of the EPG on the Nepali side, Bhek Bahadur Thapa, described the EPG report as a step forward for the bilateral consultation process. “It was not a unilateral document, it was a document created through bilateral consultation among experts appointed by New Delhi and Kathmandu,” said Mr. Thapa, who has also served as Foreign Minister of Nepal during 2004-05. The EPG report dealing with a broad spectrum of India-Nepal relations, including the Kalapani dispute and the 1950 India-Nepal Friendship Treaty was completed in 2018 but it remained under sealed covers. “It is odd that the report could not be launched here in Delhi. The Nepali side said the EPG report should be unveiled first by the Indian Prime Minister and on the same day we were supposed to return to Kathmandu for the report’s unveiling by the Nepali Prime Minister, “ said Prof. Lama, informing that they made a mistake as Kathmandu could have also unveiled the report first. “Our recommendations now can be accessed by other stakeholders in Kathmandu and I don’t think that is a positive thing,” said Mr. Lama. India, Nepal to hold 20th edition of joint military exercise Suryakiran India, Nepal to hold 20th edition of joint military exercise Suryakiran Exercise Suryakiran is a key bilateral military engagement between India and Nepal, providing an opportunity for the two armies to enhance interoperability, exchange operational experiences and strengthen coordination through joint training India, Nepal to hold 20th edition of joint military exercise Suryakiran storyline 1 The EPG was institutionalised according to an understanding that was reached during the delegation-level talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and former Nepali Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli in February 2016. The visit of Mr. Oli took place against the backdrop of months-long blockade on Nepal-India border that Kathmandu said was imposed by India but India blamed the Madhesi agitators of Nepal for imposing the blockade that hindered flow of essential items such as cooking gas into Nepal. During the time of its existence, a part of the Institute of Defence Studies and Analyses (IDSA) in Delhi served as the secretariat for the EPG. The then Director General of the IDSA Jayant Prasad was also part of the EPG. Incidentally, officials who are currently playing key roles in India-Nepal relations were also involved in the EPG process. Former members recounted that the newly appointed Indian ambassador to Nepal Sudhakar Dalela was the Joint Secretary (North) in the Ministry of External Affairs and was part of the EPG process during 2016-18. That apart, the new Nepali ambassador to India Nischal Nath Pandey also was part of the EPG process in Kathmandu.

headline: UGC-NET December 2026 City Slip Releasing Today, Here's Direct Link To Download
content: UGC-NET December 2026:The National Testing Agency (NTA) is expected to release the city intimation slips for the University Grants Commission-National Eligibility Test (UGC-NET) December 2026 today. Once released, candidates will be able to access their city slips from the official website, ugcnet.nta.nic.in. The NTA will conduct the UGC-NET December 2026 examination in Computer-Based Test (CBT) mode from December 14 to 18 and on December 21, 2026. The examination will be conducted in two shifts, from 9am to 12pm and 3pm to 6pm. The examination will be of 180 minutes (three hours), with no break between Paper 1 and Paper 2. UGC-NET is conducted to assess the eligibility of Indian nationals for the award of Junior Research Fellowship and appointment as Assistant Professor; appointment as Assistant Professor and admission to PhD; and admission to PhD only in Indian universities and colleges. The test paper will comprise two sections, both consisting of objective-type, multiple-choice questions. The medium of the question paper will be English and Hindi only, except for language papers.

headline: ‘Crores of devotees let down’: BJP slams Vijay govt for defying SC order on Deepam row
content: NEW DELHI: The controversy over the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at Tamil Nadu's Thiruparankundram hills escalated on Wednesday, with BJP national general secretary BL Santhosh accusing the TVK-led government of defying the Supreme Court's interim order and warning that Chief Minister Vijay's government would face a "civilisational and legal challenge".The remarks came after the traditional lamp was lit at the Ucchi Pillayar temple on Tuesday evening instead of the Deepathoon stone pillar, as directed by the Supreme Court. The apex court had ordered that the lamp be lit at the designated pillar at 6 pm, triggering a dispute between the state administration and organisations demanding implementation of the direction.In a post on X, Santhosh alleged that the Madurai district administration had violated the court's directions."The DM of Madurai who is a part of TN government, defies SC order and lights Karthika Deepam at Ucchapillaiyar Mandapam instead of Deepathoon Stone pillar as instructed by SC," he said.Targeting the government led by Vijay, he added, "@TVKVijayHQ Govt under @actorvijay will face both civilisational & legal challenge. They have bit more than they can chew."In another post, Santhosh accused the government of compromising the sentiments of devotees to accommodate its political allies."You people have hurt devotes & defied SC Order to please some alliance partners & you yourself is Law Minister of a Govt which will fully defied SC Order . To please some friends you let down crores of devotees," he alleged.The BJP leader's remarks came amid protests by Hindu organisations and BJP workers across Tamil Nadu over the failure to light the lamp at the Deepathoon pillar.Protests across Tamil Nadu, arrests reportedSeveral organisations staged demonstrations in different parts of the state, demanding that the government implement the Supreme Court's directions.In Ramanathapuram, members of the Hindu Front organised a protest against the state government, accusing it of failing to comply with the court order. Police detained protesters involved in a road blockade in the Kenikarai area.In Pollachi, members of Hindu Munnani staged a road blockade during the Maha Karthigai Deepam festival. Protesters alleged that Hindu organisations, including the BJP and Vishva Hindu Parishad, had been campaigning since last year for the lamp to be lit at the designated pillar.The demonstrators raised slogans against the state government and demanded that it follow the court's directions within the stipulated time. Police personnel deployed at the site removed the protesters and arrested them.Petitioners threaten contempt proceedingsAdvocate Niranjan S Kumar, who is associated with the Hindu Munnani petition in the matter, expressed disappointment over the lamp not being lit at the Deepathoon and accused the state government of deliberately disobeying the Supreme Court's interim order."We were all in the belief that the government would take immediate steps to light the lamp at the Thirupparankundram Deepathoon. We had all gathered here to see the lamp being lit by the authorities themselves. Unfortunately, at 6:02 p.m., the lamp at the Ucchi Pillayar was lit as usual, which means the order of the Supreme Court was definitely violated. I would say it was not only violated, but it is a deliberate, calculated and willful disobedience of the order of the Supreme Court. So we are all left with no other option but to approach the Supreme Court by way of contempt. I trust and hope that the Supreme Court will take note of all these actions and see that it passes serious action against the state," the advocate said.He also referred to the Supreme Court's direction asking the Madurai District Collector to submit a status report within three days after the festival."And the District Collector, Madurai, was also directed to file a status report within three days after the festival. So let's wait for the District Collector's report. In my personal view, I would say this is nothing but a constitutional breakdown. The machinery has been broken down and the State has deliberately violated the interim order of the Supreme Court. Therefore, this is nothing but a constitutional breakdown of the machinery. The Supreme Court has to take note of all these things and pass, and we expect that it will deal with this with iron hands..."Tamilisai Soundararajan accuses government of favouring alliesTamil Nadu BJP leader Tamilisai Soundararajan also criticised the Vijay government, accusing it of violating the Supreme Court's interim order and discriminating against political groups in its handling of the temple dispute."I strongly condemn the TVK government for violating the Supreme Court's interim order. Nobody is above the law. But they behaved in a way; they have violated the interim order of the Supreme Court. They should not have gone for an appeal; that is my view. They are now citing because of the Agama rules, they have lit the lamp in the Ucchi Pillayar. Till now, why didn't you say that you are cheating the people and you did not disclose where you are going to light the lamp? Before itself you should have disclosed. Why didn't you put the same argument before the Supreme Court? They did not tell about the Agama rules at that time. Madras High Court again said - don't cheat like the previous time because it cannot be excused repeatedly."She alleged that the government had taken the decision to appease its alliance partners and claimed that BJP leaders and workers were prevented from approaching the temple."I am saying only one thing to the TVK government, to CM Vijay - to pamper your alliance partners, to satisfy your alliance partners, you have taken this decision. But these alliance partners were the alliance partners of the previous government, they backstabbed them and now they have joined with you. They will definitely backstab you. You did not allow us to go near the temple. The government did not allow us to go near the temple. From our State president to our workers, they were all arrested. We were not allowed to go to the temple. But they allowed Thirumavalavan, they allowed Jawahirullah. Jawahirullah is a person with different religious beliefs. How can he talk about the religious ideology of the Hindu faith? TVK government is not treating us equally."Soundararajan further called on the Supreme Court to take note of the alleged violation."It is atrocious, disheartening and they have disobeyed the rule of law. Supreme Court should definitely consider this violation and in future, the TVK government will pay a high price for this. You can cheat the Supreme Court, you can violate the High Court but you cannot cheat the people's court. People will answer you. Because the same people answered DMK and sent them home because of the anti-Hindu attitude."Tamil Nadu BJP chief also targets district administrationTamil Nadu BJP president Nainar Nagenthran also accused the state government and Madurai district administration of failing to implement the Supreme Court's directions.Speaking to reporters in Tirunelveli on Tuesday, Nagenthran said the authorities had failed to light the lamp at the Deepathoon despite the apex court's directions and subsequent intervention by the Madras High Court.He alleged that lighting the lamp at the Pillaiyar temple after assuring the court that arrangements were being made amounted to deceiving the judiciary."Lighting the lamp at the Pillaiyar temple after assuring the court that arrangements were being made is an act of deception. It is akin to fooling a child with candy, and they are attempting to deceive the Supreme Court and High Court judges," Nagenthran said.He argued that the Madurai District Collector, as district magistrate, had the authority to implement court orders independently and should not yield to political pressure. He also said the collector should be considered the "first accused" in the matter.The BJP leader said the party would decide on further legal action based on the observations of the Supreme Court.What happened at Thiruparankundram?The Maha Deepam was lit above the Ucchi Pillayar temple at Thiruparankundram hills on Tuesday evening amid heavy police deployment and heightened tensions. However, the lamp was not lit at the Deepathoon stone pillar, which was at the centre of the legal dispute.A small team of priests associated with the Subramaniya Swamy Temple performed the lighting ceremony at the Ucchi Pillayar location, while police personnel remained deployed near the Deepathoon pillar.The Supreme Court had issued an interim direction for lighting the lamp at the designated pillar at 6 pm. The Madurai District Collector was also asked to submit a status report within three days after the festival.The dispute has since triggered protests, political allegations and demands for further judicial intervention.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: No defence data breach, says Government, as security agencies asked to audit messaging groups
content: New Delhi There has been no leak of sensitive information pertaining to the Defence Forces, a senior Defence Ministry official said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), even as security establishments reiterated advisories against sharing sensitive data on messaging applications. The official said documents circulating on social media claiming to contain defence-related information were fake and intended to create confusion. However, an advisory has been issued to all formations, directing personnel to exercise caution while using messaging platforms. “The documents pertaining to the Defence Forces circulating on social media are fake and have been developed to create chaos. There is no data leak. There is a strict advisory that no sensitive information, in any form, should be shared or discussed on messaging apps,” the official said. A high-level meeting has been convened at the Ministry of Home Affairs on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) to discuss issues related to data breaches and cyber safety. The developments come amid reports that Pakistan-based Intelligence Operatives (PIOs) have infiltrated unofficial WhatsApp groups used by Indian defence, paramilitary and civil defence personnel to gather sensitive information. An advisory issued last week to defence and security establishments, including the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs), flagged attempts by PIOs to gain unauthorised access to WhatsApp groups using spoofed or compromised mobile numbers. The operatives were allegedly functioning as "silent members" in these groups to monitor conversations and collect information. The advisory covers the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), Border Security Force (BSF), Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) and Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), among other establishments. Group administrators have been directed to conduct audits of membership lists and remove unknown and unverified members. Security personnel have also been asked to organise cyber awareness campaigns to improve vigilance against such attempts, the offical said. The Defence Forces have an indigenous messaging application for secure communication, the official said, reiterating that sensitive information must not be shared through unofficial platforms. Recently, the Ministry of Defence issued an advisory directing military personnel, including soldiers and officers, to refrain from using 87 mobile applications over concerns about data security and the potential misuse of sensitive information. Separately, Delhi Police detained a 14-year-old boy from Palwal, in Haryana, over alleged attempts to sell Agniveer-related data on the dark web. The data was purportedly sourced from a Ministry of Home Affairs test portal. Records relating to around 2,500 individuals were recovered for verification.

headline: ‘Not a single bogus vote to be added’: Akhilesh tells SP workers to monitor election commission activities
content: NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Wednesday urged the party's 'PDA sentinels' across Uttar Pradesh to monitor the Election Commission's electoral roll activities ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.In a post on X, Yadav asked party workers across the state to remain vigilant about the poll body's activities, with two principles for monitoring changes to voter lists: "Not a single bogus vote to be added, not a single genuine vote to be removed!"The SP chief also raised concerns over the credibility of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs), referring to public scepticism about the voting system."How can we trust them, when ‘Haathi ke daant khaane ke aur, dikhaane keaur’ (All show, no substance)," Yadav said.In his post, the party chief also mentioned the controversy surrounding the Chandigarh mayoral election, referring to what he called the BJP's 'Chandigarh trick'. He said people were aware of the episode and understood such political tactics.The Chandigarh mayoral election controversy centres on allegations of deliberate ballot tampering by presiding officer Anil Masih during the January 30, 2024, mayoral polls. The Supreme Court subsequently found that Masih had deliberately marked eight ballot papers cast in favour of Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)-Congress candidate Kuldeep Kumar, leading to their wrongful rejection. Later, the apex court quashed the initially declared result and declared Kumar the validly elected mayor of Chandigarh.On Tuesday, Yadav urged the Congress to identify more potential constituencies beyond the 26 seats on its priority list as the two parties negotiate a seat-sharing arrangement for Assembly elections, ANI reported.He said the discussions should be conducted in the name of the INDIA alliance rather than being limited to candidates from either the Samajwadi Party or the Congress. Yadav described the two parties' cooperation as a "historic opportunity" to defeat what he called the "communal BJP and its narrow-minded allies".He called for serious discussions that take public expectations and political realities into account, saying the alliance should aim to win in as many constituencies as possible."Among the seats you and we contest, the number we win should exceed the number we lose. Only victory will make the division of seats respectable, because only the seats we win will bring us respect," he said.Yadav also asked the Congress to share the names of all other constituencies it considered winnable, apart from the 26 already discussed. He said both parties could then assess the prospects of potential candidates in each seat.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: India condemns Houthi attack on Riyadh tower that injured two Indians
content: Two Indians were injured in an attack on a tower in Riyadh's financial district on November 24, India's Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said. India condemned the attack and continued strikes targeting civilian, economic and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia. "We strongly condemn the attack on one of the towers of the financial district in Riyadh on November 24 as well as the continued attacks targeting civilian, economic and energy infrastructure in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Two Indians are among those injured in the attack on Riyadh financial district. The Embassy of India in Riyadh is providing all possible assistance to the injured and their families. These attacks seriously endanger civilian lives, violate the sovereignty of Saudi Arabia, and undermine regional security and stability. We call for immediate cessation of such attacks. We also reiterate our firm solidarity with the people and Government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and reaffirm our unwavering support to the Kingdom in safeguarding its sovereignty, territorial integrity, and the security and safety of its citizens and residents. We earnestly hope that peace and normalcy will return to the region at the earliest," the MEA said in a press release.This is a developing story. Please refresh periodically for more updates.

headline: Police ‘handling’ of women protesters: What law says about crowd control, use of force
content: The story so far: The Delhi Police has told the Supreme Court that there is no strict rule requiring only women police officers to “handle” women in crowd-control operations. The submission came in response to allegations that women protesters and journalists were manhandled by male police officers during widespread protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. The petitions have been filed by the Network of Women in Media, India, represented by advocate Aarthi Rajan, and others, including the Delhi Union of Journalists, Free Speech Collective and the Kerala Union of Working Journalists. The Delhi Police said the legal requirement that only women police officers could arrest or search women does not amount to a mandate in crowd-control situations. “The requirement of women personnel handling women is not a statutory mandate in the context of crowd-control operations, in the same manner as it is expressly prescribed under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 in relation to searches and arrests,” the police said in its affidavit.

headline: 45 mass fish deaths reported across Indian rivers in a year, data shows
content: The mass fish deaths in the Yamuna near Delhi’s Sonia Vihar last month triggered a political war of words between the BJP and the Aam Aadmi Party, with allegations of deliberate dumping of carcasses and chemical spraying into the river. However, data show this is not an isolated incident, with at least 45 such incidents reported in Indian rivers in the past year, an assessment has found.The assessment, carried out by the South Asia Network on Dams, Rivers and People (SANDRP), examined all reported cases between November 2025 and November 2026 and found that 60% of these incidents were concentrated in four river basins -- Ganga, Brahmaputra, Krishna and Indus.The Ganga basin recorded the highest number, with nine incidents, all in the Yamuna basin, followed by the Brahmaputra with seven, Krishna with six and Indus with five.The Yamuna incidentThe findings come amid repeated fish mortality incidents in the Yamuna. Thousands of dead fish were found near Burari in North Delhi on October 14, weeks before hundreds of dead fish were seen floating near Sonia Vihar on November 11.The latter, which came a day after the launch of the Namo Yamuna River Safari, prompted Delhi water minister Parvesh Verma to accuse unidentified people of deliberately dumping fish into the river to discredit the government. The AAP rejected the allegation and blamed pollution. Delhi Police subsequently registered an FIR, but the cause of the fish deaths remains unestablished.Bhim Singh Rawat, a Yamuna activist and member of SANDRP, said the October incident was particularly unusual as mass fish deaths are more commonly reported during summer, when high temperatures reduce dissolved oxygen in the water.“I can’t recall the last such episode in winter months. The possibility in this case could be untreated industrial effluents,” he had said, pointing to drains carrying wastewater from Haryana as possible sources.The reasonsThe India-wise assessment finds that industrial effluents and chemical pollution were suspected to be the primary reasons in around 20 of the 45 incidents, while sewage and domestic wastewater were identified as possible contributing factors in around 10 cases. In some instances, inadequate water releases from dams, falling water levels, and physical obstructions in rivers also appeared to contribute to fish mortality.The problem was not confined to the Yamuna. The Indrayani in Pune recorded three incidents near Alandi in June, September and October, while the Phalguni river in Mangaluru witnessed at least three incidents in February, May and June. North and South India recorded the highest number of incidents, with 12 each, followed by West India with 8 and Northeast India with 7 -- showing that the issues remain widespread.The report also flagged gaps in investigations, with the causes of several incidents remaining unconfirmed. SANDRP said that delays in inspections, the collection of water and fish samples, laboratory testing, and public disclosure have weakened efforts to identify pollution sources and assign responsibility.In the case of the October fish deaths in the Yamuna near Burari, no laboratory investigation had established the cause or confirmed the source of pollution. SANDRP also flagged that investigations into similar fish deaths in Baghpat on October 14 were incomplete, with water samples collected two days later, after the suspected polluted water had moved downstream. Fish samples had not been collected for testing at all."This shows we need swifter action. At the same time, it also raises questions on the pollution control boards and the Central Pollution Control Board," Rawat added.

headline: 'Crawled Back To BJP': Punjab Congress Targets SAD Over Reunion, Invokes Farmers’ Agitation
content: The reunion of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections has opened a fresh political battle over the farmers’ agitation, with the Congress accusing the two former allies of putting electoral ambitions ahead of Punjab’s farmers’ interests. Taking a swipe at the reunited parties, the Punjab Congress on Wednesday invoked the farmers’ movement against the now-repealed three farm laws, accusing SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal of abandoning his earlier stand against the BJP to return to an alliance with the party. In a post on X, the Punjab Congress said, “Punjab’s farm unions have slammed the unholy BJP-SAD alliance for the 2027 elections, and rightly so.” The party alleged that Sukhbir Badal had been exposed for “crawling back to the BJP” after previously branding the BJP “anti-farmer” and “anti-Punjab”. Describing the renewed partnership as an alliance driven by the “greed for power”, Congress said the political understanding had completely overlooked the agrarian crisis facing the state. Punjab’s farm unions have slammed the unholy #BJPSADalliance for the 2027 elections, and rightly so. @officeofssbadal has been exposed for crawling back to the BJP after branding them “anti-farmer” and “anti-Punjab.” This is an alliance forged purely out of greed for power, completely ignoring Punjab’s agrarian crisis. Punjabis will not forget the sacrifices made at the Delhi border during the farm agitation. #BJPSADAlliance #PunjabFarmers #CongressForPunjab — Punjab Congress (@INCPunjab) November 25, 2026 “Punjabis will not forget the sacrifices made at the Delhi border during the farm agitation,” the party said, making it clear that the farmers’ protest is likely to remain a central political issue as Punjab heads towards another Assembly election. The Congress’s attack comes a day after the BJP and SAD formally announced the revival of their alliance in New Delhi. The two parties, which shared power in Punjab for years, had parted ways in 2020 after the Centre introduced the controversial farm laws. The Akali Dal withdrew its representative from the Union Cabinet before formally walking out of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA). The reunion has given the Congress an opportunity to question the political consistency of the Akali Dal, particularly over its earlier opposition to the farm legislation and its support for protesting farmers. Congress leaders have also raised questions about whether the BJP has addressed the issues that led to the split, including farmers’ demand for a legal guarantee on Minimum Support Price (MSP). Punjab Congress leader and Leader of Opposition Partap Singh Bajwa described the reunion as a “desperate marriage of political convenience between two rejected parties trying to save themselves from political extinction”. AICC general secretary in-charge of Punjab Sachin Pilot also questioned whether the BJP had apologised for the farm laws and whether the Akali Dal had adequately addressed the deaths of farmers during the agitation. “Has the central government or the BJP given any guarantee on MSP to the people of the country? Have they apologised for the black laws they enacted?” Pilot asked. Congress state president Pargat Singh, meanwhile, said the alliance could not erase the memories of the farmers’ movement. “Sacrificing the farmers’ martyrdom on the altar of political deal-making is a betrayal of Punjab,” he said. With the BJP-SAD partnership back on the political table, the farm laws and the 2020-21 agitation are likely to become key talking points in the run-up to the 2027 polls. For the Congress, the challenge will be to turn the renewed alliance into an electoral liability by reminding voters of the circumstances in which the two parties parted ways.

headline: India Condemns Houthi Attack On Riyadh Financial District That Injured 2 Indians
content: India on Wednesday strongly condemned the Houthi attack on a tower in Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh Financial District that left 11 people injured, including two Indian nationals, and called for an immediate cessation of attacks targeting civilian and economic infrastructure in the Kingdom. The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said the attack took place on November 24 and reaffirmed India’s solidarity with Saudi Arabia, stressing that such strikes threatened civilian lives and regional stability. “We strongly condemn the attack on one of the towers of the financial district in Riyadh on November 24 as well as the continued attacks targeting civilian, economic and energy infrastructure in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia,” the MEA said. The ministry confirmed that two Indians were among those injured in the attack, adding that the Indian Embassy in Riyadh was providing all possible assistance to them and their families. “These attacks seriously endanger civilian lives, violate the sovereignty of Saudi Arabia, and undermine regional security and stability. We call for immediate cessation of such attacks,” the statement added. According to Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defence, 11 people were injured when a tower in Riyadh’s King Abdullah Financial District. Those injured included two Saudi nationals, two Indians, three Nepalese nationals and four Egyptians. India Reaffirms Solidarity With Saudi Arabia Reiterating its support for Riyadh, India said it stood firmly with the people and government of Saudi Arabia in safeguarding the Kingdom’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. “We reiterate our firm solidarity with the people and Government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and reaffirm our unwavering support to the Kingdom in safeguarding its sovereignty, territorial integrity, and the security and safety of its citizens and residents,” the MEA said. India also expressed hope that peace and normalcy would return to the region at the earliest.
