headline: Why has the FSSAI sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri? | Explained
content: The story so far: On November 22, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), the country’s apex food-safety regulator, sanctioned prosecution against packaged drinking water manufacturer Bisleri International Pvt. Ltd. after a sample of its water was found to be non-compliant with prescribed safety standards, with the regulator declaring it unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The public-health stakes are significant. In 2023, bottled water was the principal source of drinking water for 15% of urban and 6% of rural households, as per Data For India. For consumers buying it at railway stations, airports, highway eateries and neighbourhood shops, a sealed bottle is often taken as an assurance of safety. Yet, the data submitted in Parliament in February 2025 revealed that 333 of 1,300 enforcement samples of packaged drinking water tested in 2023-24 failed to meet prescribed standards. Similarly, in 2022-23, 650 of 1,776 samples had been found non-compliant. According to the FSSAI, a sample of packaged drinking water (other than mineral water) collected from Bisleri’s premises was found to be non-compliant with the prescribed limits for “bromate” and was declared unsafe under the 2006 Act. Following an appeal by the food business operator (FBO), the sample was referred to a Referral Food Laboratory for further examination, which also declared the sample unsafe, citing the detection of “polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons” (PAHs). In its response, Bisleri has maintained that its water is safe for consumption, saying the matter concerned a batch manufactured at its Goa facility in September 2025, one of 143 manufacturing plants in its network. In a statement issued on November 23, the company said the FSSAI had collected six samples from its Goa facility on September 30, 2025. While five samples met the prescribed standards, the sixth recorded a “bromate” level of 12 micrograms per litre, against the prescribed limit of 10 micrograms per litre. Further, Bisleri said it appealed on November 22, 2025, following which the sample was sent to a referral laboratory for retesting. The laboratory, as claimed, found the bromate level within the prescribed limit but separately detected PAHs. Citing the divergent test findings, the company reportedly arranged an independent examination of the same sample at an FSSAI-approved laboratory, which, according to Bisleri, also found the bromate level within limits. The company said it submitted these results to FSSAI’s Western Regional Office on February 2, 2026, but received no further communication and understood that the matter had been closed. Water is essential for digestion, blood circulation, temperature regulation and kidney function, but its safety cannot be judged by its appearance, taste, odour or sealed packaging alone. Contamination may be microbiological, causing illnesses such as diarrhoea, cholera and typhoid, or chemical, with some substances posing risks through prolonged exposure. In India, packaged water broadly falls into two categories: (1) “packaged drinking water”, which may be sourced from surface water, groundwater or seawater and treated through processes such as filtration, decantation, reverse osmosis (RO) and disinfection; and (2) “natural mineral water”, drawn from protected underground sources and characterised by a relatively stable mineral composition. Both must meet prescribed chemical and microbiological safety standards.

headline: Maharashtra FDA cancels Inducare’s manufacturing licences again over nine unauthorised drugs, two found spurious
content: Mumbai The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) said it had cancelled the drug manufacturing licences of Pune-based Inducare Pharmaceutical and Research Foundation for the second time after the firm was found to have manufactured and sold nine drugs without mandatory product permission, all of which were subsequently declared substandard, misbranded or spurious by government analysts. Also read | Maharashtra FDA permanently cancels Pune-based pharma firm’s license over six contaminated medicines, GMP lapses https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/maharashtra/maharashtra-fda-permanently-cancels-pune-based-pharma-firms-license-over-six-contaminated-medicines-gmp-lapses/article71319250.ece The cancellation order, issued on November 23 by the Joint Commissioner (Drugs), Pune Division, directed the firm to immediately cease all manufacturing, packing, testing and distribution activities. The FDA has also proposed prosecution against the firm under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. Of the nine drugs tested, two were declared spurious after government analysts found that the claimed active ingredients were absent. Ibucare Plus, a combination of ibuprofen and paracetamol, contained no ibuprofen, while Carevita-M, a multivitamin tablet, was found to contain none of the nine specified ingredients tested. Maharashtra FDA seizes drugs, cosmetics worth ₹34.51 lakh, cancels 122 licences Maharashtra FDA seizes drugs, cosmetics worth ₹34.51 lakh, cancels 122 licences The FDA urged citizens to report instances of illegal drug manufacturing or sales, as well as suspected substandard drugs, medical devices and cosmetics, to its commissioner’s office or the nearest district office Maharashtra FDA seizes drugs, cosmetics worth ₹34.51 lakh, cancels 122 licences storyline 1 The remaining drugs failed various quality tests, with several containing significantly lower quantities of active ingredients than claimed on their labels. These included medicines used in the treatment of cardiovascular and digestive disorders. The FDA said the firm, located in the Additional MIDC area of Jejuri in Pune district, had admitted in its written response that it had not obtained separate product permissions for the nine drugs. Earlier violations The firm’s manufacturing licences had previously been cancelled on September 7 after a joint inspection conducted on July 14 and 15 revealed 25 serious deficiencies in Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP). The inspection revealed that approximately 13.86 lakh tablets of Caregyl-400 had been manufactured without mandatory batch manufacturing and packing records or test reports. Of these, 5.20 lakh tablets had already been distributed. Laboratory analysis revealed that the sampled batch contained only 32.44% of the claimed metronidazole content. Several samples of substandard drugs were also collected from the Central Medical Store of Yashwantrao Chavan Memorial (YCM) Hospital in Pimpri-Chinchwad, following which stocks worth approximately ₹1.72 crore were seized on November 4. Other irregularities included discrepancies in manufacturing and expiry dates, inadequate laboratory testing procedures, unhygienic manufacturing conditions and improper storage of finished products. Risk to patients A show-cause notice was issued to the firm on October 29, following which it submitted a written response on November 3. A personal hearing was conducted on November 23. The licensing authority rejected the firm’s contention that no patient complaints had been received, observing that the risk of treatment failure arising from spurious and substandard drugs existed even in the absence of complaints. “Ensuring that citizens have access to safe, quality and efficacious drugs is the foremost responsibility of the Food and Drug Administration. Stringent regulatory and legal action will be taken against any manufacturer who plays with the health of the general public by manufacturing drugs without product permission,” FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe said.

headline: India condemns Riyadh tower attack that injured 2 Indians, calls for end to strikes
content: India has strongly condemned the Houthi attack in Saudi Arabia's Riyadh, which injured at least two Indians. In a statement on Wednesday, the ministry of external affairs called for an immediate cessation of strikes.“We also reiterate our firm solidarity with the people and Government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and reaffirm our unwavering support to the Kingdom in safeguarding its sovereignty, territorial integrity, and the security and safety of its citizens and residents. We earnestly hope that peace and normalcy will return to the region at the earliest,” the statement added further. Also Read | IndiGo cancels flights to Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam, Madinah till November 30 At least 11 people, including two Indians, were injured when a tower in Riyadh’s financial district was targeted on Tuesday, according to Saudi authorities.The injured included two Saudi nationals, two Indians, three Nepalese nationals and four Egyptians, Saudi Civil Defence said. The authorities described the incident as a terrorist attack by Yemen’s Houthi group.The November 24 attack was the second reported strike on a tower in Riyadh’s financial district in less than a week. An earlier attack on November 19 had caused material damage to a tower and nearby buildings, but no injuries were reported.Following the attack in Riyadh's financial district, the Yemeni militant group said it would target the port of Jeddah and all other Saudi ports on the Red Sea coast if Saudi Arabia carried out threats to attack the Yemeni port of Hodeidah.This latest exchange marks a further escalation in the confrontation between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia, with attacks increasingly targeting strategic infrastructure on both sides.

headline: Arrangements in place for Mission Chakkakompan; Kerala Forest dept to tranquilize wild tusker
content: IDUKKI As the Forest Department and district administration completed arrangements on Tuesday to tranquilize and fit a radio collar to Chakkakompan at Chinnakkanal in the Devikulam forest range on Wednesday, officials said they are also planning to fit a radio collar to Murivali, another “problematic” wild elephant in the area. District Collector has issued prohibitory orders in several wards of the Chinnakkanal panchayat ahead of the operation, officials said. According to Chief Conservator of Forests D.K. Vinod Kumar, the mission is expected to take place on Wednesday once the elephant approaches Vilakku in Chinnakkanal. “Officials have been directed to identify additional spots in the area to conduct the operation,” Mr. Kumar said. “After the mission, the team will remain in Chinnakkanal for two more days as it plans to attach a radio collar to Murivali, another problematic female elephant. A proposal to dart Murivali will be submitted to the Chief Wildlife Warden. The animal is currently in Mathikettan Shola and needs to move toward Chinnakkanal before we can conduct the operation.” Two high-quality radio collars were sourced from abroad, he said. Mr. Kumar noted that a study by a Professor at the Wildlife Institute of India found that wild elephants’ aggressive behaviour decreases after they are fitted with radio collars. Elephants are now getting aggressive, increasing human–elephant conflicts. Wild elephants in Chinnakkanal have reached an aggressive level, said Mr. Kumar. Threat assessment He added that installing the radio collar is the first step, and if the animal continues to pose a threat, the Forest department will take further action to translocate it from the Chinnakkanal region. Two kumkis (trained elephants) named Vikram and Bharat have arrived in Chinnakkanal to assist with the operation, officials said. On Tuesday, the Forest department conducted a mock drill at Cement Palam, near Chinnakkanal, ahead of Mission Chakkakompan. Munnar Divisional Forest Officer Saju Varghese led the drill, which included an expert team, veterinary doctors and Rapid Response Team members. As part of Mission Chakkakompan, the District Collector declared a holiday on Wednesday for schools, tuition centers and anganwadis in wards 1, 2, 9, 10, 11 and 12 of the Chinnakkanal panchayat. The Collector also banned night camps and campfires in those wards on Wednesday. According to officials, the mission is expected to begin from 6 a.m. onwards. Two Kumki elephants, along with a 100-member team, will lead the operation. Five veterinary doctors and a 15-member tracking team are also part of the group. The tusker was camped in the 80-acre area until Tuesday evening, when it started moving toward the 301 Colony area. Officials expect to bring the animal to an open space near Cement Palam. An official said that mission-related equipment has been stored at Chinnakkanal Fathima Matha School, with two sets of each piece of equipment kept as a backup for the mission..

headline: ‘Everyone ready to work under him’: JD(U) leader Sanjay Jha asks Nishant Kumar to take charge
content: Janata Dal (United), or JD(U), leader Sanjay Jha has called on Bihar minister Nishant Kumar to take charge of the party and said everyone is ready to work under him, regardless of their position in the party. He made the comments on Tuesday as the JD(U) celebrated “Good Governance Day” to mark Bihar’s turnaround under Kumar’s father, Rajya Sabha member Nitish Kumar, who stepped down as the chief minister after almost 20 years at the helm. Nitish Kumar, the JD(U) national president, was present at the eventJha noted that the expectations from Nishant Kumar will be higher than what was expected from Nitish Kumar. “He [Nishant Kumar] will carry the burden of being compared with his father.”Nishant Kumar said he would follow in his father’s footsteps and, like him, “never compromise with crime, corruption and communalism”. Nishant Kumar paid tribute to his father, calling him a trend-setter whose visionary leadership took Bihar to new heights.Nishant Kumar joined the JD(U) in March. He was inducted into the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led National Democratic Alliance government two months later.Nishant Kumar said his father’s strong willpower and unwavering commitment to development gave Bihar’s politics and governance a new direction, helping it emerge from an era of fear, anarchy and disorder to establish new benchmarks for the rule of law, social justice, good governance and development.Bihar minister and JD(U) leader Zama Khan said that the party was confident of doing well under Nishant Kumar, who would draw inspiration from his father and carry forward his legacy.JD(U) leader Shyam Rajak said that Nishant Kumar had proven himself as an able administrator in his short stint as a health minister and also has a mass connect with workers. “He is a youth leader, and in coming days, he is definitely going to steer the party. This is a matter of happiness for us. Of course, Nitish is our leader and our future leader is Nishant,” said Rajak.BJP state spokesperson Prem Ranjan Patel said Nishant Kumar can steer the party and has the same agility, conviction and patience like his father. “ The party would certainly get strengthened once Nishant comes to the forefront as the new face. He has many qualities...maintains poise and calm like his father. Nishant being the son of Nitish is an obvious choice to take forward the legacy of his father,” Patel said.The opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal described the efforts to promote Nishant Kumar as an attempt to keep the JD(U) intact amid infighting. “Infighting among top leaders in the party is very intense, and this is why Nishant is being promoted by one section of leaders, perhaps to have more clout in the party,” said RJD leader Chittaranjan Gagan. “It would be better if JD(U) leaders pitch for elevation of Nishant as chief minister.”

headline: Karnataka HC lets cops probe BJP MLA in Form 7 case but protects him from arrest
content: The Karnataka High Court on Tuesday permitted police to continue investigating allegations of fraudulent voter deletion applications against Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) legislator C.K. Ramamurthy and three others, while directing investigators to seek the court’s permission before making arrests or filing a chargesheet.Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde passed the interim order while hearing a petition filed by Ramamurthy, Ramakrishna, Ravikumar V., and Yogesh D.R. seeking to quash an FIR registered by the Suddaguntepalya police. The four are accused of misusing Form 7—used to object to the inclusion of a name or seek its deletion from the electoral roll—to remove six members of a family from the voter list.“Under these circumstances, the prayer for stay of the proceedings is not granted at this juncture. The petitioners shall cooperate with the investigation. The respondent State shall not arrest the petitioners, and a chargesheet shall not be filed without the leave of the court,” the court said.The order followed an assurance by additional public prosecutor Anoop Kumar that the police would not arrest the petitioners if they cooperated with the investigation.The case was registered on a complaint by Tehraan Ali Khan, a BTM Layout resident, who alleged that Form-7 applications had been filed to remove his name and those of five family members from the electoral roll. He said the family had lived in Old Gurappanapalya for nearly five decades.According to the complaint, Khan approached Ramakrishna after discovering the Form 7 applications to seek their removal from the voter list. Ramakrishna allegedly told him that he signed a Form-7 application that a person identified as Ravi gave him at the MLA’s office. During a subsequent conference call, the MLA, Ramamurthy, allegedly acknowledged the submission and assured Khan that the applications would be withdrawn and the errors corrected.To be sure, the original FIR, registered on October 7, did not name Ramamurthy. The police later added his name as an accused after securing permission from the jurisdictional court.In their petition before the high court, the petitioners argued that Form 7 falls under the jurisdiction of electoral registration authorities under the Registration of Electors Rules, and the police could not assume the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) powers to decide which objection was justified.The high court, which will take up the case next on January 8, has told the petitioners to serve a copy of the petition on ECI’s standing counsel.The case is part of a series of police complaints over alleged irregularities in Form-7 submissions during the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in Karnataka.Former Congress MLA Sowmya Reddy, who lost the Jayanagar seat to Ramamurthy in the state elections, also filed a police complaint alleging that 5,698 applications seeking deletion of names were filed in the constituency, including 4,327 related to the Gurrappanapalya ward.On November 17, the high court stayed investigations in three FIRs involving 10 people accused of submitting fraudulent Form-7 applications. In those proceedings, the court referred to the role of electoral registration authorities in determining the validity of the applications. “The finding of the Registration Officer may furnish materials to take a call whether the case is made out to quash the FIR or to direct the investigation into all or any of the offences,” the court said in these cases.

headline: Fawad Khan’s Netflix Series Sparks Row: AICWA Demands Permanent Ban On Pakistani Content | News18
content: A fresh entertainment and diplomatic controversy is brewing ahead of Netflix’s scheduled December 4 premiere of Pakistani series Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo. The All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, demanding that the series not be released or streamed in India.In a letter dated November 24, AICWA president Suresh Shyamlal Gupta urged the government to intervene and prevent the show from reaching Indian audiences. The association has also called for a permanent law with strict penalties barring Pakistani content and artists from Indian OTT platforms, television channels and cinema halls.AICWA has cited the restrictions imposed on Pakistani artists after the 2019 Pulwama attack and referred to the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting’s May 8, 2025 advisory asking streaming platforms in India to stop carrying Pakistan-origin content. The association argues that the proposed Netflix release should be covered by those restrictions. n18oc_BreakingNewsn18oc_IndiaCNN-News18 is your trusted source for breaking news, updates, and in-depth analysis from around the world. headline: Assam Police Gets Smart Response Force: 65 Commandos, Including 13 Women, For Urban And Jungle Operations
content: Assam Police has added a specialised force to its operational capabilities, with Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma launching two Smart Response Units comprising 65 commandos, including 13 women. The two wings – the Urban Intervention Unit and the Jungle Intervention Unit – have been set up under the Lachit Barphukan Police Academy in Dergaon to strengthen the force’s ability to respond to emergencies, complex security situations and challenging operations. The units were formally launched on Tuesday, November 24, during the Chief Minister’s visit to the academy for the passing-out parade on Lachit Divas, which marks the birth anniversary of Ahom commander Lachit Barphukan. How Were The 65 Assam Police Commandos Selected And Trained? According to CM Himanta Biswa Sarma, the commandos were selected through voluntary participation. Around 160 police personnel underwent a month-long selection process in 2025, after which the shortlisted candidates received nearly a year of specialised training. The 65-member force comprises 52 men and 13 women. The commandos have been equipped with modern weapons and specialised operational equipment, with facilities for advanced operations, including underwater capabilities. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Office of Himanta Biswa Sarma (@officeofhbs) Their training covered command, control, communication, computer applications, information management and coordination among different forces, as reported by The Times of India. These capabilities are intended to help personnel respond more effectively to situations that require quick decisions, reliable communication and coordinated action. CM Sarma said the specialised units would improve Assam Police’s preparedness for emerging security threats and complex situations. He also directed Director General of Police Harmeet Singh to arrange a demonstration of their capabilities during the forthcoming Republic Day parade. Urban And Jungle Intervention Units: Why Does Assam Police Need Them? The two wings are designed around different operational environments. The Urban Intervention Unit is intended to strengthen police response in built-up areas, where emergencies can involve crowded locations, confined spaces and rapidly changing situations. The Jungle Intervention Unit is meant to address operational challenges in forested and difficult terrain. Assam’s varied geography, which includes urban centres, hills, forests and riverine areas, requires police personnel to be prepared for different kinds of emergencies and security operations. Peace through Strength! https://t.co/cjTZSTOZRO — Himanta Biswa Sarma (@himantabiswa) November 24, 2026 Having specially selected and trained teams can allow the police to deploy personnel with relevant skills and equipment instead of relying only on regular police units for every complex situation. The emphasis on communication, information management and coordination is also significant: effective intervention often depends not just on weapons or physical training, but on how quickly information reaches the teams involved and how different units work together. The launch is part of the broader effort to modernise Assam Police and improve its ability to deal with evolving law-and-order requirements. However, the units’ actual impact will depend on their deployment, coordination with district police and other security agencies, and their performance during real operations. Assam Police Adds 1,653 Constables And Eight Communication Sub-Inspectors The launch of the Smart Response Unit coincided with the passing-out parade of 1,653 Unarmed Branch (UB) constables and eight Sub-Inspectors from the Communication Branch at the Lachit Barphukan Police Academy. Of the 1,653 constables, 1,179 are men and 474 are women. The recruits underwent training in areas including law, tactical skills and citizen-friendly policing. CM Sarma said the eight newly trained Communication Branch sub-inspectors would strengthen emergency response and coordination across police units. Reliable communication networks are essential for sharing information, coordinating personnel and ensuring that police teams can respond quickly during critical situations. The addition of the specialised intervention wings, along with the newly trained personnel, marks another step in Assam Police’s efforts to build a force equipped to handle both routine policing and more demanding security challenges.

headline: Opinion | Dev Deepawali: A grand confluence of faith, heritage and economy | Hindustan Times
content: Prof. Sanjay Sinha, Dean, Skill Faculty of Management Studies and Research, Shri Vishwakarma Skill University.On Kartik Purnima, the eternal city of Kashi, situated on the banks of Mokshadayini Maa Ganga, is once again set to witness the extraordinary and magnificent spectacle described in our Puranas and scriptures as Dev Deepawali. It is believed that on Kartik Purnima, deities descend from heaven to celebrate Deepawali on the ghats of Kashi. When eleven lakh earthen diyas shimmer together on the crescent-shaped ghats of Kashi, the city of Lord Shiva, it will appear as though the entire galaxy has descended onto the earth. This galaxy is the visual manifestation of CM Yogi's vision, in which he views Sanatan faith as a form of cultural pride and consciousness. This very vision makes religious heritage a strong foundation for the local economy and livelihoods through spiritual tourism. Yogi government's policy of linking 'economy with faith' has ensured that every diya lit in Kashi, with its positive energy and selfless light, illuminates the homes and courtyards of even those standing at the last rung of society, bringing happiness and economic prosperity.Rivers have been life-giving for centuries. Cities situated along the Ganga bear witness to this truth. During the Kumbh and Magh Melas in Prayagraj, boatmen, pilgrimage priests and artisans earn enough to sustain themselves throughout the year. In Kashi, diyas on the ghats keep the potter's hearth burning, while boats sustain boatmen's families. The realistic form of 'development along with heritage' presented by the UP government under the leadership of CM Yogi manifests in Kashi's Dev Deepawali. This festival symbolizes that our festivals, celebrations and cultural heritage are the foundation of a strong economy. This can be described as 'livelihood along the Ganga' or a Ganga-based economy.We need to think deeply about how many people receive direct and indirect employment when eleven lakh diyas are lit on the ghats of Kashi. When the state government gives this event a grand, global scale, it indirectly ensures the livelihoods of potters, farmers who extract oil, elderly women who spin cotton, and farmers who grow flowers. The concept of 'livelihood along Ganga' remains completely incomplete without the Nishad and Mallah communities of Kashi. For these boatmen, who earn their livelihood by rowing their boats on the waves of the Ganga, Dev Deepawali is no less than a divine blessing. The unprecedented promotion of tourism by the Yogi government, a safe environment, and the new, grand form of Kashi Vishwanath Dham have led to a historic increase in the number of tourists visiting Kashi today, and the most direct and transparent beneficiaries are these boatmen. On Dev Deepawali, when lakhs of tourists from across the country and the world board bajras, boats and cruises to witness the splendor of ghats, that day will be the biggest earning day of the year for these boatmen. From ordinary bajras and small boats to state-of-the-art ro-ro boats and Alaknanda cruise, everything has been booked weeks in advance. This income paves the way for their children's education, healthcare, and a better standard of living. This is the practical aspect of Yogi government's good governance and cultural nationalism, which advocates the harmonious integration of religion and economics.The grand illumination of Dev Deepawali also lights up Kashi's service and hospitality sector. All small and large hotels, guest houses, dharamshalas and homestays in Banaras and its surrounding areas are completely occupied by tourists. This tourism boom puts money directly into the pockets of everyone, from big industrialists and capitalists to e-rickshaw drivers, auto drivers, taxi operators, tour guides and small shopkeepers selling Banarasi chaat-pakodas and tea in kulhads along the roadside. From Banarasi paan shops to the weavers of world-famous Banarasi sarees, everyone is directly benefiting from the economic wave generated by this festival. When foreign and domestic tourists explore the narrow but colorful lanes of Kashi, they also shop extensively for handloom products, Gulabi Meenakari, wooden toys, and other handicrafts. The Yogi government's visionary schemes, such as 'One District One Product' (ODOP), have already provided these local artisans with a large, organized market, and events such as Dev Deepawali act as catalysts for demand in this market. This prevents migration and creates a strong framework for self-reliance at the local level.When the eleven lakh diyas lit in Kashi on Kartik Purnima rise with their flames, they will not merely dispel darkness. Still, they will also narrate the story of UP's reconstruction, which aspires to touch the skies of modernity while remaining connected to its ancient roots. Over the past few years, we have seen how the state government has given global branding to Ayodhya's Deepotsav, Mathura-Vrindavan's Rangotsav and Kashi's Dev Deepawali. Yogi Adityanath government has clearly understood that India's soul resides in religion and spirituality. It was necessary to connect this soul with modern infrastructure, excellent connectivity, law and order, and good governance. This is why opportunities for employment and development have emerged that are more sustainable, inclusive and people-centric than any established Western economic model.Every single diya lit on the banks of the Ganga shines as proof that, when the vision is right, religion enriches life and also improves the present circumstances of the poorest person in society. When this endless series of diyas is illuminated on the ghats of the Ganga in Kashi, it will reflect not only the blessings of the deities but also the radiance on the faces of lakhs of workers, boatmen, weavers and artisans. The light of Dev Deepawali is the sunrise of a sustainable future for a self-reliant state, whose rays will rise from the waves of the Ganga and illuminate every section of society.Disclaimer: The views and opinions expressed by the author are solely their own and do not reflect the official position or views of Hindustan Times.

headline: What turtle survey says about Olive Ridley nesting, Leatherback presence in Nicobar
content: Olive Ridley turtles were the most widespread marine turtle species on India’s mainland coastline, with over 18,000 solitary nests counted in 2024-25, followed by Leatherback, Green, and Hawksbill turtles, a pan-India multi-season assessment of population trends by the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) revealed. The assessment also recorded 643 Leatherback turtle nests at Galathea Bay on Great Nicobar Island in 2023-24, followed by 478 in 2024-25. The bay is also the proposed site of a transhipment port under the Rs 92,000-crore Great Nicobar Island (GNI) mega project. Significantly, during a challenge against the project before the National Green Tribunal, the Centre submitted that the port project did not fall in the Island Coastal Regulation Zone – IA (ICRZ-IA), where ports are prohibited and the zone is accorded the highest coastal protection. Turtle nesting is one among many reasons why it is accorded this protection. The Andaman and Nicobar Forest Department’s November 2025–March 2026 turtle nesting data for Great Nicobar Island, seen by The Indian Express, revealed that 889 Leatherback turtle nests and 108 Olive Ridley nests were recorded at the Galathea Beach site. The Union Environment Ministry and WII report also found monitoring gaps, such as poor data collection from remote parts of the Lakshadweep Islands and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and underestimation of predation on turtle nests. It called for more on-site protection of turtle eggs rather than focussing solely on hatcheries, where they are relocated and also recommended flipper tagging for turtle tracking. The population assessment is not based on a direct count of marine turtles, which is practically difficult. WII relied on the nest-counting method, combining a literature review with field assessments and beach-specific nesting records maintained by state forest departments. Based on this data, for the period December 2022 to May 2025, researchers calculated the approximate number of female turtles nesting. Counting the turtles During the assessment, researchers documented marine turtle nesting numbers across 360 beach stretches in India, over 1,300 km. It covered beaches across Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Kerala, and Lakshadweep on the West Coast, and in Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, and West Bengal on the East Coast. “We have tried to assess the scale of nesting in the country for effective conservation and management interventions. Solitary nests are confirmed nesting evidence, and we have pulled data from each state,” said R Suresh Kumar, Scientist, WII, and project investigator. The report estimates that approximately 8,000 individual solitary-nesting Olive Ridley turtles nested along mainland India in 2024-25, based on an average of 2.5 clutches per female. A female Olive Ridley turtle lays eggs multiple times or ‘clutches’ and can lay 100-110 eggs in one clutch. Olive Ridley turtle numbers declined in Gujarat, attributed to the closure of river mouths and disruption of the natural formation of sandy beaches preferred by female turtles. Olive Ridley turtles were present on at least 300 of these stretches, with the highest solitary nests – 18,713 – recorded in the 2024-25 season. The nesting season typically begins in late October and ends in March. Green Turtles were largely found in Gujarat, and the rest were recorded in Lakshadweep Island and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Leatherback turtle nesting was concentrated entirely along the coasts of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. In fact, one hatchery at Galathea Bay – where turtle eggs are relocated for protection - had 626 nests in 2023-24, which included 603 Leatherback and 23 Olive Ridley, setting the highest record for any hatchery in India. While the assessment report identified the bay as a critical Leatherback nesting habitat, it did not dwell on the potential impact of the proposed transhipment report on this nesting site. Meanwhile, the Hawksbill turtle was sparsely distributed across Lakshadweep Island and Andaman and Nicobar Islands. GNI project impact Responding to a query on why the report has not accounted for the GNI project’s impact, WII Director Gobind Sagar Bharadwaj said, “The scope of the report was to identify key nesting areas, compile the status of sea turtle nesting through rapid assessments, and compile nesting and hatchery data collected by the forest department and other stakeholders. Hence, the potential impacts of the upcoming port are not evaluated in this report.” “Further, the report has provided the status of Leatherback turtle nesting in key nesting sites including the Galathea Bay and highlighted the importance of protecting the identified key nesting beaches for preserving the natural nesting habitats,” Bharadwaj said. He added that, as part of monitoring the species, a research team is tracking it year-round at the Galathea Bay site, and a satellite-tagging exercise has been initiated to assess movement patterns. The environmental clearance granted by the Union Environment Ministry for the transhipment report in November 2022 had clearly directed the project proponent that Pemayya Bay and all other Leatherback nesting sites on the western parts of GNI must remain no-development zones, as these sites are likely to be used by Leatherback Sea Turtles as alternate sites due to the impact of the International Container Transshipment Port (ICTT) at Galathea Bay. It had also directed protection of nesting beaches at Pemayya Bay, Dagmar, Alexandria Bay, and Casuarina Bay. River mouths favoured The assessments revealed insights into the conditions favoured for nesting sites, as well as data on stretches that saw high-intensity nesting. The WII report stated that ideal nesting conditions for Olive Ridley turtles were found near river mouths. Beaches near river mouths show reduced microbial load in sand, more nourishment and cyclic erosion. These factors create a favourable environment for egg development. The Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri on the east coast all drain into the Bay of Bengal, creating nourishing conditions on the shore for turtle nesting. The east coast also had a higher average emergence success rate for hatchlings at 81.5 per cent, exceeding the 64.5 per cent success noted on the west coast.

headline: Can BJP-SAD Reunion Bring Punjab Back On Track? Harbhajan Singh Says Centre-State Alignment Key To Growth
content: With the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) officially reviving their partnership ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, the political mood in Chandigarh and New Delhi has shifted sharply. For years, voters in the state have watched rival parties trade promises while debating Punjab’s stalled momentum. In an exclusive conversation with CNN-News18, Member of Parliament Harbhajan Singh shared his thoughts on the reunion between the two long-time allies, explaining why alignment between New Delhi and Chandigarh matters and outlining the coalition’s priorities once it takes office. For Singh, the revival of the alliance isn’t just a tactical move ahead of the 2027 polls; it is a rare opportunity to break a pattern that he believes has held Punjab back. Pointing to the gap between big campaign rhetoric and actual results on the ground, he argued that voters are ready to judge parties on delivery rather than slogans. “I am very happy that we have come together to contest this election and, hopefully, form the government as well. There is a lot of work to be done in Punjab. Several promises have been made by different political parties, but if you look at their performance, very little has actually been delivered.” The argument is anchored in a central pitch: governance moves with less friction when the same political alignment leads both the state and the Centre. In Singh’s view, Punjab has missed out on that dynamic. “People need to understand that when the government at the Centre and the state is the same, development can happen much faster. Unfortunately, Punjab has not had that opportunity so far. But now there is a new opportunity, and we are looking at this election as a chance to work towards the betterment of Punjab, a state that has been left behind in many areas,” said Singh. Keeping Youth and Ground Realities at the Centre Speaking about the issues the incoming government would tackle first, Singh pointed to concerns that directly affect households: drugs, sports culture, basic infrastructure and employment. Behind each of these priorities is a simpler goal: giving young Punjabis real reasons to stay and build careers at home instead of looking elsewhere for a livelihood. “I am very happy that this alliance has come together with the larger interest of Punjab in mind. Once we form the government, our focus will be on addressing the drug menace, promoting sports, improving infrastructure and creating employment opportunities for the youth. We want to create an environment where the young people of Punjab can build their future in their own state instead of having to move elsewhere for opportunities,” he added. After six years apart following their 2020 split over the farm laws, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) have formally revived their historic alliance ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. The reunion was announced on the auspicious occasion of Guru Nanak Jayanti in the presence of Union Home Minister Amit Shah, BJP president Nitin Nabin and SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal. The cricketer also sought to energise party cadres on both sides, describing the renewed partnership as a collective push towards Punjab’s future. “This is great news for Punjab. Congratulations to everyone, our party workers and all the workers from our alliance. Let’s make this alliance work and work together for the future of Punjab,” Singh said.

headline: 'Are We Beggars?' Imran Masood Sees Red As SP Stakes Claim To Saharanpur Amid UP Alliance Talks
content: The Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress may be projecting a united front ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, but the negotiations over seat-sharing are increasingly exposing the faultlines within the INDIA bloc in the state. The latest flashpoint has come from western Uttar Pradesh, where Congress MP and state working president Imran Masood has made it clear that he is unwilling to accept what he sees as a unilateral approach by alliance partner Akhilesh Yadav. “I don’t understand it. It’s beyond my understanding. Are we beggars? Will you treat us like this — that we aren’t even asking you for seats and you declared 26 seats? We didn’t even demand seats from you. So if this is your way of working, that you will dictate terms, then a self-respecting person like me does not understand these things,” Masood said, reacting to the SP’s decision to announce its first list of candidates while seat-sharing discussions were still underway. Masood’s objection, however, is not limited to the larger question of how many seats Congress will get. Sources in the Congress say Masood is particularly upset with the SP’s decision to announce candidates for Behat and Saharanpur, two constituencies in his home district where he wants Congress to field its nominees. ALSO READ | Akhilesh Establishes Who Is The Boss: Declares 5 Seats, Posts ‘Congress Must Show Winnability’ Sources told CNN-News18 that Masood is understood to be insisting that Congress contest both seats, arguing that the SP’s unilateral announcement does not uphold the principles of coalition politics. He is currently in touch with the Congress high command and is awaiting its response before deciding on his next move. Sources say he intends to make his position public after hearing from the leadership. The timing is significant. These are the same constituencies in the Saharanpur region that have featured prominently in Congress’s electoral calculations, with Rahul Gandhi expected to kick-start the party’s Uttar Pradesh campaign from Saharanpur in December. The question, therefore, is whether Congress can afford a public confrontation with its principal opposition ally just as it prepares to launch its campaign in the state. Akhilesh’s Message: Winnability Over Numbers The immediate trigger for the latest friction was the SP’s announcement of five candidates for the 2027 assembly elections on Tuesday night. The party named Umar Ali Khan from Behat, Ashu Malik from Saharanpur, Nahid Hasan from Kairana, Mehboob Ali from Amroha and Jyoti Lodhi from Lalitpur. ALSO READ | Insult Over Injury? Congress Sees Red As SP’s 26-Seat Offer For UP Polls Includes Just 1 In Amethi-Raebareli The announcement came hours after the second round of seat-sharing discussions between the two parties ended without an agreement. The SP has proposed 26 seats for Congress in the 403-member assembly, while Congress has been negotiating for a substantially larger share. The party had initially put forward a list of 181 constituencies, which was subsequently reduced to around 130-131 during the discussions. SP general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav has sought to justify the 26-seat proposal by pointing to the parties’ previous electoral performances. According to him, the offer includes two constituencies won by Congress in the previous assembly election, four where it finished second and 20 others where the SP believes Congress has a weaker electoral presence. Akhilesh Yadav, meanwhile, has repeatedly emphasised that the alliance should be guided by the winnability of candidates rather than simply the number of seats each party wants. In a post on X after the discussions, he said the first 26 seats were a beginning and that the two parties should identify other potential constituencies before jointly assessing their electoral prospects. इस बार एक ऐतिहासिक अवसर है जब हम दोनों पंथनिरपेक्ष पार्टियां मिलकर साम्प्रदायिक भाजपा और उनके संकीर्ण सोच के साथियों को हमेशा के लिए हराकर, देश को गलत हाथों में जाकर बर्बाद होने से बचा सकते हैं। हम चाहते हैं कि आप और हम जन-अपेक्षाओं व वास्तविकताओं को समझकर गंभीर विचार-विमर्श करें जिससे अधिकांश सीटों पर अपने ‘गठबंधन’ की जीत सुनिश्चित हो। जितनी सीटें आप-हम लड़ें उनमें हमारी जीत की सीटें, न जीत पाने वाली सीटों से अधिक हों। जीत ही बंटवारे को सम्मानजनक बनाएगी क्योंकि जीती हुई सीट ही सम्मान दिलाएगी। अतः आपकी टीम की तरफ़ से प्राथमिकता के आधार पर दी गई सीटों में से जिन 26 सीटों पर आज बात हो गई है, उनके अतिरिक्त अन्य सभी संभावित सीटें चिह्नित करके हमें भेज दें। फिर मिल बैठकर देखेंगे कि कौन सी सीट और उस पर कौन सा कैंडिडेट जीतने की पोजिशन में है। हो सकता है कि हम अपने आँकलन और जीत के गणितीय समीकरण के आधार पर कांग्रेस को ऐसी कई जीतनेवाली सीटों के बारे में भी बताएं जिन पर उन्होंने किसी कारणवश विचार ही नहीं किया है। हमारी कोशिश तो ये है कि जब बड़े नेता बैठें तो सभी सीटों पर ‘इंडिया गठबंधन’ के प्रत्याशी के रूप में बात हो, न कि कांग्रेस या सपा के प्रत्याशी के रूप में और सबसे अच्छी और सकारात्मक परिणाम देनेवाली बात तो ये होगी कि हम लोग अपने प्रत्याशी को ‘पीडीए प्रत्याशी’ के रूप में प्रस्तुत करें। जिस प्रकार लोकसभा में आपके संगठन ने ‘पीडीए’ के साथ पूरी तरह सहयोग किया वो सदैव सराहनीय रहेगा क्योंकि उसने ही मिलकर साम्प्रदायिक भाजपा को धूल चटाई थी अब इस बार भी हम लोग मिलकर उप्र में और फिर केंद्र में भी भाजपा को हराएंगे। ज़मीनी सर्वेक्षणों से ये बात साफ़ हो गई है कि हर शहर, मोहल्ले, गली व गाँव तक ये बात पहुँच गई है कि जो पीड़ित है, वो पीडीए है। इसीलिए पूरे प्रदेश के हर समाज, हर वर्ग के ‘पीड़ित, दुखी, अपमानित’ भाजपा के ख़िलाफ़ लामबंद हो गये हैं क्योंकि उन सबको ये विश्वास है कि ‘PDA ही NDA को हराएगा’ और पीडीए ही परिवर्तन लायेगा। सच तो ये है कि हम नहीं चाहते हैं कि सीट का बँटवारा हमारे-तुम्हारे के भाव से हो, हम तो इसे बंटवारा नहीं, ‘सीट समायोजन’ कहना चाहते हैं। कठिन समीकरणवाली सीटों पर हम मिलकर कम-से-कम दो प्रत्याशियों पर विचार-विमर्श करके जिसकी अधिक संभावना दिखेगी उसे चुनकर मिलजुल के जिताएंगे। हम नहीं चाहते हैं कि गठबंधन में एक-दूसरे पर उम्मीदवार थोपे जाएं बल्कि सहमति से तय किये जाएं, तब ही आपके-हमारे वोट आपस में ट्रांसफ़र होकर हम लोगों की जीत को सुनिश्चित करेंगे और कल को हम मिलकर कह सकेंगे कि हम लोगों ने तो पहले ही कहा था : बात सीट की नहीं, जीत की है। आपका-हमारा सबसे बड़ा लक्ष्य सरकार बनाना है। नये हालातों और समीकरण में उसके लिए हमें-आपको कुछ लोगों को एडजस्ट और एकमोडेट करना पड़ेगा। एक-दो लोग ऐसे भी होंगे जिनसे आपने और हमने चुनाव लड़ाने का वादा किया होगा लेकिन वास्तविक परिस्थितियों को देखते हुए दो-चार सीटों पर बदलाव भी करने पड़ेंगे। भावी प्रत्याशियों को भी ये समझना होगा कि हर सीट महत्वपूर्ण है, अगर किसी को सीट नहीं मिल पा रही है या मनचाही सीट नहीं मिल रही है तो निराश न हों, अगर उनके दल के बड़े नेता ने कुछ फेरबदल या बदलाव किया है तो उसके पीछे सोच सरकार बनाने की है और सरकार बन गई तो सबको सम्मान-स्थान मिल जाएगा। हर बड़ा नेता अपनी बात का मान ख़ुद रखेगा, इतना विश्वास तो अपने नेताओं पर लोगों को रखना ही पड़ेगा। इस तरह जो चुनाव लड़ा जाएगा उसमें आपका-हमारा संगठन मिलकर कहेगा कि हम दोनों के मिलने से हमारी तैयारी 806 सीटों के बराबर की है। देश की जनता ख़ासतौर से किसान, मजदूर, युवा, मध्यम वर्ग, महिलाएँ, छोटे से लेकर बड़ा व्यापारी, सच्चे अधिकारी, कर्मचारी और संपूर्ण प्रगतिशील-पंथनिरपेक्ष व उत्पीड़ित ‘पीडीए समाज’ आपकी और हमारी तरफ़ बड़ी उम्मीद से देख रहा है। आपसी समायोजन से कोई भूल किये बिना हम देश का नया इतिहास लिखने के कगार पर हैं। हम सौहार्द और सूझबूझ से ये कर भी दिखाएंगे, इसी आशा के साथ आप-हम ‘सीट की जगह जीत के समीकरण’ पर विचार करें, जिससे हम जीतें और उप्र में अपनी सरकार आए और फिर दिल्ली में भी और देश का भविष्य सँवारने में हम लोगों का योगदान हमेशा के लिए सुनहरे अक्षरों में दर्ज हो जाए। — Akhilesh Yadav (@yadavakhilesh) November 24, 2026 His message was accompanied by an appeal to Congress to identify more seats and candidates who could win, suggesting that the 26-seat proposal need not necessarily be the final word. However, another social media development has offered a glimpse into where the SP leadership may be drawing its boundaries. Yadav reposted a post by journalist Saba Naqvi, who argued that Congress should settle for around 50-60 seats, given its limited organisational structure and candidate strength in Uttar Pradesh. Naqvi suggested that the party should first discuss candidates with the SP or have the state unit identify winnable nominees who could contest on the Congress symbol. The repost is significant because it appears to endorse an argument for keeping Congress’s share within a relatively limited range, even if there is room for the initial offer of 26 seats to be expanded. In other words, while the SP may be open to discussing more constituencies, it is unlikely to accept Congress’s demand for a much larger share simply on the basis of its national political standing. Why Saharanpur Has Become A Flashpoint For Imran Masood, the dispute is also about political space and the standing of Congress in a region where the party has a significant stake. Masood represents Saharanpur in the Lok Sabha and is also the working president of the Uttar Pradesh Congress. The party’s decision to project him in the state organisation was seen as an important move to strengthen its presence in western UP. Saharanpur is particularly important to Congress after its victory in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. The party is also looking to consolidate its support among Muslim and Dalit voters in the region. The SP’s decision to field Ashu Malik from Saharanpur and Umar Ali Khan from Behat, therefore, has landed at a particularly sensitive moment for Masood and the Congress organisation. There is also a local political dimension to the announcement. Ashu Malik, the SP’s candidate from Saharanpur, is a political rival of Masood. The Congress leadership had been looking at the Saharanpur region as an important starting point for its 2027 campaign. Rahul Gandhi is expected to address a major rally in Saharanpur around December 10 as part of the party’s ‘Mission UP’ preparations. The choice of location is not incidental as Congress wants to use the region to energise its organisation and consolidate its support base ahead of the assembly elections. But with the SP having already announced candidates in two constituencies that Congress was eyeing, the party faces an awkward situation even before Rahul’s campaign gets underway. Rahul’s Balancing Act Despite the growing differences, a breakdown of the alliance is not necessarily on the cards. The Congress high command is understood to be willing to show flexibility in the negotiations, with Rahul Gandhi keen that the opposition parties put up a united fight against the BJP in Uttar Pradesh. But the message from the Congress leadership is also that accommodation cannot come at the cost of the party’s dignity and its standing among workers. This could mean Congress eventually climbing down from its initial demand and accepting a considerably smaller share than the 100-plus seats it had been seeking, provided the final arrangement gives it enough politically meaningful constituencies and a say in candidate selection. That is also where the distinction between the SP’s public messaging and the actual negotiations becomes important. Akhilesh has repeatedly said that the alliance should focus on winning rather than the arithmetic of seat distribution. His repost of Naqvi’s argument about 50-60 seats reinforces the impression that the SP expects Congress to be realistic about its current organisational strength in Uttar Pradesh. Congress, on the other hand, believes that its performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections gives it a stronger claim than its Assembly record alone would suggest. The party also wants a respectable share of seats to reassure its workers and rebuild its organisation in the state. The two sides are, therefore, approaching the same alliance from different political calculations. The Bihar Shadow And The Road Ahead There is also a larger political calculation behind Congress’s insistence on a respectable seat-sharing arrangement. The party does not want to repeat the experience of Bihar, where its alliance negotiations and electoral performance became a subject of internal criticism. The SP, meanwhile, has made it clear that it does not intend to replicate a Bihar-style seat-sharing arrangement in Uttar Pradesh. It wants to assess each constituency individually and retain control over seats where it believes its candidates have a better chance of winning. The differences have been visible in the recent rounds of discussions, with the SP asking Congress to provide names of potential candidates and justify its claims on individual constituencies. The two parties are expected to hold further rounds of negotiations, with both sides publicly maintaining that an agreement is possible.

headline: ‘Will take Bangladesh by Dec 16’: Bengal minister’s controversial remark amid tensions over alleged Hindu killings
content: West Bengal minister Arjun Singh has claimed that the country would take over Bangladesh by December 16 and that the killings of Hindus in the neighbouring country would be "avenged".Speaking to reporters in Bhatpara, he made a controversial remark about Bangladesh on Tuesday, saying, "We will take Bangladesh by December 16th. Enough is enough; there are no more excuses regarding Bangladesh. We will certainly take revenge for the way Hindus have been killed in Bangladesh; there is no doubt about that."His remarks came amid tensions in Bangladesh, where the country's State Minister for Foreign Affairs, Humayun Kobir, earlier said that former Prime Minister and Awami League chief Sheikh Hasina would only be allowed to return to the country as a prisoner, in handcuffs and under strict surveillance. Kobir reportedly made the remarks while addressing journalists after briefing foreign diplomats at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Dhaka. Dismissing Hasina's reported plan to return to Bangladesh from India on December 16, coinciding with the country's Victory Day celebrations, he said, "Desire and reality are two different things.""The reality is that a terrorist will never be allowed to return except through extradition... She is not a regular commercial passenger. She can only be brought back in handcuffs and under strict surveillance," The Business Standard quoted Kobir as saying.Earlier, Hasina's spokesperson, Syed Mozammel Ali, had informed Reuters that the former Prime Minister intended to travel from Delhi to Dhaka on December 16 aboard Bangladesh's national carrier, Biman Bangladesh Airlines.In an official communication, Ali said that Hasina had sought arrangements from the Dhaka administration for her return journey. "Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka," Ali said, according to Reuters.Separately, Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam reportedly described Hasina's demand for a state aircraft to facilitate her return as "nothing but madness". Meanwhile, A Bangladeshi minister had informed Reuters on Sunday that Hasina faced immediate arrest and imprisonment if she returned, noting that no formal talks had taken place with India regarding the dispatch of a plane for her travel.Hasina, who led Bangladesh as prime minister from 2009 until 2024, arrived in India on August 5, 2024, in the wake of a student-led agitation over public sector job quotas that escalated into a nationwide uprising against her Awami League administration.She was later handed a death sentence in absentia by Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal over charges of crimes against humanity linked to the suppression of protesters, allegations that Hasina has denied.Hasina initially declared her wish to return to Bangladesh at a virtual media briefing in August this year and has repeated those plans during several subsequent interviews. Earlier this month, she also applied for a new passport and national identity card through legal representatives in the United Kingdom.Dhaka has made repeated requests to India for her extradition, while New Delhi has maintained that the matter is under examination.

headline: Hyderabad man, 23, leaves Rs 50 lakh Goldman Sachs job, takes 50% pay cut to build India's defence technology; why young professionals are choosing 'purpose' over pay
content: HYDERABAD: Born in a hostel dormitory at Hyderabad's BITS Pilani campus, Apollyon Dynamics has come a long way from its modest beginnings. The defence-tech startup, which made headlines with its big-ticket drone contracts with the Indian Army, is now attracting attention for a different reason: Its ability to draw some of the brightest young minds away from coveted corporate careers.In a job market where lucrative pay packages, global exposure and prestigious corporate brands often define career choices, a growing number of young professionals are choosing a rather unconventional path. They are walking away from well-paying jobs at global giants such as Goldman Sachs and turning down offers from established industry players such as ideaForge to join a relatively lesser-known startup - even if it means taking a substantial pay cut.For these young professionals, however, the attraction goes beyond salaries and corporate credentials. It is the opportunity to build something from the ground up, work on products with real-world applications and contribute directly to India's defence capabilities that makes Apollyon Dynamics an appealing destination.Speaking to TOI, several of the startup's young recruits said the desire to pursue meaningful work and make a tangible contribution to society was central to their decision to leave behind conventional corporate career paths.Young talent gives up big pay to chase defence technology dreamsAt Apollyon, they said, they have the opportunity to participate in the entire product development cycle, take ownership of projects and see their ideas evolve into tangible products. For 23-year-old Soham Kumar, the decision to leave Goldman Sachs and join a relatively young defence-tech venture was hardly an obvious one. "When I was first approached by Apollyon, the idea of moving from Goldman Sachs to a startup sounded ridiculous. But I came from Bengaluru to Hyderabad, observed the launch cycles closely and saw how everything works," he said.Kumar eventually took the plunge, accepting a 50% pay cut from his previous annual package of 50 lakh to join the startup. While he had worked as a quantitative analyst at Goldman Sachs, he now leads the autonomy function at Apollyon."I wanted to contribute tangibly to the country in the defence-tech sector. I am someone who feels work can't just be your day job; it has to consume your soul. Once I was clear about my decision, it was comparatively easy to convince my parents," he added. At 23, Kumar felt he had the flexibility to make such a career move, particularly because he did not have major financial responsibilities. For him, the opportunity to work closely on defence technology and witness the development of products first-hand outweighed the financial comfort of a high-paying corporate job.That sense of ownership and involvement is a recurring theme among the startup's young recruits. They believe that while larger organisations offer financial stability, brand recognition and structured career paths, the scale of operations can sometimes leave young employees with limited responsibilities and little exposure to the bigger picture. For 25-year-old Nidhip Sharma, these factors played a decisive role in choosing Apollyon over an established name in the drone industry.'Freelance work'Sharma turned down a pre-placement offer from ideaForge to join the startup. Having developed an interest in drones as early as Class 12, he had already gained considerable exposure to the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) industry and had even undertaken freelance work with the Indian Army."In big firms, one does not get any credit. Here, at Apollyon, I get to work in depth. I am involved in every stage, from start to finish. There are more responsibilities and recognition as well. Also, the smaller the company, the better the team and the faster the execution," he said. "I am going to continue in the UAV industry. However, while I want to get involved in all aspects of it now, I eventually plan to specialise in robotics and automation," he said. The opportunity to be closely involved in building products, rather than simply contributing to an established project, was also what prompted Bharat Ram to make the move.Having previously worked on a project with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), Ram chose to wrap up the assignment ahead of schedule and join Apollyon. His association with the startup, however, had begun much earlier, when he started contributing remotely while continuing with the ISRO project."I work on the design side at the startup. Even while working on the ISRO project, I used to work with Apollyon remotely and joined them full-time this May," said Ram, who now heads Project Jet UAV.Behind this growing talent pool is Apollyon's broader ambition to build a strong team capable of developing indigenous defence technologies. The company's co-founder, Jayant Khatri, said attracting young professionals from established organisations was an important part of that effort. headline: Akhilesh Yadav Adds Insult To Injury, Congress Fumes As BJP Takes Potshots
content: The Congress-Samajwadi Party (SP) seat-sharing talks appear to be heading into rough weather, with the SP going ahead and announcing five candidates for the upcoming elections even as negotiations with the Congress remain deadlocked. Sources have told NDTV that the SP's unilateral move has left Congress leaders fuming, with many seeing it as an insult added to injury. The SP had initially offered the Congress a mere 26 seats in response to its demand for over 100, after the party had already scaled down its original demand of 181 seats. Now, the announcement of five candidates in the middle of the negotiations has further angered Congress leaders in Uttar Pradesh, who are planning to take up the issue with the party high command. What has particularly upset the Congress is that four of the five candidates announced are from western Uttar Pradesh, including Saharanpur, the Lok Sabha constituency represented by Congress UP working president Imran Masood. The five candidates announced by the SP are Umar Ali from Behat, Aashu Malik from Saharanpur, Nahid Hasan from Kairana, Mahbub Ali from Amroha - all sitting MLAs from western UP - and Jyoti Lodi from Lalitpur in Jhansi. The four western UP constituencies have substantial Muslim and Dalit populations, a combination the Congress has been eyeing as part of its revival strategy. The Congress was reportedly eyeing two of these four seats. Imran Masood hit out at the SP questioning party's seriousness about the alliance. "How can they release names even before the talks are finalised". He added that even Congress can name candidates from the same seats.

headline: 6-year-old boy dies after falling from 11th floor of Maharashtra building: Police
content: A six-year-old boy died after falling from the 11th floor of a residential building in Maharashtra’s Palghar district on Tuesday, police said.The incident took place at Navkar Tower Society in Naigaon East when the boy was playing with a girl in the corridor outside his flat. A preliminary probe suggested the boy lost his balance near a window and fell. He first hit a fire-safety pipe, before hitting the ground, the police said.He was rushed to Cardinal Gracias Hospital in Vasai but succumbed to injuries during treatment.The police have registered an accidental death report.Local residents alleged lack of safety grills in the windows along the corridors.“We have repeatedly requested the installation of the safety grills but the builder has ignored these demands. We have also raised concerns about the poor condition of the society’s lifts. One wing’s lift is currently out of service,” a resident said, seeking anonymity.There was no immediate comment from the society authorities at the time of filing this report.Local residents said the boy lost his mother 15 days ago. His father reportedly planned to send him to a hostel in Mahabaleshwar.The police said they are yet to record the father’s statement in the case.

headline: Noshki Under Fire: Rockets, Gunshots Rock Pakistan’s Balochistan Amid Rising Clashes | News18
content: Fresh violence has been reported from Noshki in Pakistan’s Balochistan province, where heavy gunfire and rocket attacks have reportedly triggered intense clashes between Baloch fighters and Pakistani security forces. Reports from the area describe exchanges of fire at multiple locations, with bank branches also said to have been targeted as tensions escalated.The latest incidents come amid a wider surge in militant activity and security operations across Balochistan, a province that has witnessed a long-running insurgency involving Baloch armed groups and Pakistani state forces. The Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and other armed organisations have repeatedly claimed attacks on military installations, security personnel and infrastructure. headline: Kerala HC declines to interfere with State govt’s reconstitution of Waqf Board
content: Kochi The Kerala High Court on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) declined to interfere with the Keralam government’s decision to reconstitute the State Waqf Board, saying that it was already functional. A Bench of justices Devan Ramachandran and Basant Balaji was hearing appeals by K S Hamza and C K Usman Haji, the former chairperson and member of the earlier board that was disbanded barely eight months into its five-year term, against a single judge order declining to stay the reconstitution of the board. The single judge, on October 17, had refused to stay the reconstitution of the board but said that it would be subject to the outcome of the petitions challenging the same. The judge had also tagged the petitions by Hamza and Haji with the earlier PILs – challenging the validity of the previous and now disbanded board – which were pending before a Bench headed by Chief Justice Soumen Sen. However, the Bench headed by the Chief Justice on October 19 dismissed the PILs as the board had been reconstituted. On Tuesday, the Bench of justices Devan Ramachandran and Basant Balaji directed the Registry that the earlier petitions of Hamza and Haji be listed before the appropriate Bench.

headline: Cauvery Dispute: Karnataka Wants Tamil Nadu To Demolish Completed Project Structures | News18
content: The long-running Cauvery water dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu has entered another legal phase, with Karnataka moving the Supreme Court seeking an immediate temporary injunction against Tamil Nadu's Cauvery (Kattalai)–South Vellar–Vaigai–Gundar Link Project.In a fresh application filed in November 2026, Karnataka has asked the court to restrain Tamil Nadu from continuing construction under all three phases of the project, including work already underway.
