headline: Keralam to increase women's representation in police force to 30 per cent: Minister Chennithala
content: Malappuram , Keralam will increase women's representation in the police force to 30 per cent through phased recruitment, while introducing reforms to improve the efficiency of the Crime Branch and Vigilance wings, Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala has said.In future recruitments, women will be inducted in a 7:3 ratio, following a Cabinet decision to enhance their representation in the force, he said.Women officers were performing well in crime detection and anti-drug operations, Chennithala said after inaugurating the newly constructed Malappuram Crime Branch unit office here on Tuesday.At present, women officers serve as Station House Officers in 63 police stations across the state, he said.The home minister said appointments to the Crime Branch and Vigilance wings are now being made purely on merit, with officers having an aptitude for investigation selected through a special examination.The examination was devised in consultation with the Director General of Police and the Additional DGP , he said, adding that these specialised wings were not meant to accommodate officers who were sidelined due to workload in the regular police force.The Crime Branch is currently handling 2,763 important cases, including 321 registered during 2026 alone. The department's priority was to complete investigations within a stipulated timeframe, he said.Chennithala said 'Operation Toofan', launched to curb the spread of narcotic drugs in the state, has been a major success, with criminal cases witnessing a 35 per cent decline following its implementation.As part of the drive, 17,351 cases had been registered and 16,593 people arrested so far, he said, particularly appreciating the Manjeri and Malappuram police teams for recently travelling to Coimbatore in Tamil Nadu and seizing 15 kg of MDMA.Methylenedioxymethamphetamine , commonly known as ecstasy or molly, is a banned psychoactive substance.He said the anti-drug operation had helped bring down criminal cases by 35 per cent in six months compared to the corresponding period of the previous year.On addressing staff shortages and excessive workload at police stations, the minister said the government was considering deploying a fixed percentage of personnel from Armed Reserve camps and police battalions to police stations.He also said steps were being taken to construct new buildings for police stations in Malappuram district that were functioning from rented premises, including those at Karipur, Edavanna, Edakkara, Pothukallu and Mankada.Under the 'My Police Station' project, 90 per cent of police stations in the state had shifted to new buildings, which had been renovated with a uniform design and colour scheme, he said.A dedicated software system had also been introduced to monitor, in real time, FIR registrations and serious crimes such as murder, robbery and missing-person cases, through a dashboard at the home minister's office.The state had additionally secured ₹100 crore from the Centre for police modernisation, while 70 per cent of old vehicles piled up in front of police stations had already been removed, he said.Announcing a further initiative, Chennithala said the old vehicles parked in front of the Malappuram police station would be cleared, and the space would be handed over to the municipality for beautification.He said investigations into crimes, including murder cases, were progressing in a manner that would enable the police to identify offenders and bring them to justice, irrespective of how much time had elapsed since the offence.The new Malappuram Crime Branch office building was constructed at ₹3.20 crore under the 2024-25 annual plan. Spread over 9,140 square feet, the two-storey facility has been built near the Malappuram police station to accommodate the unit, which was earlier functioning from two separate buildings.The modern facility includes an investigation room, rooms for the Superintendent of Police and Deputy Superintendents of Police, a conference hall, Circle Inspector rooms, an administration office and other amenities, according to officials.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: 300 BJP, Hindu outfit members booked over Thiruparankundram Deepam protests
content: NEW DELHI: Cases have been registered against around 300 members of the BJP and Hindu organisations for protesting in Tamil Nadu's Thiruparankundram on Tuesday over the non-lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon stone pillar atop the hill, news agency ANI cited Madurai Police on Wednesday.According to the police, cases have been registered under six sections, including unlawful assembly without permission, causing a breach of public peace, making controversial remarks and obstructing government servants from discharging their duties.The protests were held over the failure to light the lamp at the Deepathoon, despite the Supreme Court's interim order directing that the Karthigai Deepam be lit at the stone pillar.The Maha Deepam was instead lit above the Uchi Pillayar temple at Thiruparankundram Hills as part of the annual festival, amid heavy security and rising tensions. No lamp was lit at the Deepathoon stone pillar.A small team of priests associated with the Subramaniya Swamy Temple performed the lamp-lighting ceremony, while police personnel were deployed near the Deepathoon ahead of the scheduled time. The Supreme Court had directed that the lamp be lit at 6pm.Advocate and Hindu Munnani petitioner Niranjan S Kumar expressed disappointment over the decision and accused the state government of deliberately disobeying the Supreme Court's interim order."We were all in the belief that the government would take immediate steps to light the lamp at the Thirupparankundram Deepathoon. We had all gathered here to see the lamp being lit by the authorities themselves. Unfortunately, at 6:02 p.m., the lamp at the Ucchi Pillayar was lit as usual, which means the order of the Supreme Court was definitely violated," he said.Alleging deliberate non-compliance with the court's directions, he added, "I would say it was not only violated, but it is a deliberate, calculated and willful disobedience of the order of the Supreme Court. So we are all left with no other option but to approach the Supreme Court by way of contempt."Niranjan also referred to the Supreme Court's direction to the Madurai District Collector to submit a status report within three days of the festival. He said further action would depend on the report."And the District Collector, Madurai, was also directed to file a status report within three days after the festival. So let's wait for the District Collector's report," he said.Tamil Nadu BJP leader Tamilisai Soundararajan also criticised the state government's handling of the issue, accusing it of violating the Supreme Court's interim order and treating political groups differently."I strongly condemn the TVK government for violating the Supreme Court's interim order. Nobody is above the law. But they behaved in a way; they have violated the interim order of the Supreme Court," she said.Soundararajan questioned the decision to light the lamp at the Uchi Pillayar temple and accused the government of not informing people about the arrangements in advance."They are now citing the Agama rules; they have lit the lamp in the Uchi Pillayar. Till now, why didn't you say that you are cheating the people and you did not disclose where you are going to light the lamp? Beforehand you should have disclosed," she said.She also alleged that BJP leaders and workers were prevented from going near the temple, while leaders of some other political parties were allowed access."You did not allow us to go near the temple. The government did not allow us to go near the temple. From our State president to our workers, they were all arrested. We were not allowed to go to the temple. But they allowed Thirumavalavan; they allowed Jawahirullah," she said.Meanwhile, protests over the issue were reported from several other parts of Tamil Nadu.In Ramanathapuram, members of the Hindu Front staged a protest against the state government, alleging that it had failed to implement the Supreme Court's order. Police detained protesters who took part in a road blockade.In Pollachi, members of Hindu Munnani staged a road blockade during the Maha Karthigai Deepam festival, demanding that the state government follow the court's directions. Police removed the protesters and arrested them after they raised slogans against the government, triggering brief tension in the area.The protests came amid growing tensions over the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon stone pillar, with Hindu organisations demanding that the state government comply with the Supreme Court's interim directions.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: 69 former bureaucrats seek scrapping of Arunachal Pradesh’s Demwe dam over ecological concerns
content: A group of 69 former bureaucrats has urged the Union environment ministry to scrap the proposed 1,750 MW Demwe Lower Hydroelectric Project on the Lohit River in Arunachal Pradesh, citing concerns about its potentially devastating impact on biodiversity, indigenous communities, and the fragile ecology of the eastern Himalayas.In a letter dated November 23, also addressed to the Arunachal Pradesh chief minister Pema Khandu and the Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife (SC-NBWL), the former officials questioned the repeated attempts by successive governments to push ahead with the project despite scientific objections, legal interventions and sustained local opposition.The signatories include former Delhi lieutenant governor Najeeb Jung and former Kerala principal chief conservator of forests Prakriti Srivastava.No response was immediately available from the Union environment ministry or the Arunachal administration.What the letter saysAccording to the letter, the project would require the diversion of 1,416 hectares of forest land, submerge nearly 1,590 hectares and necessitate the felling of around 43,000 trees in an ecologically sensitive evergreen rainforest.“It (the project) is being pursued since 2011 by different governments, in spite of the havoc it will create on endemic wildlife as well as on tropical rainforests and people,” the letter stated.The former bureaucrats said opposition to the project dates back to 2010, when it received initial environmental clearance, prompting Mishmi and other indigenous communities, environmental groups and civil society organisations to mobilise against the proposed dam to protect the sacred Parashuram Kund and downstream ecosystems.They warned that the project could threaten the survival of the critically endangered white-bellied heron, as well as fragment tiger habitats and disrupt wildlife connectivity across the larger landscape encompassing Kamlang, Namdapha, and the proposed Dibang Tiger Reserve.The letter also raised questions over the project’s chequered history of regulatory approvals.When the proposal was placed before the SC-NBWL in October 2011, all its non-official expert members opposed the project, citing serious downstream ecological consequences. However, the then Union environment minister granted wildlife clearance in 2012, overriding their objections, the signatories said.The decision was subsequently challenged before the National Green Tribunal (NGT), which in 2017 suspended the project’s approvals and directed the wildlife panel to undertake a fresh examination of the proposal, including its cumulative downstream impacts.The former bureaucrats alleged that a reconstituted wildlife committee cleared the project in 2018 without undertaking the comprehensive multi-seasonal assessment sought by the tribunal, relying instead on what they described as a flawed Wildlife Institute of India study.The project remained stalled owing to financial difficulties faced by its developer, among other factors, before being acquired by the Greenko Group in 2026.Questioning the latest regulatory exercise, the signatories said the SC-NBWL, reconstituted in March 2026 with only two independent experts, considered the proposal in July primarily to approve the change of project developer from Athena to Greenko.They alleged that the committee failed to undertake a comprehensive fresh wildlife assessment in accordance with the NGT’s directions and continued to rely on scientific data from 2018.The former officials also challenged the strategic argument that large dams in Arunachal Pradesh could help India establish prior appropriation rights over river waters and counter China’s upstream hydropower activities in the Brahmaputra basin.They argued that in the absence of a bilateral water-sharing treaty, downstream infrastructure would not prevent China from diverting water upstream.The letter further claimed that nearly 70%-80% of the Brahmaputra River system’s total water volume in India originates in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam, primarily from heavy monsoon rainfall and snowmelt.The signatories urged the authorities to reconsider the project’s viability in light of its ecological, social and legal implications rather than pursuing its development despite longstanding objections.

headline: Congress's Imran Masood hits out at SP amid UP seat-sharing friction: ‘We are not beggars’
content: The Samajwadi Party (SP)'s decision to release a list of five candidates for the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections amid seat-sharing talks with the Congress has triggered friction within the Opposition alliance, with Congress MP Imran Masood on Wednesday questioning the Akhilesh Yadav-led party's “seriousness” about forging a tie-up.Masood said the SP appeared to be holding discussions with the Congress on one hand and making electoral declarations on the other, which he said raised “questions about its intent”.“Whatever is happening here, it seems that there is a lack of seriousness in this matter. While you [Samajwadi Party] are holding talks on one side, you are making declarations on the other. This indicates that the matter is not being taken seriously,” news agency PTI quoted Masood, the Congress’s UP working president, as saying.Also read: SP releases first list of 5 candidates for UP Assembly polls amid seat-sharing talks The SP on Tuesday evening released its first list of candidates for next year’s Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, renominating four sitting MLAs and fielding a former party district president in a seat held by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The announcement came hours after the SP made the Congress an “opening offer” of 26 of the state’s 403 seats during talks in Delhi."We were discussing within the alliance, the meetings took place in Delhi. And after those meetings, if a declaration is made and it is said that ‘Sir, the starting point is 26 [seats]’ — we didn't even ask you for 26 seats. We are not beggars," Masood told news agency ANI.Tuesday’s list named Umar Ali Khan from Behat and Ashu Malik from Saharanpur, both in Saharanpur district, Nahid Hasan from Kairana in Shamli, Mehboob Ali from Amroha and Jyoti Lodhi from Lalitpur. Behat and Saharanpur were reportedly among the seats in a probable list of 181 constituencies sought by the Congress, though neither side has confirmed the list. The Congress had earlier demanded that it should have a say in candidates for the seats in Saharanpur— the district from which Masood is the sitting MP.Also read: Old alliance, new dynamics: Decoding the SAD-BJP reunion“When you have made this declaration against me, I don't understand whether you want to fight me, the Congress or the BJP. It has to be decided whether you want to fight the BJP or fight us,” Masood said, according to PTI.He added: “We will discuss within our party what we should do and whether we should sit for talks or not. The decision on how to proceed in this situation will be taken by the party.”SP leader Shivpal Yadav rejected speculation of discord between the allies."There is no rift in the alliance, the alliance will remain intact," PTI quoted him as saying.

headline: BJP, Akali Dal ‘natural alliance partners’, says West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh ahead of 2027 Punjab polls
content: West Bengal Minister Dilip Ghosh on Wednesday described the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Akali Dal (SAD) as "natural alliance partners", expressing support for the continuation of their political alliance in the interest of Punjab and the nation.Ghosh said the two parties had shared an association for several years and that their partnership was based on ideological similarities and mutual understanding."The Akali Dal and the BJP are natural alliance partners—they have been with us for years, not just recently," Ghosh told ANI. He acknowledged that circumstances could sometimes lead to the two parties parting ways but maintained that their ideological alignment remained strong, providing a basis for their association to continue.Also Read | BJP now complicit in Akali Dal’s anti-Sikh actions: SAD"While circumstances may occasionally lead to a separation, there is a strong alignment in terms of ideology and other aspects," he said.Taking a swipe at the INDIA bloc, Ghosh contrasted the BJP-SAD relationship with the opposition alliance, describing the latter as an arrangement without a strong political foundation. He questioned the nature of the INDIA alliance, alleging that its formation lacked the ideological and organisational unity that he attributed to the BJP's alliance partners."In contrast, the INDIA alliance is entirely unnatural; they simply sat together, had tea for two days, and declared an alliance," he said.Ghosh further alleged that the opposition alliance had no substantial political presence across the country and dismissed it as an arrangement formed through meetings in the national capital.Also Read | BJP-SAD’s renewed alliance sets stage for 3-cornered contest in Chandigarh"The INDIA alliance has no real existence anywhere in the country—it amounts to nothing more than a tea party in Delhi," he said.Drawing a parallel with other parties associated with the BJP, Ghosh referred to the Shiv Sena and said the Akali Dal was also among the parties that had maintained an alliance with the BJP. He pointed out that several other political parties had joined the BJP-led alliance over the years."Just as the Shiv Sena is our alliance partner, so too is the Akali Dal, along with many other parties that have joined us," he said.Emphasising the importance of the BJP-SAD partnership, Ghosh said the alliance should continue, citing the interests of Punjab and the country as the reasons for maintaining the association."Therefore, in the interest of the nation and the interest of Punjab, the alliance between the Akali Dal and the BJP should remain intact and continue to move forward," he said.Also Read | Modi, Sukhbir to share stage at first joint SAD-BJP rally in Moga on Dec 8Earlier on Tuesday, Union Home Minister Amit Shah , BJP President Nitin Nabin and Shiromani Akali Dal President Sukhbir Badal met on Tuesday in the capital to formally as they signalled a tie-up between the two parties for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections and the strengthening of the National Democratic Alliance.At the BJP headquarters, leaders from both parties formally signalled an intent to take on the ruling Aam Aadmi Party and the Congress.Amit Shah said, "Both the BJP and the Akali Dal have decided to fight the Punjab Assembly elections together, and the Akali Dal will also join the NDA from today. This is a great occasion that on Guru Purab the Akali Dal, one of our oldest allies, is returning to the NDA."

headline: ‘Maybe I should do it’: Donald Trump on US government taking a stake in chipmaker Nvidia
content: President Donald Trump has said that he is open to the US government taking a stake in the chip giant Nvidia. Speaking to the New York Post, Trump said it is ‘probably not too late’ for the government to own a pice of the second-most valuable company in the world. “I thought about it. I said, ‘You know, maybe I should do it,’ but I didn’t bring it up at this point. It’s probably not too late,” Trump said. He also noted that another American chipmaker, Intel, had handed over 10% of its value to the US government last year. Trump campaigned for Huang's return Trump’s comments came a day after Nvidia’s board of directors reinstated Jensen Huang as the CEO, less than two weeks after he was let go over alleged corporate misconduct. The board, which had initiated the search for Huang’s replacement and made it clear that the doors were shut for his return, reversed its decision on Monday, allegedly under intense lobbying from the Trump White House. On Monday, Trump touted Huang’s return, saying on CNBC that he “felt very strongly about it.” Trump, a close ally of Huang, has been one of the most vocal supporters of the Nvidia co-founder returning as the chipmaker’s CEO. Over the past two weeks, Trump has pointed out that Nvidia was a critical asset for the US, both technologically and economically. Trump told CNBC that keeping Huang at the helm of Nvidia is imperative for the United States to maintain its lead over China in artificial intelligence.Nvidia share revenue of chip sales to China with USWhile there have been no prior talks of the US government taking a stake in Nvidia, in January 2026 the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) published rule-related to licensing terms; case-by-case approvals for covered AI chip sales to China required directing a share of proceeds to the US government. Under this, AI chips sold to China, the US Treasury would earn an estimated to be around 15-20% revenue-sharing cut from the sale.US government stake in IntelIn contrast, in August 2025, the US government took a 9.9% equity stake in Intel to bolster domestic semiconductor manufacturing, protect national security, and secure a direct taxpayer return on federal funding.Altman prosed giving US govt stake in OpenAIIn July 2026, amid growing scrutiny around artificial intelligence, it was reported that CEO Sam Altman discussed proposing a 5% equity stake in OpenAI to the US government. He also suggested that other leading AI companies should contribute a similar stake to a government-run fund, allowing the US public to share in AI's financial growth.

headline: Kumari Selja questions BJP’s claims on drug eradication
content: Sirsa MP and Congress leader Kumari Selja has questioned the BJP’s claims of eradicating drugs in Punjab, asking the party to first address the growing drug menace and unemployment in Haryana, where it has been in power for nearly 12 years. Citing government figures, Selja said around 1.57 lakh people had approached de-addiction centres across Haryana for treatment since 2024. A significant number of them were young people, she added.

headline: Blood Tests At Liquor Shops! Inside Madhya Pradesh's Unusual Campaign After Spurious Alcohol Deaths
content: SAGAR: A liquor shop is perhaps the last place where customers expect to be greeted by a doctor. But in Madhya Pradesh’s Bundelkhand region, medical teams are now stationed outside liquor outlets, checking customers’ health, collecting blood samples and counselling them about the risks of excessive drinking. In Sagar district, the administration has taken the exercise a step further by asking liquor-shop operators to identify their most regular customers, including those who arrive before the outlets open at 8 am. The lists are being used to help doctors reach people suspected of prolonged and excessive alcohol consumption. The campaign follows a suspected spurious-liquor tragedy in September, when 20 people died in the district’s Banda area. Investigations reportedly found that several victims were already suffering from serious liver and kidney ailments. Two more people were also reported to have died after consuming liquor in the area recently. Why Are Doctors Being Deployed Outside Liquor Shops In Sagar? Sagar Collector Dilip Kumar Yadav said the initiative aims to identify people at risk from prolonged alcohol consumption, particularly those who drink throughout the day, have existing health conditions or do not eat properly. The administration sought help from liquor-shop operators because they are familiar with customers who visit their outlets regularly. Their lists have helped health teams identify habitual drinkers for medical examinations. In an unusual public health initiative, the Madhya Pradesh administration has stationed medical teams outside liquor shops in Sagar to screen habitual drinkers. Doctors are conducting health check-ups, collecting blood samples and assessing liver and kidney function, while counselling people on the risks of excessive alcohol consumption and encouraging them to quit. The campaign follows a suspected spurious-liquor tragedy in September that claimed over 20 lives in the district. Officials say the initiative aims to identify chronic drinkers with existing health complications and provide timely medical intervention. #MadhyaPradesh #sagarmadhyapradesh #alcoholawareness #PublicHealth — News18 (@CNNnews18) November 24, 2026 The exercise, however, is not limited to people named by shopkeepers. Health workers are also visiting villages and reaching out through primary and community health centres to identify habitual drinkers who may not appear on the lists. Medical teams are conducting health assessments, collecting blood samples for liver and kidney function tests, and providing medicines where required. Doctors are also recording the mobile numbers of those screened so that they can contact them once the test reports arrive. 147 People Screened In 2 Days, 144 Blood Samples Collected The campaign began on Sunday. According to a report in The Indian Express, around 50 people were examined on the first day in Banda and Sagar, followed by 97 on Monday across Sagar city, Deori, Rahli, Khurai and Bina. Over the first two days, medical teams screened 147 people and collected 144 blood samples for further tests, according to reports. Chief Medical and Health Officer (CMHO) Dr Devesh Pateria said the exercise had already helped identify several cases of chronic alcoholism, including people showing signs of impaired liver function. Doctors are also providing Vitamin B1 and multivitamin supplements to address nutritional deficiencies associated with prolonged alcohol consumption. Those showing signs of deteriorating health are being advised to undergo further tests and seek treatment. According to Dr Pateria, the exercise is also helping the Health Department build a consolidated database of habitual drinkers. Officials hope the information will help them identify vulnerable people earlier and plan further medical interventions. Manipur’s Spurious Liquor Tragedy: 17 Dead, Hundreds Hospitalised The campaign in Madhya Pradesh comes amid another suspected spurious-liquor tragedy in Manipur, where at least 17 people had died by November 23 after consuming suspected adulterated liquor. The deaths were reported over five days, beginning November 18, with casualties in Chandel and Kakching districts. The Manipur government said 1,130 people had been screened, 228 were admitted to hospitals and 38 were undergoing dialysis, according to an update on November 23. Samples of the suspected liquor were sent to laboratories in Kolkata and Imphal for testing, while authorities seized more than 4,500 litres of suspected illicit liquor. The state government also constituted a high-level inquiry committee, chaired by Principal Secretary RK Dinesh, to investigate the incident and submit a report within a month. The suspected cause of the deaths has not been conclusively established through laboratory findings. However, the incident has once again drawn attention to the dangers of consuming illicit or adulterated alcohol. How Dangerous Is Spurious Liquor? Risks Of Methanol Poisoning And Long-Term Alcohol Use Spurious liquor can be particularly dangerous when it contains toxic substances such as methanol, an industrial chemical that may be used to adulterate illicit alcoholic drinks. Methanol poisoning can cause nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, dizziness and breathing difficulties. In severe cases, it can lead to metabolic acidosis, damage to the optic nerve, permanent blindness, kidney failure, coma and death. One of the biggest dangers is that symptoms may not appear immediately. According to medical guidance, serious effects can emerge hours after consumption, meaning a person may initially appear relatively well even as poisoning develops. Suspected exposure requires urgent medical attention. Prolonged and excessive consumption of ordinary alcoholic beverages also carries serious health risks. It can cause liver disease, including fatty liver, alcoholic hepatitis and cirrhosis, as well as damage to the pancreas, heart and nervous system. Poor nutrition and existing medical conditions can further complicate a person’s health. The Sagar administration’s campaign is therefore aimed at two related but distinct concerns: identifying health complications among habitual drinkers and encouraging people to seek medical help before their conditions worsen. The recent deaths in Madhya Pradesh and Manipur also underline the potentially fatal consequences of consuming alcohol from unverified sources.

headline: Centre allots bungalow to Dalai Lama in Lutyens’ Delhi
content: The central government has allotted a bungalow to Tibetan spiritual leader the Dalai Lama in Lutyens' Delhi, sources said.Although there is no official word from the Union Housing and Urban Affairs Ministry, sources said on Tuesday that the Dalai Lama has been allotted the bungalow on Pandit Ravi Shankar Shukla Lane.They said the allotment to Gaden Phodrang Trust -- the office of the Dalai Lama -- has been made following a request from the Ministry of External Affairs.Such accommodation is generally transferred for three years, with provision for extension.Also read: For me, finding peace of mind is most important, says Dalai LamaAccording to the website of Gaden Phodrang, the Trust is dedicated to preserving and upholding the institution of the Dalai Lama and his spiritual work, while advancing his humanitarian vision.The website states that the Trust also supports His Holiness's core commitments: promoting human values, fostering interfaith harmony, preserving Tibetan culture and identity, protecting the environment, and encouraging a deeper appreciation of ancient Indian wisdom.

headline: 'Will take Bangladesh by December 16': Bengal minister Arjun Singh vows revenge for killings of Hindus
content: NEW DELHI: West Bengal minister Arjun Singh has claimed that India would take over Bangladesh by December 16 and that the killings of Hindus in the neighbouring country would be "avenged", triggering fresh attention amid strained relations between the two countries.Speaking to reporters in Bhatpara on Tuesday, Singh made the remarks while referring to the killings of Hindus in Bangladesh. "We will take Bangladesh by December 16th. Enough is enough; there are no more excuses regarding Bangladesh. We will certainly take revenge for the way Hindus have been killed in Bangladesh; there is no doubt about that," he said.His remarks came amid heightened tensions in Bangladesh over the proposed return of former Prime Minister and Awami League supremo Sheikh Hasina from India. Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs Humayun Kobir has said that Hasina would only be allowed to return as a "prisoner, in handcuffs" and under strict surveillance.Kobir reportedly made the remarks while speaking to journalists after briefing foreign diplomats at the ministry of foreign affairs in Dhaka.Dismissing reports that Hasina intended to return to Bangladesh on December 16, coinciding with the country's Victory Day celebrations, he said, "Desire and reality are two different things.""The reality is that a terrorist will never be allowed to return except through extradition... She is not a regular commercial passenger. She can only be brought back in handcuffs and under strict surveillance," Kobir said.Earlier, Hasina's spokesperson Syed Mozammel Ali had told Reuters that the former prime minister intended to travel from Delhi to Dhaka on December 16 aboard Bangladesh's national carrier, Biman Bangladesh Airlines.In an official communication, Ali said Hasina had sought arrangements from the Dhaka administration for her return journey. "Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka," Ali said, according to Reuters.Meanwhile, Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) chief prosecutor Md Aminul Islam reportedly dismissed Hasina's demand for a state aircraft to facilitate her return, describing it as "nothing but madness".A Bangladeshi minister had also told Reuters on Sunday that Hasina would face immediate arrest and imprisonment if she returned to the country. The minister added that no formal discussions had taken place with India over arranging an aircraft for her journey.Hasina served as Bangladesh's prime minister from 2009 until 2024. She fled to India on August 5, 2024, following a student-led agitation over public sector job quotas that escalated into a nationwide uprising against her Awami League government.She was subsequently sentenced to death in absentia by Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal in a case involving crimes against humanity over the crackdown on protesters. Hasina has denied the allegations.Hasina first expressed her intention to return to Bangladesh during a virtual media briefing in August this year and reiterated the plan in several subsequent interviews.Earlier this month, she also applied for a fresh passport and national identity card through her legal representatives in the United Kingdom.Dhaka has repeatedly sought Hasina's extradition from India, while New Delhi has maintained that the request is under examination.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Two IPS officers fight at late-night party in Assam, SSP injured; CM Sarma calls it ‘personal matter’
content: A late-night party organised by senior superintendent of police (SSP) Akshat Garg in Assam's Kokrajhar district during the last weekend allegedly turned into a physical altercation between two senior Indian Police Service (IPS) officers, including the host.As per police sources, an argument broke out between Garg and deputy inspector general (DIG) of the Western Range, YT Gyatso, following a verbal disagreement and escalated into a physical confrontation in which Garg sustained multiple injuries.The incident took place at the premises of the 7th Assam Police Battalion in Saraikhola. The police department has not officially confirmed the incident or released a statement, but Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Tuesday said he was aware of the matter.Sarma, however, called it a personal matter and said, "This happened at a private party, and the officers were not on duty. This was a personal matter, and since they were not on duty, we cannot say anything."He added, "If this had happened when they were on duty, we would have intervened and taken necessary steps."Assam Police headquarters has not issued an official statement on the alleged incident so far.Sources said the DGP had asked senior IPS officer Surendra Kumar to intervene and facilitate a reconciliation between the two officers.The circumstances surrounding the confrontation, the nature of Garg's injuries, the role of others present at the gathering and whether a formal departmental inquiry has been initiated remain unclear.CM Sarma's message on police conductEarlier on Tuesday, while addressing a passing-out parade of newly recruited Assam Police personnel at the Lachit Barphukan Police Academy in Dergaon, the chief minister issued a series of instructions on how police officers and personnel should conduct themselves while dealing with the public.He told the recruits to stay away from intoxicating substances, refrain from using abusive or indecent language and ensure their speech, behaviour, and overall conduct reflected the dignity of the uniform.

headline: Dalai Lama allotted bungalow in Lutyens’ Delhi
content: The central government has allotted a bungalow to Tibetan spiritual leader the Dalai Lama in Lutyens' Delhi, sources said.Although there is no official word from the Union Housing and Urban Affairs Ministry, sources said on Tuesday that the Dalai Lama has been allotted the bungalow on Pandit Ravi Shankar Shukla Lane.They said the allotment to Gaden Phodrang Trust -- the office of the Dalai Lama -- has been made following a request from the Ministry of External Affairs.Such accommodation is generally transferred for three years, with provision for extension.According to the website of Gaden Phodrang, the Trust is dedicated to preserving and upholding the institution of the Dalai Lama and his spiritual work, while advancing his humanitarian vision.The website states that the Trust also supports His Holiness's core commitments: promoting human values, fostering interfaith harmony, preserving Tibetan culture and identity, protecting the environment, and encouraging a deeper appreciation of ancient Indian wisdom.

headline: A fist of unity, wall depicting protest at Delhi’s border: Memorial at Jalandhar village evokes 13-month farmers’ protest
content: From a tree-like structure, a giant fist of unity emerges, with its trunk and roots bearing the faces of farmers. Behind it, a mural depicts tractors rolling out, farmers marching with flags and protesters holding placards. A farmer driving a pair of bullocks evokes the agrarian roots of the struggle, while other installations recreate the barricades, protest stages and makeshift settlements. This was the setting of the 13-month-long agitation organised by the Samyukta Kisan Morcha (SKM) against the three farm laws at Delhi’s borders. Ahead of the sixth anniversary of the November 26, 2020, ‘Delhi Chalo’ call, former national-level footballer, present-day farmer and kabaddi organiser Tony Sandhu of Rurka Kalan village in Jalandhar has recreated the historic movement in a 300-square-yard memorial at his native village, capturing its journey and expressing solidarity with the farmers who have lost their lives. Having remained part of the agitation with a group of hundreds of sportspersons and youths, led by kabaddi stars Mangi Bagga Pind, late Sandeep Nangal Ambia and Nanni Gopalpur, along with Punjabi singers Babbu Maan and Jazzy B, from its beginning until the farmers returned home in December 2021, Sandhu has recreated the march from Punjab, the barricades on the way, Haryana farmers joining the protesters and the sprawling settlements at Delhi’s borders. At the centre stands a tree-like structure bearing the faces of farmers who died and topped by a giant clenched fist. “I wanted the coming generations to see how farmers remained united, stayed at Delhi’s borders for over a year and compelled the government to repeal the three laws. It was a collective struggle, and its history should never be forgotten,” he said. Sandhu, who cultivates around 125 acres of his family’s land, has strong ties with sports organisations and social service activities. The idea of building the memorial came when some NRIs proposed gifting him a car to honour his contribution. Sandhu declined, saying the agitation was a collective struggle and he did not deserve an individual reward. Instead, he suggested that they contribute towards building a memorial to preserve its history. The idea took shape on Sandhu’s paternal land, where the 300-square-yard memorial was built. He engaged several artists to create sculptures, murals and models. The project took a few years to complete and was intended as a community tribute, not a personal monument. The installation commemorates those who died during the agitation, with farmer organisations putting the toll at more than 700. “These farmers should never be forgotten. Their sacrifices are part of the movement’s history,” Sandhu said. The memorial also features a replica of the abandoned KFC Mall building near the Singhu border, where the group initially accommodated around 3,000 people. “We later started the ‘Maa Dharti Di Warisan Da Langar’, which served thousands during the agitation,” Sandhu said. “Our group wanted people coming from Punjab to feel at home. From food and bedding to fans, coolers and washing machines, we arranged their daily necessities,” he recalled. The group also facilitated national media journalists, many of whom were initially hesitant to enter the protest sites, in reaching the main stages for ground coverage, seeking impartial reporting of the movement. Punjabi singers, including Babbu Maan, along with sports personalities, village organisations and NRIs, also extended support, Sandhu said. “This group had a big impact during the 13 months of agitation through its services to the people and the movement,” farmer leader Manjit Singh Rai of the BKU (Doaba) said. Huge support poured in, but the group accepted contributions only in kind, through direct services, and not in cash. By the time farmers prepared to leave Delhi, nearly four truckloads of bedding, fans, coolers, mattresses, bedsheets and other household articles had accumulated, Sandhu said. The material was distributed among religious and social institutions. The group donated rations to Darbar Sahib, while other materials were contributed to Pingalwara, Jalandhar, and Manukhta Di Sewa, Ludhiana. Some articles were also handed over to farmer unions for future agitations. Visitors from neighbouring villages and SKM leaders now come to see the memorial. “Six years after ‘Delhi Chalo’, the memorial brings the journey — from Punjab’s first tractors to Delhi's barricades, protest sites and, finally, the farmers’ return home — back to the village, keeping alive the movement’s solidarity and sacrifices,” Sandhu concluded.

headline: NIA seeks Swiss, German help to access encrypted mail accounts in Tamil Nadu youth ‘radicalisation’ probe
content: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has sought Switzerland and Germany’s help to access two encrypted email accounts as part of its probe against banned outfit Hizb-ut-Tahrir (HuT), officials aware of the details said.A formal mutual legal assistance treaty (MLAT) request for information on a “proton mail” account has already been sent to the Swiss Confederation, while a letter rogatory (LR) – a judicial request – is being sent to Germany to access a “tuta (previously known as Tutanota) mail” account, the officials added.Proton and Tuta are end-to-end encrypted email providers based in Switzerland and Germany, respectively.Besides approaching Germany and Switzerland, NIA has sought assistance from the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) on certain financial information on HuT’s activities, the officials said.NIA’s probe pertains to alleged radicalisation and recruitment of Muslim youth in Tamil Nadu, along with other HuT activities, to promote its jihadi ideology, establish an Islamic Caliphate in India, and enforce the draft Islamic constitution of HuT founder Sheikh Taqi al-Din al-Nabhani. In May 2024, seven people were arrested in the case.“Some of the accused were also in touch with HuT members in foreign countries and the key handlers abroad have been identified. There are multiple layers of criminal involvement, including encrypted digital communications, financial transactions routed through various institutions, and international linkages. We need to unearth the whole international conspiracy,” said an official cited above, on condition of anonymity.Founded in 1953, HuT is an international pan-Islamic group that seeks to establish a caliphate rule under the Islamic law. The group's headquarters is in Lebanon and it operates in at least over 30 countries, including the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada and Australia. The outfit has a history of praising and celebrating attacks against Israel and the Jews. Countries such as Germany, Egypt, UK and several central Asian and Arab countries have banned the outfit.India also banned the group in October 2024, months after the case in Tamil Nadu was unearthed.The federal agency arrested Hameed Hussain (alleged chief coordinator of HuT), Ahamed Mansoor, Abdul Rahman, H Mohamed Maurice, Khader Nawaz Sheriff, Ahmed Ali and Faizul Hussain (head of HuT in Tamil Nadu) in May 2024. Officials alleged Hussain and others conducted secret classes every Sunday at one Modern Essential Education Trust hall in Royapettah, Chennai.In a statement in November 2024, NIA said the arrested men were “key leaders and members of HuT, and had been tasked with organising recruitment drive meetings with religious heads, ulemas, imams”.The accused, the central agency said, were in contact with their Pakistan-based HuT counterparts, and propagated their newsletters and articles on violent secession of Kashmir with military assistance (Nusra) from Pakistan. “They were provided articles that incite violence and published by the Central Media Office (CMO) of HuT,” NIA had said.The agency also said the probe found the accused were disseminating false and anti-national content. They used online platforms such as Google Meet and Zoom to propagate HuT's ideology, NIA said.

headline: Delhi AQI Today: Anand Vihar At 336, Akshardham At 327 – Which Areas Have The Worst Air?
content: Delhi woke up to another morning of polluted air on Wednesday, November 25, with the city’s average Air Quality Index (AQI) recorded at 228 at 7 am, placing it in the ‘poor’ category. The reading was marginally lower than Tuesday’s 242 at the same time, but pollution levels remained high across much of the capital. A separate reading around the Akshardham temple put the AQI at 327, in the ‘very poor’ category, according to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB). The variation in readings reflects differences across locations and monitoring points in the city. #WATCH | Delhi: Air Quality Index (AQI) around Akshardham is 327, categorised as ‘Very Poor’, as per the CPCB (Central Pollution Control Board). (Visuals shot at 07:05 am) https://t.co/MJhSS9sqQm — ANI (@ANI) November 21, 2026 Delhi AQI Today: Anand Vihar Most Polluted, Sri Aurobindo Marg Records Lowest Reading Of Delhi’s 59 monitoring stations, as many as 36 recorded AQI levels above 200, while six registered readings above 300, placing them in the ‘very poor’ category. Anand Vihar recorded the highest AQI among the reporting stations at 336, followed by Delhi Technological University (DTU) at 332. Akshardham also recorded a ‘very poor’ AQI of 327. North Campus of Delhi University registered 313, while Burari Crossing and IGNOU in Maidan Garhi recorded 305 and 302, respectively. #WATCH | Delhi: Air Quality Index (AQI) around Anand Vihar is 327, categorised as ‘Very Poor’, as per the CPCB (Central Pollution Control Board). (Visuals shot at 06:15 am) https://t.co/9ARjH39Buo — ANI (@ANI) November 25, 2026 At the other end, Sri Aurobindo Marg reported the lowest AQI at 140, followed by IMD Lodhi Road at 147 and Patparganj at 148. All three locations were in the ‘moderate’ category. PM10 and PM2.5 were the prominent pollutants in Delhi’s overall reading. PM2.5 refers to fine particles small enough to penetrate deep into the lungs, while PM10 includes larger inhalable particles. NCR AQI: Panchgaon, Gurugram Among Most Polluted Cities Air quality across the National Capital Region (NCR) also remained uneven, with several cities recording readings in the ‘poor’ category. Panchgaon in Haryana reported the highest AQI in the region at 294, followed by Gurugram at 280. Meerut recorded 248, while Ghaziabad and Bhiwadi registered 240 and 236, respectively. Bahadurgarh and Dharuhera in Haryana reported AQI readings of 231 and 229, while Delhi stood at 228. Noida recorded 215, followed by Bulandshahr at 211, Greater Noida at 209 and Baghpat at 206. Rohtak and Sonipat recorded comparatively lower readings of 199 and 190, respectively. Among the better-performing cities, Palwal had the lowest AQI in the region at 86. Panipat recorded 133, Bharatpur 141 and Hapur 142. Alwar and Faridabad reported readings of 145 and 155, respectively. India’s Highest AQI: Punjab’s Khanna Tops CPCB’s City List Among the 283 cities with valid readings in the CPCB’s 7 am dataset, Khanna in Punjab recorded the highest AQI at 323. Jalandhar followed with 304, while Panchgaon in Haryana stood at 294. Shamli in Uttar Pradesh reported an AQI of 282, followed by Gurugram at 280. Ballabgarh in Haryana and Anpara in Uttar Pradesh both recorded 255, while Ludhiana in Punjab reported 254. Mandideep in Madhya Pradesh registered 253. At the other end of the scale, Chikkaballapur in Karnataka recorded the lowest AQI at 19, followed by Madikeri at 24 and Cuddalore in Tamil Nadu at 28. Eloor in Kerala reported 30, while Koppal in Karnataka recorded 34. Aizawl in Mizoram, which featured among the cleanest cities in the previous day’s list, recorded an AQI of 38 on Wednesday. What Is Causing Delhi’s Air Pollution? Vehicular emissions continue to be a major contributor to Delhi’s fine-particle pollution. The latest source-apportionment estimates by the Air Quality Warning and Integrated Decision Support System for Emissions – Delhi (AIRWISE-Delhi) put the contribution of vehicles at 20.5% of the estimated PM2.5 load. Stubble burning in areas around Delhi accounted for 2.3% of the estimated PM2.5 pollution, while waste burning contributed 1.9%. These estimates indicate that pollution in the capital comes from multiple sources, including transport, agricultural fires and waste burning. Their relative contributions can vary with weather conditions and the movement of polluted air. Delhi Weather And AQI Forecast: Poor Air Quality Likely To Persist The India Meteorological Department’s Air Quality Early Warning System has forecast that Delhi’s air quality is likely to remain in the ‘poor’ category till November 27. The outlook for the following six days suggests that conditions could remain between the ‘poor’ and ‘very poor’ categories, indicating that the city may not see significant relief from pollution in the immediate future. The AQI scale classifies readings between 0 and 50 as ‘good’, 51 and 100 as ‘satisfactory’, 101 and 200 as ‘moderate’, 201 and 300 as ‘poor’, 301 and 400 as ‘very poor’, and 401 and 500 as ‘severe’. Delhi’s citywide reading of 228 therefore remains in the ‘poor’ category, even as several neighbourhoods have recorded much higher pollution levels.

headline: Families protest as police seal venues days after high court order against banquet halls in South Delhi's Sainik Farm
content: Many families staged a protest outside banquet halls in South Delhi's Sainik Farm, complaining that police sealing the venues led to last-minute cancellations and weddings being postponed indefinitely.This comes days after the Delhi high court directed civic authorities in the national capital to act against banquet halls operating in the area without valid permissions.On November 19, the high court gave directions while hearing a petition by a local organisation complaining about illegal marriage venues and banquet halls – those without any fire safety clearance or statutory permissions from the MCD. The judge noted that, for the safety of the people attending the functions at the venues, there should be an immediate suspension of events and commercial activities. The court also noted that these places can resume hosting events once they get necessary approvals.On Monday and Tuesday, as the Delhi Police began sealing banquet halls, allegedly without prior notice, many families who had pre-booked these venues were left shocked, as they had no venue and had lost all their money in deposits and other wedding expenses.Senior police officials said they sealed seven of the venues by Tuesday afternoon.What the affected families sayRavita Saha was supposed to get married on Tuesday but was instead found protesting outside the venue. Her father, Ram Lakhan Saha, said, “We had put in all our money and all of the arrangements were done. She was supposed to get married today. Now, what do I tell all my family members, in-laws, and the groom? My daughter is broken. Her wedding procession was ready, but we had nowhere to go.”Another woman, Aarti Singh, said, “My wedding is supposed to happen in 10 days. We had to pay for everything three months back only. Now, on Tuesday, we found the venue being locked and sealed. We had no idea. My parents are trying, but we haven't been able to find another venue. The venue people also didn’t inform us. They are not even giving a refund. Also, it's peak wedding season in Delhi. Where will I get married now?”The families marched from the W lane in Sainik Farm, where most of the venues had been sealed.Indira Singh, 50, also participated in the protest as her daughter’s wedding has been postponed indefinitely. “My daughter’s wedding is on Tuesday night. My daughter was in the salon. My husband and I were checking decorations and caterers when we found the venue was being sealed and would soon be demolished. I paid for the wedding with all my savings six months back. My daughter is heartbroken and hasn’t stopped crying. We need justice. We have been humiliated in front of our family members. The wedding was supposed to happen in three hours. Can’t the government or Delhi Police give us some time?”A senior police officer said, “The order was received over the weekend, and work was started as per the High Court’s order. We had to identify and seal all illegal banquet halls, which can be a major safety issue for the locals and the people using the venue”Many other families came with colourful wedding cards and raised slogans against Delhi police. Former Deoli MLA Prakash Jarwal also joined in the protest and alleged that a “fake” organisation was “blackmailing these halls”.“For the last 20 years, families from lower economic backgrounds in Raju Park, Tigri and Sangam Vihar have been hosting weddings at W-17 lane here. In Sangam Vihar, there’s no space or garden or wedding halls. They host weddings here because it's also cheap here. But now, some fake organisation has emerged and is blackmailing these halls. When the establishments refused, they filed a petition. Now, the HC has directed that the venues be sealed, and the next hearing is not until December 10. Now, what will women and their families do? Today, a young woman was supposed to get married. She and her family are now suffering. I don’t understand this. In 2022, MCD had said open gardens don’t need permission. This is a BJP trick to harass women.”

headline: Hisar police crack down on modified bikes, impound car over multiple traffic violations
content: In a crackdown on traffic violations, the Hisar police have issued challans of Rs 25,000 and Rs 11,000 to two Bullet motorcycle riders for using modified silencers.In the first case, Traffic SHO Inspector Chander Bhan issued a challan of Rs 25,000 to a Bullet rider near Peer Baba on NH-09 for using a modified silencer that produced loud, firecracker-like sounds. The motorcycle was also impounded.In another case, the police interceptor team fined a Bullet rider Rs 11,000 after finding a modified silencer fitted to the motorcycle in violation of traffic rules. The police said such loud noises could frighten commuters, particularly children and elderly people.In a separate incident, the interceptor team impounded a car and issued a challan of Rs 28,000 after detecting multiple traffic violations. The driver was found without a driving licence, while the vehicle did not have valid insurance or a pollution-under-control (PUC) certificate. The driver was also not wearing a seat belt.The car was additionally found fitted with unauthorised red and blue lights and prohibited black film. Its number plate, too, did not conform to the prescribed standards.Hisar SP Siddhant Jain said traffic personnel had been directed to take strict action against motorists using modified silencers, unauthorised lights and other illegal modifications, as well as those violating traffic rules.

headline: 14 years on, court revives Israeli embassy car bomb case
content: A Delhi court has taken fresh cognizance of a 14-year-old case that involved a magnetic bomb explosion on an Israeli embassy car in Delhi as part of an alleged conspiracy by Iranian suspects, observing that the material collected during the investigation was sufficient to establish that “it was an act of terror”.However, the lawyer for the sole accused named in the case, Delhi-based freelance journalist Syed Mohammad Ahmed Kazmi contended that the law does not allow a second congnizance. He also questioned the timing of the latest decision, suggesting that it could be linked to renewed hostilities between Iran and Israel and its ally US.The case dates back to February 13, 2012, when a magnetic explosive device was attached to the rear of an Israeli embassy Innova car by a motorcycle rider at about 3.15 pm at Aurangzeb Road (now Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Road). It exploded seconds later, injuring Tal Yehoshua Koren, the wife of an Israeli diplomat, and her driver. The attack was suspected to have been planned and carried out by four Iranian nationals: Houshang Afsar Irani, Mohammad Reza Abolghasemi, Seyed Ali Mahdiansadr and Sedaghatzadeh Masoud. The four had managed to flee from India and Interpol red notices were issued against them. Similar attacks took place in Georgia and Bangkok that week with the same accused individuals under radar in those countries.The special cell arrested Kazmi on March 6, 2012, for allegedly conspiring with the Iranians and receiving money from them. A charge sheet was filed against him in July 2012 under sections of the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA), Explosive Substances Act, and sections related to attempt to murder and criminal conspiracy of the IPC. Four Iranians were named as suspects, bit not in the accused column of the charge sheet. In a request sent to sent to Iran in 2012, the investigators had mentioned that the Iranian suspects were linked to the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). However, the military branch was not named in the charge sheet.A chief metropolitan magistrate (CMM) took cognizance of the charge sheet in August 2012. However, the Supreme Court set aside that cognizance on October 19, 2012, saying that a magistrate did not have the powers to take cognizance of a case arising from the scheduled offences under the National Investigation Agency (NIA) Act. It held that only a special court designed under the NIA Act can do so. The apex court also granted statutory bail to Kazmi.In the fresh order on November 19, special judge under the NIA Act at Rouse Avenue Courts, took cognizance under sections 307 (attempt to murder), 323 (causing hurt), 120B (criminal conspiracy) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and sections of the UAPA and Explosive Substances Act.“...having perused the entire material on record, this court is of the considered opinion that the CFSL report, the statements of witnesses…and the facts discovered during investigation, are sufficient to hold at this stage that a criminal offence namely a terrorist act did take place, in pursuance of a conspiracy,” the special court noted.The court also rejected Kazmi’s argument to drop the proceedings on the ground that the earlier cognizance had been rendered invalid by the top court. Baliga ruled the special court was competent to take cognizance afresh and that doing so would not amount to double cognizance.To be sure, the cognizance does not mean Kazmi is guilty of charges. The arguments on framing of charges have now been scheduled for December 7. Kazmi is currently out on bail.Advocate Mehmood Pracha, who represents Kazmi, told HT: “We will challenge this special court decision in the high court. The law is clear in this regard: there cannot be a second cognizance. Here, the Supreme Court had already set aside the cognizance taken by the magistrate.”He added that a criminal reference to decide on certain issues in this case is already pending in the Delhi High Court, and the special court should have awaited its decision.Questioning the timing, Pracha said: “Why after so many years? The only thing that has changed (since 2012) is that now there are hostilities between Iran and Israel-America.”

headline: No power can harm India as long as it reveres Sikh Gurus, says U.P. CM Adityanath
content: Lucknow Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) said that no power in the world will be able to harm India as long as it continues to hold Sikh Gurus in reverence and respect. “The sacrifice, penance, martyrdom, and spiritual consciousness of the Sikh Gurus are invaluable treasures of India’s national unity, social harmony, and cultural pride,” Mr. Adityanath said, addressing a program organised on the occasion of the 557th Prakash Parv of Sahib Shri Guru Nanak Dev Ji in Lucknow . “Through ‘Ek Onkar’, Guru Nanak Dev Ji Maharaj gave the message of uniting all humanity. His teachings remain as relevant today as they were then. We must not confine these teachings to events and celebrations alone, but imbibe them in our lives and continuously familiarize the younger generation with them as well,” he added. Referring to the spiritual and religious significance of Kartik Purnima, the U.P. Chief Minister said, “Today is an extremely sacred day for entire state. Since 4 am, I have been receiving updates on the number of devotees and arrangements at various religious sites across the state. At Shukratal in Muzaffarnagar, lakhs of devotees are taking a holy dip in the Ganga. At Garhmukteshwar in Hapur, approximately 15 lakh devotees took a holy dip on Tuesday. Meanhwhile, more than 15 lakh devotees took a dip of faith in the Ganga at Tigri in Amroha. A large number of devotees also arrived in Prayagraj and Farrukhabad, while lakhs of them visited the Ganga in Ayodhya and Kashi,”. Referring to the journeys undertaken by Guru Nanak Dev Ji and social conditions prevailing during his time, Mr. Adityanath said, “When he conveyed the message of unity to humanity, society was grappling with numerous social evils and divisions. Society was fragmented in the name of caste, untouchability and discrimination. At the same time, he said foreign invasions and external attacks posed challenges. During such difficult times, Guru Nanak Dev Ji Maharaj united all humanity through the mantra of ‘Ek Onkar’. His clear message was that God is one and we are all His children. Therefore, every human being deserves equal respect. This mantra, given by him, became a great force for uniting society at that time, and it remains relevant even today. Despite limited means and resources, Guru Nanak Dev Ji Maharaj traveled to various places and spread the message of humanity, equality and spiritual consciousness among the masses,”. Explaining the three principal teachings of Guru Nanak Dev Ji Maharaj, ‘Naam Japo, Kirat Karo, Vand Chhako’, the U.P. CM added, “Remembering God, performing kirtan and embracing the spirit of togetherness generate positive feelings within human beings. This dispels ignorance and awakens the strength of unity in society,”..

headline: In SAD-BJP reunion, Congress sees an opening, targets alliance over farm laws
content: The first meeting of the Congress’ Punjab Election Committee was held in Chandigarh on Tuesday, hours after the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) announced their alliance, with party leaders saying the reunion of the two parties could work to the grand old party's advantage in the 2027 Assembly elections. Congress leaders expressed satisfaction that the two parties had been forced to reunite after years of political decline, saying their dependence on each other reflected their “precarious” positions in Punjab. The party also believes that the consolidation of the Akali vote would benefit it. “Leaders representing predominantly rural Assembly constituencies are certain that they will be able to retain their seats because of this alliance and the anti-incumbency against the AAP,” said a senior Congress leader. The meeting was chaired by AICC general secretary in-charge of Punjab Sachin Pilot and attended by state president Pargat Singh, Leader of Opposition Partap Singh Bajwa, former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi and former state president Amrinder Singh Raja Warring, among others. Pilot said the committee held detailed discussions on candidate selection and the party’s strategy for the upcoming elections. “We are committed to ensuring that Congress wins the election and forms the government,” he posted on X. Bajwa said the SAD-BJP alliance showed that neither party was confident of its prospects on its own. He said the reunion was “a desperate marriage of political convenience between two rejected parties trying to save themselves from political extinction”, reducing its electoral arithmetic to “0+0=0”. “Sukhbir Badal is trying to ensure that BJP gets a toe-hold in Punjab through the ‘dunki route’ since they have failed at the poll hustings,” he told The Indian Express. He accused the BJP of having an “anti-minority ideology” and said the party had hurt Punjab’s interests through the Agnipath scheme and the Centre’s decision to revoke Jammu and Kashmir’s statehood. “It is good that Akalis have joined hands with them again and discredited themselves in the eyes of the people of Punjab,” Bajwa said. Pilot said the alliance partners had not answered key questions over the issues that led to their separation — the farm laws, farmers’ deaths during the agitation and the demand for a legal guarantee on MSP. “This is a compromised and a desperate alliance because neither party has explained why they parted ways six years ago. Has the central government or the BJP given any guarantee on MSP to the people of the country? Have they apologised for the black laws they enacted? And what is the Akali Dal's stance on the hundreds of people who lost their lives at the Delhi borders during the farmers' agitation?,” he asked. Pargat said the alliance could not erase the memory of the farmers’ agitation. “Sacrificing the farmers’ martyrdom on the altar of political deal-making is a betrayal of Punjab,” he said, referring to the deaths of more than 700 farmers during the agitation. Former state Congress president and Ludhiana MP Amrinder Singh Raja Warring said the two parties had remained politically aligned on several issues even while maintaining a formal distance in Punjab. He cited their support for the BJP on issues such as the Presidential election and the Uniform Civil Code, and said the questions that had triggered the 2020 split — including the farm laws and the demand for the release of Bandi Sikhs — remained unresolved. “Realising they had lost ground, both parties had now joined forces hoping to salvage something,” Warring said. He claimed Congress would defeat the alliance again in 2027, as it had done in 2002 and 2017. Gurdaspur MP Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa said the BJP-SAD should first ensure that gangsters lodged in BJP-ruled states are denied unrestricted access to mobile phones. “Gangsterism cannot be eliminated in Punjab while its remote controls are operating from elsewhere,” he said. Congress MP Gurjeet Singh Aujla said the alliance would have to answer questions over the farmers’ deaths and its earlier positions on the RSS and gurdwara control. Former minister Bharat Bhushan Ashu said the SAD-BJP “drama” of separating and coming together had been used to mislead voters for years. Pilot, meanwhile, said the alliance was unlikely to alter the Congress’s electoral assessment. “Neither party has any political space left here. It is their choice to come back together; the public will decide who the better alternative is,” he said. In a statement, Pargat said the 41-member committee discussed the party’s strategy and preparations for the 2027 polls, with emphasis on strengthening the organisation, mobilising workers at the grassroots and establishing direct contact with voters. The party also discussed candidate selection, the roadmap for its election campaign and ways to highlight issues concerning public interest, he said. Pargat said Congress had begun its preparations well in advance and described its organisational strength, grassroots workers and connection with the people as its “greatest strength”.

headline: Bengaluru Metro Blue Line Trial Begins From KR Puram, Targets Mid-2027 Opening For Public
content: Trial runs on the Phase 2A section of the Blue Line Metro corridor along Bengaluru's Outer Ring Road commenced from KR Puram on Tuesday, with public operations targeted for mid-2027, Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said. The trials began at the first four stations towards Mahadevapura and will progressively extend to other stations in the coming weeks, he said after inspecting the progress of work at Doddanekkundi Metro Station. Gowda described the Blue Line as a critical infrastructure project for Bengaluru, particularly for the Outer Ring Road (ORR), which has emerged as one of the city's major employment and mobility corridors. "An estimated 11-12 lakh people work along this stretch. The corridor is vital not only for the daily commute of thousands of employees but also for Bengaluru's economic activity and the wider growth of Karnataka and the country. The Metro is expected to provide a long-term public transport solution to the severe congestion commuters face along this stretch," he said. Here is your first look at the Blue Line of Namma Metro - the next major addition to our comprehensive set of solutions to mobility challenges in BLR. We have reached a milestone - trial runs have started on this section. From KR Pura the train is now running up to Doddenakundi. Automated signalling will be operationalised in a couple of months. Then we are ready for safety certification. We are actively pushing at every stage for early dedication to public use.

headline: Foxconn India unit faces ₹143 crore insolvency suit over unpaid vendor dues
content: By Alisha Sachdev About half a dozen vendors in India are experiencing payment delays by Foxconn Technology Group’s local unit, said people familiar with the matter, with one even filing an insolvency lawsuit to recover $15 million in unpaid dues. BCD Emprasa LLP, which leased dormitory housing in southern India for the Foxconn unit’s employees at the Bengaluru facility, has alleged that it didn’t receive payment for rent and utilities in an Aug. 12 petition to the National Company Law Tribunal’s Chennai bench. The company is seeking about ₹143 crore ($15.3 million) for past dues along with interest, service charges and damages as of July 8 from Foxconn Hon Hai Technology India Mega Development Pvt., according to the filing, which was seen by Bloomberg News. Vendors in India often initiate insolvency proceedings to recover overdue payments, though these filings rarely push a company into bankruptcy. While the dispute isn’t expected to derail Foxconn’s growth plans in India, it adds to the challenges facing the iPhone assembler as it competes with Tata Electronics Pvt. for a bigger role in Apple Inc.’s supply chain. Bloomberg News reported last year that Foxconn recalled hundreds of Chinese workers from India — though the reason wasn’t clear at the time — in a move that saw the company bring in staff from Taiwan and Vietnam to minimize the impact on production. Foxconn didn’t reply to emailed queries seeking comments on BCD’s lawsuit in India. “These defaults have caused grave financial prejudice and substantial commercial harm to the company” BCD said in an emailed response, adding that the matter was sub judice before NCLT. At least four vendors other than BCD have been waiting for several months to over a year for Foxconn to clear their dues, said people familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified discussing private information. Several were hired for construction-related work on the Bengaluru facility and were working with Foxconn for the first time. Under an April 2024 agreement with BCD, Foxconn leased 700 residential units for female employees, with rent payable regardless of occupancy and a lock-in through July 2026, according to the NCLT filing. Foxconn defaulted on an invoice due in May 2025, it said. The electronics giant also did not agree to appointing an arbitrator. Departures of some non-Indian staff have slowed payments to local contractors, the people said.

headline: Families protest as police seal wedding venues in Sainik Farms after Delhi HC order
content: Families protested against the sealing drive in Delhi’s Sainik Farms wedding venues on Monday and Tuesday after the Delhi Police acted on the orders of the Delhi high court directing civic authorities to act against banquet halls operating without valid permissions.Families allege the sealing drive led to last-minute cancellations and indefinite wedding postponements.On November 19, the high court gave the directions after a petition by a local organisation complaining of illegal marriage venues and banquet halls, those without any fire safety clearance or statutory permissions from the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD). The judge noted that for the safety of the people attending the functions at the venues, there should be an immediate suspension of events and commercial activities at the venues. The court also noted that these places can resume hosting events once they get necessary approvals.Also Read: DDA razes Sainik Farms bungalow built on land marked for bio parkOn Monday and Tuesday, as the Delhi Police started sealing the banquet halls without any prior notice, many families who had pre-booked these venues were left in disarray as they had no venue to host their function, lost all their money in deposits and other wedding expenses.Senior police officials said they sealed seven venues by Tuesday afternoon.Ravita Saha was supposed to get married on Tuesday but instead she was protesting outside the venue. Her father, Ram Lakhan Saha, said, “We had put in all our money and all of the arrangements were done. She was supposed to get married today. Now, what do I tell all my family members, in laws and the groom? My daughter is broken. Her wedding procession was ready but we had nowhere to go.”Another woman, Aarti Singh, said, “My wedding is supposed to happen in ten days. We had to pay for everything three months back only. Now, on Tuesday, we found the venue being locked and sealed. We had no idea. My parents are trying but we are not able to find any other venue. The venue people also didn’t inform us. They are not even giving a refund. Also, its peak wedding season in Delhi. Where will I get married now?”The families marched from the W lane in Sainik Farms where most of the venues had been sealed.Indira Singh, 50, also participated in the protest as her daughter’s wedding has been postponed indefinitely.“My daughter’s wedding is on Tuesday night. My daughter was in the salon. My husband and I were checking the decoration and caterers when we found the venue is being sealed and soon will be demolished. I paid for the wedding with all my savings six months back. My daughter is heartbroken and hasn’t stopped crying. We need justice. We have been humiliated in front of our family members. The wedding was supposed to happen in three hours. Can’t the government or Delhi Police give us some time?”A senior police officer said, “The order was received over the weekend and work was started according to the high court’s order. We had to identify and seal all illegal banquet halls which can be a major safety issue for the locals and the people using the venue”Also Read: HC pulls up Centre, Delhi for ‘passing the buck’ on Sainik Farms regularisationFormer Deoli MLA and Aap Aadmi Party (AAP) member Prakash Jarwal also joined in the protest.“For the last 20 years, families from lower economic backgrounds in Raju Park, Tigri and Sangam Vihar have been hosting weddings at W-17 lane here. In Sangam Vihar, there’s no space or garden or wedding halls. They host weddings here as it’s also cheap. But now some fake organisation has come up and blackmailed these halls. When the establishments refused, they filed a petition. Now, HC has directed to seal venues and next hearing is not till December 10. Now, what will women and their families do? Today, a young woman was supposed to get married. She and her family are now suffering. I don’t understand this. In 2022, MCD had said open gardens don’t need permission. This is a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) trick to harass women.”A statement from the BJP is awaited and the copy will be updated whenever it is received.

headline: Miranda House Offers 15 Certificate Courses In AI, Filmmaking, Animation
content: Miranda House, University of Delhi, is offering 15 professional certificate courses in collaboration with the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) and Eros AIVidya. The six-month programmes will provide industry-oriented training in emerging creative and digital fields, equipping students with skills in artificial intelligence (AI), filmmaking, animation, virtual reality, and the creator economy. Admissions will be based on merit and are open to eligible University of Delhi students. The courses cover areas such as AI filmmaking, influencer and creator business, avatar and digital human creation, animation, video blogging, augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) production, visual effects (VFX), scriptwriting, acting, music production, music composition and direction, sound editing, video editing and art direction. The AI filmmaking course will train students in AI-enabled content creation, while the influencer and creator business programme will prepare them for the commercial and professional aspects of the creator economy. Other courses will focus on developing students' skills in animation, acting, scriptwriting, music production, sound editing, video editing and visual effects.

headline: Bengal Cinema Row: Suvendu Makes One Bengali Film Mandatory In Prime Time | News18
content: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari has directed cinema halls and multiplexes across the state to ensure at least one Bengali film gets a prime-time screening every day. The announcement followed a meeting with representatives of the Bengali film industry at the state secretariat, Nabanna, on Tuesday, November 24.The prime-time window is between 3 pm and 9 pm. Adhikari has called for stricter enforcement of the existing rule, warning that theatres failing to comply could face legal action, including possible cancellation of licences. Screenings of films in other languages will not be prohibited, but Bengali cinema must receive a guaranteed prime-time slot. n18oc_BreakingNewsn18oc_IndiaCNN-News18 is your trusted source for breaking news, updates, and in-depth analysis from around the world.
