headline: Land acquisition compensation doubled illegally: HC directs NHAI to furnish data of last six years
content: With revelations that a competent authority in land acquisition cases doubled the compensation illegally, the Punjab and Haryana high court has directed the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) to submit a report about such instances reported in Punjab between 2019-2025.According to the court, such instances have come to light in the cases only where land was being acquired for the NHAI or the railways, and not where the state government was acquiring land for its own purposes.The court was dealing with a bunch of cases filed by NHAI on land acquisition for widening National Highway-95, that starts from Mohali and passes through Samrala, Ludhiana, Jagraon, Moga and terminates near Ferozepur.According to the judgment, the Competent Authority Land Acquisition (CALA) passed the award in 2015 and determined compensation at ₹1 crore per acre by treating the land in question as agricultural land. In 2019, some farmers submitted representation stating that their land should be treated as commercial. The CALA passed the supplementary award in July 2019 and assessed market value at ₹2 crore per acre. The NHAI had argued that the CALA could have made changes that too clerical in nature up to six months from passing the award. It could not have changed the award after 2-3 years that too without any notice to the NHAI.The bench of justice Jagmohan Bansal observed that the state authorities appear to be “either intentionally or unintentionally trying to extend undue advantage” to the landowners.Supplementary awards passed without NHAI being notified“The impugned supplementary awards have been passed after 2-4 years from the date of passing original award. The CALA has passed supplementary awards even without issuing notice to the NHAI. …it is basic principle of law that no modification in the order should be made without granting opportunity to the person who is going to be prejudiced by modification. In the case in hand, liability of the NHAI on account of supplementary awards multiplied. NHAI was prejudiced without being heard. The impugned awards have been passed without granting opportunity of hearing to the NHAI, thus, are bad in the eye of law,” it recorded.The court noted that even clerical mistake cannot be corrected beyond six months from the date of award whereas CALA has passed impugned supplementary awards even after four years from the date of original award.“..this court is of the considered opinion that the CALA had no power to review or modify its order. It became functus officio, the moment award was passed. It could correct clerical or typing mistake. The impugned supplementary awards deserve to be set aside and accordingly are hereby set aside,” the court ordered noting that supplementary awards are passed only where beneficiary agencies are NHAI, Railways etc.“No such supplementary award is passed where acquisition is for the state itself. This practice of passing supplementary awards need to be curbed,” it said, adding that if procedure adopted by the authorities is approved, it would lead to chaos and anarchy. “Any person at any time would approach collector and seek modification/review of the original award. It would certainly lead to corruption. The mechanism to challenge award would become meaningless,” it remarked, further asking the registry to send copy of the order to the chief secretary for his perusal and further necessary instructions.The court also asked the NHAI to submit a report within four months about supplementary/corrigendum awards passed by CALA during 2019 to 2025 and in how many cases NHAI had accepted the same and enhanced amount of compensation was released.

headline: 65-year-old woman killed, teen hurt in Amritsar firing; 2 arrested within hours
content: ​ ​A 65-year-old woman was killed and a 19-year-old youth injured after two motorcycle-borne assailants opened fire at the latter in Amritsar’s Chheharta area on Tuesday.Acting swiftly after the shooting, police tracked down and arrested the two accused following a brief exchange of fire later in the day.The deceased, Dalbir Kaur, was a neighbour of the intended target, Simranjit Singh, alias Gola. She was caught in the line of fire and suffered a bullet injury. Both were rushed to a hospital, where Dalbir succumbed during treatment.The accused were identified as Jagroop Singh, 18, a resident of Gurunanak Ward, and Harmanpreet Singh, alias Rapper, 18, a resident of Kot Khalsa. Both sustained bullet injuries during the police encounter and were admitted to a hospital.Amritsar commissioner of police (CP) Harmanbir Singh Gill said police teams tracked down the suspects using technical inputs and human intelligence. When intercepted, the accused allegedly opened fire at the police party, firing three rounds. The police retaliated with five rounds in self-defence, before overpowering and arresting them.Police recovered a pistol, two live cartridges, three empty shells and the motorcycle allegedly used in the crime.Preliminary investigation revealed that the attack on Simranjit was triggered by personal enmity, reportedly following an alleged insult to Harmanpreet’s turban.Police also found that the duo had allegedly been hired by gangster Ankush Bahman for ₹20,000 to conduct reconnaissance and eliminate another target. However, they diverted from the assigned target to attack Simranjit to settle their personal score.A case was registered under Sections 109, 351(2) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with Sections 25 and 27 of the Arms Act, at the Chheharta police station.Gill said further investigation was underway to establish the sequence of events, trace the source of the weapon and identify others involved in the conspiracy.

headline: Delhi air quality stays ‘poor’ at 228 as calm winds, inversion trap pollutants
content: Delhi's air quality stayed in the "poor" category on Wednesday morning, with the Air Quality Index (AQI) at 228, one point higher than Tuesday's 227, as calm winds and a stronger temperature inversion kept pollutants from dispersing.This came as Delhi's base station Safdarjung recorded a minimum temperature of 10 degrees Celsius – the lowest among the five weather stations in the city, according to India Meteorological Department (IMD) data.PM2.5 was yet again the dominant pollutant at 44 of the 56 monitoring stations, indicating the continued prevalence of fine particulate matter across the city.Anand Vihar recorded the highest AQI at 373, in the “very poor” category, while Sri Aurobindo Marg reported the lowest at 141, in the “moderate” category. Of the 56 monitoring stations, 22 were in the “moderate” category, 19 in “poor” and 15 in “very poor”.According to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), the AQI is classified into six categories: good (0–50), satisfactory (51–100), moderate (101–200), poor (201–300), very poor (301–400) and severe (401–500).Meteorological conditions continued to work against the dispersal of pollutants. At 4.30am on Wednesday, a layer of warmer air was present around 300 metres above the ground, with temperatures 9 degrees Celsius higher than the surface. This was stronger than Tuesday’s 7-degree Celsius difference at the same height.Such a temperature inversion acts like a lid over the city, preventing pollutants from rising and dispersing, and trapping smoke and dust closer to the ground until surface temperatures increase.Wind speeds below this warm layer averaged 15 kmph from the north-west, in comparison to the 20 kmph from the same direction a day earlier.Calm conditions were also recorded at Safdarjung airfield in 13 of the 14 hourly observations from 4pm on Tuesday. Meanwhile, Lodhi Road recorded a minimum temperature of 10.1 degrees Celsius, followed by Ayanagar at 10.4 degrees Celsius. Palam recorded 11 degrees Celsius, while the Ridge station registered 11.7 degrees Celsius.The minimum temperature at Safdarjung was 1.3 degrees below normal, while Lodhi Road recorded a departure of 0.1 degrees above normal. Ayanagar's minimum was 2.6 degrees below normal.The maximum temperature recorded at Safdarjung on Tuesday was 27.2 degrees Celsius, 0.5 degrees above normal. Palam recorded the lowest maximum temperature among the five stations at 24.5 degrees Celsius.No rainfall was recorded at any of the five stations in the 24 hours ending at 8.30am on Wednesday.

headline: Farmers oppose transmission line in Jind village, 50 detained
content: Tension prevailed in Dhanda Kheri village of Jind district on Tuesday after the administration deployed JCB machines to clear standing crops for a high-voltage transmission line project, triggering a confrontation between protesting farmers and police. The police detained around 50 farmers and took them to the police lines, though they were reportedly released later in the night.According to the information, the transmission line is being laid from Sikar in Rajasthan to Jind and further towards Sonepat and other locations. Farmers have been opposing the land acquisition process, alleging that the administration failed to ensure fair and uniform compensation for the acquired land.The farmers claimed a wide disparity in compensation, with some landowners being offered more than ₹1 crore while others were allegedly offered only a few lakh rupees.According to farmers, a large solar power plant is being set up in Bikaner, Rajasthan, and a high-voltage transmission network is being developed to supply electricity to Jind, Sonipat and other locations.Sushil Kumar, a farmer from Dariawala village whose standing crops were damaged during the operation on Tuesday, alleged that the administration had destroyed their hard-earned produce without consulting them.They demanded that the administration consult with affected landowners and finalise compensation rates before proceeding with land acquisition and construction work.The protesters warned of intensifying their agitation if their demands were not addressed. Officials, however, maintained that compensation was being paid according to the prescribed rules. They said the farmers were adamant about their demands, leading to their detention. Officials added that those dissatisfied with the compensation could approach the commissioner through an appeal.Farmers have announced they will stage a dharna (sit-in protest) on Koth Road starting Wednesday to press their demands. Meanwhile, police remain deployed in the village to prevent any further clashes during the ongoing work.

headline: Farmers forced to sell bajra produce at low rates: Surjewala
content: Congress general secretary and Rajya Sabha MP Randeep Singh Surjewala on Tuesday accused the BJP governments at both the state and the Centre of failing to procure bajra at the minimum support price (MSP), alleging that farmers in the state were being forced to sell their produce at significantly lower rates.Addressing protesting farmers, agricultural labourers and commission agents at the Dadri grain market, Surjewala said bajra, for which the MSP had been fixed at ₹2,900 per quintal, was being sold at ₹1,800-2,200 per quintal. He alleged that the state government’s Bhavantar Bharpai scheme had also failed to provide the promised compensation of ₹600 per quintal, with farmers yet to receive any payment.Citing government procurement figures, he claimed that the Food Corporation of India (FCI) had made zero purchases of bajra from Haryana during 2025-26 and 2026-27, while state agencies procured only 61 quintals and 420 quintals, respectively, during the two years.He alleged that Haryana produced around 13 lakh metric tonnes of bajra last year, while production this year was estimated at 15 lakh metric tonnes. At ₹600 per quintal, the price-difference compensation would amount to approximately ₹900 crore, he added.Surjewala also questioned the closure of the bajra procurement portal on November 10, five days ahead of the scheduled November 15 deadline, alleging that it had forced farmers to sell their produce to private buyers at distress prices.He demanded reopening of the portal by December 15, procurement at MSP by FCI and Haryana State Cooperative Supply and Marketing Federation Limited (HAFED), payment of the price difference within seven days and 2.5% commission to commission agents.

headline: BJP-SAD’s renewed alliance sets stage for 3-cornered contest in Chandigarh
content: The revival of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) alliance ahead of the 2027 Punjab assembly elections has come as a shot in the arm for the two parties in Chandigarh, where they are gearing up for the December 23 municipal corporation elections.The renewed tie-up is expected to help the parties consolidate their traditional voter bases and prevent a division of votes, as was seen during the 2021 civic polls.Chandigarh BJP president Jatinder Pal Malhotra said that the reunion would pave the way for a resounding victory in the forthcoming MC elections.The development has also set the stage for a three-cornered contest, with the Congress and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) — which had come together for the 2024 mayoral elections but are clear on fighting independently this time – facing a fresh challenge from the BJP-SAD combine.The two parties, which remained allies for over two decades and contested several elections together in Punjab and Chandigarh, parted ways in 2020 following differences over the Centre’s farm laws. The split had a visible impact on their electoral fortunes. While the alliance had won 21 of the 26 wards (81%) in 2016, the two parties managed just 13 of the 35 wards (37%) in 2021. The AAP, making its debut in the civic polls, emerged as the single-largest party in 2021 with 14 seats.Why the alliance matters Unlike Punjab, where the BJP considers the SAD its “big brother”, the saffron party has enjoyed an upper hand in Chandigarh. But the 2021 elections showed how SAD votes could matter in wards where the BJP was in a close contest with its rivals. In Ward 2, for instance, the SAD candidate secured 249 votes, significantly higher than BJP’s victory margin. In Ward 22, where AAP won with 2,712 votes against BJP’s 2,636, SAD candidate Reema Mahajan secured another 283 votes. A complete transfer of these votes could have changed the result in BJP’s favour.Several wards witnessed razor-thin victories, with BJP candidates winning some seats by margins of just a handful of votes. In Ward 2, BJP’s Maheshinder Singh Sidhu defeated Congress candidate by just 11 votes, while in Ward 4, AAP’s Suman Devi won by a margin of 12 votes. In Ward 34, Congress candidate Gurpreet Singh won by just nine votes.A study of the overall vote share also shows that the split may have cost the two parties. While the BJP secured 29.7% of the total votes, SAD received 2.5%, taking their combined vote share to 32%. This would have been higher than Congress’ 30% and AAP’s 26%, had the two parties contested together and their voters supported a common candidate.The SAD’s wider performance in 2021, however, remained limited, with the party winning just one of the 35 wards. Its alliance partner, the Bahujan Samaj Party, failed to win any seats. AAP won 14 wards, BJP 12 and Congress eight.What each partner brings to the tableThe BJP has traditionally enjoyed a strong support from the urban and upper middle class voters while the SAD draws support from Sikh voters and sections of the Punjabi community. SAD’s performance has also been stronger in pockets having a sizeable Punjabi electorate. For instance, it retained Ward 10 in 2016, with its candidate Hardeep Singh polling 7,894 votes, or 60% of the votes polled in the ward. The Buterla area has also remained an important pocket for the party. In the 2021 elections, SAD’s Hardeep Singh won Ward 30. The ward included the Buterla area in Sector 41-B. The result showed that SAD could retain a local support base even when contesting against its former ally.Seat-sharing being worked outIn its previous outing together – in 2016, the BJP fielded candidates in 22 of the 26 wards, while the SAD contested the remaining four. The BJP won 20 seats and the SAD one. With the number of wards having increased from 26 to 35, the SAD is now seeking a larger share in the alliance. Chandigarh SAD president Charanjit Singh Villy has indicated that the party expects a greater number of seats this time, citing the increase in wards and its organisational expansion. The final seat-sharing arrangement, however, is yet to be worked out.

headline: Sugarcane stir spreads to several Haryana districts
content: The sugarcane farmers’ agitation in Haryana has entered its second week, spreading across several cane-growing districts and disrupting the start of the crushing season. Growers are increasingly worried about delays in clearing their fields for wheat sowing.A group of farmers on Tuesday reportedly disrupted the inauguration of the 43rd crushing season of Shahabad sugar mill in Kurukshetra district. The agitation demanding a hike in the sugarcane state advised price (SAP), launched by the Bharatiya Kisan Union- Charuni (BKU-Charuni) at Saraswati Sugar Mills in Yamunanagar on November 15, has gained momentum with several other farmers’ organisations, particularly the Bharatiya Kisan Union- Tikait (BKU-Tikait), extending support. The formation of the Haryana Sanjha Sangharsh Morcha has further strengthened the stir, which has now spread to Kurukshetra, Ambala, Rohtak, Karnal and Kaithal districts as crushing operations are being inaugurated without sugarcane.After Yamunanagar, indefinite sit-ins have subsequently been launched outside the Bhadson Sugarmill in Karnal, Kurukshetra’s Shahabad sugar mill and the Naraingarh mill in Ambala district. Farmers have also staged protests at other mills, with more organisations extending support to the agitation.Local jaggery and khandsari units have emerged as an alternative market for sugarcane, but growers allege that these units are taking advantage of the agitation by offering prices substantially below the government-fixed rate.Yamunanagar and Ambala districts have a maximum of around 300 jaggery units, which collectively crush a substantial quantity of cane every season. According to reports, these units were earlier purchasing sugarcane at around ₹500 per quintal but have reduced their offers to nearly ₹350 to ₹400 following the agitation against the state’s SAP of ₹430, leaving farmers with little incentive to sell their crop to these units.“Thousands of farmers like me are eagerly waiting for the agitation to end as I have 10 acres of sugarcane to harvest and clear for wheat sowing. However, I fear that this year I may not be able to sow wheat across my entire land,” said Krishan Kumar, a sugarcane grower from Shahbad of Kurukshetra. BKU (Tikait) Haryana president Ratan Mann said that the agitation will continue until the government increases the SAP to ₹600 per quintal and all farmers of the state are united and will jointly fight for their demand.The government increased the SAP from ₹415 per quintal in 2025-26 to ₹430 for the current season and announced a further increase to ₹450 for 2027-28. Farmers have rejected the hike of ₹15 as inadequate, citing rising expenditure on diesel, fertilisers, pesticides, irrigation, machinery and labour. However, the chief minister Nayab Singh Saini has defended the government’s decision claiming that the state is providing the highest SAP in the country. But the Samyukt Kisan Morcha has announced a gherao of the CM’s residence in Kurukshetra on December 2 if the demand for ₹600 per quintal is not accepted.Hooda extended support to farmersThe protesting farmers are also getting support from the opposition parties. Former CM and Leader of Opposition Bhupinder Singh Hooda extended his support to the sugarcane farmers’ agitation, terming ₹15 hike in SAP a “cruel joke” on the farmers. “The government has raised the price by only 3%, even as inflation has skyrocketed and sugar prices have broken all records. The costs of agricultural equipment, fertilisers, seeds, pesticides, and labor have become so exorbitant that farmers are being forced to abandon farming,” he added.In Kurukshetra, farmers from BKU-Charuni led by its spokesperson Rakesh Bains were removed from the program and briefly detained.Bains had threatened to show black flags and prevent BJP cabinet ministers Arvind Sharma and Krishan Bedi from attending the program as chief guests, but agreed to let the season start officially.However, the ministers skipped attending the event physically and Sharma chose to address the gathering virtually.A police team under Shahabad DSP Siddharth tried to pacify the farmers, but Bains was adamant that they would continue their protest against the state government until it announced a raise in the SAP to ₹600 per quintal. The police later detained the farmers’ group briefly until the event concluded. Although the crushing season was kicked off, operations could not start because farmers refused to deliver the sugarcane crop to the mills.In Karnal, the 51st crushing season was kicked-off after a hawan ceremony attended by DC Anand Kumar Sharma. Here too, Sharma spoke virtually and said the CM fixed the price for sugarcane farmers in the state at ₹430 per quintal for early varieties and ₹423 per quintal for late varieties, the highest in the country.He added that the Haryana government is ensuring timely crop payments to its farmers and the online token system has saved sugarcane farmers 10 to 12 hours in transporting sugarcane to the mill.Later, speaking to reporters about the farmers’ reluctance to bring the crop for crushing to the mill, the DC said they were in touch with farmers and their issues would be resolved soon.

headline: Constitutional morality must reflect integrity, accountability: CJI
content: The Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Monday said constitutional morality must be reflected through institutional integrity, accountability and individual responsibility, emphasising that the pursuit of justice requires the courage and conviction to uphold what is right even in challenging circumstances.Addressing the inaugural session of “Dharmakshetra: The Path of Righteousness – A Colloquium Series on Law, Society and Governance” at Dr BR Ambedkar National Law University, Sonepat, virtually , Justice Kant highlighted the relevance of “Dharma” in contemporary legal and constitutional discourse.He urged students and young legal professionals to remain intellectually open, engage with diverse perspectives and critically examine arguments. Independent thinking and the ability to respond thoughtfully to challenging questions were particularly important in mooting and courtroom practice, rather than relying solely on rehearsed arguments, he said.He also emphasised that professional competence must be accompanied by consistency, responsibility and integrity. The worth of a lawyer should not be measured merely by the number of cases won but also by the manner in which cases are conducted and the confidence and trust they inspire in the justice delivery system, he said.Earlier, welcoming the CJI and other participants, vice-chancellor Devinder Singh highlighted the broader significance of Dharma, describing it as a higher moral responsibility towards truth, justice and the welfare of all, rather than merely a set of prescribed duties.He said these values are essential for strengthening the foundations of a just and inclusive society.

headline: Amid feud with wife, Hoshiarpur man mows down 85-yr-old mother-in-law
content: An 85-year-old woman died and a man’s leg had to be amputated after her son-in-law allegedly ran them over with a tempo traveller over a family dispute here, police said on Tuesday.The deceased was identified as Harbhajan Kaur and the injured man was her neighbour Jasvir Singh, alias Kakka Gujjar, aged around 55. Both were residents of New Deep Nagar in Hoshiarpur, police said.According to information, the incident took place on Monday evening when Harbhajan was standing outside Jasvir’s house. Her son-in-law Baljit Singh, a resident of Bagowal village, arrived in a tempo traveller and allegedly rammed the vehicle into the two before fleeing the scene, police said.Family members rushed both injured persons to a private hospital in Hoshiarpur, where doctors amputated one of Jasvir’s legs due to the severity of his injuries.They were then referred to the Dayanand Medical College and Hospital in Ludhiana, where Harbhajan succumbed to her injuries during treatment.According to police, Baljit and his wife had been embroiled in a domestic dispute. Four to five months ago, she left her in-laws’ residence and had been staying at her parental home ever since.Station house officer of the Industrial Focal Point Purhiran police station, sub-inspector Rajesh Kumar, said an FIR was registered against Baljit under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita on Tuesday. Raids are being conducted to arrest the absconding accused.

headline: Govt set to devolve substantive powers, responsibilities to local bodies: Saini
content: Strap: Public health engineering, drinking water supply, fire services to be transferred in a phased mannerHaryana chief minister Nayab Singh Saini on Tuesday said the state government is set to take a major policy decision to devolve substantive powers and responsibilities to local bodies.Under this initiative, important responsibilities relating to public health engineering, drinking water supply and fire services will be transferred to local bodies in a phased manner in the coming years, Saini said while addressing the valedictory session of the two-day national sammelan on empowering panchayats and municipalities in Gurugram.Saini said that devolution of more powers will increase the decision-making capacity of local bodies and enable them to manage public services more effectively according to local requirements.He said sarpanches, panches, councillors, mayors and heads of local bodies are the true flag-bearers of democracy who have been entrusted with responsibilities by the people through elections. He said they must now prove through their work that the trust reposed in them was well placed.Saini said the government can provide resources and policies, but setting priorities, ensuring that the right works are undertaken at the right places and completing them on time are the responsibilities of elected representatives.Matching grant fund for local bodiesIn a move aimed at further strengthening the financial position of local bodies, the CM announced that an additional 2% fund of the State’s Own Tax Revenue (SOTR) will be made available as matching grants.He said urban local bodies (ULBs) and panchayati raj institutions will be able to access this additional funding on a competitive basis through their project proposals. At present, the state government allocates 7% of its own tax revenue to local bodies. Saini said developing their own revenue sources is essential for making local bodies self-reliant. “To encourage their efforts in this direction, the state government has decided to provide matching grants,” he said.Under this arrangement, the state government will provide a matching grant equivalent to the additional financial resources mobilised by a local body on its own. Every additional rupee raised by local bodies will thus be matched by the state government, enabling them to double the resources available for local development, he said.The CM also announced that the leadership of local bodies generating the highest own-source revenue in their respective areas will be rewarded.Teachings of Guru Nanak Dev a source of inspiration: CMSaini on Monday said the teachings of the first Sikh Guru, Guru Nanak Dev, were not limited to any one religion, society or period, but served as a source of inspiration for all humanity.Addressing a state-level function to mark the Guru Nanak Dev’s birth anniversary on Monday night in Yamunanagar’s Bilaspur town, Saini said, “Guru Nanak Dev imparted the message of truth, service, equality and harmony to society. Challenging the walls of casteism, discrimination and inequality, Guru Nanak declared that every human being is equal in this world created by God.The CM also attended a drone show showcasing Guru Nanak Dev’s message of truth, service and equality, Sri Guru Gobind Singh’s 52-day stay at Kapal Mochan in Bilaspur and the valour of Baba Banda Singh Bahadur.

headline: 2,300 Indian pilgrims join Gurpurb celebrations at Nankana Sahib
content: The 557th Parkash Purb (birth anniversary) of Guru Nanak was celebrated with great devotion at Gurdwara Janam Asthan at Nankana Sahib in Pakistan.A sacred procession of Guru Granth Sahib was also taken out from Gurdwara Janamasthan to Gurdwara Kiara Sahib in the city on Tuesday.More than 2,300 Sikh pilgrims from India joined thousands of local and foreign devotees in the celebrations at the birthplace of Guru Nanak. A two-member consular team from the High Commission of India in Islamabad also joined the Sikh pilgrims from IndiaTalking about the teachings of Guru Nanak, acting jathedar of Akal Takht Giani Kuldeep Singh Gargaj, who led the Indian jatha, said that today, the world was going through a cold war and needed peace and love more than ever.Stressing the significance of Nankana Sahib for Sikhs, Gargaj said that the Kartarpur Corridor should remain open. He said talks were underway about reopening the Kartarpur Corridor, and expressed hope that the government of India would open the corridor soon. He also reiterated the demand to open the Lahore Diwankhana.Hamza Shehbaz, former CM of West Punjab and son of Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif, was the chief guest. He said that the Kartarpur Corridor should remain open, and assured the gathering that Pakistan would welcome the Sikhs with open arms. “Your shrines are here, come and take care of them,” he added.

headline: Rebel TMC MPs submit reply to Lok Sabha, defend exit from party
content: Twenty rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs, who merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) in June, on Tuesday submitted its response to the disqualification notices served by the Lok Sabha secretariat after taking four extensions.A senior rebel TMC leader told HT that all 20 MPs have submitted their individual replies to the Lok Sabha secretariat. Drafted by lawyers, the replies are identical, an official said. In their reply, the rebel MPs defended their decision to quit the TMC and claimed that the move did not violate any parliamentary or constitutional provisions.A month after the TMC was defeated in the West Bengal assembly elections, 20 of the party MPs met Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and submitted a letter seeking their merger with the NCPI. TMC’s floor leader Abhishek Banerjee had filed petitions seeking the expulsion of the rebel MPs on grounds of defection.The TMC had argued that the Tenth schedule of the Constitution, only approves the merger of one political party with another, but it has no provision for a merger solely between two legislative units.Defending their decision to leave the party, rebel TMC leader Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar argued that they followed all parliamentary and constitutional norms.In the letters, the rebels highlighted that they constitute 20 of 28 TMC MPs, representing more than a two-thirds majority. They have maintained that their move does not attract disqualification under the anti-defection provisions.The submission comes on the last day of the deadline set by the Lok Sabha Secretariat for the MPs to respond to notices issued by Birla on petitions seeking their disqualification under the anti-defection law.“We have submitted our replies to the Lok Sabha Speaker and have defended our decision to join the NCPI,” Ghosh Dastidar said.According to a senior functionary, the rebels also cited the recent mergers of six Shiv Sena UBT MPs joining the Sena led by Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde and the merger of six Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) MPs with the BJP in the Rajya Sabha.The development marks a significant step in the ongoing proceedings before the Lok Sabha Speaker, who will examine the replies before deciding on the disqualification petitions.A section of the TMC believes that the issue will ultimately be settled in the Supreme Court, which is already hearing the Sena case and the AAP’s appeal.

headline: The Numbers Behind The Noise: Decoding Yogi Adityanath’s 1.27 Crore 'Missing' Voters Claim
content: A week back, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath stated that 1.27 crore Hindu voters in his state had gone ‘missing’ from the state’s electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). The remark immediately triggered scrutiny across political and administrative circles. Viewed purely as a critique of the electoral machinery, the claim appears counterintuitive for a sitting BJP chief minister. Examined through the lens of party’s electoral strategy, however, the intervention reveals a calculated effort to address organisational inertia, counter caste-based political mobilisation, and recalibrate the BJP groundwork ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections, even at the cost of creating friction with the Election Commission of India (ECI) and the party’s central messaging. In the process, he has placed both his party and the ECI in an uncomfortable bind. A Wake-Up Call Disguised As A Warning? Data from recent electoral cycles, the ground surveys by certain agencies in Uttar Pradesh have been highlighting a persistent structural challenge for the BJP, in terms of voter turnout and roll management in urban and semi-urban constituencies. Following the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, internal assessments pointed to gaps in booth-level verification, where residential migration and administrative cleanups disproportionately affect unmonitored voter segments. By citing specific figures, including vulnerabilities across 28 urban local body seats and a discrepancy of 66 lakh voters between state panchayat lists and Assembly rolls, Yogi Adityanath reframed a routine revision exercise into an urgent organisational priority. The immediate impact was visible within the party apparatus. Sources in the party said that the senior BJP leaders along with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and its linked frontal organisations quickly initiated a coordinated month-long verification drive to audit booth lists and submit Form 6 applications for re-enrolment. In this context, the 1.27 crore figure functions as a mobilisation tool designed to jolt complacent cadres into active field verification. Simultaneously, by linking ‘missing’ voters to demographic shifts and reiterating his ‘batenge toh katenge’ (divided, we will be cut) formulation, the chief minister seemed to have sought to neutralise the Samajwadi Party’s caste-consolidation strategy by foregrounding religious cohesion as the primary electoral determinant for 2027. Institutional Friction and Strategic Trade-Offs While the tactical objective was cadre activation, the statement generated significant collateral complications for both the ECI and the BJP’s national leadership. The Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer’s (CEO ) office clarified that official electoral databases do not capture caste or religious identifiers, noting that the removal of over two crore entries during the SIR stemmed from standard protocols governing duplicate records, permanent relocations, and deceased voters. This clarification exposed a divergence between the chief minister’s political framing and administrative reality. For months, the BJP had defended the integrity of the SIR process against opposition allegations of arbitrary deletions. Adityanath’s remarks inadvertently lent credence to claims that the revision had produced large-scale omissions, forcing party leaders into a delicate balancing act, acknowledging privately that the comments put the organisation in an awkward position while maintaining publicly that the ECI operates without bias. Opposition parties swiftly capitalised on the contradiction, questioning the methodology behind religion-specific deletion estimates and challenging the state government’s critique of an institution it routinely defends. Ultimately, the episode reflects a deliberate political trade-off. Yogi Adityanath’s intervention prioritises long-term electoral readiness, enforcing booth-level accountability and re-establishing a unified Hindutva narrative over short-term institutional alignment.

headline: Hotel’s master key no ground to absolve occupant of drug recovery: Supreme Court
content: A person occupying a hotel room or similar rented accommodation can be held responsible for narcotics or other contraband recovered from it, and the hotel management’s access to a duplicate key cannot, by itself, be grounds to exonerate the occupant, the Supreme Court has held.Setting aside the bail granted to a man accused of possessing cocaine and MDMA in a rented accommodation in Goa, a bench of justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said accepting the reasoning adopted by the Bombay High Court would mean that no recovery made from a hotel room could ever be attributed to its occupant. Hotel managements routinely retain duplicate keys and may enter rooms for cleaning and other purposes, the bench said.“If such a reasoning is accepted, then any recovery made from a hotel or a rental facility cannot be pinned on the person occupying the room,” the bench said in an order last week. The mere possibility of access by the facility manager was not enough to discredit the prosecution’s case at the bail stage, it added.The court was hearing an appeal by the Goa government against the high court’s decision to grant bail to the man, who was booked under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act after 50.03 grams of cocaine and 15.04 grams of MDMA (ecstasy) were allegedly recovered from an Airbnb property in Vagator in January, 2025.The high court had accepted the argument that the facility manager had unhindered access to the room and could have planted the contraband before the police raid. The accused had also claimed that he was picked up from the basement of the property, detained for two days and then taken to the room, where the drugs were planted. He further alleged that he was tortured in police custody and that the police had inflicted a burn injury on his hand.Rejecting these contentions, the Supreme Court said the material before it, including the counter-affidavit filed by the accused himself, prima facie undermined his defence and supported the prosecution’s account of the raid and recovery.The bench noted that the first information report and search warrant showed that the raiding officer had received reliable information on January 22, 2025, about narcotics activity allegedly being carried out by the accused from his room. The officer had informed his superior and obtained the requisite permission to conduct the search, besides securing the seal required for the seizure of contraband.The search was conducted in the presence of independent panch witnesses, an industries inspector and a lower division clerk, as well as the facility manager. The police also video-recorded the search and seizure, the court noted.On the question of who occupied the premises, the court examined the leave and licence agreement between the property owner and the facility manager, which permitted the manager to use the premises commercially and rent them out on a daily basis.The prosecution’s case, supported by the manager’s statement, was that the premises had been rented out to the accused from January 17 to January 26, 2025, the period during which the arrest and recovery took place. The court noted that the recovery was made while the commercial licence was in force and within the period for which the premises were allegedly let out to the accused.Finding no reason to sustain the high court’s order, the bench set it aside and directed the accused to surrender within three weeks. If he does not, he will be arrested and produced before the jurisdictional court to be taken into judicial custody, subject to any order that court may pass on police custody.

headline: New Ebola Vaccines Enter Trials As WHO Temporarily Relocates Teams Due To Insecurity In Congo
content: The head of the World Health Organization said Tuesday that health staff had been evacuated from a hospital in Democratic Republic of Congo after they spent three days sheltering there from fierce fighting. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said staff from the World Health Organization, the DR Congo's health ministry and other staff had left the hospital in Akwe in Ituri -- the province at the epicentre of the DRC's deadly Ebola outbreak. They had taken refuge there "amid fierce conflict for over three days" and have been evacuated "under very challenging circumstances." The UN health agency chief said that due to the increased insecurity, an Ebola team of WHO staff and partners had been temporarily relocated "until the situation calms". A total of 5,775 deaths out of 11,762 cases have been confirmed in the vast central African country's worst-ever Ebola outbreak, according to the WHO.

headline: Meghalaya Development Beyond Tourism
content: By Erwin K. Syiem Sutnga In his 23 November 2026 article for Highland Post, Jerry Pyrtuh argues that the Shillong Peak ropeway is a symptom of a development policy that favours tourism in the capital while starving essential sectors and other parts of Meghalaya. He is right to ask who benefits from public investment. But to answer that question, we must look beyond the most visible project in Shillong and examine what has actually reached the villages. On that test, the record under Conrad Sangma is broader than Pyrtuh allows. There are two questions here. Is the Shillong Peak ropeway justified on its own merits? And has the State neglected development outside tourism? Rural road building cannot answer the first question, just as objections to the ropeway cannot answer the second. Start with roads. In his 2026–27 Budget speech, the Chief Minister reported that more than 3,300 kilometres of roads had been completed under the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana over the preceding eight years, connecting 280 previously unconnected villages. A usable road can mean a shorter journey to a hospital, a more dependable route to school and a better chance of getting a crop to market. Where roads fail after the rains, the State must identify who is responsible for maintenance and publish a schedule for repairs. Rural housing also belongs in this assessment. A Lok Sabha reply dated 3 February 2026 records 1,55,930 completed PMAY-Gramin houses in Meghalaya. This is a cumulative total, not a count attributable wholly to the period since 2018. Credit belongs jointly to the Union, successive State administrations, implementing institutions and beneficiary households. The State Budget speech reports that more than Rs 9,100 crore flowed through the rural employment guarantee programme over eight years and that Jal Jeevan Mission had reached 83 per cent of rural households with tap connections. A connection is not the same as a reliable supply of safe water, just as expenditure under MGNREGA does not establish that wages arrived on time. The mission’s separate 2024 functionality assessment found that 68.2 per cent of sampled household tap connections in Meghalaya’s Har Ghar Jal villages met its functionality criteria. That is not a statewide connection rate, or a measure of service in 2026. It shows why the State should publish village-level results on the regularity and quality of supply. For rural employment, it should publish how long workers wait for wages. The spending record is also relevant. From the State’s budget documents, PRS Legislative Research records actual expenditure in 2024–25 of Rs 1,803 crore on health and family welfare, Rs 1,494 crore on rural development and Rs 1,065 crore on agriculture and allied activities. These are sums spent, not promises of future allocations. Those sums do not tell us how well the money was spent. But to argue that tourism crowded out essential sectors, one must show which priorities lost funding or were left unmet because of those choices. A highly visible project is not, on its own, evidence of that trade-off. The same applies to women’s economic institutions. A Union Rural Development Ministry reply published on 11 August 2026 lists 47,946 women’s self-help groups in Meghalaya under DAY-NRLM. The State Budget separately reports cumulative Community Investment Fund support of Rs 415 crore and credit linkage of Rs 756 crore. Credit is repayable finance and must not be described as a government grant. The relevant questions are whether these groups can obtain affordable finance, sustain their businesses and increase women’s control over earnings. Those are questions of everyday economic independence. An assessment centred almost entirely on tourists overlooks the rural women organising production, handling accounts and seeking markets through these institutions. There is also direct assistance to producers. On 22 September 2026, the State reported a FOCUS Plus instalment of Rs 2,500 each to about 1.14 lakh beneficiaries. A payment is evidence of financial assistance, not proof that a household has escaped poverty. It should be assessed for timeliness, inclusion and productive use. But it is plainly an intervention directed towards farming families. Agricultural processing offers a more concrete example. The Eastern Ri-Bhoi Organic Farmer Producer Company runs an organic spice processing facility at Bhoirymbong, inaugurated in June 2026. In October, the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) reported the flag-off of a Singapore-bound shipment of organic spices processed there. The roughly Rs 32 crore facility is designed to process about 10,000 tonnes a year. A shipment tells us more than an inauguration or a capacity figure. It does not yet establish a regular export trade. Farmers often sell their crops with little bargaining power while others capture the value of storage, processing and marketing. The test at Bhoirymbong is how much produce the plant buys from local farmers, what it pays them and how promptly it pays. If the facility can retain a greater share of the sale value in the villages that supply it, that is development worth measuring. IFAD’s March 2026 supervision report records Megha-LAMP reaching 1,72,501 households and forming 571 Integrated Village Cooperative Societies by December 2024. The project predates Conrad Sangma’s government, having been approved in 2014. Its continued implementation deserves recognition without rewriting that history. IFAD also found that only 186 of the village societies were profitable as of March 2025, against a target of 210. A society formed is not necessarily a society that can sustain itself. The figures tell us both the scale of the work and where it still falls short. In May 2025, the World Bank reported that the Meghalaya Community Led Landscape Management Project had worked with about 400 village communities, restored nearly 10,000 hectares of forest and rejuvenated 3,000 springs. The figures come from a financing partner, but they describe a specific body of work that should figure in any account of rural development. The achievement belongs substantially to the communities that carried out the work. Their experience should inform how we protect water sources elsewhere. Communities should have access to the underlying data and a role in deciding what happens to the springs and forests on which they depend. Restoration in one district is no substitute for protecting the catchment at Lum Shyllong. The State should publish the ropeway’s projected water demand, the proposed source of supply and its assessment of the impact on nearby springs, including in the dry season. Any restoration plan must include work within the affected catchment. Whether the project proceeds or not, the work of protecting the hill and its water sources remains. Health is another essential part of the record. The Meghalaya State Health Systems Resource Center’s May 2026 brief, using HMIS data, reports recorded maternal deaths falling from 244 in 2020–21 to 106 in 2025–26. These are administrative death counts, not the maternal mortality ratio, and they do not establish that one scheme alone caused the decline. The September 2026 health infrastructure review also reported more than 110 sub-centres completed over the preceding two years. Construction must be followed by staffing, medicines, referral transport and dependable services. The government should publish which of the completed centres have opened, their hours and the services available at each. In education, the government reported in September that more than 2,000 elementary government schools had received infrastructure improvements. That is worth recording, but it tells us little about classroom learning or whether sanctioned teaching posts are filled. The deficit-school teachers’ grievances over pay and retirement benefits need a substantive response. A meeting is not a settlement, and improvements to government school buildings are no answer to the service conditions of deficit-school teachers. The strongest reason to keep the focus on basic services is that rural deprivation remains widespread. NITI Aayog’s 2023 National Multidimensional Poverty Index puts the share of rural Meghalaya’s population experiencing multidimensional poverty at 38.49 per cent in 2015–16 and 32.43 per cent in 2019–21. The two survey periods show a fall in the share of people facing overlapping deprivations in health, education and living standards, but they do not establish today’s poverty rate or isolate the effect of one government. The Comptroller and Auditor General identified 777 outstanding utilisation certificates covering Rs 5,428.54 crore as at 31 March 2025. These certificates are how departments account for the use of grants. The State should publish a department-wise reconciliation showing how many have been furnished and verified since the audit cut-off, what amounts remain outstanding and when the balance will be accounted for. A progress report should also say what action was taken where departments repeatedly failed to account for grants. Pyrtuh’s treatment of hospitality also needs reconsideration. Colonial domination involved coercive political power and subordination. A local household choosing to operate a homestay, a farmer supplying food or a trained young person providing a paid service does not, merely by doing so, enter the same relationship. Commercial hospitality can involve exploitation, but that must be demonstrated through ownership, working conditions, bargaining power and the distribution of income. We should therefore insist on local ownership, fair remuneration, protection of community resources and the freedom to refuse unacceptable projects. We should also respect the freedom to participate in an enterprise. Describing service work as inherently servile risks diminishing the agency of the very people whose dignity the argument seeks to defend. Women protesting against the ropeway deserve to be heard. So do women investing their savings through self-help groups, women producing and marketing agricultural goods, and women seeking reliable maternity care. Their interests may overlap, and their views may differ. No single political position should be treated as the authentic voice of all rural or indigenous women. Tourism should operate within ecological limits. The case for supporting it is strongest where households and communities retain a real share of the income and have a say in how their land and water are used. But a tourism policy is not a rural development policy. Rural settlements need dependable roads, clean water, schools and clinics whether or not a single visitor comes. The strongest case for Conrad Sangma’s development record rests on the breadth of implementation beyond tourism: rural connectivity, housing delivery, producer support, women’s institutions, agricultural infrastructure, village conservation and public services. Much of this work depends on Central funding, programmes begun earlier and the effort of communities and public servants. Effective leadership includes sustaining and coordinating those contributions. Implementation matters, even when the original policy was inherited. The government must answer for defective work, delayed entitlements and projects whose costs exceed their public value. Critics must account for what has been delivered. The same test applies to a ropeway and to a village road: who benefits, who bears the cost and what can the public verify?

headline: Punjab Cong to release first list of candidates soon: Pilot
content: All-India Congress Committee (AICC) general secretary and Punjab in-charge Sachin Pilot on Tuesday said that the party was conducting surveys, and would soon announce its first list of candidates.He was speaking at the Punjab Congress’ state election committee meeting held to deliberate on the party’s election strategy, strengthen its organisation in the state, mobilise workers and highlight issues concerning the public.Pilot also urged party leaders to work collectively to safeguard the rights of the people of Punjab and strengthen the party’s organisational structure.Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee (PPCC) president Pargat Singh, who led the meeting along with Pilot, said the party had already begun systematic preparations for the elections. The first meeting of the state election committee marked an important step towards advancing preparations for the elections effectively, he added.Former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi, leader of opposition Partap Singh Bajwa, Rajinder Kaur Bhattal, Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa, Manish Tewari, Vijay Inder Singla, Amarinder Singh Raja Warring, Shamsher Singh Dullo, Amar Singh, Gurjeet Singh Aujla, Sher Singh Ghubaya and Dharamvira Gandhi also attended the meeting.The meeting focused on timely ticket distribution, balancing caste equations, and ways to curb dissent after ticket distribution. Detailed discussions on the party’s strategy for the 2027 assembly elections also focused on establishing direct contact with the people and chalking out the roadmap for campaigning.

headline: Punjab grappling with 42 lakh tonnes of legacy waste
content: Around 42.76 lakh metric tonnes (MT) of legacy waste is still lying untreated at dumping sites across Punjab, while 409 tonnes of fresh municipal garbage remains unprocessed every day, according to the latest compliance affidavit filed by the state government before the National Green Tribunal (NGT).This latest disclosure follows the NGT’s July-2024 direction asking Punjab to pay ₹1,000 crore in environmental compensation to the Central Pollution Control Board for alleged failures in managing legacy waste and untreated sewage. The Supreme Court stayed the tribunal’s order in September 2024.The affidavit, submitted by Punjab chief secretary KAP Sinha on November 14 and uploaded on the tribunal’s website on November 21, reveals that while Punjab processes nearly 91% of its daily municipal solid waste, the accumulated garbage and inadequate processing capacity continue to pose a serious environmental challenge.Of the cumulative 95.88 lakh MT of legacy waste at urban local body (ULB) dumping sites, only 53.12 lakh MT has been remediated, leaving 42.76 lakh MT untreated. While 126 of the state’s 166 ULBs have completed remediation, work remains underway in 40 others. The government has set January 2028 as the deadline to clear the remaining dumps.Legacy waste refers to garbage accumulated over several years at dumping sites. Its prolonged presence poses environmental and public health risks through leachate, landfill fires, foul odour and contamination of soil and groundwater.The NGT had earlier flagged the disposal of around 403 tonnes per day (TPD) of unprocessed mixed waste at landfill sites. It had identified Tarn Taran, Sangrur, Pathankot, Patiala, Ludhiana and Jalandhar among the urban local bodies contributing to the problem. The latest affidavit acknowledges a processing gap of 409 TPD, indicating that the challenge of managing fresh waste remains unresolved.Punjab’s 166 ULBs generate approximately 4,309 TPD of municipal solid waste, of which around 3,900 TPD (90.51%) is reportedly being processed. However, large accumulations of legacy waste continue to pose a challenge in Amritsar, Jalandhar, Ludhiana and Kharar, with the government claiming that focused interventions are underway at these sites.Gaps in biodegradable, recyclable waste managementThe affidavit also highlights deficiencies in the management of biodegradable and recyclable waste. Of the 2,291 tonnes of biodegradable waste generated per day, around 1,931 TPD is being processed through composting and other mechanisms.Similarly, material recovery facilities (MRFs) handle around 1,076 TPD of dry recyclable waste against the generated 1,717 TPD. The government has acknowledged a processing gap of approximately 253 tonnes per day after accounting for material recovered through other channels.Deputy commissioners and municipal commissioners are being directed to strengthen monitoring of waste collection, segregation and processing and ensure compliance with the tribunal’s directions.Sewage treatment another challengeWastewater management also remains a challenge in Punjab. The state generates around 2,286.91 million litres of sewage per day, but treats only 2,038.80 million litres per day (MLD), leaving a gap of 248.11 MLD.Of the 172 sewage treatment plants (STPs), 147 are reportedly complying with prescribed quality parameters, four are non-compliant, 19 are undergoing stabilisation, one is under maintenance and another is being upgraded.The government cited the commissioning of nine STPs, with a combined capacity of 45.50 MLD, between February and October this year. Another 37 plants, with a combined capacity of 206.40 MLD, are under construction, while proposals for 27 additional STPs, with a capacity of 127.73 MLD, are at the tendering or planning stage.

headline: BJP now complicit in Akali Dal’s anti-Sikh actions: SAD (Punar Surjit)
content: Shiromani Akali Dal (Punar Surjit) president and former Akal Takht Jathedar Giani Harpreet Singh on Tuesday accused the BJP of becoming complicit in the alleged anti-Sikh actions of the Sukhbir Singh Badal-led Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) by renewing their alliance.Giani Harpreet recalled the controversial pardon granted to Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh during the SAD government’s tenure, alleging that the leadership had extended political patronage to Ram Rahim and spent money from the ‘Guru’s Golak’ for publicising the pardon.He said Sukhbir had admitted the party leadership’s failures in handling sacrilege cases, including failure to recover the stolen saroop of Guru Granth Sahib and ordering arrests of those responsible for the alleged sacrilege, before the Akal Takht.These admissions formed the basis of the religious punishment pronounced against Badal by the five Sikh high priests, he said, alleging that Badal subsequently backtracked on his statements.Giani Harpreet said the BJP had compromised its claims of safeguarding Punjab’s interests by aligning with a leadership accused of betraying Sikh sentiments. He asserted that the people of Punjab would reject the alliance, and the electoral defeat of the SAD and the BJP would become a defining moment in the state’s political history.

headline: Waris Punjab De questions SAD, cites farmers’ issues
content: The Akali Dal (Waris Punjab De) on Tuesday questioned the ideological consistency of the Sukhbir Singh Badal-led Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) following the latter’s renewed alliance with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The party asked SAD whether the issues that prompted the Shiromani Akali Dal to snap ties with the BJP during the farmers’ agitation had been resolved.Addressing a press conference, Akali Dal (Waris Punjab De) working president Tarsem Singh, Sarabjit Singh Khalsa and Manpreet Singh Ayali questioned whether the BJP had changed its position on farmers and Punjab or the Badals had abandoned their earlier stand in pursuit of political power.They also sought an explanation on how SAD leaders would share a political platform with Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, who had leveled serious allegations against individuals close to the Badal family in connection with the sacrilege and police firing cases. They further questioned the party’s association with BJP leader Ravneet Singh Bittu, given its earlier opposition to him and his family.The leaders said political alliances were the prerogative of parties, but decisions contrary to their earlier positions called for accountability. Political power, they maintained, should not take precedence over Punjab and Panthic interests.Statewide membership driveSeparately, the Akali Dal (Waris Punjab De) launched a statewide membership campaign to build a broad-based political platform. The leaders appealed to farmers, labourers, traders, employees, students, women and youth to join the initiative. They said that Punjab was grappling with agrarian debt, unemployment, drug abuse and gangsterism, besides unresolved issues concerning river waters, natural resources and the state’s rights.Referring to the political movement initiated under jailed MP Amritpal Singh’s leadership, they said it aimed to steer youth away from drugs and reconnect them with Sikh values and the teachings of the Gurus. The party has also launched a helpline (60009060092), website (www.adwpd.com) and a mobile application, VAHEER, to facilitate enrolment.

headline: Mohali: Aam Aadmi Clinic services may face disruption as support staff strike
content: Patients visiting Aam Aadmi Clinics across Punjab may face delays and disruption as pharmacy officers, doctors and clinical assistants will stay away from work amid a state-wide protest on November 25.The Aam Aadmi Clinics Sanjha Front has called a protest and hunger strike over demands that include regularisation of services, higher incentives and insurance cover for employees.With pharmacy officers and clinical assistants absent, doctors are likely to shoulder additional responsibilities, including patient consultations and examinations. The absence of pharmacy staff could also affect the dispensing of medicines, while clinical assistants’ absence may disrupt registration and other support services. Elderly patients, pregnant women and those dependent on regular medication could face particular inconvenience.The employees said several rounds of discussions had been held with NHM mission director Sakshi Sahni, former director of health services Dr Hatinder and finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema. They claimed their demands had received in-principle approval, but no formal orders had been issued.Apart from regularisation, the front is seeking separate incentives for national health programmes, full payment for Sundays and public holidays, and a minimum payment equivalent to 75 patients a day, irrespective of actual OPD attendance. It has urged the chief minister to intervene.

headline: Modi, Sukhbir to share stage at first joint SAD-BJP rally in Moga on Dec 8
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will address a joint SAD-BJP rally in Moga on December 8, marking the first major show of strength by the reunited allies following Tuesday’s announcement of their partnership ahead of the 2027 Punjab assembly elections.Coinciding with the birth anniversary of former chief minister and Akali patriarch Parkash Singh Badal, the rally will see Modi and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal share a public platform after a gap of seven years. The gathering is expected to set the tone for the alliance’s campaign, with both parties aiming to showcase their combined cadre base.Sukhbir announced the rally while addressing a joint press conference with Union home minister Amit Shah at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi, where the two parties formally announced the revival of their alliance.The SAD had already begun preparations for the event at Moga’s Killi Chailan village, but the venue has now been shifted to the Moga grain market. Party vice-president Daljit Singh Cheema confirmed that preparations were being stepped up for a joint mobilisation exercise.“It will be a joint show with the alliance partner BJP and we will shortly hold a meeting to finalise preparations,” Cheema said.Modi and Sukhbir last shared a public platform on November 9, 2019, during the inauguration of the Kartarpur Corridor, when Parkash Singh Badal was also present.Earlier that day, the leaders had appeared together at Gurdwara Ber Sahib in Sultanpur Lodhi before heading to the Integrated Check Post at Dera Baba Nanak, from where Modi flagged off the first batch of pilgrims to PakistanThe very next year, SAD walked out of the alliance in September 2020 over the three farm laws. Three years later, Modi met the Badal family again in Chandigarh in April 2023 to offer condolences following Parkash Singh Badal’s death.
