headline: Why government has advised against using WhatsApp Web for sensitive work
content: The Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has advised against the use of WhatsApp Web for exchanging sensitive government, organisational and financial information, flagging cybersecurity risks associated with the browser-based version of the popular instant messaging platform. In an advisory, the National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU), which functions under the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), said that authenticated WhatsApp Web sessions could, under certain circumstances, be exploited by malicious actors to gain unauthorised access to users’ accounts. Such access could allow cybercriminals to read private messages, access group conversations and impersonate account holders to carry out financial fraud, phishing and other cyberattacks. The advisory comes amid the widespread use of WhatsApp as an informal channel of communication across government departments and private enterprises in India, including for the exchange of official documents. The security risks associated with WhatsApp Web WhatsApp Web allows users to access their accounts through an internet browser on a computer by linking it to their primary mobile device. Once authenticated, the browser can continue to access the account even when the user’s smartphone is not connected to the internet. While this allows for greater convenience, it also expands the potential points of vulnerability through which an account could be compromised. For instance, if a user accesses WhatsApp Web on a shared computer and leaves the account logged in, another person with access to the computer could potentially read their private conversations or send messages on their behalf. A computer infected with malicious software could also expose sensitive information accessible through the browser. This assumes significance in the context of financial fraud. A cybercriminal impersonating an account holder could exploit the trust of their colleagues, friends or family members to solicit money or confidential information. Importantly, the concerns flagged by the government do not necessarily point to a flaw in WhatsApp’s end-to-end encryption, which also extends to linked devices. While encryption protects messages from being intercepted and read during transmission, it cannot prevent someone with access to a compromised or unattended device from reading messages already decrypted on it. What the government has recommended “Government, organisational, financial, confidential or other sensitive information should preferably not be exchanged through WhatsApp Web sessions on computers,” the advisory said. The government has recommended that users manually log out of WhatsApp Web after every session, emphasising that merely closing the browser window or tab does not necessarily terminate an authenticated session. Users have also been advised against accessing their accounts on public or unfamiliar computers, including those at cyber cafes, hotels and public kiosks. Where the temporary use of WhatsApp Web is unavoidable, the government has recommended using a trusted computer in private or incognito browsing mode, followed by manually logging out. However, private browsing does not protect users against malicious software already installed on a computer. Users can also periodically review the list of devices linked to their WhatsApp accounts through the mobile application and remotely disconnect unfamiliar devices. The government has further recommended regularly updating operating systems, browsers and security software, avoiding downloads from untrusted sources, and remaining vigilant about any unusual activity on WhatsApp accounts.

headline: ‘Hyderabadi Biryani Aur Pulao Sad Gaye Hain’: Azam Khan Dismisses Owaisi-Chandrashekhar Tie-Up For UP Polls | Exclusive
content: “Wo zamane tab ke the jab main jail mein tha (Those were the days when I was in jail)!” That is how Samajwadi Party’s biggest Muslim face, Azam Khan, reacted when asked about the growing traction of Asaduddin Owaisi. Speaking exclusively with CNN-News18 in Rampur, Azam Khan completely dismissed the challenge from Owaisi and his alliance with Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad ‘Ravan’. Khan said that Muslim voters have stood, and will continue to stand, by the Samajwadi Party irrespective of new entrants like AIMIM. The comment came ahead of a grand joint rally by AIMIM and the Azad Samaj Party. Both Owaisi and Chandrashekhar ‘Ravan’ are scheduled to appear together in Lucknow on Thursday, November 26, to showcase their alliance for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls. Azam Khan, however, remained completely dismissive of the alliance’s prospects. “Hyderabadi biryani aur pulao dono sad gaye hain. Koi naya pakwan laaiye tab baat badhegi (Both Hyderabadi biryani and pulao have gone stale. Bring a new dish, only then will things move forward),” he commented. “People are very intelligent now. Earlier kids would fly kites, play kabaddi, kancha (marbles); now they play games on laptops and computers. They are aware of issues—of who is doing what. People are sensible enough to know who they should vote for,” Azam Khan said when pressed further about Owaisi throwing his hat into the UP election ring for Muslim votes. Azam also appeared defiant amid fresh notices from the Uttar Pradesh Police. Rampur police reportedly issued a fresh notice to the Samajwadi Party leader asking him to join a reinvestigation into a 2006–2007 case of alleged encroachment and demolition. When asked if he was worried that the multitude of cases could prevent him from contesting the upcoming polls, Azam said, “Mujhe chunav ladne se kaun mai ka laal rok sakta hai? Mera chunav meri cycle hai. Mera election meri cycle hai. Cycle ladegi, cycle jeetegi (Who on earth can stop me from contesting elections? My election is my cycle. The cycle will fight, the cycle will win).” Playing down the Enforcement Directorate (ED) investigation that led to his prolonged incarceration, Khan said, “ED apna kaam kar rahi hai, hum apna kaam kar rahe hain (The ED is doing its job, we are doing ours). You must have heard the comments made by judges in the Supreme Court and High Court. I have nothing to say after that.” Khan also took a dig at the establishment, alleging that an atmosphere of fear had been unleashed across the country. “Dar to hai. Agar hukmaran zalim ho, to log darte to hain. Aur wo dar hi hai jo log khamosh hain. Apne dil ki baat bata nahi rahe hain. Sirf chunav ke din apni baat kehte hain. To main hi nahi… dara hua to poora desh hai(There is fear, after all. If the ruler is tyrannical, people do get scared. And it is that very fear that keeps people silent. They aren’t speaking their hearts out; they only speak their minds on election day. So it’s not just me—the entire country is living in fear),” Azam Khan responded when asked if he feared further legal trouble and its impact on his political and personal life. “Samajwadi hain badi chhoti soch ke. Alawa cycle ke unhe kuch nazar hi nahi aata. Na motor ke baare mein sochte hain, na helicopter ke baare mein (Samajwadis are people of very modest thinking. Apart from the cycle, they don’t see anything else. They neither think about cars nor about helicopters),” Khan signed off when asked about what was personally at stake for him in the upcoming polls.

headline: 'Backstabbed Countless Devotees': BJP Fumes At Vijay's TVK Over Karthigai Deepam Row
content: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Wednesday accused Tamil Nadu’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government of “betraying” the people of the state and “backstabbing” countless devotees of Lord Muruga. His remarks came a day after the Karthigai Deepam lamp at Tamil Nadu’s Thiruparankundram Hill in Madurai was lit at the customary Uchipillayar Mandapam on Tuesday, November 24, despite a Supreme Court order permitting the ritual at the disputed Deepathoon stone pillar. In a post on X, BJP’s national spokesperson CR Kesavan wrote, “The TVK-Congress Government, which defied the SC order and prevented the lighting of the sacred Karthigai Deeepam at the Depathoon, has betrayed the Tamil people and backstabbed countless devotees of Lord Muruga.” He accused the TVK-Congress government of adopting a “discriminatory” approach and “gravely insulting” the sentiments of crores of Hindu devotees. “The discriminatory TVK-Congress government has gravely insulted the sentiments of crores of Hindu devotees by humiliating and demeaning them as second-class citizens. The TVK -Congress Govt led by Mr. Joseph Vijay is nothing but a bigoted clone of the erstwhile DMK Govt when it comes to abusing and crushing Hindu faith to peddle their vote bank politics of communal appeasement”, Kesavan said. The TVK-Congress Government which defied the SC order and prevented the lighting of the sacred Karthigai Deeepam at the Depathoon,has betrayed the Tamil people and backstabbed countless devotees of Lord Muruga The discriminatory TVK-Congress government has gravely insulted the sentiments of crores of Hindu devotees by humiliating and demeaning them as second-class citizens. The TVK -Congress Govt led by Mr. Joseph Vijay is nothing but a bigoted clone of the erstwhile DMK Govt when it comes to abusing and crushing Hindu faith to peddle their vote bank politics of communal appeasement. The people of Tamilnadu and devotees of Lord Muruga will never forget nor forgive the TVK-Congress Govt for their prejudiced politics of polarization. The intolerant TVK-Cong regime will meet the same dismal fate as the DMK. — C.R.Kesavan (@crkesavan) November 25, 2026 “The people of Tamilnadu and devotees of Lord Muruga will never forget nor forgive the TVK-Congress Govt for their prejudiced politics of polarization. The intolerant TVK-Cong regime will meet the same dismal fate as the DMK”, he added. What Is The Controversy? Hindu organisations and many devotees have been demanding that the annual lamp-lighting ritual, known as the Karthigai Deepam, be held at the Deepathoon, a stone pillar on the upper reaches of Thiruparankundram Hill, which is located about 50 metres from the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya Dargah. However, the Tamil Nadu government has opposed the move, citing concerns over communal harmony and law and order issues. On November 20, the Supreme Court granted permission for the ceremonial lamp to be lit at Deepathoon on November 24 as a one-time arrangement. Subsequently, the state government filed a review petition. On Tuesday, the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court also directed the district administration, police and temple authorities to follow the Supreme Court order. Despite the apex court’s intervention, the annual lamp was lit at the customary Uchipillayar Mandapam, triggering a political row between the BJP and the TVK-Congress government.

headline: From the Urdu Press: ‘Why Sonia Gandhi’s memoir has put her opponents on back foot’
content: From the Rajasthan panchayat election results to the upcoming Assembly elections in states like Uttar Pradesh and Punjab. The Urdu dailies have turned their lens on a fresh election season, reading in the BJP's setback in the Rajasthan rural polls a larger challenge for the ruling party. The dailies also put a spotlight on the seat-sharing negotiations between the Opposition INDIA bloc allies, Samajwadi Party and Congress, for the UP elections which may define national politics in the coming months. SIASAT Referring to Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, the Hyderabad-based Siasat, in its November 20 editorial, points out that the book has become a bestseller, setting publishing records. Sonia’s book on the story of her life and the Gandhis, weaving personal with political with candour, has set off conversations and debates in various circles, drawing both praises and criticism, the editorial says. The memoir’s account of several watershed developments, which have shaped the history and politics of modern India, is of remarkable significance, it notes. “Sonia Gandhi has said that she was reluctant to write the book but was persuaded to do so by her children Rahul and Priyanka besides some family friends. She says various misconceptions about the Gandhi family have been spread over the decades and that she decided to write her memoir to tell its story and set the record straight. She has also welcomed criticism of her book, which reflects her generous character.” The daily states that stung by Sonia’s book, some quarters have been going after her without having read it. “The Congress leader's political opponents, including trolls and a section of TV anchors, have sought to tear into her book. This is part of their cynical propaganda, which is not based on a valid critique of the book based on its thorough, objective reading,” it says. There has been a tradition of dissent in the country, which has always been respected, the edit notes. “However, the attacks on Sonia’s book by her detractors have been driven by political reasons, which betray their frustration and intellectual bankruptcy,” it adds. URDU TIMES Pointing to the BJP’s debacle in the Rajasthan panchayat elections, which saw the Congress registering a resounding win in the Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad polls across the state, the Mumbai-based Urdu Times, in its November 21 editorial, says that these results should be a wake-up call for the BJP as it indicates a significant anti-incumbency. “While the BJP leaders have claimed that their party would rule the country for 50 years, political arrogance often backfires,” it says, adding that like other arenas in life a political system is also marked by the rise and fall of its players. The daily points out that in the Rajasthan rural polls the Congress made inroads into the turfs of several BJP heavyweights including ministers and their family members. While Rajasthan is due for the Assembly polls in November 2028, the coming few months would witness elections in some major states including UP and Punjab, it notes. “The BJP’s trump card has been its politics of polarisation, which seems to be losing steam now. There seems to be discontent among various backward and vulnerable communities in UP, where the INDIA bloc allies are holding talks for a seat-sharing pact,” the edit says. “Former Congress chief minister Ashok Gehlot has also said that the countdown for the BJP’s exit from power has begun.” SIASAT Commenting on the Supreme Court’s order suspending the life sentence of two convicts in the Bilkis Bano case and granting them bail, Siasat, in its November 18 leader, says the case has remained one of the most heinous crimes convulsing humanity. During the 2002 Gujarat communal riots, Bilkis, then a young pregnant woman, was gang-raped and seven of her family members, including a three-year-old daughter, killed, in which 11 accused were convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment. The editorial points out that in August 2022, the Gujarat government had released the 11 convicts under its remission policy. Bilkis challenged it in the apex court, which in January 2024 quashed their remission, sending the convicts back to the prison. “The SC ruling suspending the sentence of two of the convicts has terrified and shocked Bilkis Bano, who has vowed to challenge it. She has asked how could the court pass such an order without informing and hearing her. She believes that she should have been issued a notice and allowed to make her submission before the court while hearing an appeal by the convicts,” the daily states, adding that Bilkis along with her family has now moved out of Gujarat as she has been feeling “unsafe” following the release of the two accused. The editorial says that there have been allegations that the government’s counsel had not argued effectively to oppose the convicts’ pleas in the court. The suspension of their sentence may also pave the way for the release of other convicts on bail, it notes. “This would not only put a question mark over the process of justice but also cast a shadow on the roles of the government’s law enforcement agencies and public prosecution in the Bilkis case,” the edit says, adding that the government should promptly take effective measures to address such concerns.

headline: In Amethi and Rae Bareli, Congress has the legacy, Samajwadi Party has the numbers
content: If offering just 26 seats was not enough, the Samajwadi Party (SP) has left the Congress even more livid by including just one Assembly seat from the Lok Sabha constituencies of Amethi and Rae Bareli — the pocket borough of the Gandhis — in its initial offer. The electoral history of the 10 Assembly constituencies which make up the two parliamentary seats offers a window into why the SP may have been reluctant to offer more in the region. However, later that day, in a note posted on X, SP president Akhilesh Yadav told the Congress that his party remains open to discussing seats and that winnability should drive the negotiations. Electoral history The Congress's claim to the Assembly seats in the region rests largely on its long political association with the Gandhi family. Rahul Gandhi’s uncle Sanjay Gandhi, father Rajiv Gandhi, mother Sonia Gandhi, and the Leader of Opposition (LoP) himself have represented Amethi, while Rae Bareli has been represented by former PM Indira Gandhi, Sonia, and now Rahul. The two constituencies have remained central to the party's political identity in Uttar Pradesh. However, the Assembly election history presents a very different picture. The Congress failed to win even one of the 10 Assembly constituencies in the 2022 elections, in which the party’s campaign was helmed by Rahul Gandhi’s sister and current Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. The SP won six, while the other four went to the BJP. A closer look at the election history of these 10 seats shows that 2007 was, in many ways, the last significant electoral high for Congress in the region. Several Assembly seats that the party had won over successive elections, including Bachhrawan, Sareni, and Amethi, are among those where its last victory came in 2007. In other constituencies, such as Harchandpur and Rae Bareli, the Congress managed a victory in 2017, but failed to sustain its presence. Since 2012, the electoral contest in most of these constituencies has increasingly shifted to the SP and BJP. The SP consolidated its position in Amethi, Gauriganj, Bachhrawan, Harchandpur, Sareni and Unchahar, while the BJP made inroads in Rae Bareli, Bachhrawan and Sareni at different points. The 2017 hope The 2017 Assembly elections briefly offered the Congress some hope, with the party winning Harchandpur and Rae Bareli, but these gains proved temporary. By 2022, the party had been pushed out of the electoral contest altogether. For Akhilesh Yadav, the argument is not about the Gandhi family's historical association with Amethi and Rae Bareli, but about the political reality on the ground, according to party insiders. The SP has emerged as the principal challenger to the BJP across much of this belt, while the Congress has struggled to establish a viable Assembly-level presence. The picture in Amethi The five Assembly constituencies under Amethi — Amethi, Gauriganj, Jagdishpur, Salon and Tiloi — illustrate the gradual erosion of Congress's influence. In the Amethi Assembly seat, the Congress's Ameeta Singh last won in 2007. In 2012, the seat went to SP leader and former minister Gayatri Prajapati. The BJP captured it in 2017, and in 2022 it returned to the SP, with Gayatri Prajapati's wife contesting as the party candidate. Gauriganj has been another important constituency for the SP. Rakesh Pratap Singh won the seat three consecutive times since its formation in 2012. However, after being expelled from the SP for anti-party activities, he moved closer to the BJP. The remaining constituencies also reflect the Congress's limited Assembly presence in the region. The party has struggled to convert the Gandhi family's political association with Amethi into electoral victories there. Rae Bareli: SP's stronger claim The five Assembly constituencies under Rae Bareli — Bachhrawan, Harchandpur, Rae Bareli, Sareni and Unchahar — provide an even stronger explanation for the SP's position. Bachhrawan, a reserved constituency, was once a Congress stronghold. The party won it straight from 1967 to 1991 and got it back in 2007 with the win of Raja Ram Tyagi. But the SP won in 2012, the BJP in 2017 and the SP again in 2022. Harchandpur and Rae Bareli offer an interesting account of Congress's brief revival in 2017 and how it subsequently lost even that ground. The Congress's Rakesh Singh won Harchandpur and Aditi Singh captured the Rae Bareli Assembly seat in 2017. However, both subsequently shifted to the BJP. While Aditi Singh retained Rae Bareli in 2022 as a BJP candidate, Singh lost Harchandpur to the SP's Rahul Rajpoot. The contrasting fortunes of the two former Congress MLAs underline how the party's limited Assembly-level revival in the Gandhi family's backyard was subsequently absorbed by the BJP in one constituency, while the SP consolidated its position in the other. Sareni, too, has increasingly become an SP stronghold. The Congress last won the constituency in 2007, with Ashok Kumar Singh winning the seat. The SP returned in 2012 with Devendra Pratap Singh, the BJP in 2017, and the SP reclaimed it in 2022. Unchahar has been represented by Manoj Kumar Pandey since its creation in 2012. He won three consecutive elections on an SP ticket before defecting to the BJP. Lok Sabha legacy versus Assembly reality The contrast between the two levels of elections is at the heart of the disagreement. The Gandhi family's association with Amethi and Rae Bareli has given Congress a political and symbolic advantage that few other constituencies in Uttar Pradesh can match. Rahul Gandhi's victory from Rae Bareli and the party's victory in Amethi in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections further reinforced this association, though Rahul’s loss from Amethi in 2019 had underlined that the family’s grip had slipped. Moreover, these victories came in an alliance with the SP and do not necessarily reflect the Congress's independent organisational strength in these constituencies. For Akhilesh Yadav, therefore, the question is not how long the Gandhi family has represented these Lok Sabha constituencies, but how many Assembly seats Congress can realistically win on its own. With the SP having won six of the 10 seats in 2022, it claims to have a stronger electoral argument for retaining most of the constituencies. There is also a local leadership question. Giving seats to the Congress would mean potentially overlooking SP leaders and aspirants who have built their political bases over several elections. In constituencies such as Gauriganj, where the party is dealing with the fallout of a former MLA's expulsion and political realignment, the stakes are even higher. The Congress, meanwhile, wants to use its 2024 Lok Sabha revival to regain political space in UP and rebuild its organisation ahead of the 2027 elections. A token allocation in a region historically associated with the Gandhi family would underline the extent of its dependence on the SP. More than a strained relationship between allies, the offer of just one seat, Jagdishpur, reflects the changing balance of power in a region where the Congress continues to enjoy a formidable Lok Sabha legacy, but the SP has acquired a much stronger Assembly-level presence.

headline: Policy upgraded hours before transit? Insurer told to pay Rs 14.6L
content: Chandigarh: The Chandigarh District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has directed an insurance company to pay Rs 14.6 lakh to a city-based apple trader whose insurance claim for damaged goods was rejected after a road accident.The commission also ordered the insurer to pay 9% annual interest along with Rs 30,000 as compensation for mental harassment and Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses.The case concerns Jaswinder Singh, a 59-year-old apple merchant from Chandigarh, who had taken an insurance policy to cover apples and pears transported by road across India.According to the complaint, Singh already had an insurance policy valid from July 21, 2023, to March 31, 2024. On Aug 12, 2023, he paid an additional premium of Rs 24,780 to increase his insurance cover by Rs 1 crore.The insurer subsequently issued an enhanced policy showing a total insured amount of Rs 1 crore, with a maximum limit of Rs 20 lakh per vehicle.The dispute arose when a truck carrying Singh’s apple consignment met with an accident on Aug 16, 2023, causing extensive damage to the goods. After a survey and inspection, the trader sought compensation for his losses.However, the insurance company rejected the claim arguing that the consignment had been loaded and weighed at 3:31pm on Aug 12, while the enhanced policy became effective only at 7:03pm that day. The company maintained that the journey had started before the insurance cover came into force.The commission, however, found gaps in the insurer’s argument. It noted that the insurer had failed to produce reliable evidence, including a fresh insurance proposal form, to establish that the Aug 12 transaction was for an entirely new policy rather than an enhancement of the existing cover.The commission also examined transport records. While one weighing receipt mentioned 3:31pm, another receipt showed the loaded truck was weighed at 7:38pm, after the policy became effective. A toll plaza record further showed that the vehicle crossed a toll point around 7:51pm, approximately two kilometres from the loading location.These records weakened the insurer’s claim that the insured transit had begun before the policy started. The commission held that rejecting the claim on such a technical interpretation amounted to deficiency in service and an unfair trade practice.While the trader had claimed Rs 14.8 lakh, the commission accepted the surveyor’s assessed loss of Rs 14.6 lakh.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. headline: A stir and an assurance: Protesting staff get impromptu hearing from new J&K chief secretary
content: Protesting paramedical and other non-gazetted employees at the Government Medical College (GMC), Rajouri, on Tuesday stopped the cavalcade of Jammu and Kashmir's newly appointed Chief Secretary Dr Sajjan Singh Yadav — during his maiden official visit to the border district. Yadav, however, stepped out of his car to talk with the protesters and personally assure them of finalisation of their long-pending service rules within a month. Yadav, who took over as Chief Secretary of J&K last week, had come to GMC, Rajouri, to review the facilities. While he was leaving the campus, the protesting employees stopped his cavalcade. After the employees apprised the chief secretary of prolonged uncertainty over their career progression, the latter told them that though he had assumed charge of the office only three days ago, he was aware of the issue and had discussed it with the Secretary, Health and Medical Education Department. Pointing out that the service rules have been forwarded to the Finance Department for approval, he said these will thereafter require nod from ARI (Administrative Reforms, Inspections) and Training Department and vetting from Law Department, before being submitted to the Lieutenant Governor for final go-ahead. Yadav assured the protesters that he would personally intervene in the matter, adding he would convene a meeting of all the departments concerned within the next 24 hours to expedite the approval process. The entire process would be completed within a month and recruitment rules notified accordingly, he said, appealing to the staff to suspend their agitation and resume duties. Nearly 3,000 paramedical and other non-gazetted employees in all the five medical colleges established in J&K in 2019 are on a strike since November 16. Besides Rajouri, protests are underway at the newly established medical colleges at Anantnag, Baramulla, Doda, and Kathua. The protesting staff have alleged that prolonged delay of seven years in finalisation of their service rules after their recruitment in 2019 has not only stalled their career progression, but also affected fresh recruitment in these institutions, ultimately impacting the healthcare services and patient care. Medical services hit With resident doctors also holding separate protests demanding an increase in their monthly stipend, the continued agitation of non-gazetted employees has adversely hit the medical and patient care services in GMCs in the five districts. Nadeem Ahmed Mir, one of the members of the coordination committee of non-gazetted employees of all the five medical colleges spearheading the agitation, said the committee members will hold a meeting on Tuesday to discuss the assurance given by the chief secretary. However, the agitating employees were wary of calling off their agitation as the earlier assurance given to them by Health Minister Sakeena Itoo regarding formulation of their service rules by September 30 had remained unfulfilled, he said. “Even after the expiry of the deadline fixed by her, the employees maintained patience for more than a month and went on strike only last week when they felt that nothing was forthcoming from the government,” he added. About the new CS Yadav, a Harvard graduate public health expert and a 1995-batch AGMUT cadre IAS officer, has been visiting various places in the Union Territory, after taking over as new Chief Secretary of J&K on November 18. A day after assuming charge, he had his first field inspection by visiting various areas of Jammu city, including Raghunath Bazar, Bahu Plaza and Apsara Road High Street in Gandhi Nagar. He also visited the Tawi Riverfront Development Project and reviewed beautification, infrastructure upgrades and sanitation works carried out under the Jammu Smart City Mission. On November 22, he inspected M A Stadium and Khel Gaon at Nagrota and interacted with the athletes and the coaches, directing sports bodies to maximize Khelo India and Fit India initiatives to upgrade training facilities and foster a stronger sporting culture.

headline: TOI ground report: Illegal groundwater extraction rampant across Cyberabad
content: Hyderabad: The city’s acute water shortage has fuelled the rampant illegal extraction and commercial sale of groundwater across the Cyberabad region. When TOI visited the area, on Tuesday, it found multiple operators openly engaged in the practice -- equipped with heavy machinery and elaborate surveillance systems.At several locations, groundwater was being extracted using high-powered motors, stored in underground sumps and pumped directly into private tankers stationed at the sites for commercial sale. Several such operations were found near lakes, in agricultural fields and even within residential neighbourhoods.Under the Telangana WALTA Act, 2002, the extraction of groundwater for commercial sale is prohibited in over-exploited areas, residential localities and recharge zones where such activity depletes public or private water sources and adversely affects domestic water supply. Yet, a majority of the private operators found by TOI were extracting groundwater from residential areas or locations falling within lake buffer zones.Just a few metres from Thammidikunta lake in Hi-Tec City, recently inaugurated by Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy, several water tankers were found operating along Hitex Road, transporting groundwater extracted from the area. Tankers were seen moving in and out continuously, while high-powered motors had been installed to draw groundwater. The extraction activity was found to be taking place within the lake’s buffer zone.A little off the Outer Ring Road, in Vattinagulapally, TOI spotted groundwater being drawn using motors near agricultural fields and channelled into a sump before being transferred into private tankers. At another location along Vattinagulapally main road, behind a petrol pump, operators were found filling private tankers with groundwater. A makeshift shelter had been erected at the site to house the motors, sump and other equipment used for the operation.Similar operations were found in Tellapur, where at least four groundwater extraction points were identified. Some operators had converted tent house shops into extraction facilities, while others had erected makeshift huts around pipelines, motors and pumping equipment to keep the operations out of sight. Osmannagar, too, has witnessed similar activity, with extraction points equipped with pipelines, motors and electricity meters set up along roadsides.What is particularly striking is the elaborate surveillance maintained by some operators. Several extraction points had as many as 20 to 30 CCTV cameras to monitor their premises and keep a close watch on movement in the surrounding areas. When TOI tracked some tankers leaving these extraction points, they were found heading towards commercial and residential hubs in Gachibowli and Hi-Tec City.Residents rue groundwater depletionResidents of several localities alleged that large-scale extraction was depleting the groundwater table. “Despite recent enforcement operations, groundwater extraction reportedly continues at certain locations. At Divine Space residential community, for instance, residents alleged that operators were continuing to extract groundwater illegally, affecting borewell levels in the surrounding area. Recently, we staged a protest demanding that the operators stop the activity,” said E Ramana, president of the Tellapur Neighbourhood Association.Residents also claimed that much of the groundwater extraction and supply happened late at night, making it difficult for them to monitor the operations.Quality questionedApart from groundwater depletion, residents have raised concerns over the quality of water supplied through private tankers.“Tanker operators often claim that the water is sourced from rivers and treated or purified before being supplied to consumers. However, when we paid around Rs 4,000 for private tankers and subsequently got the water tested through third-party agencies, nearly 80% of the samples tested so far turned out to be borewell water,” said Dr Sai Ravi Shanker, president of the Federation of Gated Communities Cyberabad.HYDRAA to declare water pressure zonesOfficials of the Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA) said that, given the dependence of hostels, hotels and commercial establishments on private water tankers, certain exemptions had been extended to facilitate water supply.“However, we are looking at stricter restrictions in areas facing severe groundwater depletion. We recently asked the groundwater department to identify colonies and localities where groundwater levels have fallen sharply. Based on the department’s assessment, we will notify such localities as ‘water pressure zones’, where groundwater extraction will be completely prohibited,” said AV Ranganath, commissioner, HYDRAA.He added: “Extraction points found operating in these notified areas would face immediate enforcement action, including sealing of facilities.”You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. headline: Toxic fumes kill 3 in septic tank; contractor arrested
content: Hyderabad: Three young workers cleaning a septic tank at a gated residential complex in Bachupally died after allegedly inhaling toxic gases on Tuesday, with police arresting the contractor who had engaged them and probing whether mandatory safety measures were ignored.The tragedy occurred at Dinesh Auric Apartments when one of the workers reportedly developed breathing difficulties after entering the septic tank. The other two went in to rescue him but were also overcome by suspected toxic fumes. All three died.The deceased were identified as K Shanmukh Rao (24), Suresh (25) and Yella Pawan (25). The three hailed from Kotabommali in Srikakulam district of Andhra Pradesh and had been living in Hyderabad for the past 10 years, earning their livelihood through septic tank cleaning work.Bachupally police rushed to the apartment complex after being alerted, retrieved the bodies and shifted them to Gandhi Hospital for postmortem examination. A case was registered and an investigation launched.Bachupally inspector P Dali Naidu said: “Preliminary findings suggested that toxic gases accumulated inside the septic tank had caused the workers to suffocate. The exact cause of death would be established through postmortem reports and further investigation.“Police were also examining whether the workers had been provided with adequate protective equipment, whether the gas levels inside the tank were tested before cleaning began, and whether mandatory safety procedures were followed.The role of the apartment management in allowing the work to be carried out is also under examination.Police identified the contractor who engaged the workers as Pallalappa DC Ravi (33), a Bengaluru native currently residing at Chitrapuri Colony. He was arrested under BNS provisions relating to negligence and endangering the personal safety of others.The deaths also triggered tension at the apartment complex after family members of the workers arrived there. They alleged that the bodies had been shifted to Gandhi Hospital without informing them and that security personnel prevented them from entering the complex.Heated arguments followed between the families, residents and security personnel, and a minor scuffle was reported before the situation was brought under control.The incident has once again put the spotlight on the deadly risks associated with hazardous manual cleaning of septic tanks and sewers.The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013, prohibits hazardous manual cleaning of sewers and septic tanks without prescribed protective equipment and safety procedures and provides for penal action for violations.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. headline: Capital crusaders: As police pushes rewards for flagging violations, Delhi residents turn traffic monitors
content: Twenty-six-year-old Aftab Ahmed works at a private telecom company in north Delhi’s Roop Nagar. But for the past year, every free minute – even during his lunch breaks – armed with his mobile phone, he steps down from the office to photograph and record motorists jumping red lights, riding without helmets, driving on the wrong side and flouting other traffic rules. He then uploads the photos as evidence on Delhi Police’s Traffic Prahari app.Ahmed says he joined the app after a friend lost her life at the age of 28 in a road crash in west Delhi’s Paschim Vihar. He believes that the tragedy could have been averted had his friend, who was on a bike, been wearing a helmet. “Instead of remaining a silent witness to such dangers on Delhi’s roads, I decided to do something about it. Another friend of mine told me about the app,” said Ahmed.His efforts, aside from being a public service, have also yielded monetary benefits – till March this year, he says he has earned more than ₹2 lakh from the rewards received for reporting violations on the app.B.Tech student 21-year-old Mohammad Faizan had seen a number of accidents in his neighbourhood, northeast Delhi’s Bhajanpura, caused by wrong-way driving and riding a bike without a helmet. Faizan said he told traffic personnel deployed in the area multiple times about the violations. However, his complaints did not yield long-term results and he was often scolded by the personnel, and even locals.“In August last year, a traffic police official asked me to become a traffic crusader instead of just raising complaints about the problems in the area. My frequent reporting has resulted in a dip in traffic violations in Bhajanpura and Yamuna Vihar,” said Faizan, who has earned ₹15,000 from his time on the app.Becoming a sentinelDelhi Traffic Police launched the smartphone-based app “Traffic Sentinel” in December 2015, allowing registered users to report 11 common traffic violations to the traffic police — driving against the flow of traffic, yellow line violation, parking on footpath, triple riding, defective number plate, driving without seatbelt, riding a two-wheeler without helmet, stop line violation, red light jumping, dangerous/zig zag driving, and using mobile phone while driving.The scheme was re-launched as “Traffic Prahari” on September 1, 2024. The aim, deputy commissioner of police (traffic) SK Singh said, was to empower citizens to inculcate road discipline among drivers. According to traffic police data, the app has more than a million (1,081,687) registered users as of October 31 and hundreds of challans are generated from their contributions every day.The process is relatively simple: a Traffic Prahari has to take a clear photograph or video of the vehicle involved in a traffic violation. They then have to upload it to the Prahari App, clearly mentioning the type of traffic violation being reported, date, time and place and exact location of the recorded violation, as well as the registration details of the vehicle.“Every reported violation is scrutinised by the Delhi Traffic Police personnel at the enforcement centre at traffic police’s headquarters in Todapur. If violation is found correct, then a notice and challan number is generated, otherwise violation is rejected with reason,” the DCP said.On their end, once traffic police receive a report, a notice under section 133 of the Motor Vehicles Act is issued to the registered owner of the vehicle.“The alleged violator is provided the option to compound the offence within a stipulated time period. If the violator does not respond to the notice, a court challan is issued against the registered owner of the offending motor vehicle and sent to the court for initiating further legal proceedings under the relevant provisions of law,” said a senior officer.A traffic sentinel may be called in the court for testimony only where the offender challenges the reported traffic violation.“However, such types of cases are rare. A traffic sentinel cannot be summoned by any other authority,” the second officer added. There are no criminal or civil liabilities. A total of 2,46,842 traffic violations had been reported till October 31 this year, up from 1,18,249 last year in the same period.The rewardFor each successful report for a certain violation, the user is also awarded points. These points can be added up to earn cash prizes and commendation certificates.For instance, a wrong-side driving violation earns a user five points, while three points each is awarded for uploading a video of red-light jumping, dangerous or zig-zag driving, and using mobile phones while driving. Each Yellow line violation or parking on footpath report earns two points. One point each is given for the remaining five violations.The top four traffic sentinels who earn the most points every month get cash prizes of ₹50,000, ₹25,000, ₹15,000, and ₹10,000 depending on their position. The reward encourages public participation in policing the city’s roads and creating awareness among commuters, said additional commissioner of police (traffic) Dinesh Kumar Gupta.“I have earned more than 10,000 points on the app since I joined the initiative. The accumulated points earned me ₹2 lakh until March this year,” said Ahmed.The riskWhile the role is voluntary and the process is relatively simple, it has its own risks and threats.“A while back, a person claiming to be a Delhi Police head constable called me over a traffic challan that was generated because of the evidence I uploaded to the app. I don’t know how he found out about me,” recalled Ahmed, adding that the man disconnected the call after Ahmed threatened to report him to the police.A senior police officer said details of registered praharis are not disclosed to anyone or anywhere. “There is a possibility that persons making the threatening calls impersonated police personnel,” added the officer.30-year-old Prince Bera, an IT consultant who lives in Uttam Nagar, said he too had faced threats and violence from commuters who spotted them recording their traffic violations.People, he said, do not believe in the authority they get from the app alone since no identity cards have been issued to them. They also rarely get any assistance from police personnel when they are facing pushback in public.“Earlier public representatives were issued identity cards but they were widely misused, forcing the department to discontinue the scheme. However, any Traffic Prahari facing issues in public can approach a traffic police official or the local police for assistance,” the officer quoted above said.Despite this, the sentinels continue to report violations. Atul Kumar Bhatia, 41, a corporate sales manager who joined six months ago, said he was motivated to do this by the news of various accidents. “Breaking traffic rules in Delhi is very common but the violators don’t realise that one bad decision can cause life-long suffering for loved ones.”

headline: Before polls, UP chief election officer flags slow voter enrolment in Noida, Gr Noida
content: At a late-evening meeting attended by Uttar Pradesh Chief Election Officer Navdeep Rinwa and other election officials in Noida on Monday , senior officers flagged the poor performance of the Gautam Buddha Nagar district in the last seven days in terms of voter enrolment, The Indian Express has learnt. According to a senior state election officer, while Gautam Buddha Nagar, where Noida and Greater Noida are located, lags behind, Ghaziabad, the neighbouring district, performed better. This comes as the state is expected to hold Assembly elections next year in February. The UP draft electoral roll was published on November 17 as part of a Special Summary Revision exercise, registering an addition of 18.84 lakh voters to the list. Gautam Buddha Nagar district logged a rise of 22,346 voters, compared with the final roll published following a Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, on April 10 this year. In Ghaziabad, 61,235 new voters registered. The seven days that followed were closely watched across districts, when claims and objections were filed, officers said. The performance was assessed based on two indicators — the number of Form 6 received per polling station in the district and inclusion of potential voters in the electoral roll. In the last seven days, an officer said, about 20 forms were filled at each of Ghaziabad’s 3,000-odd polling booths, while at Gautam Buddha Nagar, an average of six forms were filled at each of its 1,926 polling stations. In this parameter, out of the total 75 districts in the state, while Ghaziabad ranked first, Gautam Buddha Nagar stood at 32. Explaining the second parameter, the officer said, the total number of registered electors on the rolls are subtracted from the population projection till 2036. “We then estimate the number of eligible population still out of the rolls. Ghaziabad has the state’s highest at 10 lakh, followed by Noida at around 9 lakh.” While Ghaziabad has covered 5.15% of its eligible population in the last seven days, ranking 19 in the state, Noida has barely covered 1.14%, dropping to the 72nd position, the officer said. At the meeting, district-level officers were also asked to speed up the process, and act against those not performing their duties, the officer added. People can file claims and objections till December 16. The final electoral roll will be published on January 4 next year, while special voter registration camps will be held on November 28 and 29 in both the districts. An election official, meanwhile, explained possible reasons and hurdles officials face on ground. “Many people have come from other cities and settled here. A sizable portion of them don’t wish to get their names deleted from their previous voter list in their native cities,” the officer said, requesting anonymity, adding that though society groups are being roped in to facilitate the activity, many do not feel it’s important to take part in the process. Another officer further pointed to the workload. “The election duty is an additional task assigned to people who already have their primary duties, such as teaching. It is becoming increasingly difficult for them to balance both,” the officer added.

headline: Sandeep steps in as MLAs air grievances
content: Hyderabad: AICC Telangana in charge BM Sandeep Kumar continued his outreach to Congress leaders on Tuesday, extending his Hyderabad stay by a day and holding another round of meetings amid grievances among some party legislators over cabinet berths, constituency funds and other issues.Sandeep met minister Ponnam Prabhakar, Peddapalli MLA Ch Vijaya Ramana Rao and leaders from other constituencies on Tuesday.On Monday night, he met Munugode MLA Komatireddy Raj Gopal, who complained about the party leadership not honouring an assurance to give him a cabinet berth and alleged that adequate funds were not being provided for development works in his constituency.Raj Gopal also reportedly raised the denial of a road contract to his agency and complained about the language used by chief minister A Revanth Reddy against legislators protesting what they considered injustice.Sandeep is reported to have assured Raj Gopal that he would look into the issues raised by him. At the same time, he advised the MLA against publicly criticising the party, chief minister or ministers, including in the media.Sandeep left for New Delhi on Tuesday and is expected to return to Hyderabad on Thursday to participate in the Samvidhan Raksha March.The Telangana Congress will organise the march on Nov 26, Constitution Day, following a call from the AICC.The rally will begin at the BR Ambedkar statue on Tank Bund and conclude at the Indira Gandhi statue on Necklace Road. Sandeep, Revanth, TPCC president B Mahesh Kumar Goud and deputy chief minister Bhatti Vikramarka will participate. headline: Civic body repolls: SAD-BJP alliance to face first poll challenge ahead of 2027
content: The newly announced Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD)-BJP alliance is set to face its first political test ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, with candidates of both parties pitted against each other in the upcoming local body re-elections in the state.The two parties have fielded candidates against each other in 30 wards of the Patiala Municipal Corporation (MC), 15 wards of the Baghapurana Municipal Council and five wards of the Dharamkot Municipal Council. The situation has triggered political speculation, particularly in Patiala, over whether the two allies will contest the civic elections separately or eventually work out a joint strategy.The alliance was announced at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi on Tuesday.In Patiala, the key question is whether the SAD and BJP leaderships will allow their candidates to continue campaigning against each other or direct them to support candidates of the alliance partner. Although the deadline for withdrawal of nominations has already passed, the possibility of a post-nomination understanding cannot be ruled out.The outcome assumes significance as the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) needs at least eight seats to protect the Mayor’s chair and retain its political control over the civic body.Jaspal Singh Bittu Chatha, in-charge of the SAD’s Patiala (rural) Assembly segment and Amarinder Singh Bajaj, in-charge of the Patiala (urban) Assembly segment, said they were awaiting directions from the SAD high command regarding the Patiala MC elections.BJP Women’s Wing president Jai Inder Kaur said she would apprise the state leadership of the situation and explore the possibility of a local-level understanding to contest the MC elections jointly.“If we contest the MC re-elections jointly, no doubt, the alliance will gain a majority in the House and bag the Mayor’s post,” she claimed.If the two parties eventually decide to contest jointly, candidates of one party could be asked to scale down their campaigning and extend support to those fielded by the alliance partner. A mutually agreed seat-sharing arrangement, potentially based on the winnability of candidates, could also be worked out.However, if both parties continue to contest against each other, it could create confusion among their traditional supporters, particularly in wards where both parties have fielded candidates. The electoral outcome could also have implications for the political composition of the Municipal Corporation House and the future control of its leadership.

headline: Delhis new liquor policy seeks to stem cross-border purchases
content: Delhi's next liquor policy could address an unusual contradiction in its excise system: consumers crossing the city's borders to buy cheaper or better-stocked liquor, while the government loses revenue from purchases that could otherwise take place within the Capital.Officials aware of the matter told The Tribune that the policy was being prepared by a committee headed by PWD Minister Parvesh Verma. The draft had received the Centre's approval and is awaiting implementation, officials said. The existing policy, which had been extended several times, expires on March 31, 2027.The Delhi Government is preparing a plan to raise excise duties, rationalise retail margins and expand the availability of premium domestic and imported brands. The policy, expected to be introduced after the Punjab Assembly elections, will retain government-controlled retail outlets operated by four state corporations, rather than reopen the sector to private retailers.The proposed changes are significant because Delhi's excise duties have remained unchanged since 2014, while maximum retail prices (MRPs) were last revised four years ago. Official sources believe the price gap between Delhi and neighbouring markets, including Gurugram, Faridabad, Noida and Ghaziabad, has encouraged consumers to buy liquor outside the Capital.The government hopes that revising duties and improving brand availability will bring some of this spending back into Delhi's excise network. However, consumers could end up paying more if the higher duties are passed on through retail prices.The existing retail model also has a structural flaw. Fixed retailer margins mean that selling a cheaper bottle can generate the same margin as selling a premium one. This leaves retailers with little financial incentive to stock expensive brands in greater quantities, thereby restricting consumer choice.The proposed rationalisation of margins is intended to address this imbalance by offering retailers better returns on premium products. This could improve their availability across liquor categories, although the extent of the change will depend on the final margin structure and how retailers respond.The political sensitivity surrounding the exercise is considerable. The BJP had made the previous AAP government's 2021 excise policy a major election issue. However, a trial court discharged Arvind Kejriwal, Manish Sisodia, K Kavitha and 20 others in the CBI corruption case in February 2026. The CBI has challenged the order in the Delhi High Court.The challenge for the new government will be to increase revenue without making Delhi an even more expensive market. Unless revised prices remain competitive with those in neighbouring NCR cities, higher duties could end up reinforcing the very cross-border purchasing pattern that the policy seeks to reverse.

headline: Musi River Project Phase-1 Work From January 2027
content: Hyderabad: The work on Phase 1 of the Musi rejuvenation project will commence in Jan 2027. The tender process for Phase 1 has already been initiated, and necessary arrangements are being made to start work early next year.Municipal administration and urban development officials gave chief minister A Revanth Reddy an update on the Musi project, Personal Rapid Transit System (PRTS) and other projects on Tuesday during a review meeting that also covered the integrated fruit market at Koheda, radial roads and Mir Alam Tank, among other projects.The CM directed officials to expedite and complete all projects taken up in CURE and PURE areas (within and outside the ORR) under the purview of the municipal department.Officials informed him that under Phase 1 of the Musi rejuvenation project, the 9.20-km stretch from Himayatsagar to Gandhi Sarovar has been designated as ‘Zone-1 A’, and the 11.8-km stretch from Osmansagar to Gandhi Sarovar as ‘Zone-1 B’.They also explained to the CM the techno-economic feasibility of Phase 1 of the PRTS, including alignment options from Kukatpally, passing through Raidurg, up to Biodiversity Junction.They also presented alignment proposals extending from Begumpet Metro Station through Secretariat, Basheerbagh and Ranigunj. The CM directed them to identify suitable locations for PRTS depots, specifically around Necklace Road, Raidurg and People’s Plaza, and study their feasibility.“Plans should be developed to include multi-level parking facilities in the vicinity of these depots. Comprehensive studies and detailed plans should be prepared regarding routes, depot construction, and other related aspects,” the CM told officials.The CM also enquired about the progress of development works under the Mir Alam Tank project and was informed that officials were working towards completing the project by Jan 2028. He directed them to ensure the removal of accumulated silt from Mir Alam Tank, in addition to carrying out its overall development.Revanth also reviewed the progress of the integrated fruit market development works at Koheda and directed officials to accelerate construction without compromising on quality. He also said road construction must be completed along with the market development works.The Cyberabad municipal commissioner presented various designs for a foot overbridge at the IIIT Junction, within the CMC limits. The CM examined the designs and made suggestions, including establishing a multi-level car parking facility near the bridge.HYDRA commissioner AV Ranganath briefed the CM on the progress of lake restoration and the protection of govt assets. He also presented proposals for setting up Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs) at necessary locations as part of the lake restoration initiative.The CM instructed officials to expedite the construction of the STPs and directed that necessary measures be taken to restore stepwells across the city.Officials also briefed the CM on the progress of radial road construction and land acquisition, following which he directed them to accelerate the work.On the progress of the modern goshala (cow shelter) currently under construction at Gandipet, the CM directed officials to expedite work to ensure its completion by March 2027.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news.
