headline: School nurturing dreams in Mohammed Rafi’s village in Amritsar
content: Located in Kotla Sultan Singh, the native village of legendary playback singer Mohammed Rafi, Sri Dasmesh Senior Secondary Public School has been providing quality English-medium education to rural students of Majitha tehsil since 1981. The school was established after the authorities failed to find suitable land in Majitha town.It is among the four schools established under the Punjab Defence and Security Relief Fund Educational Society. The other three institutions were set up at Badal village, Anandpur Sahib and Talwandi Sabo in Bathinda district.The society is headed by the Chief Minister, while the Principal Secretary to the Chief Minister serves as its secretary. Its members include the Punjab Education Secretary, Deputy Commissioners of Bathinda, Sri Muktsar Sahib and Amritsar, Director of Dasmesh Academy, Sri Anandpur Sahib, and five eminent persons nominated by the chairman.At the district level, a Local Management Committee (LMC) oversees the day-to-day functioning of the school. The Deputy Commissioner, Amritsar, serves as its chairman, while the Majitha SDM is its manager. The committee also comprises district officials, the Majitha MLA and the president of the Parent-Teacher Association (PTA).At a time when access to quality English-medium education was limited in rural areas, the establishment of the school helped fulfil the aspirations of many parentsSpread over 10 acres, the school has modern infrastructure and sports facilities, including a shooting range. Two village panchayats donated 10 acres of land to the institution, which reportedly generates an annual income of over Rs 8 lakh to meet its expenses.School principal Vinod Sharma said the co-educational institution currently had 940 students on its rolls. At the senior secondary level, it offers medical and non-medical streams. The campus houses a well-stocked library, laboratories, a computer lab, audio-visual equipment and facilities for creative arts, besides indoor and outdoor games.Situated away from major towns and cities, the institution aims to provide modern education while ensuring the overall development of rural children. Besides academic excellence, the school focuses on nurturing individual talents and abilities, inculcating values such as honesty, self-discipline, compassion, punctuality, teamwork and dignity of labour among students. It also encourages independent thinking and a scientific outlook.

headline: Jensen Huang apologises to Nvidia staff at 'hardest company meeting', says he is attending daily therapy | Hindustan Times
content: Jensen Huang addressed employees at a company-wide meeting on Tuesday, apologising for the behaviour that resulted in his brief departure from Nvidia, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the meeting. He admitted that he had disappointed the workforce.Huang opened the meeting at Nvidia’s headquarters by expressing gratitude to Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress for overseeing the company during his nearly two-week absence as CEO, as per the sources mentioned in the report.The 63-year-old CEO described the gathering as “the hardest company meeting” he had ever faced, acknowledging that his actions breached Nvidia’s code of conduct. Also read | US announces 'largest-ever anti-scam' crackdown, charges over 800 defendants and recovers $8 billionHe also expressed gratitude for the opportunity to return to the helm of the company he co-founded nearly 30 years ago and told employees that he was attending therapy every day, Bloomberg reported.Huang denies government pressure drove comebackJensen Huang returned to the CEO position on Monday after President Donald Trump intervened in support of his reinstatement. His departure less than two weeks earlier followed revelations of relationships with a subordinate and another woman allegedly linked to Chinese intelligence.The reinstated CEO said Nvidia’s board made the decision to reinstate him after reviewing the available evidence, stressing that his return was not driven by his status as a “tech bro” or any belief that he was above the law, nor was it simply the result of pressure from senior government officials.He told employees that the board had assessed the facts and received assurances that his reinstatement posed no national security concerns.Huang promises to improve after comebackHuang’s return, approved by Nvidia’s board on Monday, caught much of the company’s senior leadership off guard. Just last week, executives had sought to reassure employees and stakeholders that the chipmaker could continue performing strongly even in his absence.Footage circulated by employees on Monday captured Huang arriving at Nvidia’s headquarters in Santa Clara, California, where staff greeted him with cheers and applause. Addressing workers briefly in one of the building’s entrance areas, he pledged that he “will do a better job.”Also read | CDC issues health advisory for Iowa residents ahead of US Army's planned 5-ton chemical explosionNvidia shares, which surged nearly 31% on the day Huang returned, fell by more than 7% during Tuesday’s trading session. The company’s market value has also dropped by nearly $2 trillion from the record high it reached in October.

headline: Maharashtra FDA commissioner warns against unlicensed sale of whey protein, misleading health claims
content: Mumbai Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe on Monday (November 23, 2026) warned of stringent action against gym operators selling health supplements without requisite authorisation and manufacturers making misleading claims about their health benefits, following a State-wide compliance order aimed at regulating the manufacture, marketing and sale of nutraceutical products. Who is Tukaram Mundhe, the IAS officer leading Maharashtra’s FDA crackdown? storyline 1 Also read | Why did Tukaram Mundhe withdraw his petition after dragging the Centre to court? | Explained https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/maharashtra/why-did-tukaram-mundhe-withdraw-his-petition-after-dragging-the-centre-to-court-explained/article71727214.ece Speaking to reporters in Pune, Mr. Mundhe raised concerns over the manner in which health supplements, particularly whey protein and nutraceutical products, were being marketed and consumed, especially among students and youngsters. “Health supplements, whether whey protein or nutraceutical products, are being presented and used in an improper manner. Their branding, marketing and the claims being made about them are misleading. It is necessary to verify whether these claims are genuine,” he said. Tukaram Mundhe withdraws petition after dragging Centre to the court Tukaram Mundhe withdraws petition after dragging Centre to the court FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe had challenged FSSAI over the constitutional validity of a few regulations. The petition had challenged the creation of a few posts by the Centre, claiming it was against the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 Exclusive Tukaram Mundhe withdraws petition after dragging Centre to the court storyline 1 Mr. Mundhe said only authorised food business operators were permitted to sell such products and warned against unsubstantiated claims promising muscle gain or other health benefits. Urging youngsters to exercise caution while consuming supplements, he emphasised the importance of physical exercise and natural sources of protein for muscle development. He also raised concerns over the actual protein content in products being marketed as protein supplements. The Commissioner said manufacturers, wholesalers, retailers and gym operators were individually responsible for ensuring that the products they sold complied with food safety regulations. Sellers could not shift the responsibility for violations onto manufacturers, he said, adding that merely possessing a food licence did not entitle businesses to sell substandard or adulterated products. Compliance order The remarks come days after the Maharashtra FDA issued a State-wide comprehensive compliance order on November 20 under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, to regulate health supplements, nutraceuticals and foods for special dietary and medical purposes. The order mandates that gymnasiums, fitness centres and pharmacies obtain the requisite food licence or registration before selling such products, irrespective of whether they hold licences under other laws. It also prohibits claims about the treatment, cure, or prevention of diseases, as well as endorsements suggesting that doctors or nutritionists recommend products. The restrictions extend to advertisements on social media, e-commerce platforms and promotional content by influencers. The FDA has directed officials to conduct risk-based inspections, with particular emphasis on sports nutrition products, weight-loss supplements, sales at gymnasiums and online platforms. Under the existing provisions of the Act, misleading advertisements and operating a food business without a licence could attract penalties of up to ₹10 lakh each.

headline: Natural farming push fails to bring profits for growers
content: Growers are struggling to get remunerative prices for their produce due to inadequate promotion of natural farming products and 15 per cent commission being charged by the marketing platform of Dr YS Parmar University of Horticulture and Forestry, Nauni in Solan district.The university’s ‘UHF Naturals Store’, which became operational on July 18, lacks key facilities such as refrigeration, essential for enhancing the shelf life of perishable products like fruits.Jiwan Singh Rana, a progressive farmer of Gharjarot village in Kangra district, who sold his dragon fruit through the store, rues that he had supplied 150 kg of A-grade dragon fruit to the university store on August 1 and another 150 kg on August 31.He says that the produce was sold only weeks later, resulting in a considerable quantity of the fruit getting spoiled. “After investing thousands of rupees on transporting my produce from Kangra district and paying 15 per cent commission to the university store, I did not make profit,” he adds.Growers lament that in the absence of adequate promotion of natural farming products by both state government and university, consumers remain largely unaware of the nutritional benefits of such produce. Consequently, farmers struggle to find sufficient buyers, defeating the very purpose of promoting natural farming as a remunerative livelihood activity in the state.“Natural farming products have a high nutritional value as their production does not involve chemical pesticides or synthetic fertilisers. This farming practice relies on naturally available local resources and also helps rejuvenate soil health while promoting digestive health,” opine health experts.The absence of accredited laboratories to certify their produce as naturally farmed is adding to the woes of the growers. This makes it difficult for farmers to establish the authenticity of their products, further limiting their ability to secure remunerative prices in the market.An official of the university, however, justifies the 15 per cent commission, stating that it is necessary to meet the recurring operational expenses of the store, including the salaries of two employees, rent and electricity charges.He adds, “The UHF Naturals is an outcome of the Himachal Pradesh Government’s Prakritik Kheti Khushhal Kisan Yojana (PK3Y), aimed at promoting natural farming and developing sustainable agricultural systems. The UHF Naturals provides marketing and retail space to Natural Farming Farmer Producer Companies from across Himachal Pradesh, enabling them to showcase and sell their produce. It also offers university departments an opportunity to market their raw and value-added products while extending support to university-based start-ups.”

headline: Cane price row casts shadow over Shahabad mill’s crushing season
content: The inauguration of the 43rd crushing season at the Shahabad Cooperative Sugar Mill on Tuesday turned into a show of protest, with agitating farmers confronting the police, opposing the virtual participation of a BJP minister and reiterating their demand for a sugarcane price of Rs 600 per quintal.The confrontation unfolded as leaders of the Bhartiya Kisan Union (Charuni), who have been staging a dharna outside the mill, attempted to register their protest against the government's failure to announce the demanded cane price. The farmers had threatened to show black flags to BJP ministers Arvind Sharma and Krishan Bedi and prevent them from entering the mill premises.While Cooperation Minister Krishan Bedi skipped the event, Cooperation Minister Arvind Kumar Sharma joined virtually. However, the farmers, led by BKU (Charuni) spokesman Rakesh Bains, objected to his virtual participation as well, declaring that no BJP leader would be allowed to participate in mill-related programmes until the government announced a price of Rs 600 per quintal for sugarcane.DSP Shahabad Siddharth, SHO Surinder Sindhu and mill officials attempted to pacify the protesters, but the talks failed to defuse the tension. The farmers raised slogans against the government, following which Bains and fellow farmer leader Jasbir Singh Mamumajra were forcibly removed and detained briefly.Addressing the event virtually, Arvind Sharma said the cooperative sector was playing a significant role in empowering farmers. He said the Shahabad mill, considered the economic backbone of the region's farming community, would be strengthened through modern technology and increased crushing capacity.He said the government was committed to protecting farmers' interests and had directed the mill management to ensure that growers faced no inconvenience. The Cooperation Department, he added, was focusing on modernisation and capacity expansion of sugar mills across the state.Mill Managing Director Dr Indrajit said all preparations for the new crushing season had been completed. The mill has set a target of crushing around 58 lakh quintals of sugarcane this season, with emphasis on maximising crushing and improving sugar recovery.However, despite the formal inauguration, crushing operations could not begin as farmers withheld their cane supplies in support of the ongoing agitation.Later, Bains accused the police of misbehaving with farmers and tearing his clothes during the confrontation. Alleging that the SHO had treated him like a murder accused, he said such conduct by a police officer was unacceptable.Bains warned that if the government failed to announce the demanded price, farmers would prevent BJP leaders from entering their villages. The standoff has thus cast a shadow over the start of the crushing season, with the mill's operations dependent on the resolution of the price dispute.

headline: Raft and glory: Punjab’s powerpuff girls glow with gold
content: From practising on the relatively calm waters of a canal in the city to navigating the challenging Grade 4 rapids of the Ganga, Punjab’s first women’s rafting team has scripted a remarkable sporting success, bringing home overall silver in the 18th National Rafting Championship held at Devprayag, Uttarakhand, from November 17 to 22.The achievement is significant not merely for the medals, but for what it represents: the arrival of women from Punjab in a demanding adventure sport traditionally dominated by specialised teams and institutions such as the Army, the ITBP and NIMAS.Team Punjab Khalsa, comprising five students of Khalsa University, Amritsar, was trained by the Punjab Association for Rafting and Adventure Sports (PARAAS) at Tara Wala Pul on the Upper Bari Doab Canal. Although the members had experience in rowing and water sports, the national championship was their first exposure to competitive white-water rafting. They received a brief river training session at Devprayag, located at the confluence of the Alaknanda and Bhagirathi rivers, before entering the competition.Competing against experienced teams from Jammu and Kashmir, the Army, the ITBP and other institutions, the women secured the overall silver in the women’s category. Their medal tally included a gold in Slalom and Marathon, a silver in Sprint and RX, and a bronze in the mixed team event alongside Jammu and Kashmir. The ITBP won the Gold Cup.For PARAAS president Gunbir Singh, who has spearheaded efforts to introduce adventure sports among Punjab’s youth, the victory validates the potential of a generation willing to explore sporting disciplines beyond conventional arenas.“Punjab’s women’s team has made us all proud. It’s time the state took notice of this remarkable achievement at the national level. This is a firm beginning that has strengthened our confidence in the youth of the region,” he said.Founded in 2024, PARAAS has systematically built the institutional framework for rafting in Punjab. It received state recognition in June 2025 and subsequently secured affiliations with national and international rafting bodies, while developing trained judges and participants. A felicitation ceremony was organised at Tara Wala Pul, the very place where the team’s journey began. Captain Shreya Chandel and team members Mehakdeep Kaur, Namrata, Navya and Kangna Koundal were congratulated along with team coordinator Sonam. Gunbir said conquering Grade 4 rapids on a free-flowing river on their maiden competitive outing was no ordinary achievement. For Punjab, the medals mark more than a sporting milestone. They demonstrate how modest beginnings, institutional support and opportunities for women can create pathways into entirely new sporting arenas.

headline: Rohtak: 5,314 vacancies in medical colleges, 450 pharmacist posts unfilled: Hooda
content: Former Chief Minister and Leader of the Opposition Bhupinder Singh Hooda on Tuesday accused the BJP government of weakening Haryana’s education and healthcare systems, alleging widespread staff shortages and inadequate basic facilities in government institutions.Addressing a press conference, Hooda said nearly half the teaching and non-teaching posts in government-aided colleges were vacant. Of the 2,831 sanctioned teaching posts, 1,394 (49.2%) were unfilled, while 785 of the 1,668 non-teaching posts were vacant. He added that 56 of the 97 aided colleges were functioning without principals.Highlighting the shortage of teachers in schools, Hooda said 723 government primary schools were being run by a single teacher each. These teachers, apart from handling academic responsibilities, were also expected to manage cleaning and midday meal arrangements. Nineteen of these schools had been designated as Model Sanskriti Schools, he pointed out.He also raised concerns over drinking water quality, claiming that water in 398 schools up to Class XII had been found unfit for consumption. The findings were based on samples collected from 6,000 schools, while another 7,800 schools were yet to be assessed, he said.Hooda alleged that inadequate funding had also affected the midday meal scheme, forcing schools to purchase essential supplies, including milk, curd, vegetables, jaggery and flour, on credit. In several cases, teachers were paying for these supplies from their own pockets and subsequently seeking reimbursement, he added.Turning to healthcare, the Congress leader said more than 450 of the 1,064 sanctioned pharmacist posts in government hospitals were vacant, while government medical colleges had 5,314 vacancies for doctors and paramedical staff.Citing a report from June, Hooda said 2,572 of the 3,843 sanctioned doctor posts in Haryana’s eight government medical colleges were vacant. Another 2,742 paramedical positions were also unfilled.The situation was particularly alarming in newer medical colleges, he claimed. Jind had 555 vacancies against 559 sanctioned posts, Mahendragarh 492 against 559, and Bhiwani 477 against 552. Even PGIMS- Rohtak, the state's largest medical institution, had more than 40% vacancies among doctors and Group-A staff, he added.Hooda also extended support to sugarcane farmers protesting against the state government's procurement price hike of Rs 15 per quintal. Describing the increase as inadequate, he said the 3% hike failed to account for rising inflation and record-high sugar prices.

headline: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang After Trump Defends CEO, Cites US Government Input
content: Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as its chief executive, president and board member, reversing its decision to accept his voluntary resignation just days earlier. The move comes after US President Donald Trump publicly defended Huang, calling his departure a “tragedy” and praising his contribution to America's AI industry. Nvidia said its board received input from senior US government officials before making the decision and was confident Huang posed no national security risk. Trump also revealed that he had discussed artificial intelligence with Chinese President Xi Jinping during their dinner meeting, though he clarified that Huang's situation was not part of their conversation.

headline: Kurukshetra officials to adopt government schools, file visit reports online
content: To improve the academic environment and infrastructure in the government schools, the government officials have been directed to adopt and visit the schools in their respective areas and update their reports on the MIS portal.As per the Kurukshetra Deputy Commissioner Vishram Kumar Meena, theEducation Department has developed a school visit module on the MIS portal and through this module, officials can ‘adopt’ schools, conduct visits and submit their reports online. This will enable the department to receive timely and accurate information regarding the actual status of schools, existing facilities and any shortcomings. The objective is to ensure that no school suffers from a lack of basic infrastructure. The school visit module will make the monitoring of schools more transparent and effective.The Sub-Divisional Magistrates (SDMs), Tehsildar, Block Development and Panchayat Officers (BDPOs), and other department heads have been told to adopt schools within their respective jurisdictions, conduct regular visits and upload their reports onto the MIS portal. The objective is to ensure that officers go beyond routine inspections and take a personal interest in improving the academic environment and infrastructure of their adopted schools.Meena explained that, in addition to visiting schools assigned to or adopted by them, officials may also conduct visits to schools selected at random. They also have the option to relinquish an adopted school. All officials are required to use the school visit module on the MIS portal. The officials can generate their login credentials via the registration link on the MIS portal. Subsequently, they will be able to upload their reports within the school visit module.The officials may adopt or choose as many schools as they wish for the purpose of these visits. They will also be required to upload their feedback or observations regarding the school, along with relevant photographs and PDF documents.TheDC said the officials have been instructed to visit the schools, engage with students, teachers, and parents, and document any genuine challenges or issues on the portal. The feedback from the students, teachers and parents will help in improving the academic environment and results of the government schools.

headline: Minister performs ground breaking ceremony of link road in Shimla’s Nawar region
content: Education Minister Rohit Thakur today visited the Nawar region of the Jubbal-Nawar-Kotkhai Assembly constituency in Shimla district and laid the foundation stone for the Tutupani-Nalavan link road, to be constructed at a cost of Rs 8.62 crore.He also inspected the Umladwar-Gahloon-Kadivan link road being built with NABARD assistance. The minister said around Rs 7.6 crore was being spent on the project and nearly 50 per cent of the work had been completed.Referring to the Tutupani-Nalavan link road, Thakur said the state government had fulfilled a long-pending demand of local residents. He said the road would improve connectivity and transportation facilities, providing a boost to horticulture and other economic activities in the region.Describing roads as the backbone of development, the minister said strengthening road infrastructure was crucial given the Nawar region’s potential for horticulture and tourism.Thakur said development projects worth crores of rupees were under way in every panchayat of the Nawar region and were being implemented uniformly across the constituency. He assured residents that efforts would be made to complete all key projects within the next year.Later, the minister inspected the under-construction buildings of the Government Senior Secondary School and the Primary Health Centre (PHC) at Kuthadi village. He said the school building was being constructed at a cost of Rs 3.52 crore and about 40 per cent of the work had been completed, while the PHC building was coming up at a cost of Rs 1.4 crore.Thakur directed officials to complete both buildings by May 2027 and ensure quality standards were maintained throughout the construction process.

headline: Refused to pay extortion money, fruit seller attacked
content: A fruit seller, Harikesh (33), was allegedly threatened and attacked for refusing to pay Rs 30,000 as monthly extortion to Manish Gujjar, a resident of Paplota village near Kalka in Haryana.Harikesh, a migrant from Uttar Pradesh, had reportedly refused to give in to the demand, angering the accused. On November 22, Gujjar allegedly threatened him twice before sending two youths in a black Scorpio vehicle to intimidate him while he was selling fruit at the Sabzi Mandi near the Lakkar Bridge around 7:30 pm.One of the youths got out of the vehicle and attacked Harikesh with a stick before fleeing with his accomplice. The victim’s nephew and friends, who were present at the spot, intervened and came to his rescue. They also alerted the police through the helpline. A police team reached the spot after receiving the complaint, but the assailants had fled by then.A case under Sections 308(4), 351(3), 115(2) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) has been registered. An investigation is underway, a police official said.

headline: Meghalaya shares early childhood policy plans at UK Parliament talks
content: Shillong: A delegation of 20 Meghalaya legislators led by assembly speaker Thomas A Sangma joined a dialogue on early childhood development at UK Parliament in Westminster, discussing public investment in children’s health, nutrition and learning.Meghalaya govt organised Early Childhood Development (ECD) Policy Dialogue with global education organisation Think Equal, the assembly secretariat said in a statement issued on Tuesday. It described the event as Meghalaya’s first parliamentary engagement of its kind.UK parliamentary representatives, researchers and advocates also attended the discussions on governance, public spending and early childhood development.Meghalaya additional chief secretary Sampath Kumar said evidence of childhood stunting and nutrition challenges had prompted the state’s leadership, including CM Conrad K Sangma, to rethink spending priorities and recognise the importance of investing in children’s development.“Meghalaya’s ECD Mission, a whole-of-govt and whole-of-society approach, is bringing together health, nutrition, early learning, responsive caregiving and parental wellbeing. It is strengthening community capacity through training of around 22,000 frontline functionaries and an ECD fellowship of over 1,600 youth across all 12 districts,” Kumar elaborated.Julian Huppert, former MP for Cambridge and founding director of Intellectual Forum at Jesus College, University of Cambridge, called for more public investment in the earliest years of life rather than relying mainly on interventions after problems emerge.Think Equal founder and president Leslee Udwin said the social and emotional abilities children develop in their formative years shape how they relate to themselves and others.“Through its partnership with Think Equal, Meghalaya is bringing structured social and emotional learning to approximately 6,188 early childhood development centres, with a planned reach of around 200,000 children,” the assembly secretariat said.The dialogue also examined Greater Manchester’s experience of political leadership and collaboration across public institutions to support children and families. It opened opportunities for Meghalaya and Greater Manchester to continue learning from each other and working together, the statement said.Participants discussed possible collaboration in research, institutional learning and international policy exchanges, including a Commonwealth learning platform.Speaker Sangma spoke about the aspirations countries share despite their different circumstances.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Guwahati | Silver Rate in Guwahati | Bank Holidays in Guwahati | Public Holidays in Guwahati | Guwahati AQI | Weather in Guwahati | Petrol Price in Guwahati | Diesel Price in Guwahati | CNG Price in Guwahati | LPG Price in GuwahatiStay updated with the latest Guwahati news.
