headline: Man held with 819 gm charas in Chamba
content: The Special Task Force (STF), Kangra, arrested a 33-year-old man after recovering 819 grams of charas from his possession during patrolling on the Chanvas-Tissa road in Churah subdivision of Chamba district on Monday night.The accused has been identified as Rakesh, a resident of Bara village in Jungra panchayat of Churah tehsil. The STF team intercepted him and recovered the contraband during a search of his backpack.A case was registered against the accused under relevant sections of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act at the STF police station in Kangra district.STF Assistant Police Inspector Parmesh Sharma said further investigation was underway to ascertain the source of the contraband and its intended destination. He also urged the public to come forward and join hands in the fight against drugs.

headline: Deputy CM takes part in yajna at Una shrine
content: Deputy Chief Minister Mukesh Agnihotri participated in a yajna at the Dera Baba Rudranand Shrine at Nari village in Una district on the occasion of Panch Bhishma and Koti Gayatri Mahayagya on Tuesday.He said that the Dera was of immense spiritual significance and revered saints had done penance here. He lauded the efforts of the current Seer, Swami Hemanand Maharaj, for undertaking a series of developmental works for the welfare of devotees at the shrine. Kutlehar MLA Vivek Sharma was also present on the occasion.Agnihotri later visited the Kila Baba Bedi Gurdwara in Una city and paid obeisance to Guru Nanak Dev on the occasion of his 557th birth anniversary. He said that the Guru’s life was dedicated to the welfare of mankind and his preaching still hold true. Spiritual leader Baba Sarabjot Singh Bedi was also present on the occasion.

headline: In Tarn Taran, Shivraj Singh Chouhan praises Booh farmers for avoiding stubble burning
content: Union Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan visited Booh Havelian village near Harike Pattan and interacted with farmers on crop residue management under the Khet Bachao Abhiyan. He urged farmers to avoid stubble burning to preserve soil fertility and protect beneficial insects.During the visit, Chouhan reviewed the wheat crop and farm machinery used by progressive farmer Major Singh. Dr Nirmal Singh, an official of the Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK), Booh, briefed him on equipment and techniques for soil management.Chouhan praised the farmers of Booh village, saying they had not burned crop residue on nearly 700 acres since 2018. Farmers also shared their experiences and highlighted their problems.Former village sarpanch Gurnam Singh urged Guru Angad Dev Veterinary and Animal Sciences University (GADVASU) and the KVK-Booh to adopt villages and promote employment opportunities for rural youth in agriculture and animal husbandry.Chouhan assured the farmers that their concerns would be addressed. He also said successful farmers would be invited to Delhi to share their experiences. He inspected an exhibition showcasing products related to allied agricultural activities organised by the KVK-Booh.During the visit, the minister planted a sapling in connection with the Gurpurb of Guru Nanak Dev and reiterated his commitment to serving farmers. He said people should work honestly, following the teachings of Guru Nanak Dev.When asked about the farmers’ demand for loan waivers, Chouhan said he had not come on a political platform but to interact with farmers. He highlighted the subsidies provided on urea, DAP fertilisers and machinery used for crop residue management.He also stressed the need to implement the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana in Punjab to compensate farmers for crop losses caused by natural calamities. He said he had written to CM Bhagwant Mann last year regarding the implementation of the scheme.BJP leaders, including advocate Jaskaran Singh Toot, district president advocate Satnam Singh and Harjit Singh Miyapur, were also present.

headline: BJP protests minister’s remarks against Armed Forces in Himachal Pradesh
content: Activists of the Una district BJP and its youth wing, the Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM), today staged a protest at the district headquarters against the alleged remarks made by Revenue Minister Jagat Singh Negi against the Armed Forces in the state Assembly.The police had received information that the activists would burn the minister’s effigy during the protest. A couple of uniformed personnel were deployed near the venue at Rotary Chowk in Una city to prevent the attempt. However, the BJYM activists set the effigy on fire at a secluded spot and ran towards the road intersection carrying it. Policemen on duty rushed to seize the effigy, resulting in a minor scuffle.Later, BJP district president Shyam Minhas condemned the minister’s alleged remarks against the Indian Armed Forces. He said the world had witnessed the valour of Indian soldiers during Operation Sindoor. He added that Armed Forces personnel were the country’s pride and honour and were always ready to make sacrifices for the nation. Any attempt to tarnish their image would not be tolerated, he said.The Una district BJP demanded a public apology from the minister and urged Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu to remove Jagat Singh Negi from the Cabinet over his alleged irresponsible and anti-national remarks. BJYM activists also raised slogans against Negi and demanded his resignation.Kinnaur BJP stages protest against minister’s remarksReckong Peo: The Kinnaur BJP today staged a protest rally in Reckong Peo against the alleged controversial remarks made by Revenue, Horticulture, Tribal Development and Public Grievances Redressal Minister Jagat Singh Negi about Indian soldiers during the ongoing state Assembly session.BJP leaders and workers, including members of the Kinnaur BJP, BJP Mahila Morcha, BJP Yuva Morcha and other party organisations, took out a rally through the Reckong Peo market and condemned the minister’s alleged remarks.Addressing the rally, BJP leader and former Vice-Chairman of the State Forest Corporation Surat Negi demanded an unconditional public apology from Jagat Singh Negi for his remarks against Indian soldiers. He said the BJP would continue its protest if the minister failed to apologise. He also urged the state government to ask the minister to resign from the Cabinet immediately on moral grounds.

headline: BJYM, police scuffle during a protest against Revenue Minister in Shimla
content: A scuffle broke out between Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM) activists and police personnel when protesters attempted to burn the effigy of Revenue Minister Jagat Singh Negi during a demonstration against his remarks on Operation Sindoor made during the recent Winter Session of the Himachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly.Hundreds of BJYM members gathered outside the Deputy Commissioner’s office, raising slogans against the minister and demanding his resignation. As the protesters moved to burn Negi’s effigy, police personnel deployed at the site intervened. The protesters resisted, leading to a brief scuffle between the two sides.BJYM state general secretary Sushil Kadasholi, along with several BJP and Yuva Morcha leaders and workers, participated in the protest. Addressing the gathering, Kadasholi termed Negi’s remarks on the Indian Army and Operation Sindoor as “extremely unfortunate and condemnable”.“The entire country is proud of the valour of the Indian Army. Therefore, comments questioning the Army’s valour are unbecoming of a person holding a responsible constitutional position,” he said.Kadasholi alleged that the minister had abandoned political decorum and restraint. “He should publicly apologise to the people of the country and the Indian Army for his remarks and immediately resign from the Council of Ministers on moral grounds,” he said.Condemning the police action, Kadasholi alleged that the force was acting under pressure from the state government and attempting to suppress the voices of activists. He said peaceful protest was a fundamental democratic right and any attempt to curb it was highly condemnable.

headline: Himachal’s IIT-Mandi hosts annual meet of IIT librarians
content: The Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Mandi, hosted the 12th Annual Pan-IIT Librarians Meet on November 22 and 23, bringing together librarians and library professionals from IITs across the country to discuss emerging technologies, institutional collaboration and the future of academic libraries.The two-day meeting provided a common platform for participants to exchange experiences, share best practices and explore strategies to strengthen library services across the IIT system. The inaugural session was attended by the Director of IIT-Mandi.A key focus of the discussions was the implementation of the One Nation One Subscription (ONOS) initiative, Open Access and Article Processing Charges (APCs). Participants reviewed the progress, coverage and usage of ONOS while discussing the challenges faced by IIT libraries. The deliberations covered APC support mechanisms, publisher agreements and possible solutions for accessing journals not covered under existing arrangements.The meeting also addressed the structure of the library cadre, recruitment rules and career progression of library professionals. Participants explored the possibility of developing a common framework across IITs by harmonising designations, recruitment practices and promotion opportunities.An expert lecture on “Reimagining the Modern Academic Library: Technology, Innovation, Well-being and Professional Excellence” was delivered by Dr Jadhav, former Librarian at IIT-Madras. The lecture highlighted the evolving role of academic libraries and the need to balance technological advancements with professional excellence and staff well-being.Capacity building and professional development of library staff also featured prominently in the discussions. Participants emphasised the importance of training in Artificial Intelligence (AI), programming and scripting, data analytics, research support tools, mentoring and reskilling to prepare library professionals for emerging technological challenges.Strengthening collaboration among IIT libraries through Inter-Library Loan (ILL), Document Delivery Services (DDS) and resource sharing was another major agenda item. Discussions focused on developing a common discovery and request portal and introducing standardised protocols to improve access to academic resources.The programme also featured interactions with publishers and representatives of scholarly information services, focusing on emerging APC models, AI-based databases and research tools. Participants discussed the proposal to establish an IIT Libraries Consortium to facilitate collective negotiations, resource sharing and improved access to scholarly information.On the second day, participants joined a tree plantation drive on the IIT-Mandi campus, reaffirming the institute’s commitment to environmental sustainability. An open discussion and panel session on the future roadmap for IIT libraries explored proposals for launching an open-access journal and introducing regular newsletters to improve communication and information exchange.Participants also visited various units of the IIT-Mandi Library to familiarise themselves with its facilities and services.The annual meeting concluded with a shared emphasis on professional networking, institutional cooperation and the development of technologically advanced, inclusive and future-ready academic libraries across the IIT system.

headline: Hisar: Former MLA and BJP leader Kuldeep Bishnoi meets CM, seeks subdivisional status for Adampur
content: Former MLA and BJP leader Kuldeep Bishnoi met Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini in Chandigarh to raise a range of issues concerning the Adampur Assembly constituency.This comes amid allegations of “neglect” of the constituency in development works levelled by Congress MLA Chander Prakash.Bishnoi, accompanied by BJP MLA from the neighbouring Nalwa constituency Randhir Panihar, submitted an eight-point development agenda to the Chief Minister on Monday.He sought subdivisional status for Adampur and tehsil status for Balsamand, ownership rights for residents of Ravidas Nagar, land ownership rights for residents of villages in the Beed area at concessional rates, expediting electricity connections to dhanis and improving health facilities.Development works in Jawahar Nagar and villages falling under Adampur Mandi were also taken up.The Congress MLA has raised the issue of the lack of development in Adampur, including during his visits to villages in the constituency.Bishnoi seemed to be irked by these allegations, as his father, Bhajan Lal, who used to represent Adampur, was Haryana’s longest-serving Chief Minister.The issue snowballed into a row when Kuldeep’s son Bhavya Bishnoi, who was defeated by Chander Prakash in the previous elections, attended some official functions related to development works.Supporters of the Congress MLA alleged that this was a violation of protocol since Bhavya did not hold any official position in the government.Against the backdrop of the row, Bishnoi recently made a pointed remark about the Congress MLA, asking him to visit his office and debate the issue of development with his personal assistant.Meanwhile, during his meeting with the CM, Bishnoi raised the shortage of canal water in the area and sought an adequate supply for at least two weeks, besides demanding the cleaning of canals and watercourses.Bhavya Bishnoi, too, took up the matter of eviction notices issued by the Haryana Shahari Vikas Pradhikaran to Scheduled Caste families living in a locality in Adampur. In a representation to the CM, he sought ownership rights for around 400 families.Kuldeep Bishnoi also raised the issue of the continuation of the services of part-time teachers and guest faculty at Guru Jambheshwar University of Science and Technology (GJUST), Hisar.He submitted a memorandum seeking a resolution of their concerns.Bishnoi said the Chief Minister had accepted his demand for the continuation of their services and issued directions in this regard.

headline: PM Modi, Sukhbir Badal’s personal push and ground surveys: How BJP-Akali Dal alliance came about
content: The BJP-Shiromani Akali Dal reunion may have taken over six years to materialise since their separation on September 26, 2020, but the realisation that an alliance was necessary had begun to dawn much earlier.The first realisation came soon after the 2022 Assembly election results. In this first electoral test after their split, both parties were routed. History repeated itself in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, with the SAD reduced to one seat and the BJP to nil.Today's final call on the alliance, well-placed sources say, was driven by two factors: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal's personal interest in reuniting to "save Punjab"; and political pragmatism, with surveys indicating that the two parties were barely in the fight if they went alone and could be force multipliers if they contested together.Related news: ‘Thag jod’ aimed at protecting political interests: Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann on SAD-BJP alliancePanthic factor behind BJP’s ‘chhota bhai’ move in PunjabFrom ‘chhota bhai’ to big brother: Amit Shah says Akali Dal will lead Punjab alliance, keep CM post“Both sides realised that a reunion was important to try and get back at the helm and rescue Punjab from its current financial mess. Punjab’s total debt is projected to reach Rs 4.47 lakh crore by March 31, 2027, even as the state was in surplus a decade ago… The social mess mirrored by rising drug addiction, law and order breakdown and religious conversions is equally challenging," an Akali leader said.In fact, the first signs of a thaw appeared in April 2023 when then BJP president JP Nadda attended the last rites of SAD patriarch Parkash Singh Badal in Lambi near Bathinda. It was for the first time since the SAD quit the NDA over the farm bills that leaders of the estranged allies had come together, though on a sombre occasion.On June 11 this year, PM Modi, in an NDA resolution endorsed by all constituents, saluted alliance stalwarts Parkash Singh Badal of the SAD, Bal Thackeray of the Shiv Sena and Atal Bihari Vajpayee of the BJP. The gesture was seen as PM Modi’s way of warming up to old allies--Sukhbir and Uddhav Thackeray.The August meeting between PM Modi and Sukhbir was the biggest signal that a reunion was on the cards. Then came the deployment of PM Modi’s trusted aide CR Patil in Punjab. Known for election management, Patil led several surveys that suggested the electoral benefits of a BJP-Akali alliance. The feedback was shared across the Sangh Parivar and everyone eventually came around.Reliable sources say the RSS in Punjab was the strongest votary of the BJP’s "go solo" plan, which Home Minister Amit Shah also endorsed. The plan remained intact even after three Punjab leaders--Sunil Jakhar, Manpreet Badal and Jai Inder Kaur--told Shah at a strategy meeting in Delhi on June 13 that an alliance was a must to get into the fight.But very lately as survey after survey spoke clearly about the necessity of an alliance, both sides sat together and finalised the nuances. Insiders say PM Modi was the biggest factor behind the alliance and he had directed everyone to work towards it in the interests of the “border state and national security”.This explains why Shah today said the alliance was meant to foster Hindu-Sikh unity, besides salvaging Punjab from the burden of drugs and narco-terrorism being heaped upon it by forces inimical to India. Shah had visited Punjab and met the families, including of Parvinder Singh Jhota, who lost their wards to drugs. Parallel to that, Shah vowed a drug-free Punjab by December 31, 2029.The Tribune, which consistently reported that the alliance was on the cards, has further reliably learnt that the RSS was always in favour of going it alone, but came around once PM Modi took the stand that a pact was about Punjab and not just about one election.Brass tacks also weighed in. From its highest points in 2007 and 2012, the SAD fell from 48 seats in the Assembly in 2007 to three in 2022, and the BJP from 19 seats to two. In 2012, the SAD won 56 seats and the BJP 12. These results had triggered attempts on the part of the BJP and the Akalis to reunite for the 2024 Lok Sabha elections also, but seat-sharing talks failed after the SAD refused to cede space the BJP had sought.Results were again poor. The Akali Dal won one seat of the 13 and the BJP drew a blank. How much were the estranged allies willing to risk in 2027 was, therefore, the question. The answer was “not much”.

headline: Quality education a priority in Himachal: Rajesh Dharmani
content: Technical Education Minister Rajesh Dharmani said providing quality education and better opportunities to students was a top priority of the state government. He was addressing students at the annual function of Government Senior Secondary School in Marhana village of Bilaspur district today.He said the government was working to equip government schools with modern facilities and provide a better academic environment to ensure that students in rural areas had equal access to quality education. The government was establishing Rajiv Gandhi Model Day-Boarding Schools and developing more than 850 educational institutions as Institutions of Excellence, with a special focus on providing modern academic facilities.Dharmani said that, to address teacher shortages and improve the quality of education, the government was focusing not only on regular recruitment but also on comprehensive teacher training. He added that teachers had been sent on exposure visits to countries such as Singapore to gain first-hand experience of modern teaching methods.Additionally, the Vidya Samiksha Kendra was being used to monitor academic activities in schools in real time and ensure the optimum utilisation of available resources. The minister announced a grant of Rs 5 lakh for various development works and improving student facilities at the school.Speaking about development works in the village, Dharmani said more than Rs 40 lakh had been spent on the maintenance and improvement of roads in Marhana panchayat through the Public Works Department (PWD). The works included the construction of retaining walls at various locations, installation of paver blocks in vulnerable areas and construction of drainage systems along most stretches of the road. Repair work on the road connecting the village had also been completed.He said around Rs 7.50 lakh was being spent on the renovation and improvement of the Marhana dispensary building. Another Rs 10 lakh had been sanctioned to the PWD under the Mukhyamantri Gram Sadak Yojana to improve the access road to the Dalit settlement in Marhana.

headline: Gurugram tops state in old vehicle scrapping registration
content: Gurugram has emerged as Haryana's leading district in registering old commercial vehicles for scrapping under the Parivartan scheme, with 5,436 trucks and buses listed on the Transport Department's portal. Faridabad ranks second with 5,043 registrations.Across Haryana's 14 NCR authorities, a total of 21,246 old commercial vehicles have been registered so far, comprising 15,225 trucks and 6,021 buses. Of the registered trucks, 11,634 fall in the heavy vehicle category. The difference between Gurugram and Faridabad is just 393 vehicles, while neighbouring Palwal has recorded 812 registrations. Together, Gurugram and Faridabad account for nearly half of the state's total.However, the figures indicate that the scheme has made a relatively slow beginning. Haryana has identified around 1.08 lakh BS-IV and older trucks and buses in its NCR areas for replacement, including approximately 92,000 trucks and 16,000 buses. The registrations so far cover only about one-fifth of the identified vehicles. The available data does not specify how many of these vehicles have actually been dismantled.Gurugram's registrations comprise 4,158 trucks and 1,278 buses. Faridabad, on the other hand, has registered 4,351 trucks and 692 buses. Thus, while Faridabad leads in truck registrations, Gurugram has a higher number of buses. Faridabad's truck category includes 3,855 heavy, 338 small and 158 medium vehicles. Its bus registrations comprise 423 heavy, 178 medium and 91 small vehicles.Under the Centre's Rs 9,585-crore Parivartan programme, owners are required to scrap BS-III and older vehicles at registered facilities in Haryana. The incentives include a 100% exemption from motor vehicle tax for 10 years, waiver of registration fees, 5% interest subvention on loans for five years and a minimum 8% discount on the ex-showroom price of replacement vehicles.Buyers opting for BS-VI diesel and CNG vehicles can also receive monthly fuel vouchers ranging from Rs 1,200 to Rs 4,800 for five years. Those purchasing electric vehicles are eligible for one-time assistance ranging from Rs 64,000 to Rs 2.56 lakh.Regional Transport Authority official Munish Kumar said the Parivartan, or 'new journey', scheme aims to phase out old commercial vehicles and encourage the adoption of BS-VI and electric vehicles.However, the history of enforcement highlights the challenge of translating policy into actual scrapping. Pollution control board data submitted to the National Green Tribunal showed that, as of January 2025, Haryana's NCR districts had 17.57 lakh vehicles beyond the prescribed age limits of 10 years for diesel and 15 years for petrol vehicles. Against this, only 6,537 vehicles had been deregistered, accounting for less than 0.4% of the total.

headline: Govt procurement of barley from Pangi farmers rises 445 per cent in a year
content: From a traditional subsistence crop to a promising source of income, barley is witnessing a remarkable turnaround in the tribal Pangi valley of Chamba district. Government procurement has soared nearly 445 per cent in a year, with 172 farmers selling 542.86 quintals of naturally grown barley worth Rs 43.43 lakh this season, against just 99.74 quintals worth Rs 5.98 lakh procured from only 34 farmers last year.The sharp rise in barley procurement follows the decision of the state government to increase the minimum support price (MSP) to Rs 8,000 per quintal, giving farmers a strong financial incentive to expand cultivation.The figures reflect a growing shift towards natural farming in the remote valley, where farmers are increasingly viewing barley not only as a traditional food crop but also as a commercially viable agricultural option.The transformation is particularly significant for Pangi, where difficult terrain, harsh winter and limited agricultural opportunities often restrict farmers’ income options. Barley has traditionally been an important part of the valley’s farming system and food culture, but its cultivation was largely limited to household consumption.Pangi was declared the state’s first natural farming sub-division on April 15, 2025, when Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu had visited the valley.Initially, an MSP of Rs 60 per kg was announced for naturally grown barley. The rate was subsequently increased by Rs 20 per kg to Rs 80 per kg in 2026, substantially improving returns to growers.The higher support price has also helped revive interest in a traditional crop that is well suited to the region’s agricultural conditions. Instead of encouraging a shift towards resource-intensive commercial crops, the initiative seeks to make locally adapted farming practices economically rewarding. It also offers an opportunity to conserve traditional barley varieties and strengthen the region’s agricultural identity.The Agriculture Department and the Agricultural Technology Management Agency (ATMA) project have been working to expand the natural farming movement through awareness programmes and technical assistance.Farmers are being trained in the preparation and use of jeevamrit, natural fertilisers and other locally prepared inputs, besides adopting appropriate crop management practices. The objective is to reduce dependence on chemical fertilisers and pesticides while improving soil health and promoting sustainable agriculture.Officiating Resident Commissioner, Pangi, Amandeep Singh says that the enhanced support price has generated considerable interest among farmers in natural farming. The initiative is strengthening the rural economy while opening up additional avenues of income and self-employment in the valley.Agriculture Department subject matter specialist Naresh Nayak says that farmers are being provided technical guidance to expand natural barley cultivation and benefit from the government’s procurement scheme. The department is making efforts to encourage more farmers to take up natural farming and take advantage of the assured procurement facility, he adds.Beyond its economic significance, barley holds an important place in Pangi’s traditional food culture. For generations, the grain has been a staple of local diets. It is also used in preparing traditional fermented beverages such as “Patar”.

headline: Farmers’ anger, Bandi Singhs issue set to test SAD-BJP alliance
content: While the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) are busy invoking nostalgia from their 15-year rule and projecting their renewed alliance as a sign of electoral revival, the road ahead is unlikely to be easy for either party.From the issue of Bandi Singhs to a balm on the wounds of farmers, the reunion faces several tests.A senior SAD leader said the alliance was the outcome of nearly three months of back-channel negotiations, with seat-sharing being discussed at a later stage. “The SAD will face tough questions from farmers. I believe the party will not settle for anything less than an agriculture package, the release of Bandi Singhs and the promotion of agriculture-based, non-polluting industries,” the leader said, requesting anonymity.Notably, before the alliance was announced, two major farmer unions had extended support to the SAD.The leader said Akalis had factored in the optics of reviving the alliance after they walked out of it over the deaths of nearly 700 farmers during the 2020-21 anti-farm laws agitation.Despite being projected as the ‘bada bhai’ (big brother), the SAD may find it difficult to secure a dominant share of seats as the BJP, having expanded its organisational base since the 2020-21 break-up, is keen to consolidate its position.SAD spokespersons Daljit Cheema and Maheshinder Singh Grewal said people were experiencing political fatigue and were tired of governments remaining in confrontation with the Centre. “Wherever we went, people asked us about the alliance. We are upbeat about the development,” Cheema said.

headline: State spends 90 per cent of revenue on  salary & pension, highest in nation
content: Himachal makes the highest expenditure of 90 per cent of the total revenue on the payment of salaries, pension and interest in the country as compared to an all-state average of 82 per cent. These are the findings of the latest State of State Finances Report published by the PRS Legislative Research. Himachal Pradesh’s capital outlay has been pegged at Rs 3,090 crore for the current financial year against Rs 10,229 crore in the revised estimates for 2025-26. This reflects a decline of Rs 7,139 crore.The PRS analysis also shows a sharp reduction in the asset creation budget as the allocation has fallen from Rs 10,229 crore in revised estimates to Rs 3,090 crore for 2026-27.Another worrisome factor in the report is the outstanding debt of over 40 per cent, as only three other states — Punjab, Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland — fall in this category. In sharp contrast to these four states, the consolidated debt of other states is 28 per cent.The hill state’s own tax revenue from sources like State Goods and Services Tax (GST), stamp duty, VAT etc., is estimated to be a mere 5.5 per cent of its Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP), which is lower than the national average of 7 per cent. Maharashtra (7.7 per per cent), Punjab (7.2 per cent) and Karnataka (6.7 per cent) have a higher tax revenue to GSDP ratio.The overall fiscal indicators of the cash-trapped Himachal, which also faces severe geographical constraints, present a grim picture as the revenue deficit is also at a high of 2.4 per cent of the GSDP. This assumes importance in light of the fact that the revenue deficit of most of the states has been pegged at a mere 0.71 per cent of the GDP.The revenue deficit has steadily increased post Covid at mere 0.23 per cent in 2022-23. Ten states have consistently reported a revenue deficit and five states, including Chhattisgarh, Karnataka and Telangana, have moved from surplus to deficit.The report highlights that states have cumulatively estimated to spend four lakh crore rupees on unconditional cash transfer (UCT) schemes in 2026-27. The beneficiaries include women, farmers, elderly, widows and persons with disabilities. Himachal estimates to spend a mere 2 per cent of the revenue receipts on the UCT while nine states, including West Bengal, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, spend over 10 per cent of their revenue receipts on the UCT schemes.

headline: Palestinian Ambassador cites historic ties with India at varsity youth fest in Hisar
content: Palestinian Ambassador to India Abdullah Mohammad Abu Shawesh cited the historical ties between the two nations while adding that cooperation between India and Palestine goes beyond modern diplomatic relations and has roots in history.The Ambassador was the chief guest in the youth festival in Guru Jambheshwar University of Science and Technology (GJUST) which concluded yesterday. He was the Guest of Honour in the function today.Addressing the gathering of students, Abu Shawesh maintained that India is one of the world’s oldest and richest civilisations, with a rich legacy of philosophy, literature, science, art and spiritual thought. He said the historical presence of India in Palestine could still be traced through places such as the Indian Hospice in Jerusalem and the graves of Indian soldiers in Gaza and Haifa.The Ambassador also interacted with students on this occasion. Motivating the students, he said that the younger generation is entering a world that is full of possibilities. He said that however, the greatest assets of any nation were not merely its technology or natural resources, but also the imagination, knowledge, determination and character of its people.He emphasised that education should not be confined to obtaining a degree. “It should instill the courage to ask questions, the confidence to think independently and the determination to bring about positive change,” he said while responding to questions from the students during the interaction.

headline: Himachal: Apple yield falls sharply; scientists blame injudicious fertiliser use
content: Himachal Pradesh has witnessed a sharp decline in apple productivity over the past four decades. In 1981, apple productivity in the state was over 10 tonnes per hectare. In 2023, it declined to around 4.3 tonnes per hectare, according to an article published in ‘Indian Horticulture’, a journal brought out by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR). A team of scientists from the Dr YS Parmar University of Horticulture and Forestry, Nauni in Solan, has authored the article.The scientists point out that apple productivity declined by over 50 per cent in 2023 compared to 1981. Even in the best production years in recent times, productivity had barely crossed six tonnes per hectare. Such a steep fall in yield is startling, particularly when the apple industry has witnessed several scientific and technological advancements, along with the availability of pesticides and fertilisers to control diseases and boost production. For record, productivity in advanced apple producing nations such as New Zealand is over 55 tonnes per hectare.Usha Sharma, one of the co-authors of the article and senior scientist at the Krishi Vigyan Kendra, Shimla, says that the injudicious and unbalanced use of pesticides and fertilisers is one of the major reasons behind the decline in productivity. “The rampant use of pesticides and fertilisers has affected soil and plant health, resulting in the decline in productivity. Chemicals and climate change are other factors affecting productivity,” she adds.She points out that the use of pesticides and fertilisers was very limited until the early 1980s. It was the outbreak of scab, a fungal disease, in 1983-84 that pushed growers towards the regular application of pesticides to protect their produce from it and other diseases. “Over the years, the use of pesticides and fertilisers has become quite injudicious, affecting both soil and plant health,” she adds.According to the article, the prolonged and intensive use of chemical inputs has contributed to soil degradation. Many orchards are now experiencing reduced soil fertility, poor water-holding capacity and a decline in beneficial soil microbial populations.The scientists have also pointed out that changing climatic conditions, including warmer winters and irregular rainfall patterns, are adversely affecting apple production. Traditional varieties are increasingly finding it difficult to adapt to these changing environmental conditions. The current year is a classic example of how adverse weather, particularly during the flowering stage, can hit apple production. This year, production is unlikely to exceed 1.70 crore boxes, which will be among the lowest in recent years. The scientists have suggested natural and regenerative farming as a sustainable alternative to improve soil health, biodiversity and ecological balance.

headline: WHO chief calls on US to lift oil blockade on Cuba, citing health impact
content: World Health Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called on Tuesday for the immediate lifting of the US fuel blockade on Cuba, warning that the measure was putting the lives of children at risk."The intensification of fuel restrictions and sanctions is causing direct harm to the Cuban people, especially the most vulnerable," Tedros said on a recent visit to Cuba that included tours of several healthcare facilities in Havana."It is endangering their lives, including the lives of children."During his three-day visit, the official said his organization would contribute $2 million to help strengthen Cuba’s national immunization program and provide essential medical equipment to healthcare facilities.Also Read | Entrepreneurs in Cuba are snapping up American fuelsLike the World Health Organization, the United Nations has also repeatedly warned of a growing humanitarian crisis on the island, calling the US fuel blockade a violation of international law and the human rights of all Cubans.The Cuban government says US sanctions have led to daily power outages lasting 20 hours or more, critical shortages of medicines and surgical supplies, and a decline in health indicators, such as infant mortality rates.Washington argues the energy blockade is intended to push for political change on the island, and says that exports of food and medicine are subject to legal exemptions.Tensions between the two nations have soared since the administration of US President Donald Trump ramped up pressure on Cuba since January, imposing a fuel blockade on the island and stiff sanctions against ​a swath of Cuban officials and state entities.Also Read | UN condemns US sanctions on Cuba as 17 countries vote against resolution amid Washington's pushAn annual non-binding resolution calling for an end to a US embargo on the island has passed in favor of Cuba in ​the UN General Assembly by wide margins every year since 1992.

headline: FSSAI Scrutiny Limited To One Goa Batch, Now Out Of Circulation: Bisleri
content: Packaged drinking water maker Bisleri International on Tuesday said the FSSAI scrutiny related to just one batch manufactured at its Goa plant in September 2025, which is no longer in circulation, adding that subsequent testing found bromate levels in the sample within permissible limits. The company said all its 143 manufacturing plants remain operational and compliant with FSSAI regulations, with the Goa facility also continuing operations without any suspension order from the regulator. "Bisleri produces more than 50,000 batches annually. FSSAI's sale prohibition applies only to one Batch GO 270, manufactured in Goa on 27 September 2025. There are no stocks of this batch in the market currently," it said. "The FSSAI has categorically and conclusively clarified on 23rd November 2026 that bromates were found below the permissible limit on re-testing of the above batch sample." Responding to an FSSAI clarification issued on November 23, Bisleri said the regulatory action related exclusively to batch GO 270, manufactured on September 27, 2025, and that no stocks from the batch were currently available in the market. The company said FSSAI had clarified that bromate levels detected on retesting the batch sample were below the permissible limit. Separately, it acknowledged that one of six samples tested in a subsequent round had reported polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) at 0.144 micrograms per litre. Another sample from the same batch had cleared all parameters.

headline: CDC issues health advisory for Iowa residents ahead of US Army's planned 5-ton chemical explosion | Hindustan Times
content: The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has activated an emergency response in Iowa ahead of the US Army's planned detonation of around five tons of lead azide. The agency is working with state officials to prepare for possible exposure to lead dust and air pollution from the operation.At the request of Iowa, the CDC is supporting the state's Department of Health and Human Services in preparing recommendations to protect residents. It has also formed a team of specialists in toxicology, public communication and public health emergency response.The agency is preparing to help assess the health effects on nearby communities after the detonation if required. Its response comes as concerns grow over the possible release of lead particles into the air during the planned explosion.CDC tells residents how to protect themselves The CDC has issued several safety recommendations for people who may be affected by the operation. Residents have been asked to monitor official alerts and either stay indoors or evacuate if they are inside the designated evacuation zone. They should wait for state officials to confirm that the air is safe before returning home. Also Read: Federal court allows Army to blast unstable lead azide barrels at Iowa ammunition plantThe agency has also advised people to keep their doors and windows closed and seal gaps to stop outdoor air from entering their homes. Those with a furnace have been asked to set it to recirculate indoor air.Residents with air filters have been advised to consider replacing them before the detonation. The CDC recommends using filters rated MERV 11 or higher, if possible.It has also warned about the risk of lead dust entering homes on clothing and footwear. People who believe their shoes may have been exposed should remove them before entering a building. The agency has also advised washing clothes and hands before touching the face or eating.For indoor cleaning, residents should follow instructions from the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services on how to safely remove lead dust.Army says controlled detonation is the safest optionThe US Army plans to destroy 68 barrels containing around five tons of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown on Wednesday morning, as per the Associated Press. Officials have warned that the ageing chemical has become unstable and could cause a chain-reaction explosion if left in storage.Also Read: Trump's halts Army's plans to detonate bomb-making chemicals in Iowa, pending court approvalThe operation has raised concerns among residents and environmental groups over possible health and environmental effects. The Army, however, has maintained that controlled detonation is the safest option.Officials have added barriers around the blast site and plan to use ballistic gels, foams and thousands of gallons of water to limit the spread of lead dust. The detonation was also moved to Wednesday to allow more time for safety measures and take advantage of better wind conditions.The Army expects the wind to carry the plume southwest, away from Burlington, while maps released by officials show its expected path towards Missouri.The CDC's response is focused on helping Iowa prepare residents for possible exposure and supporting public health assessments after the operation.

headline: Haryana recommends IFS officer’s termination over illegal felling of 2,585 trees
content: The Haryana Forest Department has recommended termination of the services of Indian Forest Service (IFS) officer Jhalkar Uyake over alleged negligence and involvement in the illegal felling of 2,585 trees in the Alipur-Sikargarh Reserved Forest in Faridabad, officials familiar with the developments said on Tuesday. The recommendation has been forwarded to Additional Chief Secretary, Environment, Forests and Wildlife, Sudhir Rajpal, and is now under consideration by the state government. If approved by the Chief Minister, the proposal will be referred to the Centre for a final decision on the officer's termination, highly placed sources told The Indian Express. Uyake was not available for comment. However, it is learnt that he too had, earlier this month, flagged the large-scale illegal felling of mature green kikar trees in reserved forest area. A 2022-batch IFS officer, Uyake was serving as Deputy Conservator of Forests (DCF), Faridabad, when the alleged illegal felling took place. He was suspended on November 18 over allegations of negligence in preventing the felling and alleged involvement in the case. The investigation revealed an alleged systematic clearance of nearly 25 acres of reserved forest land and the unauthorised removal of hundreds of tonnes of timber, officials said. “Initially, the illegal felling of nearly 2,000 trees was detected, but subsequent counting has established that 2,585 trees were felled. Around 3,000 quintals of wood have also been recovered,” a senior Forest Department officer told The Indian Express. Officials suspect that contractors engaged for plantation-related work were involved in the felling in connivance with forest personnel responsible for protecting the reserved forest. In a report submitted on November 16, Chief Conservator of Forests (CCF), Gurugram, Subhash Yadav, flagged the alleged involvement of field-level forest staff and stated that Uyake was aware of the felling of mature trees and the transportation of timber to different locations. Another senior departmental officer also raised allegations against Uyake in a communication to Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (PCCF) and Head of Forest Force K C Meena, describing the matter as serious. The state government suspended Uyake under Rule 3(1) of the All India Services (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1969, on November 18, citing allegations of negligence in preventing the illegal felling. However, in a communication dated November 12 to Meena, Uyake himself had flagged the large-scale felling of mature green kikar trees in the reserved forest, alleging negligence and possible connivance among field staff. He said that during an inspection on the morning of November 11, he had witnessed extensive felling at a site where CAMPA-funded plantation work was underway across nearly 19 hectares, involving the planting of around 64,000 saplings. Suspecting that the plantation work was being used as a pretext for commercial timber extraction, Uyake said the illegal activity could have been continuing for nearly two months, or even before the tender was awarded. He alleged gross negligence and possible connivance on the part of Range Officer Afzal Khan and Foresters Ankit Kumar and Sandeep Kumar, who had failed to prevent or report the felling despite clear instructions that no standing tree was to be cut. Uyake had also flagged discrepancies between the plantation progress reported by field staff and the actual conditions at the site, alleging possible manipulation of official records and concealment of unauthorised activities. He said he had ordered an immediate halt to plantation and site-preparation work, lodged a complaint with the DCP, Central, Faridabad, seeking registration of an FIR, and initiated action against the contractor. He had also sought the suspension of the three forest officials pending an investigation, citing supervisory lapses and possible collusion. On November 20, the state government dismissed Afzal Khan, Ankit Kumar, and Sandeep Kumar in connection with the illegal felling. Invoking Article 311(2)(b) of the Constitution, the government dismissed them without a regular departmental inquiry, citing their alleged connivance with contractors and the impracticability of conducting such an inquiry. Meanwhile, a team of senior Forest Department officers visited the Alipur Reserved Forest on Tuesday to assess the damage. Police have also registered an FIR on the basis of a complaint lodged by the department regarding the illegal felling.

headline: Cops stop Mehbooba‘s Sheshnag trek amid BRO construction row
content: SRINAGAR/JAMMU: Amid the row over BRO’s construction work near the 11,780-foot-high Sheshnag Lake in Jammu & Kashmir, PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti Tuesday attempted to trek to the spot but was stopped by police at Chandanwari, some 12 kms from the site.“My worst fears were confirmed today when police stopped me from proceeding towards Sheshnag. The questions surrounding construction in this fragile glacial ecosystem are only growing louder. What is being concealed today could become a man-made disaster tomorrow. The Amarnath cave, yatra route and surrounding mountains must be protected as one ecological whole,” Mehbooba said.After a video of an earthmover purportedly near Sheshnag began circulating, the BRO (Border Roads Organisation) had clarified it was only carrying out post-Amarnath Yatra works in compliance with all applicable safety and environmental norms and its primary objective was to safeguard pilgrims throughout the yatra.MLA Hasnian Masoodi of the governing National Conference, however, rejected the BRO’s response. “If the track is being made safer, why are earthmovers being taken over there? This shouldn’t happen,” he added.Environmental activists say Sheshnag is a glacial lake and an ecologically fragile zone surrounded by steep slopes and glacial deposits. The lake is the source of the Lidder river, which flows downstream to Pahalgam and beyond into the Kashmir Valley. Sheshnag is among 14 high-risk glacial lakes identified in Jammu & Kashmir.Environmental activist Raja Muzaffar Bhat warned that constructing a road around the Sheshnag glacier would be an environmental disaster. “More and more people must approach the Supreme Court, the National Green Tribunal (NGT) or the high court,” he said.On Monday, Congress MP and spokesperson Pawan Khera had said Sheshnag was not a construction site but a fragile Himalayan ecosystem and a sacred lake for both Hindus and Muslims.Meanwhile, BJP has defended the project, accusing Kashmir-based political parties and the Congress of communalising the issue.State BJP spokesperson Girdhari Lal Raina said certain political elements seem to have found a new pretext to communalise the atmosphere in the Amarnath Yatra track-widening issue. He said the BRO has clarified that the work concerns widening and stabilisation of vulnerable stretches of the existing Chandanwari-Amarnath track to ease congestion and improve pilgrim safety.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Burglars target five villas in Aushapur gated community, decamp with ₹10.3-lakh loot
content: Hyderabad: Burglars targeted five locked villas at the Jagathswapna gated community in Aushapur and escaped with valuables worth about ₹10.3 lakh on Sunday night. The thefts came to light on Monday, following which police registered two separate cases based on complaints lodged by the victims.In the first case, D Vijayalaxmi (53), a homemaker, said she and her family had left for their native place on Nov 9 following the death of a relative. At about 10 am on Monday, the community’s security guard noticed that the lock of their villa had been damaged, and informed them over phone. The family immediately returned to the villa and found household articles scattered. “About 40 tolas of gold, two kg silver and ₹1.75 lakh in cash was stolen by the burglars,” the complainant alleged. The stolen property was collectively worth ₹10.15 lakh, the complainant said.In the second case, Dr P Arun Mitra, who works at AIIMS, lodged a complaint on behalf of his colleague Dr Durgesh Pralad, whose villa was also burgled on Sunday night. After the security guard alerted Durgesh, Arun Mitra visited the house at his colleague’s request. They lodged a complaint stating that a wristwatch worth ₹12,000 and ₹7,500 in cash were stolen from the villa.According to Ghatkesar police, burglars also broke into three more villas in the same community but no theft was reported from there.Police registered the cases under sections 331(4) (housebreaking by night) and 305(a) (theft in a building) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The CLUES team collected fingerprints from the crime scenes. The prints were reportedly matched with a previous offender from Uttar Pradesh. headline: 73.3 lakh left off draft roll, barely 1,000 file fresh forms in Telangana
content: Hyderabad: Barely 1,000 of the 73.3 lakh voters left out of Telangana’s draft electoral roll have submitted fresh enumeration forms after the Election Commission gave eligible electors another chance to get their names included.The Telangana chief electoral officer’s (CEO) office said reports from districts showed that only around 50 to 100 people in each district has so far come forward to submit fresh enumeration forms.The largest group excluded from the Aug 17 draft roll comprised 45.1 lakh electors recorded as having permanently shifted from their registered addresses. Another 11.2 lakh were listed as absent or untraceable, while 9.2 lakh were identified as deceased and 6.7 lakh as voters already enrolled elsewhere.Explaining how absent, shifted, dead and duplicate (ASDD) entries were identified during the Special Intensive Revision, the CEO’s office said: “This was done only after house-to-house visit and due enquiry by BLOs (booth-level officers) and not done unilaterally.”The fresh enumeration forms provide one route for eligible voters to get back onto the rolls. Election officials said many voters who found their names missing had already applied through Form 6 before the EC provided the additional opportunity. BLOs will collect fresh enumeration forms until Nov 30, while the final roll is scheduled to be published on Dec 22.99% of flagged electors clearedSeparately, officials scrutinised 92.8 lakh electors already on the draft roll whose records had drawn notices. District reports as of Nov 20 showed that nearly 99%, or 92 lakh, had been cleared for inclusion in the final roll.These included 60.1 lakh electors whose records showed logical discrepancies and 31.8 lakh whose entries could not be matched with earlier rolls.Of the 2,64,87,213 electors on the draft roll, officials marked 2,63,96,341, or 99.6%, for inclusion in the final roll. Another 58,772 were marked ineligible, while decisions were pending in 32,100 cases.Hyderabad has seven in 10 pending casesHyderabad accounted for 22,958 pending cases, or 71.5% of the state total. In comparison, only 29 cases were awaiting a decision in Rangareddy and 22 in Medchal-Malkajgiri.Across Telangana, officials marked 35,934 unmapped electors ineligible, compared with 21,885 electors whose records showed logical discrepancies.Rangareddy recorded the highest number of electors marked ineligible at 13,493, including 11,471 unmapped voters. Mulugu had the highest proportion, with 1.39% of its draft electorate marked ineligible, compared with 0.22% statewide.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. headline: Rs 4.5 crore missing from panchayats’ accounts, Haryana orders forensic audit
content: The Haryana Development and Panchayats Department has ordered a forensic audit into financial transactions after nearly Rs 4.5 crore was found missing from bank accounts of several Panchayati Raj Institutions. A senior government officer told The Indian Express on Tuesday that the audit would be conducted by the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), a Government of India research and development organisation, to determine how unauthorised transfers took place and identify possible lapses in the banking and payment systems. Developed in 2022, the Fund Disbursement Management System (FDMS) of the Haryana Development and Panchayats Department has been functioning without any reported errors, the officer said, adding: “The possibility of a lapse in the banking system, however, cannot be ruled out.” The officer also pointed to the “absence of” a daily account reconciliation facility and “incomplete” KYC compliance for gram panchayat accounts, saying: “Proper KYC verification by the bank would have ensured that OTP-based transaction alerts were sent to the gram panchayats concerned.” The officer said the FDMS neither generates nor sends payment orders for the disputed transactions, yet funds were transferred to other bank accounts. “This has raised questions about how the transactions were processed without authorisation through the department's fund disbursement system.” Another officer said most disputed transactions took place over two days on November 14 and 15. The department has lodged a complaint with the Cyber Wing of the Haryana Police in Panchkula after discovering that nearly Rs 75 lakh was fraudulently transferred from seven accounts maintained with a nationalised bank to a private company in the given period. The transactions were allegedly carried out without the digital signatures of the department's authorised officers, the official said. Fatehabad Zila Parishad chairperson Suman Khichar said more than Rs 80 lakh went missing from PRIs' bank accounts in the district, adding: “We have informed the department about it.” Meanwhile, in an effort to strengthen cybersecurity and financial safeguards, the Finance Department on Monday ordered all government departments, boards, corporations, authorities and universities to immediately implement mandatory cybersecurity controls and financial safeguards for digital payment infrastructure and cloud-based systems. “In light of the evolving threat landscape targeting public digital infrastructure, it is imperative to secure all government funds, transaction pipelines, and application hosting environments,” said Sudhir Rajpal, Additional Chief Secretary (Finance), Haryana, in the directive.

headline: 5.6 lakh consumers in Delhi clear water bills, Rs 3,618 cr in penalties written off
content: More than 5.66 lakh consumers have cleared their pending water bills under the Delhi Jal Board's (DJB) Late Payment Surcharge (LPSC) Waiver Scheme, and dues to the tune of Rs 3,618 crore in penalties have been written off, according to the Delhi government. The DJB has collected Rs 1,076 crore in old dues. Under the scheme, consumers who pay the original or principal amount of their unpaid water bills do not have to pay the late payment surcharge that piled up over the years. The scheme is meant to encourage consumers to clear long-pending dues voluntarily, according to the government. Of the 13.39 lakh eligible households, 5.48 lakh, or about 41%, have used the scheme so far. They paid Rs 854.54 crore in principal dues and received waivers worth Rs 1,886.89 crore. Commercial consumers were brought under the scheme later. Of the 70,312 eligible commercial consumers, 18,275, or about 26%, have availed the benefits of the scheme. They have paid Rs 221.61 crore and received waivers worth Rs 1,731.84 crore. Even as households that availed the scheme outnumber commercial consumers 30 to one, the dues written off are nearly the same. On average, each commercial consumer received a waiver of about Rs 9.5 lakh, against about Rs 34,000 for a household. Water Minister and DJB chairman Parvesh Sahib Singh said consumers came forward voluntarily to clear their dues. "Our intention is not merely to recover dues, but to make it easier for every eligible consumer to settle their account and get the benefit of the rebate," he said. The DJB is now carrying out an e-KYC drive to identify every eligible consumer. "Our work is not over yet," Singh said, adding that the aim was to complete e-KYC for all eligible consumers, extend the waiver to them and meet the board's target for recovering principal dues. The government said the money recovered would strengthen the DJB's finances and help improve water supply and sewerage services. It has appealed to consumers who have not yet availed of the scheme to complete their e-KYC.

headline: Andhra Pradesh extends Employees Health Scheme facilities to retired transport staff
content: VIJAYAWADA The Andhra Pradesh Public Transport Department (APPTD) has advised its unit officers to step up awareness and facilitate enrolment of retired employees in the Employees Health Scheme (EHS), following the government’s permission to extend medical benefits to the staff who retired on or after January 1, 2020. In a circular issued on Monday, the officials said the government had permitted the Chief Executive Officer of Dr NTR Vaidya Seva Trust to extend EHS facilities to retired APPTD employees on payment of the prescribed one-time subscription. The scheme also covers their spouses. They said 10,249 employees had retired or ceased service between January 1, 2020, and October 2026, of whom 7,844 had enrolled in EHS so far. Retired employees enrolled in the scheme are entitled to medical facilities at EHS-empanelled hospitals and APSRTC dispensaries. The department had also issued instructions earlier this year extending outpatient (OP) facilities at APSRTC dispensaries and hospitals. These include consultation, treatment, diagnostic investigations and supply of medicines for ailments covered under EHS. As retired employees have been showing interest in joining the scheme, unit officers have been asked to conduct awareness programmes at every depot on the second Tuesday and Wednesday of each month to explain its benefits and facilitate enrolment. Officers have also been instructed to collect the details of retired employees who have not yet enrolled, through a Google Form, and facilitate the generation of login credentials from Dr NTR Vaidya Seva Trust so that they can access the scheme’s benefits.

headline: Brigade Group acquires 2.25-acre in Secunderabad for ₹180 crore
content: HYDERABAD Brigade Group has acquired a 2.25-acre land parcel in Secunderabad for ₹180 crore and proposes to develop the site into a premium residential project with an estimated revenue potential of around ₹1,000 crore. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/telangana/brigade-group-to-acquire-225-acres-in-secunderabad/article70571234.ece “Hyderabad continues to be a key growth market for Brigade and this acquisition further strengthens our presence in the city. As we scale our presence in Hyderabad, we remain focused on acquiring strategically located land parcels that offer strong development potential,” said Amar Mysore, executive director, Brigade Enterprises. Secunderabad is an established location with strong connectivity and access to social and commercial infrastructure, making it well suited for a premium residential development, he said in a release on Monday. Located between MG Road and Necklace Road, Secunderabad, the proposed development will benefit from the area’s central location, established social and commercial infrastructure, and strong connectivity to key parts of Hyderabad, Brigade Group said.

headline: No permission sought for November 26 anti-SIR march, says Delhi police
content: NEW DELHI No permission has been sought from the Delhi Police for a protest march against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, scheduled for November 26, a senior New Delhi police told The Hindu. However, the organisers have maintained that they have intimated the police about the proposed demonstration. The Delhi wing of the People Against SIR platform, a collective of multiple organisations opposing the voter roll revision exercise, has called for a peaceful march on Constitution Day from Valmiki Sadan on Mandir Marg to Jantar Mantar, demanding the scrapping of SIR and the restoration of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, among other demands. Maimoona Mollah, a representative of People Against SIR, told The Hindu that an intimation letter had been sent to the Delhi Police regarding the march earlier this week. “We make sure not to ask for permission but only inform the police about the march,” she said. People Against SIR was formed in October 14 following an emergency consultation in Delhi attended by representatives of more than 200 organisations. The national platform brings together 145 civil society groups, farmers’ unions, workers’ organisations, and women’s and youth groups across 18 States to campaign against the SIR exercise. According to information shared by the platform, participants will assemble at Valmiki Sadan at 12.30 p.m. on November 26 before marching to Jantar Mantar. The organisers have also announced plans to burn copies of the SIR notification during the demonstration. The platform has claimed that more than 50% of the voters who were on Delhi’s electoral rolls in January 2025 and voted in the February 2025 Assembly election have either been deleted or categorised as doubtful following the revision exercise. It has also alleged that 13.3 crore voters have been removed from electoral rolls across the country since the SIR exercise began in Bihar last year. The organisers have described SIR as an attack on the Constitution and the right to vote, alleging that the exercise disproportionately affects marginalised communities, including minorities, Dalits, transgender persons, women, migrant workers and the homeless. The march will also demand the restoration of pre-SIR electoral rolls, no elections being conducted on the basis of revised rolls, impeachment and legal action against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, and the repeal of the 2023 law governing the appointment of election commissioners. November 26 marks the adoption of the Constitution of India in 1949.

headline: Days before Jharkhand High Court Chief Justice’s retirement, Supreme Court Collegium proposes successor
content: NEW DELHI Hardly three days before the retirement of incumbent Jharkhand High Court Chief Justice M.S. Sonak, the Supreme Court Collegium headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) proposed the transfer of Karnataka High Court Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru to the office. Who is Justice Surya Kant, the 53rd Chief Justice of India? storyline 1 Also read | Hemant Soren writes to CJI to urgently appoint Jharkhand HC Chief Justice successor https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/jharkhand/hemant-soren-writes-to-cji-to-urgently-appoint-jharkhand-hc-chief-justice-successor/article71730713.ece The Collegium’s decision has come shortly after Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren wrote to the Chief Justice of India, expressing concern about a lack of decision regarding a successor to Justice Sonak, who is superannuating on November 27. Hemant Soren | Weathering the political storm storyline 1 Hemant Soren writes to CJI to urgently appoint Jharkhand HC Chief Justice successor storyline 1 Mr. Soren had highlighted that a Chief Justice to the State High Court should ideally have been recommended by the Supreme Court Collegium in advance, and cleared by the Union government as per the Memorandum of Procedure for appointment of judges to the constitutional courts. Justice Mahesh Sharadchandra Sonak sworn in as Chief Justice of Jharkhand High Court Justice Mahesh Sharadchandra Sonak sworn in as Chief Justice of Jharkhand High Court Chief Minister Hemant Soren, Chief Secretary Avinash Kumar and other senior officials were present on the occasion. Justice Mahesh Sharadchandra Sonak sworn in as Chief Justice of Jharkhand High Court storyline 1 The Chief Minister, as the head of the State government, had expressed objections about any interim arrangement, making it clear that the State High Court must have a regular Chief Justice at the helm. Mr. Soren, in his letter to the CJI and the Collegium judges, had reportedly pointed out that frequent transitions accompanied by extended interim arrangements disrupt administrative continuity, affect institutional planning and create uncertainty within the judicial establishment. On Tuesday (November 24), the Supreme Court Collegium proposed that Justice Bakhru take over as the Chief Justice of Jharkhand High Court upon the retirement of the incumbent Chief Justice. The ball is now with the government to clear the Collegium resolution and notify the appointment of Justice Bakhru by November 27. The Collegium has recommended Justice M.S. Ramachandra Rao, Chief Justice of the Tripura High Court, to be transferred as the Chief Justice of the Karnataka High Court in the place of Justice Bakhru. In a separate resolution on November 24, the Collegium recommended the appointment of Himachal Pradesh High Court judge, Justice Vivek Singh Thakur, as Chief Justice of the Tripura High Court following the transfer of Justice Rao to the Karnataka High Court.

headline: From guitarists to comedians, AI clones are copying real performances and taking the views
content: You may have come across videos of Jensen Huang, Elon Musk, Sam Altman and Dario Amodei dancing to Uptown Funk by Mark Ronson and Bruno Mars. Watch one, and your social media feed is suddenly packed with similar clips, all featuring the same dance steps from the original video. Or think of the videos in which cats replace Vincent Vega and Mia Wallace dancing to Chuck Berry’s You Never Can Tell in Pulp Fiction. These are, needless to say, AI-generated videos made with any of several easily accessible apps. Now imagine a popular guitarist replaced by an AI-generated images created without her consent. What you get is a realistic fake depiction of a real person. It is a new trend taking over social media feeds, and the technique has been dubbed reskinning. AI is not just replacing celebrities in popular videos. It can also make a fake video of a stand-up comedian telling a real comedian’s jokes. Yet the industry is taking a hands-off approach. BBC Verify recently reported on the ordeal of UK guitarist Sophie Lloyd, who tours with Machine Gun Kelly. Accounts keep reskinning her performances with over-sexualised AI characters. One account published hundreds of short clips of an AI-generated guitarist, several of which copied Lloyd’s performances right down to the music, the movements and even the facial expressions. The giveaways are often in the details: distorted fingers playing chords that do not match the music, or guitar strings that stay still when strummed. Some of these accounts use their avatars to promote and sell adult content. And celebrities are not the only ones being replaced in these AI-generated nuggets. Popular content creators are going through the same ordeal. A dancer’s video was reskinned with an AI-generated bunny that went on to draw millions of views, far more than the original. The account behind it was promoting courses on how to make money from AI content.

headline: ‘Himachal Feels Like Home’: CJI Surya Kant Reconnects with State, Praises Clean Air at Dharamshala University Convocation
content: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Justice Surya Kant’s emotional association with Himachal Pradesh found a special expression during the 10th convocation of the Central University of Himachal Pradesh in Dharamshala on Sunday, as he described the hill state as his home and recalled his brief but memorable tenure as Chief Justice of the Himachal Pradesh High Court. Speaking before students, faculty members and distinguished guests, Justice Surya Kant said that although he had spent only around seven months in Himachal Pradesh as Chief Justice of the state High Court, his emotional connection with the state had endured. “I have some emotional attachment with Himachal Pradesh. I feel that Himachal is my home,” he remarked, drawing thunderous applause from the gathering. Recalling his appointment in October 2018 as Chief Justice of the Himachal Pradesh High Court, he said that despite having had limited time in the state, his association with Himachal had continued over the years. Expressing his pleasure at returning to Dharamshala, the CJI said the invitation from the state government and the Central University had provided him an opportunity to spend at least a day amidst the natural beauty of Himachal. In a particularly candid observation, apparently contrasting the experience with the deteriorating air quality in the national capital, Justice Surya Kant said he had the opportunity to breathe clean, crisp air and enjoy clean oxygen in Himachal Pradesh.

headline: No refund after cancelling hiking shoe order, retailer told to pay advocate Rs 20,067
content: A customer, an advocate who cancelled a hiking shoe order after selecting the wrong size did not get his Rs 10,067 refund, even though the retailer claimed it had returned the money. Finding that the company failed to prove the amount reached the customer's bank account, a Himachal Pradesh Consumer Commission has directed it to pay him Rs 20,067. The Kangra District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission president Hemanshu Mishra and members Arti Sood and Narayan Thakur were hearing Akshay Thakur's complaint alleging that he had not received a Rs 10,067 refund after cancelling an online order for two pairs of hiking shoes, and seeking a refund with 18 per cent annual interest, Rs 20,000 compensation for mental agony and harassment, and Rs 20,000 towards litigation expenses. “Withholding of the complainant's rightful funds, coupled with the lack of transparent communication and deficient customer support, constitutes a clear and distinct act of deficiency in service and unfair trade practice on the part of the Opposite Party (the retailer), causing avoidable financial loss, mental agony, and harassment to the complainant. Therefore, the complaint deserves to be allowed,” the commission said on November 13. Thakur ordered two pairs of men's mid-ankle hiking shoes for Rs 10,067, including delivery charges on October 10, 2025. Realising immediately that he had selected the wrong size and quantity, he tried to cancel the order. However, the application generated another order for the same shoes. He then cancelled that order too, but alleged that despite the cancellation being accepted and repeated follow-ups with customer support, the promised refund never reached his bank account. Customer says refund never reached his account According to the complaint, each pair cost Rs 4,999. With Rs 69 in delivery charges, Thakur paid Rs 10,067 through UPI. He said the application generated another order for the same product, size, and quantity instead of cancelling his first order. He then submitted a second cancellation request, which was accepted with a refund promised within seven to 10 working days. The company said it refunded Rs 10,067 on October 10, 2025, when the replacement order was cancelled. It said a fresh order was generated after Thakur requested a replacement for the wrong size, and the refund was processed to his original payment account after cancellation. The company relied on a refund processing record and alleged that Thakur, an advocate, had filed a frivolous complaint despite receiving the money. It sought dismissal with exemplary costs. Processing receipt is not proof of refund The commission said the issue was whether Rs 10,067 had actually reached the customer's bank account. It found that the company's document only mentioned that refund processing would take three to five working days and the amount would be credited within five to seven working days. The company did not produce a bank statement, ledger, clearing house confirmation or other financial record proving actual credit. It said a service provider claiming to have completed a refund had to prove credit; an internal processing status was insufficient. Thakur stated in his sworn affidavit that he had not received the money. With no evidence establishing actual credit, the commission found his claim unrebutted. It rejected the allegation that the complaint was frivolous, noting that Thakur had exercised his statutory consumer right. The commission held that the failure to establish the refund, along with deficient customer support and a lack of transparent communication, amounted to deficiency in service and unfair trade practice. It also ordered Rs 5,000 compensation for mental agony, humiliation and harassment, and Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs. Takeaway If a company claims to have refunded your money, an internal payment status or refund receipt alone may not be enough to establish that the money reached your bank account. Consumers can seek proof of actual credit and approach the consumer commission if their refund grievance remains unresolved. Aggrieved consumers may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states (Himachal Pradesh: 1800-180-8087) or call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance.
